title: Impact of a hospital digital coordination centre on patient flow in a large tertiary centre
abstract: Hospitals globally are under increasing strain due to rising demand and constrained capacity. This interrupted-time-series study evaluates the impact of a digital coordination centre, implemented on August 28th of 2023, where a multidisciplinary operational team (comprising data scientists, patient flow managers, facilities managers, patient transport and nursing staff, for example) use real-time data dashboards showing measures of emergency department (ED) crowding and inpatient utilisation to optimise patient flow in an Australian metropolitan tertiary hospital. Analysis of 191,415 emergency department arrivals admitted to acute care and 187,783 acute inpatient episodes between July 2020 and July 2025 showed substantial improvements in measures of patient flow: 33% decrease in ED length of stay, 73% increase in hospital admissions from the ED within four hours of arrival, 7% decrease in inpatient length of stay, and 5% increase in discharges completed before noon. These changes coincided with a broader programme of organisational and operational reform, of which the DCC was a central integrating component. Hence, the findings support digitally enabled coordination centres as an effective contribution the overall strategy for improving hospital operational efficiency.

title: Access Block and Ambulance Ramping: The Canaries of the Healthcare System.
abstract: Objective To identify evidence-based factors leading to the global challenge of hospital access block and inform strategies to improve emergency access performance. Methods A mixed methods approach was followed comprising an umbrella review of published systematic reviews, qualitative analysis of the perspectives of patients and healthcare workers, and quantitative analysis of contextual factors and 6 years of ambulance, emergency inpatient and ward movement records for the 25 largest public hospitals in Queensland, Australia. Results A key set of findings and recommendations were identified to improve emergency access that are practical and actionable. These comprise the introduction of inpatient discharge metrics and monitoring to shift focus from the front door of hospitals to the 'back door'; increasing support for primary care, community care, aged care, NDIS and vulnerable groups; maintaining demand-side strategies such as increasing inpatient-equivalent care alternatives (e.g., hospital in the home, acute care within nursing home services); investment in prehospital flow; improving hospital processes such as extended-hour discharge lounges; improving workforce; and revising funding policies. Conclusions The study findings fill a gap in the evidence regarding challenges and recommendations for improving patient flow within hospital emergency departments and across the broader health system. Focussing efforts at the 'back end' of the inpatient journey is a critical step to improve emergency care outcomes.

title: Comprehensive hemodynamic assessment of the Fontan pathway using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Objectives Conventional hemodynamic assessment of Fontan circulation relies on limited quantitative measurements. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical value of comprehensive flow visualization using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging to characterize patient-specific hemodynamic patterns in extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection. Methods Eight patients with extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection underwent four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging at a median of 13.7 years postoperatively (interquartile range: 9.0-16.4 years). The Fontan pathway was segmented into five regions: extracardiac conduit, superior vena cava, central confluence, left pulmonary artery, and right pulmonary artery. Energy loss, maximum velocity, and kinetic energy were quantified for each segment using iTFlow software. Clinical outcomes were assessed during follow-up. Results Median age at total cavopulmonary connection was 1.8 years (interquartile range: 1.5-3.5), with 18 mm conduits in seven patients and 22 mm conduit in one patient. During a median follow-up of 17.3 years, two patients underwent re-operation after magnetic resonance imaging evaluation (tricuspid valve replacement and ascending aortic reconstruction); all remained alive without Fontan failure. Energy loss differed significantly across segments (p = 0.011), being highest in the conduit and central confluence, with remarkable inter-patient variability superimposed (conduit values varying 35-fold from 0.025 to 0.887 mW). Maximum velocity strongly correlated with energy loss (r = 0.92, p = 0.001), suggesting velocity may serve as an accessible surrogate. Atrioventricular valve regurgitation severity did not consistently correlate with energy loss. Conclusions Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging with iTFlow software enables comprehensive hemodynamic assessment throughout the Fontan pathway, revealing substantial patient-specific heterogeneity in energy efficiency. With larger cohorts and correlation with clinical outcomes, this technique may become a valuable screening tool for post-Fontan evaluation and long-term surveillance.

title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems.
abstract: The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and wearable biosensors is transforming healthcare by allowing continuous, real-time monitoring and more intelligent clinical decision-making. This review explores AI-driven monitoring, smart intravenous (IV) infusion automation, and wearable biosensors, and proposes Intelligent IV Automation and Smart Patient Synchronization (INFUSYNC), a conceptual framework synchronizing monitoring, automated fluid delivery, and predictive analytics. The literature shows meaningful progress: wearables increasingly support non-contact monitoring with near clinical-grade accuracy for select parameters, while infusion pumps with dose-error-reduction and AI-assisted decision support are reported to improve delivery precision and safety. Predictive models further support early detection of physiological decline. Progress remains uneven, however: most AI-enabled infusion systems are prototype-stage, closed-loop control remains rare, and interoperability, data security, and privacy remain underdeveloped. Future systems will need compatible, security-by-design, clinically validated, feedback-controlled architectures. Overall, this review outlines a clear but early-stage trajectory toward integrated smart-health environments for IV therapy.

title: Refining ECPR candidate selection: from fixed criteria to a dynamic probability-of-benefit framework.
Active patient queue dynamics in a district hospital emergency centre: a cross-sectional analysis.
journal: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence
abstract: Introduction Emergency Centre crowding is a persistent challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where resource constraints exacerbate mismatches between demand and capacity. Clinician productivity is central to EC flow and is typically measured using patients per hour (PPH), but this does not capture concurrent workload. The active queue (AQ), operationally defined as unresolved clinician-attributed patient episodes at any point during a shift, may complement PPH by capturing the concurrent nature of EC clinical work. This study aimed to describe AQ dynamics at a district-level EC and identify the clinician, shift, and flow factors associated with variation in queue size. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted using data from 1 289 clinician shifts across three four-week periods in 2019 at a South African district-level EC. AQ was derived from timestamped patient flow data. Associations with clinician, shift, and system-level factors were assessed using one-way ANOVA and Spearman's rank correlation. Results Median AQ was 1.50 (IQR 1.00-2.25), with a median peak AQ of 3.00 (IQR 2.00-4.00). AQ varied significantly by clinician category, employment type, and shift type (all p Conclusions Emergency clinicians routinely manage concurrent patient loads, with AQ demonstrating a consistent mid-shift plateau. AQ complements PPH by capturing the concurrent dimension of clinician workload that throughput measures alone cannot reflect, with relevance to staffing and operational planning in district-level EC settings.

title: Emergency department extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: Current concepts, systems-based implementation, and future directions.
abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has emerged as a time-critical resuscitative strategy for carefully selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and other reversible causes of circulatory or respiratory failure. As the role of emergency department ECMO (ED ECMO) continues to expand, emergency physicians have become integral members of multidisciplinary extracorporeal resuscitation teams. This review aims to summarize the current evidence on ED ECMO while highlighting practical considerations for program implementation, workflow optimization, and future directions. This invited narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the indications, patient selection, cannulation strategies, pericannulation management, and postcannulation physiological challenges of ED ECMO, with particular emphasis on extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. In addition to published literature, practical aspects of ED ECMO implementation, including multidisciplinary team organization, operational governance, workflow optimization, quality metrics, and institutional experience, are discussed. Emerging concepts such as artificial intelligence-assisted decision support, digital twin-enabled system modeling, and regional implementation strategies are also reviewed. Current evidence indicates that successful ED ECMO depends not only on technical proficiency but also on timely patient selection, standardized protocols, efficient multidisciplinary coordination, and optimized operational systems. Contemporary implementation frameworks emphasize integrated governance, continuous quality improvement, and structured performance metrics to enhance clinical effectiveness. Emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and systems modeling, may further improve patient selection, operational efficiency, and program scalability. ED ECMO should be regarded as a comprehensive, systems-based resuscitation strategy rather than a standalone rescue procedure. Future progress is likely to depend on the integration of evidence-based patient selection, standardized workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, intelligent operational systems, and continuous quality improvement. The development of regional ED ECMO networks supported by robust emergency medical service infrastructure may improve timely access to extracorporeal resuscitation and optimize patient outcomes.

title: Comparison of Visual and Ocular Hemodynamic Outcomes Following Trifocal vs Bifocal Intraocular Lens Implantation in Patients With Cataract and Myopia.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
abstract: BACKGROUND This retrospective study from a single center aimed to compare postoperative visual, structural, and ocular hemodynamic outcomes following implantation of a trifocal intraocular lens (IOL) in 67 patients and a bifocal IOL in 67 patients with combined cataract and myopia. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 134 patients (268 eyes) with cataract and myopia treated between June 2022 and June 2024 were retrospectively analyzed and divided into a bifocal IOL group (n=67; 134 eyes) and a trifocal IOL group (n=67; 134 eyes). All patients underwent standardized phacoemulsification with capsular bag IOL implantation and were evaluated 6 months postoperatively. Outcomes included visual acuity, intraocular pressure, anterior chamber depth, axial length, lens thickness, mean blood flow density, pulsatility index, and resistance index. Generalized estimating equation models were used to account for inter-eye correlation. RESULTS Compared with the bifocal IOL group, the trifocal IOL group showed lower postoperative intraocular pressure (P=0.003) and anterior chamber depth (P=0.004) and improved oculus dexter visual acuity (P=0.003). Lens thickness was lower postoperatively, whereas axial length remained stable between groups. Mean blood flow density increased (P=0.020), whereas pulsatility index (P=0.003) and resistance index (P=0.002) decreased. Adverse events were less frequent in the trifocal IOL group (P=0.029). However, the observed differences were modest, with uncertain clinical significance. CONCLUSIONS Trifocal IOL implantation was associated with limited postoperative differences in visual and hemodynamic outcomes compared with bifocal IOL implantation. These findings require cautious interpretation and validation in larger prospective studies with longer follow-up.

title: Neuropsychological input during hyper-acute stroke admission is associated with improved discharge outcomes.
Primary umbilical endometriosis mimicking a urachal fistula: a case report.
abstract: Background Umbilical endometriosis is an uncommon form of extrapelvic endometriosis and may be misdiagnosed as other umbilical or urachal disorders. Cyclic umbilical bleeding or discharge is an important clinical clue, but the diagnosis is often confirmed only after surgical excision and histopathological examination. Case presentation A 31-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a history of umbilical discharge for more than one year. The symptom occurred predominantly during menstruation and was characterized by recurrent umbilical discharge with occasional bloody secretion. Physical examination revealed mild erythema and swelling of the umbilicus, without active discharge at the time of examination. Preoperative computed tomography of the lower abdomen and pelvis showed no obvious abnormality. The initial clinical diagnosis was urachal fistula with possible umbilical infection. The patient underwent surgical excision of the umbilical lesion under general anesthesia. Intraoperatively, purulent discharge was observed at the umbilicus, and complete excision of the umbilical lesion was performed. Histopathological examination revealed endometrial glands and stroma beneath the squamous epithelium with hemosiderin deposition, while immunohistochemistry showed CD10, CK7, and PR positivity with negative/weak ER expression, supporting the diagnosis of umbilical endometriosis. Conclusion This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge of primary umbilical endometriosis presenting with chronic umbilical discharge. Careful assessment of menstrual history, imaging findings, and pathological examination is essential for accurate diagnosis.

title: Impact of E-visits on Outpatient Volume and Service Time: Evidence from a Large Public Hospital in China.
journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery

title: Association between anesthetic fresh gas flow and postoperative inflammatory response in laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Perioperative inflammation is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, and anesthetic management may modulate this response. However, the influence of fresh gas flow strategies during volatile anesthesia on perioperative inflammatory responses has not been adequately characterized. Evidence in obese surgical patients remains particularly limited despite the chronic low-grade inflammatory state and exaggerated responses to surgical stress associated with obesity. In this retrospective cohort study, 155 obese adult patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy under sevoflurane anesthesia were evaluated. Patients received either low-flow (1 L/min, n = 76) or standard-flow (4 L/min, n = 79) anesthesia. Perioperative changes (Δ = postoperative - preoperative) in red cell distribution width (RDW), C-reactive protein (CRP), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were assessed using preoperative and 24-hour postoperative values. Between-group changes in these 3 designated primary outcomes were compared, and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed as adjusted supportive analyses. Intraoperative hemodynamic and oxygenation parameters and postoperative hospital length of stay were evaluated as exploratory secondary outcomes. ΔRDW and ΔCRP were greater in the standard-flow group than in the low-flow group (both P < .001) and remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (α = 0.0167), whereas no statistically significant between-group difference was observed for ΔNLR (P = .902). After adjustment for the measured covariates and calendar period, standard-flow anesthesia remained associated with greater ΔRDW and ΔCRP. No statistically detectable between-group differences were observed in the longitudinal hemodynamic and oxygenation outcomes or postoperative hospital length of stay. Low-flow sevoflurane anesthesia was associated with smaller postoperative increases in RDW and CRP compared with standard-flow anesthesia in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. These findings suggest an association between fresh gas flow strategy and selected postoperative inflammatory marker changes during bariatric surgery.

title: Clinically Actionable Prevention and Management of Major Complications During Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Support: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
abstract: Durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) have become an established therapy for selected patients with advanced heart failure as bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy. Despite major progress in continuous-flow pump design and perioperative care, long-term benefit remains constrained by a recurrent burden of right heart failure, aortic regurgitation, pump thrombosis, stroke, bleeding, infection, and end-organ dysfunction. Because these events often arise from the interaction of altered hemodynamics, hemocompatibility-related injury, chronic antithrombotic exposure, and the practical complexity of longitudinal device care, a complication-centered management framework is clinically useful. This contemporary narrative review focuses on actionable prevention, surveillance, and treatment strategies for the major complications encountered during durable LVAD support. Rather than providing a broad device-oriented overview, we emphasize clinically relevant decision points across the perioperative and long-term course, including right ventricular protection, antithrombotic balance, structured monitoring for aortic regurgitation and hemolysis, prevention of driveline infection, and multidisciplinary outpatient follow-up. By organizing current evidence around practical management pathways, this review aims to support earlier recognition of adverse events and more durable long-term support.

title: Evaluation of Hospital Preparedness and Response to Trauma Through a Full-Scale Disaster Drill: A Multimethod Study
abstract: Abstract Background Hospitals play a central role in managing trauma-related mass casualty incidents (MCIs), and full-scale simulation exercises (FSSEs) are widely used to test institutional preparedness. This study aimed to assess the structure and execution of a trauma-related disaster drill, identify systemic gaps in triage, communication, and patient disposition, and analyze the operational flow of the hospital incident command system (HICS). Methods A multimethod retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary-care hospital following a full-scale trauma disaster drill simulating a two-bus collision with approximately 100 casualties. A standardized five-domain checklist was scored independently by three observers, and inter-rater agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa. Time-motion analysis tracked five simulated patients from arrival to disposition. HICS activation and role performance were mapped using a swim lane process-flow analysis and compared against expected protocol benchmarks. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Results Inter-rater reliability across checklist domains was moderate to good (overall Fleiss' kappa = 0.558). Triage was initiated without measurable delay from patient arrival, but downstream processes were slower. HICS activation (14 minutes 52 seconds) and triage-officer assignment (16.8 minutes) both exceeded protocol benchmarks, while siren activation (29 minutes 56 seconds) and initial patient triage were within expected limits. Thematic analysis of interviews identified four major domains of concern: planning constraints, communication gaps, resource/logistical barriers, and team role confusion. Conclusions Frontline clinical response, particularly triage, was a consistent strength, but systemic inefficiencies in communication infrastructure, command coordination, and resource logistics represent the principal barriers to optimal mass casualty response.

title: Harnessing the Power of Education for a Low-carbon Future in Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review.
journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
abstract: Climate change poses a significant threat to public health, with the healthcare sector being a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. Anaesthesia and the operating room are notable contributors within this sector, particularly because of volatile inhalation gases such as desflurane and nitrous oxide. Therefore, improving sustainability in anaesthesia is a clinical and ethical imperative. This review examines recent advances in leveraging education to promote low-carbon anaesthesia practices. We summarize evidence on how various educational interventions and formats can reduce the carbon footprint of anaesthesia and discuss implementation strategies, challenges, and future directions. Many studies demonstrate that educational programs reduce the use of high global warming potential anaesthetic agents. Programs vary widely in scope, ranging from single-session lectures and surveys to multi-year sustainability task forces and formal policy changes, some of which have resulted in up to a 90% reduction in volatile agent emissions. Combining multiple techniques (such as lectures, posters, and vaporizer labeling) has been associated with substantial reductions in volatile agent emissions and with improved organizational readiness for sustainability initiatives. These education-driven shifts toward environmentally friendly approaches, such as low-flow techniques, total intravenous anaesthesia, and regional anaesthesia, have proven effective, cutting costs, maintaining patient safety, and reducing carbon emissions. Educational initiatives represent a practical and cost‑efficient strategy to reduce carbon emissions in anaesthesia practice and in healthcare. By integrating environmental stewardship into anaesthesia training and policy, anaesthesiologists can lead the transition of healthcare to low-carbon care.

title: Greener Surgery, Greener Hospital: Organizational Strategies for Carbon Footprint Reduction in Anesthesia and Perioperative Departments
Case Report: Endovascular repair for true lumen collapse after frozen elephant trunk for type A aortic dissection.
abstract: Introduction Frozen elephant trunk (FET) was applied in the treatment of type A aortic dissection, enabling one-stage repair of the aortic arch and proximal descending aorta while promoting true lumen expansion. However, inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen is a rare but catastrophic complication that may cause true lumen collapse and life-threatening visceral malperfusion, with limited reports on its endovascular management. Case presentation Here, we present the case of a 44-year-old female who underwent Bentall procedure, total arch replacement, and FET implantation for acute type A aortic dissection at a local hospital. Postoperatively, she developed visceral malperfusion manifesting as abdominal distension, hepatic and renal dysfunction, and elevated lactate levels. Computed tomography angiography revealed that the FET stent had been inadvertently deployed into the false lumen, resulting in true lumen collapse. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed, establishing a "FET-false lumen-true lumen" pathway with an additional stent graft to redirect aortic flow into the true lumen. Computational fluid dynamics analysis showed that the postoperative hemodynamics have been significantly improved. The patient's organ function normalized, and she was discharged two weeks later, remaining asymptomatic at 8-month follow-up. Conclusion Endovascular reintervention with additional stent grafting to establish a flow-redirection pathway is a feasible and effective strategy for true lumen collapse following inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen. Prompt recognition, timely imaging confirmation, and immediate intervention are paramount to mitigating the risks associated with this serious complication.

title: Delayed diagnosis of a traumatic gluteal pseudoaneurysm with arteriovenous fistula and dual arterial supply mimicking a buttock abscess after a stab wound: a case report.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

title: Case Report: Serplulimab-induced checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with underlying COPD: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background Serplulimab, a first-line therapy for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), can cause checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP). The clinical features and outcomes of serplulimab-induced CIP in patients with Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stage IV chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain unclear. Case description An 80-year-old man with ES-SCLC and preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD received first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy. After achieving an initial partial response, chemotherapy was discontinued due to reduced tolerance following bacterial pneumonia, and he was continued on serplulimab monotherapy. Three days after the first maintenance dose of serplulimab, he presented with acute severe chest tightness, dyspnea, and hypoxemia and was admitted to the hospital 4 days later. Chest CT revealed new bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Extensive workup for infection, acute exacerbation of COPD, and tumor progression was negative; the case was ultimately classified as grade 4 serplulimab-induced CIP. He was treated with high-dose methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, and empiric anti-infective therapy, with significant clinical improvement. Follow-up CT at 2 months post-discharge showed significant resolution of pulmonary infiltrates. Conclusions Severe, life-threatening CIP can occur in elderly patients with ES-SCLC and preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD. In this patient, prompt recognition, intensive immunosuppression, and permanent programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor discontinuation contributed to a favorable outcome. Whether preexisting GOLD stage IV COPD confers an increased risk of severe CIP in this understudied population warrants further investigation.

title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygen Versus Conventional Oxygen Therapy and Non-Invasive Ventilation for Acute Respiratory Failure in the Emergency Department: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Beyond the Larynx: New Insights Into Upper Airway Responses to Mechanical Insufflation-Exsufflation.
abstract: This case report describes a 44-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and ineffective secretion clearance despite home use of mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E). He reported upper airway obstruction, respiratory discomfort and recurrent aerophagia during therapy. Dynamic assessments using transnasal flexible laryngoscopy and videofluoroscopy under different MI-E settings showed that upper airway responses were strongly influenced by inspiratory flow, pressure levels, expiratory time and cervical positioning. Higher inspiratory flow and pressure induced supraglottic closure and airflow diversion to the oesophagus. In contrast, lower inspiratory flow combined with reduced expiratory pressure and shorter expiratory time improved glottic opening, maintained airway patency and enhanced cough mechanics. Spontaneously adopted cervical extension optimized airflow and minimized oesophageal insufflation, whereas neutral alignment impaired cough efficiency. These findings emphasize the importance of individualized MI-E settings and patient-specific biomechanics in optimizing therapy in ALS.

title: The Fast Care Model and Clinical Leadership in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Introduction The increasing use of emergency departments for the management of minor emergencies represents a major global challenge, with negative implications for organizational efficiency and patient flow. Despite the adoption of different throughput models, prolonged waiting times and incomplete care pathways remain common. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a nurse-led Fast Care model, based on early assessment and continuity of care, in improving the management of minor emergencies and patient flow within the emergency department. Methods A randomized clinical trial was conducted in a university emergency department. Adult patients presenting with minor emergencies were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to Fast Care or usual care. The primary outcomes were waiting time and overall length of stay. Secondary outcomes included the number of patients who left without being seen and 72-hour emergency department readmission rates. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Results A total of 801 patients were enrolled. Compared with usual care, participants in the Fast Care group experienced reductions of 77.6 minutes in waiting time, 156.9 minutes in treatment time, and 178.1 minutes in overall length of stay. In the Fast Care group, the care pathway was completed in nearly all cases, with early departures (patients leaving before clinical evaluation) occurring in 2.5% of participants, compared with 32.2% in the usual care group. Discussion The nurse-led Fast Care model improved patient flow and reduced delays in the management of minor emergencies, supporting a more efficient and appropriate emergency department care pathway.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.

title: Angiography-derived fractional flow and clinical outcomes in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
abstract: Background To explore the association between fractional flow (FF) and clinical outcomes in patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS), and to evaluate its potential role in patient stratification. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included symptomatic ICAS patients hospitalized between March 2019 and May 2024. FF values were derived from digital subtraction angiography using an angiography-based computational method. Patients were stratified according to a pre-specified FF threshold of 0.76 and treatment modality (interventional vs. conservative). Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) at discharge and 12 months. Results Among patients with FF ≤ 0.76, no worsening in mRS between discharge and 12 months was observed in 96.3% of the interventional group and 78.6% of the conservative group ( p = 0.017). In a post hoc analysis, improvement of at least one mRS point occurred in 46.3 and 17.9%, respectively; however, discharge mRS scores differed between groups, and the difference in improvement was not statistically significant when the analysis was restricted to patients with discharge mRS ≥ 1. No significant differences in mRS or NIHSS improvement were observed between treatment strategies in patients with FF > 0.76 ( p > 0.05). In contrast, stratification based on degree of stenosis (DS% ≥ 70%) did not differentiate clinical outcomes between treatment groups. These findings suggest that FF-based stratification may be associated with differences in functional outcomes across treatment strategies. Conclusion FF may provide additional information for risk stratification in symptomatic ICAS patients and may help identify clinically relevant subgroups for further evaluation. However, these findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.

title: Clinician-Reported Consequences and Patient Outcomes in Disputed Emergency Department Admission Referrals: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Patients in the emergency department (ED) who need admission depend on an inpatient team agreeing to take responsibility for their care. This systematic review examined patient outcomes, patient experiences, and clinician-reported consequences associated with inpatient specialties disputing, declining, redirecting, or deferring ED admission referrals. The review was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261538117) and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. MEDLINE, Embase, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and the Health Management Information Consortium database were searched on 12 October 2026, and the reference lists and citing articles of included studies were checked. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and appraised quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool; findings were synthesised narratively, and confidence in qualitative findings was assessed with GRADE-CERQual. Twenty-four studies reported in 28 articles (2005-2026) from 10 countries were included, five of them identified by citation searching. Most of the evidence came from clinicians' reports, and only one study reported outcomes for patients known to have had a disputed referral: in that audit of 109 rejected admission requests, 97 patients (89.0%) were eventually admitted, 66 (60.6%) under the first team contacted, and ED length of stay increased with the number of teams involved. Two record-based studies counted disputes or refusals without reporting outcomes separately for the patients affected. Two hospital-wide interventions that limited bed rejections or clarified emergency physician admitting authority were followed by shorter waits, without concurrent controls. In one interview study, patients who were receiving residents considered inappropriately transferred described more negative experiences. In a qualitative analysis of survey accounts, 40 of 139 physicians (29%) reported that a patient had experienced an adverse event or near miss after transfer from the ED; in a separate survey, 36 of 126 physicians (29%) reported a handoff-related adverse event or near miss. Clinicians attributed disputes to diagnostic uncertainty, workload, bed pressure, unclear or unequal rules on which team must accept, referral timing, and specialty identity and hierarchy. Disputes over which team accepts an ED admission are commonly described, rarely measured, and a potentially modifiable source of delay, but their effect on patient outcomes cannot yet be estimated. Recording the number of teams contacted and the time from first referral to acceptance would allow hospitals to measure the problem and test solutions.

title: Hospital crowding as a quality problem: redesigning reliability in early acute care.
journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care

title: All-Oral PI3Kδ and HDAC Inhibition with Parsaclisib Plus Chidamide and Step-Down Maintenance in Relapsed or Refractory Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma: A Phase Ib Trial.
abstract: Single-agent targeted therapies for relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma (R/R peripheral T-cell lymphoma [PTCL]) produce modest, short-lived responses, underscoring the need for tolerable, chemotherapy-free combinations. In an open-label, single-arm Phase Ib trial at two tertiary hospitals, we evaluated parsaclisib plus chidamide with step-down maintenance. Adults with R/R PTCL received parsaclisib 10-20 mg once daily plus chidamide 20 mg twice weekly for 8 weeks using 3+3 escalation; patients without progression or unacceptable toxicity continued parsaclisib 2.5 mg once daily plus chidamide 20 mg twice weekly. Primary endpoints were Cycle 1 dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), treatment-related adverse events, and recommended Phase II dose; antitumor activity and biomarker correlates were exploratory. Twelve screened patients were enrolled and treated. One Grade 3 hepatotoxicity DLT occurred; no maximum tolerated dose was reached; parsaclisib 20 mg once daily plus chidamide 20 mg twice weekly was selected for Phase II. No Grade 4 treatment-related events or treatment-related deaths occurred. Objective and complete response rates were 58% (95% CI, 28-85) and 42% (95% CI, 15-72). With 26.8 months' median follow-up, 2-year progression-free and overall survival rates were 33.3 and 66.7%. Exploratory analyses suggested TET2 alterations and natural killer-cell expansion as correlates of durable remission. This regimen warrants prospective validation (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05083208).

title: OHVIRA Syndrome with Incomplete Vaginal Obstruction, Hematocolpos, and Pyocolpos Despite Regular Menstruation in an Adolescent: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA) syndrome is a rare congenital Müllerian anomaly characterized by uterus didelphys, obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal anomaly. Patients with complete vaginal obstruction typically present shortly after menarche with severe dysmenorrhea and cyclic pelvic pain. Incomplete obstruction may permit partial menstrual drainage, resulting in atypical manifestations and delayed diagnosis. We report incomplete OHVIRA syndrome presenting with preserved menstrual flow despite hematocolpos and pyocolpos. The Zhu classification distinguishes complete obstruction (Class 1) from incomplete obstruction (Class 2), in which some menstrual outflow may occur despite persistent obstruction. In this case, findings supported incomplete obstruction, although a specific small septal opening was not documented. Case presentation A 13-year-old postmenarchal girl was referred with persistent brown vaginal discharge following menstruation and recent right lower abdominal pain. She reported regular menstrual cycles for one year without dysmenorrhea. Examination revealed normal external genitalia with an intact hymen. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated uterus didelphys, hematocolpos, and non-visualization of the left kidney, raising suspicion of OHVIRA syndrome. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging confirmed uterus didelphys with duplicated cervices and left-sided hematocolpos. According to the Zhu classification, the case was classified as Class 2 OHVIRA syndrome, indicating incomplete vaginal obstruction. According to the ESHRE/ESGE classification, the uterine, cervical, and vaginal anomalies were described as U3b-C2-V2, corresponding to a complete bicorporeal uterus, double cervix, and longitudinal obstructing vaginal septum, respectively. The patient underwent genitoscopy, transverse incision and complete excision of an oblique vaginal septum, drainage of retained collections, vaginal irrigation, and hymenorrhaphy. Approximately 50 mL of purulent material mixed with retained menstrual blood was evacuated, consistent with pyocolpos associated with chronic incomplete obstruction. Microbiological culture was not performed; therefore, the causative organism could not be identified. Cefazolin was administered preoperatively and postoperatively. Postoperative ultrasonography demonstrated complete resolution of the hematocolpos without residual pelvic fluid. During 6 months of telephone follow-up, the patient reported no recurrent symptoms; in-person reassessment was limited by school commitments and distance from the hospital. Conclusion Incomplete OHVIRA syndrome should be considered in postmenarchal adolescents with persistent postmenstrual brown vaginal discharge, even when menstruation is regular and dysmenorrhea is absent. Preserved menstrual flow does not exclude obstructive Müllerian anomalies. Pelvic ultrasonography, renal evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging, and endoscopic assessment are important for diagnosis and surgical planning. Early recognition and complete vaginal septum excision can relieve obstruction and treat retained collections; long-term reproductive outcomes cannot be determined from the available follow-up.

title: From structural repair to biomechanical compatibility: Aortic stiffness after open and endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: Evaluation of aortic repair has traditionally prioritised perioperative safety, exclusion of the diseased segment and durability. As endovascular treatment expands to younger patients, attention is turning towards the biomechanical compatibility of prosthetic grafts with the native aorta. Native aortic compliance supports Windkessel function, whereas grafts create a compliance transition that may accelerate pulse-wave transmission, alter wave reflection and increase left-ventricular load. This narrative review distinguishes established evidence from emerging concepts after open surgical repair, endovascular aneurysm repair and thoracic endovascular aortic repair. Carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) is the accepted reference non-invasive measure of regional aortic stiffness; cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived segmental pulse-wave velocity and distensibility provide complementary information. Brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity, the cardio-ankle vascular index, and augmentation index assess different territories or haemodynamic properties and are not interchangeable with cfPWV. Left-ventricular strain and mass are downstream cardiac outcomes. Clinical evidence generally reports increases in measured arterial-stiffness indices after endovascular repair, whereas findings after open repair are heterogeneous. Treatment length, landing-zone location, oversizing, anatomy and baseline vascular phenotype may be as important as graft fabric or stent-frame category. Conflicting comparisons of polyester and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene arise from small, non-randomised studies using non-equivalent endpoints and do not support a reliable ranking of commercial devices. Emerging 4D-flow CMR, simulation and compliant graft materials illustrate a shift from structural exclusion alone towards compliance-aware repair, but evidence of improved outcomes remains insufficient. Future studies should use standardised longitudinal stiffness, blood-pressure and cardiac assessments and relate biomechanical changes to hypertension, ventricular remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Organ Malperfusion and Mortality in Acute Type 1 Aortic Dissection with Iliac Extension: A Retrospective Single-Center Study Focused on Mesenteric Malperfusion and the Source-Clearance Hypothesis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mesenteric malperfusion is the most lethal and least recognizable complication of acute type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to examine organ-specific malperfusion patterns and 30-day mortality in acute type 1 aortic dissection with iliac extension, and to evaluate whether the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and superior mesenteric artery (SMA) origin pattern add predictive value for mesenteric malperfusion syndrome within a "source-clearance" framework. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 80 consecutive patients with acute type 1 aortic dissection extending to the iliac arteries who underwent surgical repair between January 2020 and March 2026 were reviewed. Malperfusion (preoperative finding) and malperfusion syndrome (end-organ injury persisting despite central repair) were defined for six organ systems; visceral branch origin and planimetric true lumen ratio were assessed on computed tomography angiography (CTA). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Results: Thirty-day mortality was 33.8%; 60% of patients had malperfusion, and mortality rose with the number of organs involved (0/1/≥2: 12.5%/32.1%/70.0%). Mesenteric malperfusion ( n = 21) carried the highest mortality (71.4%); all nine patients who developed mesenteric syndrome died. Cerebral malperfusion was most frequent ( n = 27); all nine who improved postoperatively survived, whereas mortality was 81.8% in the 22 who developed the syndrome. Preoperative shock or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) (odds ratio [OR] = 7.02), mesenteric malperfusion (OR = 6.24), LAR (OR = 1.07 per 0.01 unit) and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS; OR = 0.75 per point) were independent predictors. LAR and SMA origin pattern were uncorrelated (r = -0.04) and together raised the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for mesenteric syndrome from 0.861 to 0.955; mortality was 75% with mixed SMA origin ( n = 8). Conclusions: Malperfusion is a dose-dependent risk spectrum; mesenteric involvement is its most lethal component, increasing mortality six-fold independently of hemodynamic and metabolic status. Joint interpretation of LAR and SMA origin pattern offers a practical, validation-pending framework for perioperative management of the mesenteric circulation in centers without a hybrid operating room.

title: Practical efficiency of coupling targeted temperature management to brain temperature versus systemic temperature in febrile brain-injured patients. The Brain-TTM study: A randomized controlled pathophysiology trial.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism

title: Angiographically Occult Perforator Ischemia Detected by Motor-Evoked Potential Monitoring during Woven EndoBridge Deployment: A Case Report.
abstract: Objective To demonstrate that intraoperative motor-evoked potential (MEP) monitoring can detect angiographically occult perforator ischemia caused by intermediate catheter-induced luminal occupation and flow restriction during Woven EndoBridge (WEB; Terumo Neuro, Aliso Viejo, CA, USA) deployment, which would otherwise remain unrecognized. Case presentation A woman in her 60s underwent WEB deployment for an unruptured left middle cerebral artery aneurysm under general anesthesia with intraoperative MEP monitoring using an optimized transcranial electrical stimulation protocol. Immediately prior to device deployment, MEP amplitudes abruptly disappeared in the right extremities. DSA showed preserved lenticulostriate artery opacification; however, the M1 segment was nearly completely occupied by the intermediate catheter. Catheter-induced perforator ischemia was suspected, and the catheter was promptly withdrawn to the cavernous internal carotid artery. MEP signals fully recovered within approximately 4 minutes, and WEB deployment was completed without further incident. Postoperative MRI revealed a small lacunar infarction in the lenticulostriate territory, but the patient was discharged without neurological deficits. Conclusion Intermediate catheter-induced luminal occupation of the parent artery can cause angiographically occult perforator ischemia detectable only by functional monitoring. MEP monitoring may serve as a critical safeguard during WEB deployment and other neuroendovascular procedures involving large-bore intermediate catheters in perforator-rich arterial segments.

title: Current status, challenges and future development of self-service appointment platforms in hospital radiology departments in China: a narrative review
A standardized ECPR activation protocol and resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load: a retrospective multicenter study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate changes in resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load associated with implementation of a standardized extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) activation protocol. Methods This retrospective multicenter observational study included 103 consecutive patients with in-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR at three tertiary hospitals in Guangdong Province, China. The control group included 30 patients treated from September 2019 to December 2023, and the post-implementation group included 73 patients treated from January 2024 to December 2025. Outcomes included resuscitation-process measures, clinical outcomes, and perceived nursing workload assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), a multidimensional measure of perceived workload. Results Compared with the control group, the post-implementation group had shorter ECPR preparation time (2.87 ± 2.32 vs. 8.60 ± 1.34 min), ECMO priming time (14.83 ± 2.88 vs. 19.07 ± 1.18 min), and ECMO initiation time (35.01 ± 2.36 vs. 54.12 ± 3.55 min), and a higher one-time readiness rate of disposable supplies (100% vs. 50.0%; all P P P = 0.069). Favorable neurological outcome at discharge was more frequent after implementation (30.1% vs. 10.0%; crude OR 3.88, 95% CI 1.07-14.15; P = 0.036), and the association persisted after adjustment for SAVE score and time-to-ECPR-decision (adjusted OR 3.79, 95% CI 1.02-14.08; P = 0.047). Conclusion Implementation of the standardized ECPR activation protocol was associated with shorter ECPR preparation, priming, and initiation times, lower perceived nursing workload, and higher odds of favorable neurological outcome at discharge. Thirty-day survival was numerically higher but did not differ statistically. Given the retrospective pre-post design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

title: Recurrent Ovarian Torsion Despite Previous Oophoropexy in a 9-Year-Old Prepubertal Girl: A Pediatric Emergency Department Perspective.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Ovarian torsion is an uncommon but time-sensitive gynecologic emergency in children. Diagnosis may be challenging because symptoms can be nonspecific and Doppler ultrasonography may demonstrate residual ovarian blood flow. Although oophoropexy may be performed to reduce recurrence, torsion can recur after fixation. CASE REPORT A 9-year-old prepubertal girl with a history of left ovarian torsion treated by laparoscopic detorsion and oophoropexy presented with 2 days of severe intermittent left-sided abdominal pain and 1 day of vomiting. She was afebrile and hemodynamically stable, without peritoneal signs. Transabdominal ultrasonography demonstrated an enlarged left ovary measuring 41×37×32 mm (approximately 27 mL), with diminished vascularity and faint internal flow on color and power Doppler imaging. Urgent laparoscopy confirmed recurrent left ovarian torsion of approximately 360°. The ovary was viable, and no ovarian cyst or adnexal mass was identified. Detorsion and utero-ovarian ligament plication were performed, preserving the ovary. At 8-week follow-up, ultrasonography demonstrated normalization of the left ovarian size to 16×14×24 mm (approximately 2.7 mL), with no adnexal lesion or pelvic free fluid. CONCLUSIONS Recurrent ovarian torsion can occur despite previous oophoropexy. Residual Doppler flow should not exclude torsion when clinical suspicion remains high. Prompt surgical evaluation can permit detorsion and ovarian preservation.

title: Numerical simulation of aortic hemodynamic effects modulated by the intra-aortic rotary blood pump with different speed modes.
Development and preliminary validation of a CD161 immunoscore-based screening method for latent tuberculosis infection in a Chinese training cohort.
Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: Objective To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. Methods A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. Results The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). Conclusions Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Third lumbar transverse process syndrome with acute abdominal pain as the main clinical manifestation: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Third lumbar transverse process syndrome is an uncommon musculoskeletal cause of referred abdominal pain. Because acute abdominal pain is appropriately evaluated first for visceral, vascular, urinary, and surgical emergencies, a spinal or paraspinal pain generator may be overlooked. Patient concerns A 66-year-old man presented with persistent left lower-quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the left lower back. Baseline pain intensity was 7/10 on a VAS, and the pain was aggravated by postural change, standing, and walking. Diagnoses Serial laboratory tests, endoscopy, ultrasonography, CT/CTA, and specialist consultations did not identify a visceral, urinary, surgical, or hemodynamically significant vascular disorder sufficient to explain the pain. Targeted musculoskeletal examination showed focal tenderness and increased soft-tissue tension around the left L3 transverse process, movement-related pain, and a visually estimated compensatory apparent leg-length discrepancy. These findings supported a clinical diagnosis of third lumbar transverse process syndrome presenting as referred abdominal pain. Interventions The patient received Tuina manual therapy, two acupotomy closed-release procedures at palpation-defined tender points in the left lumbar and gluteal regions, and adjunctive pharmacotherapy. Outcomes At discharge on February 9, 2021, the abdomen was soft without tenderness or rebound tenderness. Abdominal pain had resolved completely at the 2-week follow-up. Routine annual telephone follow-up of former inpatients was then conducted once yearly for 3 years, with no recurrence reported. Lessons After urgent abdominal and vascular disorders have been excluded, history taking and targeted examination of the lumbar transverse processes may identify a musculoskeletal source of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain.

title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula in Adult Acute Care: Physiological Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Persistent Misconceptions.
abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy is widely used in emergency, intensive care, perioperative, and procedural settings, but it is often conceptually assimilated to non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation (NIPPV). This interpretation is physiologically misleading. HFNC is an open high-flow oxygen system whose main effects derive from dead-space washout, improved stability of inspired oxygen fraction (FiO 2 ), heated humidification, patient comfort, and only modest flow-dependent positive airway pressure. Its open interface also facilitates eating, drinking, speaking, and secretion clearance. Clinical evidence supports HFNC mainly in selected patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, where it may reduce intubation compared with conventional oxygen therapy. However, evidence is more heterogeneous in hypercapnic respiratory failure, cardiogenic pulmonary edema, immunocompromised patients, obesity, and settings requiring substantial pressure support or ventilatory unloading. NIPPV remains preferred in acidotic hypercapnic COPD exacerbations, while CPAP or NIPPV is indicated in selected pressure-responsive conditions such as cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Persistent excessive effort or clinical deterioration requires timely assessment for invasive ventilation. HFNC should therefore be regarded as optimized high-flow oxygen therapy rather than as "non-invasive ventilation through nasal prongs." Recognizing this distinction may improve patient selection, guide escalation, and avoid overinterpretation of its clinical effects.

title: Bilateral Iatrogenic Pneumothorax After Acupuncture in a 26-Year-Old Woman Presenting With Cough, Pleuritic Chest Pain, and Tachycardia: A Case Report.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Acupuncture is widely used and generally safe, but pneumothorax is a serious complication of needling in the neck, shoulder, or upper back. Bilateral pneumothorax is rare and can present with nonspecific symptoms, delaying diagnosis. This case report highlights the presentation of immediate cough during upper-back needling, delayed presentation with bilateral pneumothorax despite preserved oxygenation, and radiographic regression during specialist-supervised conservative inpatient management. CASE REPORT A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with persistent cough, pleuritic chest pain, and difficulty taking a full breath 2 days after acupuncture in the trapezius region. She was otherwise hemodynamically stable, with a blood pressure of 132/93 mm Hg and oxygen saturation of 100% on room air, but had marked tachycardia (140 beats/min at triage) and decreased right-sided breath sounds. Chest radiography showed bilateral apical pneumothoraces measuring 21 mm on the right and 17 mm on the left. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism and confirmed bilateral pneumothoraces up to 23 mm without hemothorax. Preserved blood pressure and oxygenation, absence of respiratory compromise, and availability of specialist inpatient monitoring supported conservative management without pleural intervention. Serial radiographs showed regression to 6 mm on the right and 9 mm on the left before discharge. CONCLUSIONS Recent acupuncture involving the neck, shoulder, or upper back should prompt consideration of pneumothorax in patients with chest pain, cough, dyspnea, or unexplained tachycardia, even when oxygen saturation is normal. Conservative inpatient management may be feasible only in carefully selected patients with bilateral procedure-related pneumothorax under close specialist clinical and radiographic surveillance.

title: Hospital-wide interventions to reduce emergency department overcrowding: Data-driven strategies and clinical governance at an Italian teaching hospital.
Axillary Dacron Graft Versus Direct Femoral Arterial Cannulation for Peripheral VA-ECMO After Heart Transplantation: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) remains a major cause of early morbidity and mortality after heart transplantation, and peripheral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) represents an established rescue therapy for severe cases. Although direct femoral arterial cannulation is commonly used because of its rapid deployment, axillary artery cannulation through a Dacron graft provides antegrade arterial perfusion and may represent an alternative approach. This study compared early clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications between these two arterial cannulation strategies. Methods: In this retrospective single-center observational study, 42 consecutive adult heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD were included. Patients were divided according to arterial cannulation strategy into direct femoral cannulation (DFC, n = 25) and axillary Dacron graft cannulation (ADG, n = 17). Baseline recipient and donor characteristics, perioperative variables, postoperative outcomes, vascular complications, successful VA-ECMO weaning, and survival to hospital discharge were compared. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for major clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications. Results: The primary composite endpoint of cannulation-related complications occurred in 0/17 patients (0%) in the ADG group and 3/25 patients (12.0%) in the DFC group (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.01-3.80; p = 0.260). Successful VA-ECMO weaning was achieved in 94.1% versus 92.0% ( p = 1.000), and survival to hospital discharge was 76.5% versus 64.0% (OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.46-7.32; p = 0.505). Stroke occurred in 5.9% versus 16.0% (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.03-3.23; p = 0.632), while renal replacement therapy was required in 35.3% versus 52.0% (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.14-1.79; p = 0.353). No statistically significant differences were detected between groups. Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in successful VA-ECMO weaning or survival to hospital discharge were observed between axillary Dacron graft and direct femoral arterial cannulation. No statistically significant differences in neurological, vascular, or other major postoperative outcomes were detected. Although several complications occurred numerically less frequently with axillary cannulation, the limited sample size and wide confidence intervals preclude conclusions regarding comparative superiority. Axillary Dacron graft cannulation may therefore represent a feasible alternative in selected heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique. Materials and methods In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention. Results Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively. Conclusion TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

title: Physiological Effects of High-Flow Tracheal Oxygen vs. Pressure Support Ventilation in Neurosurgical Patients with Brain Tumors Facing Delayed Extubation: A Pilot Study.
Contrast‑enhanced ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy of vascular malformations in the head and neck: Initial clinical experience in a paediatric case series.
abstract: Purpose Vascular malformations of the head and neck pose therapeutic challenges due to complex anatomy and proximity to critical structures. Percutaneous sclerotherapy guided by digital subtraction angiography is effective for low-flow malformations but involves radiation and iodinated contrast. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound offers a radiation-free alternative with real-time visualisation of intralesional contrast. Methods We retrospectively analysed contrast-enhanced ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy procedures for head and neck malformations in children under 6 years performed since 2021, assessing feasibility, safety and clinical outcomes. Six interventions in six patients (44 days to 3.5 years) were included. Results Contrast-enhanced ultrasound confirmed intralesional needle placement in all cases without evidence of extralesional contrast leakage. Sclerotherapy with Fibrovein or Aethoxysklerol was successfully performed in every procedure. No contrast-related adverse events occurred and all patients showed at least temporary clinical improvement. Conclusions Contrast-enhanced ultrasound therefore appears feasible and safe for guiding sclerotherapy of venolymphatic malformations in the head and neck, enabling real-time verification without ionising radiation or iodinated contrast. The technique may be particularly valuable in paediatric patients requiring repeated interventions.

title: Factors Associated With Prolonged Emergency Department (ED) Length of Stay (LOS) at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Nepal: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background Emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS) is an important indicator of healthcare efficiency and patient flow. The duration of ED stay is influenced by a complex interaction of patient-related, clinical and system-level factors. Prolonged LOS (> 4 h) contributes to ED overcrowding and adverse patient outcomes. However, limited data exist regarding factors influencing ED LOS in Nepal. Method A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in the ED of KIST Medical College and Teaching Hospital (MCTH), a tertiary care hospital in Lalitpur, Nepal, from May 15, 2025, to May 30, 2025. All patients presenting to the ED during the study period were eligible for inclusion. Consecutive patient records were reviewed. ED LOS was defined as the time from patient arrival to ED exit. LOS was summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR). Group differences were assessed using the Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Variables with p 4 h). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Results A total of 395 patients were included. The median ED LOS was 3.58 h (IQR 2.42-5.00). A total of 161 (40.8%) experienced prolonged ED LOS, while 234 (59.2%) had a LOS of ≤ 4 h. In univariate analysis, age, triage category, number of specialty consultations, payment method and requirement for advanced investigations were significantly associated with prolonged ED LOS ( p Conclusions ED LOS in this tertiary care hospital was primarily influenced by patient age, time of presentation, consultation processes and administrative factors. Strengthening interdepartmental consultation processes and improving ED workflow efficiency may help reduce prolonged ED stay and overcrowding.

title: A 2-year prognostic assessment of patients with coronary borderline lesions based on three-vessel quantitative flow ratio and the development and internal validation of a risk prediction nomogram.
abstract: Objective To investigate the prognostic value of three-vessel quantitative flow ratio (3V-QFR) in patients with borderline coronary lesions (QFR 0.75-0.80) over a 2-year period; to identify key variables using LASSO regression; and to construct and internally validate a personalized nomogram model for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 2 years. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with coronary artery disease who were treated at Ordos Central Hospital from January 2021 to December 2024, underwent coronary angiography revealing at least one borderline lesion in a major coronary artery, and received a QFR assessment. Patients were followed for up to 24 months after discharge through outpatient visits, telephone follow-up, and electronic medical-record review. The primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of MACE during the 2-year follow-up period. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to explore the nonlinear relationship between 3V-QFR and the risk of MACE. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression evaluated 19 prespecified candidate predictors using 10-fold cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule. A nomogram was constructed based on the selected factors, and the model's discriminatory power, consistency, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples that repeated the complete preprocessing, variable-selection, and model-refitting pipeline. Results A total of 138 patients with borderline lesions were enrolled (33 in the MACE group and 105 in the non-MACE group). Among 33 first MACE events, 20 were ischemia-driven revascularizations, 9 were non-fatal myocardial infarctions, and 4 were all-cause deaths. RCS analysis showed an overall association between lower 3V-QFR and higher MACE risk, whereas evidence for nonlinearity was not statistically strong; multivariable regression supported 3V-QFR as an independent predictor. LASSO regression identified four optimal predictors of 2-year MACE through 10-fold cross-validation: 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP levels. The final model included 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP. The apparent AUC was 0.869 (95% CI 0.802-0.936), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.842 (95% CI 0.771-0.913); calibration and decision-curve findings were considered exploratory. Conclusion Lower 3V-QFR was associated with higher 2-year MACE risk in this retrospective development cohort. The 3V-QFR-based nomogram showed promising internal performance and may support exploratory risk stratification; independent external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

title: Design of an Early Exercise Program for Hospitalized Patients: "Let's Move".
journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy
abstract: Background Hospital-associated deconditioning (HAD) affects up to 30% of older adults during acute hospitalization, leading to functional and cognitive decline and adverse long-term outcomes. Purpose To develop and pilot "Let's Move," an implementation-oriented early exercise program designed to support mobility in hospitalized patients. Methods An action-research study was conducted at a tertiary hospital in two stages: (i) program design based on an electronic health record (EHR) needs assessment and targeted protocol review; and (ii) pilot implementation among clinically stable adults aged ≥ 18 years, hospitalized for ≥ 48 h, without physiotherapy referral. Outcomes included Hopkins Highest Level of Mobility (JH-HLM) functional status, adherence, and safety, complemented by qualitative interviews and a focus group. Results In Stage 1, 1399 adult inpatients without rehabilitation referral were identified (median age, 65 years [IQR, 46-78]; length of stay, 3 days [IQR, 2-4]) with circulatory diseases predominating (57.18%). Among 26 participants enrolled in the pilot, 17 were evaluable for adherence, with 13 (76.5%) classified as adherent. Walking ≥ 75 m was the most frequent JH-HLM assessment category, no adverse events or in-hospital deaths occurred, and 25/26 participants (96.2%) achieved individualized goals. Qualitative findings supported relevance and feasibility and informed refinements, including sessions every 2 days and standardized educational materials. Discussion "Let's Move" is a structured early-mobilization program developed through action research that integrates brief patient education with low-intensity exercise for routine inpatient care. It provides a practical workflow to support early mobility and warrants broader evaluation to assess its effectiveness and scalability.

title: Pituitary Apoplexy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism in a Neurologically Complex Patient: A Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare endocrine emergency resulting from either acute haemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland. Although apoplexy occurs most frequently in a pre-existing pituitary adenoma, apoplexy could be the first presentation of a previously unknown adenoma. Acute headaches, visual disturbances, and neurological symptoms are common presenting symptoms in apoplexy; however, these symptoms may overlap with other neurological emergencies, which necessitate a holistic approach of clinical, radiological, and hormonal evaluation for suspected cases of apoplexy to confirm the diagnosis. Here we present a diagnostically challenging case of a 66-year-old man who presented with a sudden severe headache. His background history included a presumed intraventricular neurocytoma under surveillance. Initial CT head scan suggested possible haemorrhage within a known intraventricular mass (neurocytoma) with no obvious changes within the pituitary gland. However, subsequent MRI head demonstrated radiological features consistent with pituitary apoplexy. Later in his admission, he exhibited bilateral peripheral visual field constriction and early papilledema on fundoscopy. Hormonal testing showed evidence of hypopituitarism. The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous hydrocortisone replacement. During admission, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, for which he was treated with anticoagulation. While he was on anticoagulation, he developed intracranial haemorrhage, which led to his death after discharge from the hospital. This case demonstrates the importance of considering pituitary apoplexy in a challenging radiological and clinical presentation. A pre-existing neurological lesion (neurocytoma) makes a holistic approach, including MRI imaging and early hormonal evaluation are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment of pituitary apoplexy. The clinical challenge of having concurrent haemorrhagic and thrombotic events necessitates an individualised approach after balancing the benefits and risks of using anticoagulation treatment.

title: Contribution of a Digital Immunotherapy Management System Focusing on Improved Patient Adherence and Clinical Outcomes in House Dust Mite Rush Subcutaneous Immunotherapy Evaluated with a Before-After Design.
abstract: Background Rush subcutaneous immunotherapy (RIT) requires frequent injections, strict treatment intervals, and long-term follow-up. Digital management integrates injection scheduling, reminders, treatment records, and patient-reported follow-up. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the association of a digital immunotherapy management system with adherence and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing RIT. Methods This single-center retrospective conventional treatment (Before) followed by digital treatment (After) study design was used to evaluate patients who underwent house dust mite (HDM) RIT at a tertiary hospital in China between January 2022 and May 2025. Patients treated before implementation of the digital immunotherapy management system were assigned to the conventional management group (CMG), whereas those treated after implementation were assigned to the digital management group (DMG).
