Adherence, maintenance therapy completion, pulmonary function, inflammatory and immunological indicators, the Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ), and the Combined Symptom and Medication Score (CSMS) were compared. Results A total of 129 patients were included, 58 in the CMG and 71 in the DMG, with no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the two groups (all P > 0.05). At 1 year, 49 patients in the CMG and 66 patients in the DMG were evaluated. Good on-time injection adherence (72.7% vs 46.9%, P=0.005) and maintenance completion (81.8% vs 61.2%, P=0.014) were higher in the DMG. The DMG had higher forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1; P=0.037) and forced vital capacity (FVC; P=0.035), and lower RQLQ (P Conclusion Digital management was associated with better injection adherence, maintenance completion, and selected clinical outcomes, while inflammatory and immunological findings require cautious interpretation. Digital management may help patients maintain regular injections and complete maintenance therapy during long-term RIT. Temporal confounding limits causal inference; prospective multicenter studies are needed.

title: Perioperative Management of a Spinal Cord Stimulator During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Case Report.
abstract: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established treatment for chronic neuropathic pain, and patients with an implanted stimulator are presenting with increasing frequency for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We describe an 88-year-old man with a high-frequency (10 kHz) spinal cord stimulator for chronic back pain who underwent transfemoral TAVI under sedation for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. After consultation with the implanting pain service, the stimulator was switched off with the patient's own remote control, which was kept in the procedure room; rapid ventricular pacing was delivered through a bipolar right ventricular lead so that the pacing current was confined to the myocardium and remote from the pulse generator; and external defibrillator pads were positioned away from the generator and the course of the leads. The procedure was uneventful. The patient tolerated the interruption of therapy without clinically significant pain; a new left bundle branch block after valve deployment was identified on an artefact-free trace, stimulation was resumed after the procedure with analgesia equivalent to baseline, and subsequent interrogation confirmed normal device function. The case illustrates the application of a precautionary strategy informed by manufacturer labelling and analogous evidence; because the stimulator was off throughout, it does not establish that any individual measure was necessary. We examine how the hazards of the cardiac catheterisation laboratory differ from those of the operating theatre and propose a structured six-step approach to the management of a spinal cord stimulator during TAVI.

title: Models of Care for Mental Health Nurse Practitioners in Emergency Department Settings: A Scoping Review Across High-Income Countries.
journal: International journal of mental health nursing
abstract: This scoping review examined and synthesised existing literature on models of care involving Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (MHNPs) practising or consulting within Emergency Department (ED)-based Emergency Mental Health (EMH) services. EDs are a key access point for mental health care and often provide first contact or after-hours support for people experiencing crisis, reinforcing their central role within the mental health system. The review highlights the need for timely, safe and specialised mental health care within EDs to strengthen the quality, safety and responsiveness of EMH services. Given the limited ED-specific MHNP literature, studies involving related advanced mental health nursing roles were also included where functions overlapped with MHNP practice, although these roles were not considered equivalent. Using Arksey and O'Malley's framework, 13 ED-specific studies were included: two quantitative, two qualitative, five mixed-methods, three realist or realist-informed evaluations and one descriptive or pilot service evaluation. Three themes were identified: consumer outcomes and timely access to care; MHNP roles within ED service models; and stakeholder perspectives and systemic challenges. Across studies, MHNPs and related advanced mental health nursing roles were associated with improved access to specialist assessment, enhanced care coordination, reduced psychological distress and high consumer and staff satisfaction. However, evidence was largely derived from early-stage, single-site evaluations. Barriers relating to role visibility and organisational support also limited sustainability. Overall, MHNP roles remain under-researched, highlighting the need to identify system-level enablers supporting effective integration and impact.

title: Medical Economic Impact of Daikenchuto in Colon and Rectal Cancer Surgery: A Nationwide Observational Study.
journal: Journal of the anus, rectum and colon
abstract: Background Daikenchuto is a traditional Japanese herbal medicine (Kampo) that has been widely used because of its low cost and minimal side effects. It is used for early patient recovery after abdominal surgery and to prevent postoperative paralytic ileus in various surgeries, including colon and rectal cancer. Many studies have reported the usefulness of perioperative administration of Daikenchuto; however, few have examined its association with healthcare economics. Methods This observational study used data from the National Database (NDB) Sampling Dataset. This study included patients with colon or rectal cancer who underwent colectomy, anterior resection (AR), low anterior resection (LAR), or abdominoperineal resection (APR) between January 2013 and December 2022. The comparison was based on Daikenchuto administration. Results Overall, 3,759 patients underwent colectomy (Daikenchuto -: 3,111 vs. Daikenchuto +: 648), 675 underwent AR (567 vs. 108), 1,269 underwent LAR (1,105 vs. 164), and 348 underwent APR (310 vs. 38). Postoperative hospital stay was shorter in patients who received Daikenchuto: for colectomy, 13.8 vs. 13.0 days (P = 0.001); for AR, 15.3 vs. 13.0 days (P = 0.002); for LAR, 17.6 vs. 14.5 days (P Conclusion Perioperative Daikenchuto administration was associated with shortened the length of hospital stay and lower postoperative hospitalization costs in colon and rectal cancer surgeries.

title: Early Outcomes of Dorsal Onlay Buccal Mucosal Graft Urethroplasty for Female Urethral Stricture Disease: A Single-Center Experience.
abstract: Background and Objectives : To evaluate the surgical, functional, and perioperative outcomes of Dorsal Onlay Buccal Mucosal Graft Urethroplasty (DO-BMGU) in women with Female urethral stricture (FUS) disease. Materials and Methods : A retrospective analysis was performed including women who underwent DO-BMGU for FUS at a single tertiary referral center between January 2018 and October 2025. The primary outcome was freedom from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence. Secondary outcomes included perioperative outcomes, complications, and changes in maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax) and postvoid residual urine volume (PVR). Results : Twenty women with a mean age of 52.9 ± 14.7 years were included. The median stricture length was 2 cm (IQR 2-3), and all patients had undergone previous urethral dilatation. Median operative time was 65 min (IQR 60-80), with a median hospital stay of 3 days (IQR 3-4). During a median follow-up of 12 months (IQR 12-24), 18 patients (90%) remained free from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence. Two patients developed recurrent symptomatic narrowing and were successfully managed with urethral dilatation. At the 3-month objective functional assessment, mean Qmax improved significantly from 6.1 ± 2.3 to 20.4 ± 5.8 mL/s ( p p Conclusions : DO-BMGU was associated with favorable early objective functional outcomes and a high rate of freedom from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence, with few clinically significant complications in this small cohort. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm the long-term durability of this technique.

title: Influenza A (H1N1) virus infection complicated by checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a common, potentially severe adverse event in cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy, with glucocorticoids as the standard first-line treatment. Traditionally, glucocorticoids are avoided in confirmed viral pneumonia because they may delay viral clearance and increase secondary infection risk. No standardized strategy is available for managing concurrent CIP and viral pneumonia, and inappropriate treatment can lead to irreversible clinical deterioration. Patient concerns Following neoadjuvant immunotherapy, the patient developed concurrent influenza A (H1N1) infection and CIP, accompanied by persistent respiratory dysfunction and progressive pulmonary lesions. Diagnoses Combined with the patient's immunotherapy history, respiratory symptoms, imaging changes, and positive influenza A (H1N1) etiological results, a final diagnosis of concurrent CIP and H1N1 viral pneumonia was established. Interventions The patient initially received antiviral and empirical antibiotic therapy. Due to ongoing clinical deterioration and poor response to anti-infective treatment, glucocorticoids were reinitiated to target CIP after comprehensive evaluation. Outcomes The patient showed early radiographic worsening and intractable respiratory failure with no response to initial anti-infective management. After glucocorticoid administration, clinical symptoms and pulmonary lesions improved significantly, achieving a favorable recovery. Lessons Isolated antiviral and antibiotic treatment may fail to control disease progression in patients with concurrent CIP and influenza A pneumonia. Timely and rational glucocorticoid use can reverse clinical deterioration and improve prognosis even in the setting of active viral infection. This case provides practical evidence for the individualized management of overlapping CIP and viral pneumonia.

title: How Does Physician Clinical Experience Affect Quality of Care, as Measured by Length of Stay?
abstract: Introduction Length of stay (LOS) is a widely utilized metric of hospital quality and operational efficiency. Prolonged LOS is associated with increased healthcare costs, greater risk of hospital-acquired complications and infections, and reduced bed turnover, negatively affecting patient outcomes and institutional performance. Hospitalists and internal medicine physicians play an integral role in determining a patient's readiness for discharge and facilitating timely transitions of care. Examining factors that influence LOS, including physician characteristics such as clinical experience or time since graduation of residency or licensure may inform strategies to enhance quality of care. Methods We performed a literature search of PubMed with no restrictions on time, setting, or language to examine the relationship between physician clinical experience (measured in years since licensure or graduation) and inpatient LOS. Results Results were mixed and inconclusive. Four out of nine included articles found that physician clinical experience was associated with shorter LOS. Two articles associated a longer LOS with more years in practice. Finally, three out of our nine studies noted no differences in LOS by physician clinical experience. Discussion Collectively, the evidence to date suggests that physician clinical experience alone is not a consistent determinant of LOS, but this is modified by extensive heterogeneity in methodology among included studies. More precise characterization of clinical experience, encompassing factors such as duration of inpatient exposure and patient complexity, is needed. Conclusions More research with standardized definitions of experience, adjustment for case complexity, and exploration of process-level factors is needed to determine if and how physician clinical experience affects LOS.

title: Oral health in cancer patients: results of a monocentric survey.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

title: Much of the excess mortality in immunocompromised patients with viral severe acute respiratory infection occurs after ICU discharge.
Efficiency of Dual Minor Procedure Rooms in Plastic Surgery: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
Implementation of patient discharge management in a university hospital through action research.
abstract: Objectives to establish and implement a Hospital Discharge Management Committee in a university hospital, and to assess the group's perception of the committee's planning and implementation. Methods a qualitative study, conducted through action research. It took place in a university hospital in northeastern Brazil, over 12 months, following four phases: situational diagnosis; action planning; action implementation; and assessment. Results the committee was established and implemented in the hospital, with a collaboratively constructed work process. Instruments and workflows were developed, including eligibility criteria, patient recruitment and admission procedures, a readiness scale, as well as follow-up, discharge, and post-discharge workflows, structuring a model to support continuity of care. Final considerations the committee was implemented to monitor patients in the pilot unit. In the group's perception, there was an improvement in patient and caregiver monitoring, as well as a positive assessment of committee formation and methodology used, valuing each individual contribution.

title: Computed Tomography Perfusion in Suspected Ischemic Stroke: Patient-Related Pitfalls and Practical Clues Beyond Automated Interpretation.
abstract: The management of suspected ischemic stroke has evolved significantly, largely due to advancements in imaging technologies such as Computed Tomography Perfusion (CTP). This narrative review aims to delineate the practical applications and limitations of CTP in acute stroke evaluation, particularly in challenging scenarios. It is organized around illustrative clinical and imaging cases regarding small subcortical infarctions, posterior fossa ischemia, abnormal reference hemispheres, chronic steno-occlusive disease, the simultaneous involvement of multiple vascular territories, luxury perfusion, diaschisis, and systemic hemodynamic abnormalities. We discuss the core-penumbra paradigm, emphasizing the need for accurate interpretation of perfusion maps to guide therapeutic decisions. While automated CTP analyses enhance diagnostic efficiency, they can overlook critical patient-specific factors and exhibit variability in performance across different software platforms. Limitations in detecting small infarcts, particularly in lacunar strokes, highlight the necessity for qualitative visual assessments alongside quantitative data. Individualized case evaluations are crucial, as discrepancies between automated readings and qualitative interpretations can influence the management of single cases. Furthermore, we propose an integrated approach that combines automated assessments with human expertise to improve diagnostic precision and treatment efficacy. Future research should focus on refining CTP methodologies and enhancing their applicability in diverse clinical contexts to optimize patient management in acute ischemic stroke situations.

title: Making better use of patients' time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms.
Area-Level Correlates of Inpatient Care Self-Sufficiency in Subnational Health Planning Areas: A Disease-Stratified Ecological Study from Aichi Prefecture, Japan.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Japan organizes inpatient care through secondary medical areas (SMAs), but evidence linking area-level care self-sufficiency with population need, healthcare supply, and socioeconomic context is limited. We quantified disease-stratified self-sufficiency across Aichi Prefecture and examined its ecological correlates. Methods: This cross-sectional ecological study analyzed fiscal-year 2024 Diagnosis Procedure Combination discharges from 203 of 276 acute-care hospitals across 11 SMAs. The dataset comprised 396 cells (11 SMAs × 18 Major Diagnostic Categories × surgical/non-surgical strata) linked to census, healthcare-resource, household, and pooled 2020-2024 standardized mortality ratio (SMR) data. Pre-specified single-predictor regressions at the SMA level ( n = 11) were supplemented by spatial and cluster-robust sensitivity analyses. Self-sufficiency represented observed resident-to-provider flows within the participating hospital network. Results: Mean self-sufficiency ranged from 34.0% to 88.3% across SMAs (intra-class correlation, 0.54) and was 8.5 percentage points lower for surgical cells (95% CI, 5.9-11.1). Greater shares of residents aged ≥75 years (β = -12.80; 95% CI, -22.84 to -2.75) and households containing an elderly member (β = -13.53; 95% CI, -23.02 to -4.05) were the strongest negative correlates. Supply-density estimates were consistently positive; in the cell-level sensitivity model, physician, general-bed, and psychiatric-bed densities were associated with above-median self-sufficiency (ORs, 2.51-3.16). Exploratory analyses suggested differing patterns across acute and chronic conditions. Conclusions: Self-sufficiency varied substantially across planning areas and was associated with demographic, household, supply, and mortality characteristics. These findings support disease-specific evaluation of regional concentration versus local completion but do not establish causal or individual-level relationships. Multi-prefecture studies with individual-level case-mix adjustment are needed before resource-allocation applications.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Followed by Lung Cancer Resection in an Older Patient: A Case Report.
abstract: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: We report findings from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial (EUCT No. 2024-514590-22-00, STOP-DCI), an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending-dose, first-in-human trial to determine safety and evaluate clinical outcome for the MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 in patients with severe spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). In Phase 1b (N = 11), three cohorts received a single intracerebral ventricular (ICV) bolus (8.55 µg, 17-28.5 µg). In Phase 2a (N = 16), two cohorts were given three ICV injections of 28.5 µg EDV2209 or placebo over 18 h, beginning within 8 h of SAH onset.The study found an equal distribution of adverse events between treatment and placebo with no treatment-associated safety concerns. Outcomes and mortality were as expected or better for patients with severe SAH in the patients treated with EDV2209. Pharmacokinetics were reproducibly stable in the CSF with no detectable levels of EDV2209 in plasma.Treatment with EDV2209 was considered safe and was interpreted to provide potential benefit for improving patient outcome following severe SAH. These results provide a rationale to continue with a Phase 2b / 3 study powered to determine efficacy as well as safety.

title: Sialorrhea possibly associated with bupropion: a case report and review of potential mechanisms.
abstract: Background Bupropion is typically associated with xerostomia (dry mouth) rather than increased salivation. However, its prescribing information lists "increased salivation" as an infrequent adverse reaction. Case presentation We report the case of a 59-year-old female patient with the diagnosis of comorbid anxiety and depressive disorders. The patient experienced no sialorrhea while on a combination of venlafaxine and low-dose quetiapine. However, after switching venlafaxine to bupropion, she developed significant sialorrhea. The sialorrhea was severe: she had to carry tissues and a plastic bag during the day, and at night the pillow was frequently soaked. Gradual discontinuation of quetiapine did not resolve the symptom. The sialorrhea completely remitted only after bupropion was discontinued and replaced with escitalopram. The Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was 6, indicating a "probable" relationship. Conclusion This case suggests that bupropion may induce sialorrhea, potentially through a synergistic mechanism involving noradrenergic pathways when combined with quetiapine. Clinicians should be aware of this rare adverse effect when prescribing bupropion, particularly in combination therapies. Therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical pharmacist collaboration may help prevent such adverse events.

title: Association between preserved ratio impaired spirometry and postoperative pulmonary complications in patients undergoing lung cancer resection.
abstract: Background Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are associated with adverse clinical outcomes and increased hospitalization-related costs. Preserved ratio impaired lung function (PRISm) is a lung function phenotype distinct from obstructive lung disease, and little is known about the effect of PRISm on PPCs. The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PRISm and PPCs in patients undergoing lung cancer resection. Methods This retrospective cohort study involved patients who underwent lung cancer resection in the thoracic surgery case database between January 2019 and June 2019 at Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital. Demographics, preoperative measurements of spirometry, operative characteristics, PPCs, and length of stay were assessed. Results The incidence of PPCs in the three groups was 36.84% in the PRISm group, 23.39% in the normal spirometry group, and 51.57% in the COPD group. Using a variable-selection strategy (forced clinical confounders plus univariable screening at P p = 0.008], and the relationship was not statistically different between PRISm and COPD groups [odds ratio (OR) = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.38-1.04; p = 0.071]. In subgroup analyses, non-restrictive PRISm was not associated with a significantly increased risk of PPCs relative to restrictive PRISm (adjusted OR = 1.32, 95% CI: 0.59-2.95; p = 0.494). Conclusions Compared with normal spirometry, PRISm was independently associated with a higher risk of PPCs in patients undergoing lung cancer resection. Preoperative identification of PRISm may refine preoperative risk stratification. Candidate targeted strategies, such as preoperative pulmonary rehabilitation, lung-protective intraoperative ventilation, and intensified postoperative surveillance, warrant prospective evaluation. The risk did not differ significantly between PRISm subtypes, though this finding requires further validation.

title: Bridging data availability and data use: A qualitative study on frontline managers' perspectives on data-driven decision making in hospital departments.
Bilateral Internal Thoracic Artery Grafting in Coronary Surgery: A Three-Tier Decision Framework.
abstract: The left internal mammary artery grafted to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) is the main determinant of survival in coronary artery bypass grafting, but the choice of the second graft remains controversial. The use of both mammary arteries offers a greater long-term survival benefit compared with a single mammary artery graft; however, this advantage is delayed and diminished when compared with a single mammary artery graft plus a radial artery graft. Furthermore, this approach is associated with a higher risk of sternal complications and, via mechanisms of competitive flow and steal phenomenon, of perioperative coronary malperfusion. This article proposes organising the clinical decision-making process according to three hierarchical levels: (1) absolute contraindications based on the patient's medical history that preclude the use of a particular graft (thoracic irradiation, subclavian artery disease, acute aortic dissection); (2) the haemodynamic adequacy of the graft for the target coronary territory; (3) the assessment of the risk of delayed sternal healing in the individual patient, where skeletonization has reduced the historical significance of diabetes. Overlaying these is a transversal variable represented by the harvesting technique (pedicled mammary artery vs. skeletonized mammary artery, together with the surgeon's learning curve), which re-interprets apparently unfavourable results and distinguishes the risk associated with the graft itself from that of the surgical procedure. The model aims to rationalise patient selection and reduce the persistent underutilisation of bilateral mammary artery grafting. It should be noted at the outset that this survival advantage rests largely on observational and propensity-matched evidence and has not been confirmed on an intention-to-treat basis by the only adequately powered randomised trial, so that the model proposed here is offered as a framework for selection rather than as a claim of established superiority.

title: Disseminated <i>Klebsiella pneumoniae</i> Infection Causing Multisystem Abscesses and Necrotising Fasciitis in an Immunocompetent Patient: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Disseminated Klebsiella pneumoniae infection that concurrently produces a liver abscess, bilateral pulmonary abscesses and necrotising fasciitis is uncommon in patients without overt immunocompromise. Definitive designation of a hypervirulent strain requires the string test and virulence-gene testing, which are not always available at the point of care. Case presentation A previously healthy 48-year-old man, in whom a contaminated lower limb wound was the suspected portal of entry, subsequently developed a liver abscess, multiple bilateral pulmonary abscesses, necrotising soft-tissue infection of the left lower limb and sepsis with circulatory instability. Culture of the liver-abscess aspirate yielded a mucoid K. pneumoniae that was susceptible to carbapenems, ceftazidime/avibactam, amikacin and levofloxacin, among other agents. Because neither the string test nor virulence genes (e.g., rmpA , iucA ) were examined, the isolate was described only as having a clinically hypervirulent phenotype based on mucoid colony morphology and the multisite invasive pattern. Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii were recovered sequentially from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and sputum and were interpreted, in context, as airway colonisation or ventilator-associated tracheobronchitis. After multisite percutaneous drainage, repeated debridement with vacuum sealing drainage, staged antimicrobial therapy and organ support, the patient recovered and was discharged; at the 3-month follow-up, the lesions had largely resolved without recurrence. Conclusion This case suggests that multisite metastatic abscesses in an immunocompetent individual should raise suspicion for invasive K. pneumoniae infection. Early, adequate source control together with rational antimicrobial stewardship appears central to a favourable outcome. The conclusions are limited by the single-case design and the absence of molecular confirmation of hypervirulence.

title: Function-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate with bladder neck and 12 o'clock urethral mucosal preservation for large-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia: a single-center retrospective case series.
abstract: Background Large-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) poses a significant surgical challenge, as conventional transurethral resection yields suboptimal tissue removal efficiency and high rates of ejaculatory dysfunction. While endoscopic enucleation techniques (e.g., HoLEP and PKEP) offer improved efficacy, the systematic preservation of functional anatomical structures - particularly the bladder neck and anterior urethral mucosa - remains inadequately addressed in current practice. Objective To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and functional outcomes of function-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate (FP-PKEP) - a modified technique incorporating systematic preservation of the bladder neck circular fibers and the 12 o'clock urethral mucosal strip - in patients with large-volume BPH. Methods This single-center, retrospective case series included 52 consecutive patients with large-volume BPH (prostate volume >80 mL, International Prostate Symptom Score [IPSS] > 20, maximum urinary flow rate [Qmax] Results All 52 patients (mean age 67.8 ± 7.2 years; mean prostate volume 93.7 ± 15.2 mL) successfully underwent FP-PKEP without conversion. Mean operative time was 72.5 ± 15.8 min; postoperative hemoglobin decrease was 9.8 ± 4.2 g/L; catheterization duration was 2.8 ± 0.9 days; and hospital stay was 4.2 ± 1.3 days. At 3 months, IPSS decreased from 26.1 ± 3.0 to 6.8 ± 2.6 ( P P Conclusions In this uncontrolled case series, FP-PKEP showed a favorable safety profile and achieved significant relief of bladder outlet obstruction, with promising early urinary continence and ejaculatory outcomes. The systematic preservation of the bladder neck and 12 o'clock urethral mucosa warrants further evaluation in prospective randomized controlled trials, as these preliminary findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Appointments Do Not Guarantee Higher Patient Satisfaction: Departmental Heterogeneity in Outpatient Waiting Performance
abstract: Abstract Background Appointment systems are intended to improve patient flow and service quality, but an appointment may not entail a shorter actual wait or greater satisfaction in every department, even within the same hospital. We compared actual waiting time and satisfaction with waiting between patients with appointments and walk-in patients across two outpatient departments, and explored how appointment-window alignment and expectation fulfillment related to satisfaction. Methods We conducted a cross sectional survey of single waiting episodes among patients attending the ophthalmology and gynecology outpatient departments in a tertiary hospital in china. 996 questionnaires were analyzed. Adjusted models containing an appointment status by department interaction assessed departmental heterogeneity, controlling for age, sex, educational, and previous visits. Appointment only exploratory analyses compared expected call times with scheduled windows and evaluated whether actual waiting exceeded expected waiting. Results After adjustment, patients with appointments waited 6.43 minutes less than walk-in patients in ophthalmology (95% CI: −9.02 to − 3.84; Holm-adjusted P

title: Non-invasive ventilation for general paediatricians.
abstract: Over the past two decades, non-invasive ventilation (NIV) has transitioned from being primarily used in specialist intensive care units to becoming a standard intervention in high dependency units, general paediatric units, emergency departments, and increasingly, patients' homes. Despite this expansion, many general paediatricians still perceive NIV as outside their primary expertise. With this review, we aim to address that gap and equip general paediatricians with the knowledge and confidence to appropriately initiate NIV, monitor its effectiveness, and recognise when escalation of care is required. We narratively reviewed the physiological rationale for non-invasive respiratory support (NRS), including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and the two principal modalities of NIV-continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP)-and summarised disease-specific evidence from recent literature, including randomised trials, systematic reviews, and international consensus statements. This is a narrative rather than a systematic review: we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Paediatric Respiratory Reviews for English-language publications from January 2018 to June 2026 using the terms "non-invasive ventilation", "high-flow nasal cannula", "CPAP", "BiPAP", and "children", supplemented by references already known to the authors, and selected articles for relevance and recency, prioritising randomised trials, systematic reviews, and consensus statements. HFNC is an oxygenation device rather than a ventilatory device, and its mechanism, clinical applications, and therapeutic goals differ from CPAP and BiPAP. We introduce the Indications, Contraindications, Equipment, Mode and settings, Assessment and monitoring, Next steps (ICEMAN) framework as a practical tool for structured and safe initiation of NIV in routine clinical practice, and apply it across bronchiolitis, acute severe asthma, pneumonia and hypoxaemic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease, and obstructive sleep apnoea. Conclusion The essential requirements to initiate NIV outside the PICU are well-trained staff, appropriate monitoring, a reliable oxygen supply, and a clear plan for escalation to a higher level of care. Selection of patients for NIV outside the PICU requires careful attention to indication, contraindications, equipment, monitoring, and escalation pathway by using frameworks like ICEMAN. What is known • HFNC, CPAP, and BiPAP are established, physiologically distinct respiratory therapies now used well beyond the PICU. What is new • The ICEMAN framework, updated with PALICC-2 ARDS criteria, gives non-specialists a structured, teachable approach to safe NIV initiation.

title: Effects of enhanced recovery after surgery and prehabilitation interventions on postoperative outcomes after lung resection in patients with lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Lung resection is the standard curative treatment for resectable lung cancer; however, postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) and prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS) remain major barriers to recovery and healthcare efficiency. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) and prehabilitation are distinct perioperative strategies that differ in their timing, intervention components, and mechanisms of action, but both aim to optimize patients' perioperative condition and improve postoperative recovery. However, their effectiveness compared with conventional perioperative care based solely on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) has not been comprehensively synthesized. Objectives To assess the effectiveness of ERAS and prehabilitation in reducing PPCs, shortening LOS, and improving patient-reported outcomes following pulmonary resection for lung cancer. Subjects and methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs involving adults undergoing pulmonary resection for primary lung cancer. Searches of PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, RISS, KISS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform identified studies published between January 2015 and May 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) for PPCs and mean differences (MDs) for LOS. Patient-reported outcomes were synthesized narratively according to the SWiM guideline. Results Ten RCTs involving 1,569 participants met the inclusion criteria. ERAS and prehabilitation significantly reduced PPCs compared with conventional perioperative care (OR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36-0.65, p I 2 = 97.9%), and the 95% prediction interval crossed the null. Narrative synthesis demonstrated consistent improvements in anxiety, depression, postoperative pain, pulmonary function, quality of life, and functional recovery. Conclusion ERAS and prehabilitation are effective perioperative strategies for improving outcomes after pulmonary resection for lung cancer. Their implementation in routine clinical practice may reduce postoperative complications, accelerate recovery, and improve healthcare efficiency. Further multicenter RCTs are needed to optimize intervention components, standardize outcome measures, and strengthen evidence for long-term and patient-reported outcomes. Systematic review registration CRD420261373242.

title: Clinical outcomes and cost analysis of elective spine surgery in ambulatory surgery centers versus hospital outpatient departments: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background The shift of elective spine surgery to ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) and hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) is driven by advances in minimally invasive techniques and cost-containment pressure. Comparisons between settings are confounded by patient selection bias, leaving true cost and safety differences unresolved. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020) compared clinical outcomes, operative efficiency, and costs of elective spine surgery in ASCs versus HOPDs across twelve observational studies (49,054 patients). Data were pooled using random-effects models; methodological quality was assessed with risk of bias in nonrandomized studies of interventions V2. Results ASC patients were significantly younger and healthier. Clinical outcomes were equivalent across settings (reoperations relative risk [RR] 0.80; complications RR 0.88; 30-day readmissions RR 0.94). ASCs demonstrated superior operative efficiency (blood loss mean difference [MD] -20.24 mL, p = 0.01; operative time MD -15.05 min, p = 0.03) and 25-45% cost savings for single-level lumbar procedures. Conclusion For younger, healthier patients undergoing single-level procedures, ASC spine surgery is as safe as HOPD surgery and offers superior efficiency and cost savings, provided rigorous patient selection is maintained.

title: Confluence Stones at the Junction of the Cystic Duct and an Aberrant Anterior Sectoral Bile Duct: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Confluence stones usually arise when gallstones impacted in the cystic duct migrate toward the biliary confluence. Surgical treatment can be technically demanding because of chronic inflammation and distorted anatomy. Confluence stones at the junction between the cystic duct and an aberrant bile duct are extremely rare. We report a successfully treated case of confluence stones arising at the junction of the cystic duct and an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct with a communicating accessory bile duct. Case presentation A 38-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain, and biliary stones were detected. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct draining independently into the common bile duct. Biliary stones were identified both within this duct and at its junction with the cystic duct. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography confirmed the biliary anatomy and additionally revealed a communicating accessory bile duct between the anterior and posterior sectoral ducts. The stones within the distal portion of the aberrant duct were removed endoscopically, but the impacted confluence stones could not be extracted. Therefore, open surgery was performed. After exposure of the junction, the confluence stones were removed through a semicircumferential incision. Complete stone clearance was confirmed by intraoperative cholangioscopy and cholangiography. The patient was discharged on POD 11 with no bile leakage. At 14 months postoperatively, she remained asymptomatic and had experienced no episodes of cholangitis. Conclusions We report a rare case of confluence stones arising at the junction of the cystic duct and an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct. Preoperative assessment of the drainage territory and intraoperative evaluation of the duct diameter, ischemia, and tissue fragility are essential for appropriate and safe repair of the bile duct defect. The repair strategy should not rely on presumed bypass flow through a communicating accessory bile duct because its functional capacity cannot be reliably predicted.

title: Office hysteroscopic removal of an intrauterine device-myoma complex using an 18.5-Fr hysteroscope and blue laser in a postmenopausal woman with cervical atrophy: a no-anesthesia approach.
Pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and SCE after colonic ESD: a case report.
abstract: Background Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become a widely accepted technique for en bloc resection of colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs). Although the procedure is generally considered safe, complications including bleeding and perforation may occur. The simultaneous development of pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and extensive subcutaneous emphysema following colorectal ESD represents an exceptionally rare but potentially serious adverse event. Case summary A 56-year-old female patient underwent ESD for a granular-type LST measuring 8 mm × 20 mm located in the ascending colon. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia with tracheal intubation and carbon dioxide insufflation. Complete en bloc resection was achieved, and the post-ESD mucosal defect was closed with 16 titanium clips. Approximately 3 h after the procedure, the patient developed progressive neck swelling without respiratory distress or chest pain. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a small amount of pneumothorax on the right side and fluid pneumothorax on the left side (lung compression Conclusion This case demonstrates that extensive gas extravasation involving multiple body compartments can occur as a rare complication of colorectal ESD, particularly when procedures are performed in the retroperitoneal portion of the colon under general anesthesia with positive pressure ventilation. Prompt recognition, timely CT evaluation, and conservative management in hemodynamically stable patients can lead to favorable outcomes without the need for surgical intervention.

title: Influence of bed occupancy and patient characteristics on bedspacing practices: a multicentre retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objectives Hospitals cohort similar patients in departments. When departments are operating under high bed occupancy, patients may be relocated from the admitting department to a ward belonging to an off-service ward of a different clinical specialty. This process, often referred to as bedspacing, is not well understood and may have a negative impact on patient safety. As such, the objective of this study is to investigate the impact of patient characteristics and bed occupancy on bedspacing. Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Nine hospitals in a Swedish healthcare region between 2015 and 2019. Participants 2 34 325 patients above the age of 18 who experienced unplanned hospital admission. Outcome measurements Bedspacing operationalised as patients that were admitted to a cohorting department but physically located in an off-service ward. Results The most important determinants of bedspacing were diseases of the genitourinary system (HR 1.23 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.31)) and musculoskeletal system (HR 1.37 (95% CI 1.27 to 1.47)). Patients with diseases of the circulatory system (HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.61)) and nervous system (HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.57)) were less likely to be bedspaced. Other patients characteristics such as age (HR 0.954 (95% CI 0.940 to 0.970 per SD increase), registered sex (HR 0.841 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.86) for men) and marital status (HR 1.194 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.23) for widows/widowers) were also found to influence bedspacing. Regarding bed occupancy, the HR of being bedspaced was 1.46 (95% CI 1.39 to 1.54) when comparing above 115% to less than 85% bed occupancy. Conclusions Both clinical and non-clinical patient factors influenced bedspacing. Bedspacing was positively associated with bed occupancy with substantial variation across departments and operationalisations of bedspacing. Future research should differentiate between different types of bedspacing and bed occupancy to identify conditions under which bedspacing may be safe and equitable.

title: Early out-of-bed mobilisation within 48 hours after acute stroke and in-hospital complications: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Early mobilisation is widely promoted in acute stroke care, but observational evaluations can be biased because sicker patients often mobilise later. Objective To evaluate the association between early out-of-bed mobilisation (≤48 hours) and in-hospital complications and to describe discharge outcomes. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using routinely collected clinical data from a single centre (admissions from May 2024 to May 2025). Patients were included in the primary analysis if time to first mobilisation was recorded. The exposure was mobilisation within 48 hours versus after 48 hours. The primary outcome was any in-hospital complication. Secondary outcomes were favourable discharge modified Rankin Scale (0-2), discharge to home and length of stay. Confounding by indication was addressed using propensity score overlap weighting based on pre-exposure covariates. Relative risks (RR) were estimated using overlap-weighted modified Poisson regression with robust SEs. Risk differences (RD) used bootstrap resampling (500 replicates). A landmark analysis restricted to length of stay ≥2 days was used to reduce immortal-time bias. Results The dataset included 400 admissions; mobilisation timing was recorded for 371 patients (mean age 70.1 years, SD 11.5; 46.6% female; 82.7% ischaemic stroke; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale 10 (IQR 6-14)). Among recorded cases, 245 (66.0%) were mobilised within 48 hours. In overlap-weighted analyses, early mobilisation was associated with lower complication risk (RR 0.689, 95% CI 0.498 to 0.953; p=0.024), with RD -0.123 (bootstrap 95% CI -0.233 to -0.005). In the landmark cohort, the association remained similar (RR 0.709, 95% CI 0.513 to 0.979; p=0.036). Discharge outcomes were directionally favourable but less precise after weighting. Conclusions In routine acute stroke care, early out-of-bed mobilisation within 48 hours was associated with fewer in-hospital complications and remained robust in a landmark sensitivity analysis. Longer-term functional outcomes should be evaluated in studies with post-discharge follow-up.

title: Enterobacter-Related Deep Sternal Wound Infection After Cardiac Surgery with Delayed Negative-Pressure Wound Therapy Success: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Deep sternal wound infection (DSWI) is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening complication after median sternotomy and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prompt recognition and coordinated surgical-medical management are essential to prevent mediastinal extension, prolonged hospitalization, and reconstructive morbidity. Case presentation We report a 70-year-old man with multiple comorbidities (including diabetes mellitus, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and hypertension) and a history of heavy tobacco exposure. He underwent CABG with an initially uncomplicated postoperative course. Twenty days after discharge, he re-presented with systemic deterioration and severe sternal wound dehiscence with necrotic tissue and clinical sternal instability, consistent with DSWI. Deep-tissue cultures isolated Enterobacter spp, enabling culture-directed antimicrobial therapy. Species-level identification was not available in the archived records, and definitive radiologic confirmation of mediastinitis or sternal osteomyelitis was unavailable. Because of delayed presentation and ongoing wound complexity, negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT) was initiated as an adjunct strategy. The patient subsequently demonstrated progressive clinical improvement and wound stabilization, without immediate need for flap reconstruction, with plastic surgery input for delayed closure planning. Conclusion This case highlights that Gram-negative organisms such as Enterobacter can cause DSWI and supports the importance of deep microbiologic sampling to guide therapy. It also illustrates the use of NPWT as an adjunct following delayed presentation. Although clinical wound stabilization was observed after NPWT initiation, the effectiveness of delayed NPWT cannot be inferred from a single case or limited follow-up.

title: Arthroplasty centers logistically separated from general orthopedic departments were associated with a more successful implementation of a standardized day-case setup : A Danish cohort study of 6718 procedures from a fast-track multi-center collaboration.
journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
abstract: Background Day-case hip and knee arthroplasty can reduce bed occupancy and improve cost-effectiveness, which is crucial for addressing the increasing demand among hip and knee osteoarthritis patients. This study investigated how different arthroplasty center setups were associated with the implementation and day-of-surgery (DOS) discharge rates of a standardized day-case setup. Materials and methods We included unilateral primary hip and knee arthroplasty patients from seven fast-track arthroplasty centers, all implementing a standardized day-case setup in September 2022 with identical eligibility and discharge criteria. Centers were categorized as: Satellite Arthroplasty Centers (SACs): Only primary arthroplasties, separate logistics. Elective Arthroplasty Centers (EACs): Complex primaries, revisions, separate logistics. Arthroplasty Unit Orthopedic Departments (AUOs): Primary and revision procedures, integrated into a general orthopedic department. We compared DOS discharge rates from September 2022 to September 2023 with a baseline period (July 2019-December 2019) using crude percentages. We compared the DOS discharge rate for day-case-eligible patients in study period between the center types using mixed effects models. Results We included 6718 patients (1357 SAC, 4309 EAC, 1052 AUO) during the study period and 3974 in the baseline period. DOS discharge rates increased post-implementation across all centers (SAC: 3.9% to 30%, EAC: 5.5% to 23%, AUO: 7.4% to 14%). Compared with AUOs (36%), successful DOS discharge among eligible patients was more likely in SACs (54%; adjusted OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1; adjusted risk difference 25 percentage points, 95% CI 5.9-44) and EACs (60%; adjusted OR 3.8, 95% CI 1.7-8.5; adjusted risk difference 31 percentage points, 95% CI 13.8-48). Conclusions Arthroplasty centers with logistics separate from the general orthopedic department, SACs and EACs, were associated with higher rates of successful DOS discharge among eligible patients during implementation of a standardized day-case pathway, despite integrated arthroplasty units, AUOs, having higher day-case surgery use before implementation.

title: Necrotising fasciitis following abdominoplasty performed abroad: a case report.
abstract: Background Cosmetic medical tourism has grown considerably in Europe, with many patients travelling abroad seeking lower-cost procedures. However, heterogeneous practices and the absence of postoperative follow-up inherent to geographical distance may lead to life-threatening complications with delayed management. We report a case of necrotising fasciitis following abdominoplasty performed abroad. Case presentation A 42-year-old female patient underwent abdominoplasty, liposuction, and gluteal lipofilling in a foreign country. The postoperative course was complicated by anaemia, wound dehiscence, and an inflammatory syndrome, initially managed conservatively. Her condition deteriorated, necessitating medical repatriation. On admission, clinical examination revealed abdominal soft tissue necrosis with fever and purulent discharge, alongside a severe inflammatory response on laboratory investigations. Emergency surgical exploration confirmed extensive necrosis of the abdominal fascia and a gluteal collection. Wide debridement with bacteriological sampling and drainage were performed. Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy was initiated, and postoperative vasopressor support was required. An early second-look procedure was performed the following day. Following vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) therapy, reconstruction with a split-thickness skin graft was carried out. The patient was discharged after six weeks of hospitalisation with significant aesthetic sequelae. Clinical relevance Necrotising fasciitis is a rare but potentially fatal condition whose prognosis depends on the promptness of management. Medical tourism, owing to heterogeneous practices and lack of postoperative follow-up, may lead to diagnostic and therapeutic delay, exposing patients to this type of complication. Even in cases of favourable outcome, functional and aesthetic sequelae can be significant.

title: Multimodal Ayurveda Intervention in the Management of Recurrent Pilonidal Sinus: A Case Report.
abstract: Pilonidal sinus (PNS) is a chronic inflammatory condition that primarily originates from hair follicles in the natal cleft at the base of the spine and may also occur in other areas such as the axilla and umbilicus. A 25-year-old male patient presented to the outpatient department (OPD) of the surgery unit at the National Ayurveda Teaching Hospital, Borella, in November 2022 with complaints of pain and purulent discharge from the sacral region near the anus, accompanied by intermittent fever for 5 days. Clinical examination revealed a tender swelling in the sacral area with a discharging sinus opening and multiple scar marks from previous surgeries. The patient had previously undergone two surgical procedures (wide excision and primary closure) for the same condition. Based on the clinical findings, the case was diagnosed as a recurrent PNS with abscess formation. Management was initiated with incision and drainage of the abscess, followed by application of a semisolid paste of Apamarga Theekshna Kshara , a herbomineral alkaline preparation from the whole plant of Achyranthes aspera L., burnt conch shells (a source of calcium carbonate) and a paste of the roots of Plumbago indica L. (added to improve and to achieve the maximum potency of Kshara ). Microbiological culture of the pus revealed the presence of beta hemolytic Streptococcus (group G) and coliform. Internal medications, including Pancha tikta decoction, Sudarshana Choorna (powder), Triphala Guggulu (tablets), Amurta Guggulu (tablets), and Kaishora Guggulu (tablets), were administered to manage the infection and fever. During the postoperative period, the wound was cleansed with a polyherbal decoction ( Pancha valkala ) prepared from the aqueous extracts of the barks of Ficus religiosa , Ficus benghalensis , and Ficus racemosa . Wound dressings were performed using the same decoction mixed with Apamarga Kshara powder (herbomineral alkaline paste prepared from the whole plant of Achyranthes aspera L.and burnt conch shells) (without adding P. indica L roots. Hence, it's in medium potency). Once a healthy wound bed was achieved, dressing was continued with Seethodaka Taila, a medicated oil known for its wound-healing properties, for 3 months until complete wound healing was achieved. The patient was followed up for 3 years, during which no recurrence was reported. This case suggests that the multimodel ayurveda management approach may be a potential clinical experience that may encourage further study.

title: Uterine Preservation and Maternal Outcomes Across FIGO Severity in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: A Six-Year Retrospective Cohort in Vietnam.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Uterus-preserving management of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is increasingly reported, but preservation rates are difficult to interpret without considering disease severity and maternal morbidity. We aimed to estimate short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge and describe maternal outcomes by FIGO clinical severity. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 291 women with clinically diagnosed PAS and intraoperative FIGO grading who underwent cesarean delivery at Hung Vuong Hospital, a tertiary maternity referral hospital in Vietnam, from 2019 to 2024. The primary outcome was short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge, defined as no hysterectomy during the index operation or before discharge. Secondary and exploratory analyses described hemorrhage and maternal morbidity across FIGO severity. Results: Short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge was achieved in 282/291 women (96.9%; 95% CI 94.2-98.4), including 72/79 with FIGO grade 3 (91.1%; 95% CI 82.8-95.6). Major hemorrhage occurred in 81/291 (27.8%) and severe maternal morbidity in 25/291 (8.6%); no maternal deaths occurred. In FIGO grade 3, major hemorrhage occurred in 51/79 (64.6%), high-volume red-cell transfusion in 37/79 (46.8%), and severe maternal morbidity in 21/79 (26.6%). Conclusions: Most women retained the uterus through hospital discharge in this cohort, but women with FIGO grade 3 had high rates of hemorrhage, transfusion, and maternal morbidity. Without a concurrent planned-hysterectomy comparator, this study cannot compare the effectiveness of uterine preservation with hysterectomy.

title: Identification of Issues Contributing to Longer Length of Stay and Higher Readmission Rates for Parkinson's Patients Admitted to Hospital.
abstract: Background People with Parkinson's disease (PD) are a vulnerable cohort of people, more likely to suffer serious health-related problems when admitted to hospital. Literature suggests that health service improvement utilising a robust health care redesign framework, can improve local service delivery and outcomes for hospitalised PD patients. Aim/objectives This healthcare redesign project aims to identify the issues that contribute to PD patients experiencing a longer length of stay (LOS) and (re)admitting to a tertiary hospital in Sydney, Australia. Quantitative analysis of hospital data previously identified comorbidities present on admission that impact LOS and acquired complications that significantly extend LOS. This paper demonstrates the benefits of utilising mixed methods to provide a comprehensive picture of the PD patient's inpatient experience. Methods Mixed-methods healthcare redesign diagnostic tools were used to gather evidence and understand the issues. Results Seventy-eight percent (n = 831) of PD patients admitted to the emergency department were triage category 1, 2 or 3. 58.5% of PD patients have their PD medications charted within 4 h of admission. Their average LOS was 13 days. Data triangulation identified several barriers to optimal care, with prioritisation activities identifying three high-impact, feasible targets for improvement: PD medication management during nil-by-mouth periods, timely medication charting and timely discharge planning. Root causes (lack of formalised care pathways, limited access to resources and poor coordination of PD services) were identified as contributing to PD patients experiencing a longer LOS and higher readmission rates. Poor communication between clinicians within the hospital, fragmented transitions between hospital and community services and limited access to specialist resources were identified as key system-level barriers requiring prioritisation in the subsequent redesign phase. Conclusions The use of mixed methods provided a rich understanding of the PD patient experience of a hospital admission and prolonged length of stay. This study identified system-level barriers to optimal Parkinson's disease care, providing clear targets for service redesign to improve patient outcomes and hospital efficiency. Addressing gaps in Parkinson's disease medication management, discharge planning and interdisciplinary communication may improve inpatient outcomes, reduce avoidable complications and decrease hospital length of stay and readmissions. Implications for nursing practice Nurses play a critical role in advocating for and leading improvements in the quality, safety and efficiency of care for PD patients. This subsequently improves the PD patient's hospital experience. Nursing practice should focus on prioritising accurate and timely medication management, strengthening communication between clinicians to expedite discharge planning and advocating for PD-specific knowledge and education to improve patient outcomes, reduce length of stay and service efficiencies. Patient and public contribution Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, reporting or dissemination of this healthcare redesign project.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning to support early planning of hospital Length Of Stay
Making It Count: A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Pediatric Hospital Billing at a Community Hospital.
Integration of Non-Thermal Plasma into the Thyroidectomy Surgical Workflow: A Prospective Pilot Study on Early Postoperative Safety and Tissue Recovery.
abstract: Background: Thyroidectomy is a cornerstone treatment for thyroid pathologies but carries risks including recurrent laryngeal nerve injury, hypoparathyroidism, and cervical haematomas. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) may improve local haemostasis and tissue healing, although its safety within the cervical neurovascular axis requires human validation. Methods: This prospective, interventional, single-arm pilot study evaluated the feasibility, reproducibility and early postoperative safety of integrating atmospheric-pressure NTP (0.5 W/cm 2 ) into the standard thyroidectomy workflow in 30 patients. Safety endpoints included the absence of thermal injury, neurovascular complications, or surgical-site morbidity. We assessed healing and aesthetic outcomes using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) and Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS). Results: NTP integration achieved 100% technical feasibility, without reactor failures, gas-delivery interruptions, or thermal anomalies. No major acute complications occurred, including obstructive haematomas, recurrent laryngeal nerve injuries, or severe postoperative hypocalcaemia (0/30; 0.0%). Early incisional assessments showed favourable scores (median VSS: 1.2, IQR: 1.0-2.0; median POSAS overall opinion: 1.1, IQR: 1.0-1.5), reported descriptively at the 14-day postoperative milestone. Intraoperative biophysical evaluations and postoperative clinical tracking revealed no overt thermal anomalies or deep structural alterations, supporting high biological safety. Conclusions: Integration of NTP into the endocrine neck surgery workflow demonstrates technical feasibility, logistical efficiency, and a favourable early postoperative safety profile. The intervention is associated with a favourable early incisional healing profile without compromising adjacent vital structures. These preliminary findings support NTP as a reproducible, reliable surgical adjunct and provide a robust clinical and methodological basis for endocrine surgical practice.

title: Delayed intraparenchymal pneumocephalus causing internal capsule injury after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Pneumocephalus is a rare but serious complication after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (ETSS), usually associated with CSF leakage and occasionally progressing to tension pneumocephalus. Delayed intraparenchymal pneumocephalus causing focal brain injury after ETSS for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst (RCC) is exceptionally rare. Observations A 74-year-old woman underwent ETSS for recurrent RCC and was discharged on postoperative day (POD) 10 after an uneventful early course. On POD 37, she developed sudden left hemiparesis and mild dysarthria. Head CT demonstrated pneumocephalus extending from the sella toward the right internal capsule without rhinorrhea. With conservative management, the pneumocephalus gradually resolved, revealing parenchymal injury involving the posterior limb of the right internal capsule on CT and MRI. She later reported repeated nose blowing after discharge, including on the morning of symptom onset. Intraoperative endoscopic review revealed a depression in the anterior perforated substance, anatomically corresponding to the ruptured RCC and subsequent injury site. Lessons In recurrent or ruptured RCCs, occult communication between the sellar region and adjacent brain may permit air entry after postoperative Valsalva maneuvers. Strict counseling, recognition of high-risk parenchymal findings, and airtight multilayer reconstruction with a vascularized mucosal flap may reduce this risk. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26647.

title: Correction: Implementation of an AI-Assisted Workflow for Rehabilitation Discharge Summary Creation: Evaluation of Documentation Efficiency, Usability, and Hallucinations in a 290-Bed General Hospital in Japan
An Evaluation of ICU Follow-Up Clinic Attendance and Subsequent Healthcare Resource Utilization in Wales, United Kingdom: A Retrospective, Population-Level Data-Linkage Study.
abstract: Importance Postintensive care syndrome encapsulates the long-term physical, psychologic, and cognitive impairments often seen among ICU survivors. Post-ICU follow-up clinics may support recovery and reduce avoidable healthcare utilization, but population-level evidence remains limited. Objectives To identify patient characteristics associated with follow-up clinic attendance and evaluate differences in healthcare resource utilization (HRU) across three groups: invited and attended, invited but did not attend, and not invited. Design setting and participants A retrospective cohort study using anonymised, linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales, United Kingdom. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with ICU admissions between 2016 and 2023 who survived to discharge were included. Follow-up clinic data were obtained from three regional health boards (healthcare organizations responsible for delivering National Health Services in Wales) with follow-up clinic availability. Main outcomes and measures HRU outcomes included ICU readmissions, emergency department attendances, hospital admissions (elective and emergency), hospital bed days, outpatient appointments, and general practitioner (GP) events. Multivariable models assessed associations between clinic attendance and HRU. Results Of 6491 eligible patients, 761 attended a follow-up clinic, 1473 were invited but did not attend, and 4257 were not invited. Among invited patients, attendance was associated with increasing age, comorbidity, deprivation, and ICU length of stay. Compared with attendees, nonattendees and those not invited had higher adjusted odds of ICU readmission (odds ratio [OR] = 2.81 and 2.22, respectively), elective admissions, and hospital bed days. No significant differences were observed for emergency admissions or GP events. Attendees were more likely to have 4 or more (non-follow-up clinic) outpatient appointments. Conclusions and relevance Clinic attendance was associated with differences in several HRU domains. Variability in access and engagement suggests potential inequalities in post‑ICU recovery pathways. Standardizing referral practices and expanding clinic availability may improve outcomes for ICU survivors.

title: The association of a team management model based on Timing It Right theory with outcomes after cesarean section.
abstract: To evaluate whether a team management model based on Timing It Right theory was associated with postoperative recovery, breastfeeding outcomes, and readiness for hospital discharge among women undergoing elective cesarean section. This single-center, nonrandomized quasi-experimental study used a sequential (nonconcurrent) control design. Women undergoing elective cesarean section were recruited by convenience sampling. Participants treated from April to June 2023 received routine perioperative clinical pathway management and served as the control group, whereas participants treated from July to September 2023 received the same routine pathway plus a team management intervention based on Timing It Right theory. Outcomes related to postoperative recovery, lactation, breastfeeding self-efficacy, and readiness for hospital discharge were compared between groups at prespecified time points. A total of 97 cases were studied in the 2 groups, including 49 cases in the control group and 48 cases in the intervention group. Comparing the postoperative clinical data of the 2 groups, the number of active steps and the time of the first urination in the intervention group were better than those of the control group in the postoperative period of 24 and 48 hours (P < .05); comparing the postoperative lactation situation of the 2 groups, the amount of lactation in the intervention group was better than that in the control group in the postoperative period of 48 and 72 hours (P < .05), and breastfeeding confidence in the intervention group (126.65 ± 15.894) was better than that of the control group (110.13 ± 17.662), and the difference between the 2 groups was statistically significant (P < .05). In addition, the total discharge readiness score of the intervention group (98.55 ± 12.261) and adaptability dimension (39.65 ± 6.851), anticipatory support dimension (26.06 ± 3.875) were better than that of the control group (82.46 ± 15.276, 33.06 ± 6.166, 20.48 ± 3.968), and the difference between the 2 groups was statistically significant (P < .05). In this single-center, nonrandomized sequentially controlled study, the team management model based on Timing It Right theory was associated with better early postoperative activity, earlier first urination, more favorable lactation status at 48 and 72 hours, higher breastfeeding self-efficacy, and greater readiness for hospital discharge.

title: Indirect ICU Admissions From an Australian Emergency Department: Risk Factors and Outcomes.
Multidisciplinary Perioperative and Post-Acute Care for Older Adults with Hip Fracture and Cognitive Impairment or Dementia: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Hip fracture care becomes more complex when an older adult has cognitive impairment. Pain may be expressed behaviorally, consent and goals of care may require supported decision-making, delirium can be difficult to distinguish from baseline impairment, and rehabilitation must accommodate altered learning and communication. Unlike reviews focused predominantly on individual management domains, this narrative review integrates evidence across the entire care pathway, from emergency assessment and perioperative management to inpatient care, post-acute rehabilitation, and discharge planning, with particular emphasis on how cognitive impairment affects care coordination and continuity. The most consistent priorities are timely surgery after correction of reversible instability, reliable recognition and treatment of pain and delirium, early supported activity, and access to rehabilitation adapted to the person's abilities. Cognitive impairment changes how these elements are delivered; it is not, by itself, a reason to withhold them. Decisions about discharge and longer-term recovery are better anchored in prefracture function, transfer ability, residence, caregiver capacity, and the patient's goals than in a cognitive label alone. In advanced dementia, operative and non-operative management are both active care pathways and require explicit discussion of comfort, transfers, nursing burden, survival, and previously expressed values. Direct evidence is most limited for patients with moderate or severe dementia, who are commonly excluded from trials despite being among those most vulnerable to gaps in care.

title: The intent is good but… exploring barriers and enablers to clinical pathway use in regional Australian Emergency Departments.
journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
abstract: Background Clinical pathways can improve the quality, safety, and efficiency of care, but their integration into routine emergency department (ED) practice remains challenging. Factors influencing pathway use, particularly organizational and contextual determinants, are often overlooked, despite their importance for successful implementation and sustainability. These challenges may be amplified in regional EDs facing workforce and resource constraints. This study examined the barriers and enablers influencing the use of fractured neck of femur (NOF) and suspected stroke pathways in regional Australian EDs to inform service improvement and pathway redesign. Methods A qualitative exploratory study was conducted across regional EDs in Tasmania. The study utilized big picture mapping workshops and semistructured interviews to examine pathway use in real‑world clinical settings. Twenty-five clinicians participated in three multidisciplinary mapping workshops, and 14 clinicians took part in in‑depth interviews. Mapping identified key steps and decision points within fractured NOF and stroke pathways, while interviews explored clinicians' experiences and perceptions. Data were deductively analysed using the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results Mapping revealed common care processes but significant site-level differences, including inconsistent pathway initiation. Interviews revealed that pathway use was influenced by factors across CFIR domains: complexity and workflow misalignment were barriers, with digital integration a valued enabler (Innovation). Time pressures and resource limitations affected pathway use (Outer setting). Leadership buy‑in and champions enabled use (Inner setting). Clinicians expressed concern about diminishing clinical judgement (Individuals domain), while Implementation process domain barriers included limited collaboration. Conclusion Pathway use in Tasmanian EDs is influenced by barriers and enablers across CFIR domains. Simplifying pathways and ensuring adaptability were perceived to improve usability, while misaligned workflows and paper-based processes hinder uptake. Addressing resource constraints, fostering leadership engagement, and strengthening education are essential. Embedding planning, collaboration, and feedback will ensure pathways remain practical, evidence-based, and deliver timely, standardized care.

title: When intact mucosa hides a malignancy: solid-type primary intraosseous carcinoma (PIOC, NOS) of the mandible: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Introduction Primary intraosseous carcinoma, not otherwise specified (PIOC, NOS) is a rare odontogenic carcinoma that arises within the jawbone from odontogenic epithelial remnants, with no initial connection to the oral mucosa. Its non-specific clinical and radiographic features overlap with benign odontogenic and inflammatory lesions, so diagnosis is often delayed and rests on histopathology. The 2017 and 2022 World Health Organization (WHO) classifications recognize PIOC, NOS without formal subtypes; earlier schemes described a solid ( de novo ) type arising without a cystic or tumorous precursor. Case A 53-year-old man with no tobacco or alcohol history presented with painful right mandibular and cheek swelling, purulent discharge through a cutaneous fistula and mobile right mandibular molars, persisting despite management as an odontogenic abscess. The oral mucosa was intact and there was no sensory disturbance. Cone-beam computed tomography showed a destructive radiolucent lesion from the right mandibular first molar to an impacted third molar, with buccolingual expansion, cortical thinning and probable lingual perforation. After extraction of the molars, incisional biopsy showed invasive well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with keratin pearls and bone trabeculae encased by tumor nests, without a cystic or odontogenic tumor component. Staging CT identified no suspicious primary tumor within the imaged regions. The diagnosis was PIOC, NOS under WHO 2022; the tumor was well differentiated (Grade I) and corresponded to the historically described solid ( de novo ) type. Segmental mandibulectomy with right neck dissection revealed a 7-cm tumor with perineural and lymphovascular invasion and four positive level I lymph nodes; margins were clear. Postoperative radiotherapy (40 Gy in 20 fractions) with concurrent cisplatin followed. In August 2026, CT showed an operative-bed mass suspicious for locoregional recurrence, and paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy began in September 2026. Conclusion Solid-type PIOC, NOS can mimic benign odontogenic and inflammatory lesions beneath an intact mucosa. A destructive jaw lesion that fails to respond to treatment for infection should be biopsied without delay. Keratin pearls, infiltrative epithelial nests and bone invasion without mucosal continuity are decisive for diagnosis, and the nodal metastasis and suspected recurrence in this case underline the need for continued oncologic surveillance.

title: Repeat Hospitalizations and Their Costs in the 6 Months After Acute Myocarditis
Outcome-specific risk factors for dehydration and acute kidney injury readmission after ileostomy: A US National Cohort Study, 2016-2022.
journal: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
abstract: Aim Single-centre pathways have reduced dehydration and acute kidney injury (AKI)-specific readmission after ileostomy from 17%-28% to single-digit rates, but whether these gains translated nationally is unknown. We examined how discharge destination relates to outcome-specific readmission, quantified 30-day readmission rates and encounter costs from 2016 to 2022 and identified risk factors at the population level. Method Retrospective cohort study using the United States Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD, 2016-2022). Adults undergoing ileostomy creation were included. The primary outcome was 30-day readmission for dehydration or AKI. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified risk factors for composite readmission, with home-discharge effects compared between dehydration- and AKI-specific outcomes.
