Relevance to clinical practice Findings are similar to other studies within the sub-Saharan region and highlight the need to strengthen workforce training, particularly in critical and paediatric care, improve access to essential equipment and standardise care protocols to enhance patient safety and outcomes. The study demonstrates the importance of strengthening the multidisciplinary critical care workforce.

title: Effectiveness of a multicomponent PDCA-based infusion safety management strategy in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis: a non-randomized historical-control study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between a multicomponent PDCA-based infusion safety management strategy and intraoperative peripheral intravenous (PIV) outcomes in adults with pulmonary tuberculosis. Methods This non-randomized historical-control study included 92 adults undergoing thoracic surgery: 46 historical controls receiving routine infusion management and 46 patients receiving a multicomponent intervention integrating PDCA-based quality improvement, staff training, standardized protocols, interdepartmental collaboration, audit and feedback, and two auxiliary devices. Baseline demographic and surgical characteristics were comparable between groups. Results Compared with historical controls, the intervention group had lower rates of erythema/tenderness [8.7% vs. 69.6%; RR, 0.13 (95% CI, 0.05-0.33)], catheter dislodgement [2.2% vs. 28.3%; RR, 0.08 (95% CI, 0.01-0.56)], and catheter occlusion [4.3% vs. 43.5%; RR, 0.10 (95% CI, 0.02-0.40); all P ≤ 0.001]. Catheter dwell time was longer [5.0 vs. 3.0 days; Hodges-Lehmann difference, +2.0 days (95% CI, 1.0-2.0)], whereas hospital stay was shorter [11.0 vs. 19.0 days; difference, -7.0 days (95% CI, -10.0 to -5.0)]. Satisfaction scores were also higher [95.0 vs. 91.5; difference, +3.0 points (95% CI, 2.0-4.0); all P Conclusion The multicomponent PDCA-based strategy was associated with fewer PIV-related safety events, longer catheter dwell time, and higher satisfaction. However, because the intervention combined process changes with two devices and used a historical control, the observed differences cannot be attributed independently to PDCA or either device.

title: How Multidisciplinary Teams Are Reshaping Adult IBD Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Current guidelines strongly endorse integrated multidisciplinary team (MDT) approaches to manage the complexity of patients with IBD. Evidence from formal multidisciplinary case discussions suggests an impact on diagnostic and treatment decisions, while studies of broader integrated IBD services report associations with improved disease control, quality of life, and healthcare utilization. However, implementation remains heterogeneous across centers, with variability in team composition, meeting frequency, referral criteria, and access to specialist services. Future directions include standardization of MDT composition and processes, definition of quality indicators, extension of specialist expertise through hub-and-spoke networks and telemedicine, and integration of patients as active partners in care. Digital tools may support communication and remote follow-up, whereas the role of artificial intelligence in MDT decision-making remains investigational and requires clinical validation. Multidisciplinary care should be regarded as a core organizational principle of modern IBD management. Realizing its full potential will require sustained investment, workforce planning, and prospective research to ensure equitable, high-quality, and sustainable care across diverse healthcare settings.

title: Home-based rehabilitation after hip or knee arthroplasty among rural older adults in China: a qualitative study.
abstract: Background Older adults in rural China may face difficulties accessing continuous and professional rehabilitation after hip or knee replacement. This study explored their experiences of home-based rehabilitation, focusing on barriers, coping strategies, and healthcare support gaps. Method A descriptive phenomenological study was conducted from January to March 2025 in the orthopaedic outpatient clinics of two tertiary hospitals in Nantong, China. Twenty-one rural adults aged 60 years or older who had undergone primary hip or knee replacement within the previous 6 months were recruited using maximum variation sampling. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were conducted, and data were analysed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Results Three themes and nine subthemes were identified: (1) Challenges in Physical Rehabilitation: Pain, Functional Limitations, and Exercise Adaptations, including The Helplessness and Grassroots Wisdom in Pain Management, Adaptations and Misunderstandings of Prescribed Exercises, and Loss of Daily Function and Role Changes; (2) Limited Family and Community Support, including Emotional Debt in Familial Care, Limited Rehabilitation Capacity in Village Clinics, and Reluctance to Seek Neighbor Support; and (3) Negotiating Traditional Beliefs and Modern Rehabilitation, including Barriers to Formal Rehabilitation and Reliance on Traditional Remedies, Views on Aging and Prioritizing Family Needs, and Folk Beliefs and Medical Advice. These findings showed that participants' rehabilitation experiences were shaped by physical limitations, discontinuity of family and community support, and the interaction between traditional beliefs and modern rehabilitation practices. Conclusion Home-based rehabilitation after hip or knee replacement among rural older adults is shaped by physical, family, cultural, and service-related factors. Potential approaches include accessible rehabilitation materials, structured follow-up, caregiver support, and stronger coordination between tertiary hospitals and rural primary care services; however, their feasibility and effectiveness require further evaluation.

title: Respiratory effort during sleep predicts mortality in patients with suspected obstructive sleep apnea.
journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
abstract: Rationale Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) confers increased risk of morbidity and mortality through mechanisms like exaggerated negative intrathoracic pressure and hypoxemia. Objectives Evaluate the association between negative esophageal pressure (PES; a surrogate of respiratory effort) during sleep and long-term all-cause mortality in suspected OSA patients. Methods Patients referred with suspected OSA (2003-2016) underwent overnight respiratory polygraphy with PES monitoring. PES, mean oxygen saturation (mSpO2), apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), total time in bed (TiB), and time in bed spent above different PES thresholds (10-60 cmH2O) were recorded. Clinical data and mortality until June 2024 were obtained from medical records. Mortality was analyzed using multivariable Cox regression. Results In 16 083 patients (26% female; median age 48 years), median PES was 12.8 cmH2O (IQR 8.7-18.4). Median mSpO2 was 94% (93%-95%), and median AHI was 10 (4.3-21.1); 16% had AHI ≥ 30. During median follow-up of 15 years (IQR 12-18), 1497 (9.3%) died. Patients in the third and fourth quartiles of median PES had increased mortality risk compared to the first quartile. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), comorbidities, AHI, and mSpO2, median PES remained associated with mortality, with the third quartile showing increased risk (hazard ratio [HR] 1.21; 95% CI, 1.03-1.43; P = .024). Longer time spent above higher PES thresholds was associated with increased mortality. Risk rose across quartiles of percentage of TiB at each threshold and increased further with more negative thresholds in the highest quartile. Conclusion Respiratory effort, measured by PES during sleep, independently predicts all-cause mortality, and provides prognostic information beyond traditional OSA metrics including AHI and hypoxemia. This supports respiratory effort as a useful component of comprehensive clinical evaluation.

title: Transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker in a 97-year-old patient with severe kyphosis and tortuous femoral veins: a case report.
abstract: Background Leadless pacemaker systems offer significant benefits for frail older adults by avoiding pocket- and lead-related complications. However, anatomical challenges including severe spinal deformities and significant venous tortuosity can complicate conventional transfemoral or trans-subclavian implantation. Case report A 97-year-old man with severe kyphosis, tortuous femoral veins, and high-grade atrioventricular block was referred for permanent pacing. Supine positioning for subclavian access was not feasible, and the femoral anatomy posed an unacceptably high procedural risk. Following a multidisciplinary assessment and procedural planning, a transjugular approach was selected. Implantation was performed with the patient in the left lateral decubitus position, using adapted fluoroscopic projections and temporary femoral pacing as backup. An Aveir ventricular response leadless pacemaker was successfully delivered via the right internal jugular vein. Final device parameters were satisfactory, with a sensing amplitude of 8.5 mV, a pacing threshold of 0.5 V at 0.4 ms, and an impedance of 510 Ω. No perioperative complications occurred. At follow-up, exertional dyspnea had resolved, and device performance remained stable. Conclusion This case demonstrates that transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker can be a safe and feasible alternative for older adults with complex anatomical limitations that contraindicate standard pacing approaches. Careful preprocedural assessment and adaptation of intraoperative techniques are essential for procedural success in high-risk settings.

title: Clinical Recovery Following Conservative Management of a Large Presumed Brain Abscess with a Concomitant <i>Streptococcus intermedius</i> Lung Abscess in a Severely Malnourished Young Adult in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Brain abscess is a life-threatening condition requiring prompt antimicrobial therapy and, when feasible, neurosurgical drainage. Management can be particularly challenging in resource-limited settings where neurosurgical intervention, microbiological confirmation, and follow-up imaging may be unavailable. We report a case of a large presumed brain abscess occurring concurrently with a Streptococcus intermedius lung abscess in a severely malnourished young adult managed in a resource-limited setting. Case presentation A 22-year-old Eritrean man presented with one week of progressive left-sided weakness preceded by four weeks of productive cough, fever, and weight loss. He was severely malnourished (BMI 14 kg/m 2 ), febrile, and had impaired consciousness with flaccid left hemiplegia. Non-contrast CT and MRI showed a 4 × 3 cm right parietal intracranial lesion with surrounding edema and moderate midline shift, presumed to represent a brain abscess. Chest imaging revealed a right lower-lobe lung abscess, from which Streptococcus intermedius was isolated; blood cultures were negative and echocardiography was normal. Neurosurgical drainage was unavailable. He was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole with supportive and nutritional care. His GCS improved from 10/15 to 15/15 within three days, and he regained independent ambulation by four weeks. He completed four weeks of intravenous antibiotics and was discharged clinically stable with oral antibiotics to complete seven weeks of antibiotics. No follow-up neuroimaging was available, but he remained clinically well during three years of telephone follow-up. Conclusion This case illustrates the challenges of managing a large presumed brain abscess when neurosurgical drainage and follow-up neuroimaging are unavailable. Despite the absence of microbiological confirmation from the brain lesion, the patient achieved sustained clinical and neurological recovery following prolonged antimicrobial and supportive treatment. The case emphasizes diagnostic vigilance and resource-adapted care while recognizing that clinical recovery does not establish radiological resolution or replace standard neurosurgical management when feasible.

title: A Retrospective Study Analysing the Outcomes of Anxiety, Depression, and Sleep Disorders in Post-Chemotherapy Patients With Breast Cancer Based on Symptom-Targeted Supportive Psychological Nursing.
abstract: Background To analyse the differences in supportive psychological nursing care received by patients with breast cancer during and after chemotherapy. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted, selecting 152 patients with breast cancer who received standardised chemotherapy and completed follow-up at our hospital between April 2022 and April 2025. Patients were divided into a supportive care group (n = 76) and a routine care group (n = 76) based on differences in supportive psychological nursing care in their medical records and nursing documentation. The levels of depression, anxiety, psychological distress and sleep quality after chemotherapy were then compared between the two groups. Results Depression and anxiety levels in the supportive care group were lower than those in the routine care group ( p p p Conclusions Supportive psychological nursing care was associated with improved depression and anxiety in patients with breast cancer after chemotherapy.

title: Association of early neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio trajectories with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) is characterized by potentially reversible myocardial dysfunction accompanied by a profound systemic inflammatory response. However, the prognostic significance of early dynamic changes in the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with SIC remains unclear. This study aimed to identify distinct early NLR trajectories and examine their associations with cardiac recovery and live discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with SIC admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Hebei Cangzhou Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine. NLR values were collected at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h thereafter. Latent class mixed modeling was used to identify distinct 72-h NLR trajectories. A 72-h landmark design was applied. The primary outcome was live ICU discharge within 28 days, with ICU death treated as a competing event and analyzed using Fine-Gray regression. The secondary outcome was cardiac recovery by days 5-7, defined as a follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥50% or an absolute increase of ≥10 percentage points from baseline. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery. Results A total of 510 patients contributed 2,040 longitudinal NLR measurements. Three distinct trajectories were identified: low-stable ( n = 230, 45.1%), high-decreasing ( n = 170, 33.3%), and persistent-high ( n = 110, 21.6%). The geometric mean NLR changed from 7.85 to 6.16, from 18.47 to 8.01, and from 14.95 to 22.87, respectively, during the first 72 h. Live ICU discharge occurred in 85.7%, 67.1%, and 36.4% of patients in the three groups, respectively. Compared with the low-stable group, the adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios for live ICU discharge were 0.49 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.38-0.63; P P P = 0.004) and 0.27 (95% CI, 0.14-0.51; P Conclusions Early 72-h NLR trajectories were independently associated with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with SIC. A persistent-high trajectory identified patients with the poorest prognosis, whereas a high-decreasing trajectory was associated with intermediate outcomes. Serial assessment of NLR may provide a simple and clinically accessible tool for early risk stratification in SIC, although prospective external validation is warranted.

title: Burden of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) on Severe Acute Respiratory Infection and Projected Cost Offsets of Implementing a Regional Adult RSV Vaccination Programme.
abstract: Objective: RSV is a significant contributor to severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) admissions. Despite national recommendations for RSV vaccination in Ireland, they have not been implemented due to cost concerns and evidence gaps. We assessed RSV-SARI tertiary healthcare engagement to determine healthcare utilisation costs and potential savings in patients following RSV vaccination. Methods: RSV SARI admissions over two winter seasons (2024/25 and 2025/26) at a tertiary centre in Ireland were assessed. Sociodemographic and disease-specific variables were recorded, and their relationship with outcomes investigated. Potential cost offsets which may present following a successful RSV vaccination campaign were calculated. Results: There were 168 RSV admissions during the study (54% aged ≥75). Median length of stay was 6 days and was significantly longer in patients aged ≥75. Having a chronic neurological disease was associated with increased length of stay. The 90-day readmission rate was 24%. Vaccinating ≥75-year-olds in the hospital catchment area would cost €3,712,500, while predicted admission avoidance post-vaccination would save €1,197,692, or €111.77 per vaccine administered. Vaccine costs of €49 would be cost-neutral at the hospital level. Conclusions: RSV disproportionately affects patients ≥75 years of age. Projected vaccine cost offsets in this population are substantially different from those previously used to inform national policy.

title: Sustained Clearance of Candida auris Colonisation After Hospital Discharge: A Community Follow‐Up Cohort Study
Safety and Cost-Analysis of Same-Day Versus Next-Day Discharge Following Complex Ablation Procedures: A Single-Centre Observational Study.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
abstract: (1) Introduction and objectives: The most common practice after a complex ablation procedure (CAP) is next-day discharge (NDD) following an appropriate observation period. However, the use of same-day discharge (SDD) has increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic. We aimed to evaluate the safety and cost-analysis of an SDD strategy for patients undergoing CAP. (2) Methods: This was a single-centre, retrospective observational study of patients undergoing CAP between January 2021 and July 2024, with intracardiac echocardiography used in all procedures. (3) Results: A total of 250 CAPs were performed, with a complication rate of 20.4% in the initial cohort. Forty-five patients were excluded, mainly because of significant procedural complications or severe pre-ablation medical conditions. The final analysis included 205 patients: 70 in the SDD group and 135 in the NDD group. Multiple patient and procedural characteristics were evaluated and compared between the groups. Among patients included in the final analysis, the overall complication rate was low (8.8%), with no differences between groups (early minor complications, 5.4%: 8.6% vs. 3.7% for SDD vs. NDD, p = 0.191; late major complications, 0.5%: 0% vs. 0.7%, p = 1; late minor complications, 3.4%: 2.9% vs. 3.7%, p = 1). There were five deaths (2.4%), none of which were procedure related. The SDD policy for CAP during this period would have saved €479.84 ± €248.09 per patient. (4) Conclusions: An SDD strategy was feasible and cost-saving and seemed to not increase periprocedural complications compared with an NDD strategy.

title: Mitigating climate-related health risks in Lebanon: implementation of national standards for climate-ready hospitals.
journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
abstract: Background Climate change increasingly disrupts healthcare systems worldwide by simultaneously increasing service demand and undermining infrastructure reliability. Hospitals face escalating risks from extreme weather, energy insecurity, and water scarcity, while contributing nearly 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. These challenges are particularly acute in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, where fragile health systems and resource constraints heighten vulnerability. Lebanon's health sector exemplifies this intersection of climate risk and systemic fragility. This study aimed to develop nationally tailored standards for climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable healthcare facilities in Lebanon, translating international climate-health frameworks into actionable, context-specific guidance aligned with national legal and operational realities. Methods A multiphase methodology was applied, including a scoping review of international standards and guidance (WHO, ISO 14001, ISO 9001, ISO 26000), structured consultations with key national and international stakeholders, and synthesis of draft standards into thematic areas. Clauses were aligned with existing Lebanese environmental and health legislation to ensure compliance and to prioritize urgent mandatory actions over longer-term strategic actions. Results The resulting standards comprise 10 thematic areas covering governance, environmental management, climate emergency preparedness, community engagement, sustainable procurement, and performance monitoring. Legal screening enabled phased implementation, distinguishing urgent compliance-driven actions from longer-term strategic enhancements. Implementation assessment demonstrated that the standards could guide gap identification, cost estimation, and prioritization of climate-resilience investments at facility level. Conclusion Climate-resilient healthcare standards for Lebanon provide a practical framework for strengthening service continuity during climate shocks while reducing the sector's carbon footprint. Institutionalization and MoPH-led enforcement will be essential for long-term uptake.

title: Sustainability and Integrated Energy Recovery Scheme for Health Care Waste Management for Megacity Dhaka: Through Material Flow and Life Cycle Assessment.
abstract: A sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management strategy for Dhaka integrating material flow analysis and comparative life cycle assessment is proposed. The current scenario (SC1), heavily reliant on landfilling, low recycling, and incineration without energy integration, is compared with the proposed alternative scenario (SC2), with higher material recycling, waste-to-energy conversion, and heat integration. Using gate-to-grave life-cycle assessment across eighteen ReCiPe 2016 midpoint (H) impact categories, the proposed SC2 outperforms SC1 in ten categories, notably acidification potential by 96%, land-use potential by 97%, climate change impacts by 78%, and marine eutrophication by 44%, while PM formation potential falls by 20.499 kg PM 2.5 -eq and energy resource depletion becomes a net credit through 20572 kWh/day of recovered electricity. However, trade-offs are observed in the toxicity, eutrophication, and photochemical oxidant formation categories, notably carcinogenic human toxicity (∼3.8x increase), marine ecotoxicity (∼2.3x increase), freshwater eutrophication (∼97% increase), and photochemical oxidant formation potential (∼3x increase). The proposed scheme also supports Bangladesh's drive toward SDG 7 and 13 outright, and toward SDG 3, 6, 11, and 14 once the toxicity and oxidant formation burdens are controlled. Our findings can provide a substantial quantitative framework for improving existing systems to achieve sustainability with a circular economy strategy.

title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
abstract: Background Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk. Aim The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups. Study design This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC). Results This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons. Conclusions Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes. Relevance to clinical practice Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

title: A Doubly Robust Approach to Evaluating the Impact of Hospital Length of Stay on Post‐Fracture Recovery in Older Adults With Cognitive Impairment
Identifying Frailty and Its Associated Factors Among Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury in Vietnam.
abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of long-term disability and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where post-discharge rehabilitation services are often limited. Frailty is a multidimensional construct encompassing physical, cognitive, psychological, and social vulnerability. After TBI, multidimensional frailty may overlap with disability, depressive symptoms, persistent neurological problems, and social vulnerability. However, little is known about Groningen Frailty Indicator (GFI)-defined frailty among adults after hospital discharge for TBI in resource-limited settings. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 212 adult patients discharged after TBI from Thai Binh General Hospital, Vietnam. Data were collected via structured telephone interviews during a study period extending from January to August 2020. Frailty was measured using the GFI and operationally defined as a score of ≥ 4. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with GFI-defined frailty status. Results The prevalence of GFI-defined frailty was 36.8%, despite the majority (93.9%) having mild TBI. In the adjusted logistic model, female sex was associated with lower odds of GFI-defined frailty than male sex (aOR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15-0.87), and rural residence was associated with lower odds than urban residence (aOR = 0.24; 95% CI: 0.09-0.66). Current smoking (aOR = 2.80; 95% CI: 1.10-7.14), post-injury sequelae (aOR = 2.39; 95% CI: 1.15-4.98), depressive symptoms (aOR = 3.24; 95% CI: 1.23-8.54), and friend-group support (aOR = 1.58; 95% CI: 1.07-2.34) were associated with higher odds of GFI-defined frailty. Overall, 33.0% of participants reported post-injury sequelae, and 10.2% experienced catastrophic health expenditure. Friend-group support was positively associated with frailty, suggesting that higher reported support from friends may reflect greater support needs among frail patients after discharge rather than a harmful effect of social support. Conclusions GFI-defined frailty was common among reachable adults discharged after TBI from this single hospital. The identified relationships are cross-sectional associations and may partly reflect overlap between frailty, functional limitation, psychological burden, and social-support needs. Post-discharge follow-up should consider functional, psychological, social, occupational, and financial vulnerability in addition to neurological symptoms. Multicenter longitudinal studies incorporating pre-injury status and rehabilitation exposure are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Palliative Care Involvement in Relation to Rapid Response Events: A Focus on Care Intensity at the End of Life.
abstract: Objectives To examine current practice patterns of palliative care involvement in relation to rapid response (RR) events and to evaluate its association with ICU utilization and intensity of care received before death. Design Retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent a RR event. Setting General medical, cardiology, oncology, and observation patients admitted to a tertiary care academic medical center in the United States. Patients Adults (≥ 18 yr) with an RR event. Interventions None. Measurements and main results A total of 903 RR events occurred in 616 unique patients. The palliative care team was involved in 110 of 616 (17.9%) patients. Palliative care (PC) involvement was not associated with differences in repeat RR events or ICU transfer rates following an event. In-hospital mortality or hospice discharge occurred in 32.0% (197/616). Palliative care was involved in 36.5% (72/197) of these patients. PC involvement was associated with lower intensity of care within 24 hours before death after adjustment for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, pre-RR code status, and RR trigger (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.26; 95% CI, 0.14-0.47; p Conclusions Palliative services may be underutilized in the RR patient population, a group with a high in-hospital mortality rate; when palliative care is consulted, it may be associated with a reduction in the intensity of interventions at the end of life.

title: Mapping the symptom management journey across the treatment cycle for breast cancer patients: A qualitative study.
abstract: The aim of this study is to identify the multidimensional needs of breast cancer patients in symptom management using a patient journey map, providing an evidence-based foundation for optimizing nursing interventions. This descriptive qualitative study recruited 15 breast cancer patients from a tertiary hospital in Hefei for semi-structured interviews between January and August 2024. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's 7-step method to construct a comprehensive journey map. The symptom management journey comprised 3 phases: screening and diagnosis, the perioperative period, and the ongoing treatment phase. Twenty-two themes were categorized into tasks, emotions, and pain points. Tasks included symptom detection and rehabilitation; emotions encompassed generalized anxiety and stigma; and pain points highlighted barriers like symptom misinterpretation and the risk of loss to follow-up. The map visually illustrated the dynamic evolution of patient needs. The findings highlight distinct stage-specific patterns in patients' needs and barriers during symptom management. The patient journey map serves as a structured framework for identifying key intervention nodes and supporting more targeted, stage-oriented nursing care.

title: Epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of infective endocarditis over a decade in a tertiary care hospital in Oman.
abstract: Objectives Infective endocarditis (IE) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, although data from Oman and the Gulf region are limited. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, microbiological profile, and in-hospital outcomes of definite IE in a tertiary care hospital in Oman. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients admitted between 2006 and 2016. Cases were identified from electronic medical records using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification code I33.0. The modified Duke criteria were applied retrospectively and only definite IE cases were included. Results Among 172 screened patients, 130 (75.6%) met the criteria for definite IE. The mean age was 42.3 years, and the median symptom duration before diagnosis was 14 days. Native valve IE occurred in 113 (87.0%) patients and prosthetic valve IE occurred in 17 (13.0%). Staphylococcus species were the most commonly isolated pathogens (43.1%), among which Staphylococcus aureus accounted for 38.5%. In-hospital mortality was 31.5%, and mortality was lower in patients who underwent surgery than in those who did not (18.0% vs 40.0%; P = 0.011). Conclusion In this Omani cohort, IE affected a relatively young population and was characterized by predominant S. aureus infection and high in-hospital mortality. These findings support context-specific empiric therapy, early echocardiographic evaluation, and timely surgical assessment.

title: Recovery experiences and perceptions of quality of life after percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction: An interpretive descriptive qualitative study.
abstract: Background Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is the standard treatment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction, a life-threatening acute coronary syndrome requiring urgent revascularization. Despite increasing access to this intervention in sub-Saharan Africa, evidence on patients' lived experiences of recovery remains limited. This study explored patients' experiences of recovery and quality of life following primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction in Tanzania. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed. Fourteen patients who had undergone primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction were purposively sampled at a national referral cardiac centre and interviewed within three months after PCI. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Participants perceived quality of life after PCI as an evolving experience closely linked to their recovery, with improvements in one aspect often accompanied by ongoing challenges in others. Six interrelated themes emerged: physical symptoms, functional capacity and daily activities, emotional responses, coping and illness perceptions, social support and relationships, and health system interactions and communication. Although participants generally reported symptom improvement and gradual functional recovery, persistent fatigue, activity limitations, emotional uncertainty, and unmet informational needs continued to influence their quality of life. Family support and adaptive coping helped participants adjust to life after PCI, while healthcare communication shaped their confidence in managing recovery. Conclusion Recovery after primary percutaneous coronary intervention extends beyond survival to include physical, emotional, and social dimensions. Holistic, patient-centred post-intervention care is needed to support long-term recovery in resource-limited settings.

title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
abstract: Aims Hip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture. Methods This multicentre prospective randomized trial compares transfusion strategies after hip fracture in patients aged ≥ 60 years. We initially planned to randomize 1,984 participants with anaemia, defined as haemoglobin ≤ 90 g l -1 , to one of two transfusion strategies: liberal transfusion (aim haemoglobin 90 g l -1 to 110 g l -1 ), or restrictive transfusion (aim 75 g l -1 to 90 g l -1 ). The intervention lasts from randomization to hospital discharge or 30 days post randomization, whichever is soonest. The primary outcome measure was a composite of death or MACE adjudicated by blinded clinical experts. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and quality of life, evaluated at 120 days. Cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation will also be reported. Results This trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, HTA award (National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) 130875) and registered at ISRCTN 28818784. Ethical approval was obtained to recruit patients in the UK. As recruitment fell short of the initial target, and following consultation with the funder, we refined our primary outcome to include myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS), and reduced the required sample size to 842. Conclusion Recruitment commenced on 10 June 2022. The first participant was recruited on 16 June 2022. We will engage clinicians and healthcare planners to implement the findings. We plan to recruit until 31 October 2026. Results will be disseminated to clinicians, policymakers, patients, and the public.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Electronic Medical Record-Based Machine Learning Model for Frailty Prediction in Hospitalized Patients: Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Frailty is prevalent among hospitalized patients and is associated with increased risk of complications, prolonged hospitalization, higher mortality, and health care costs. Existing frailty screening tools, including the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) and Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), have limitations related to subjectivity, resource intensity, or reliance on retrospective data, limiting their use in routine acute care. Early identification of frailty is critical to support targeted interventions and resource allocation, yet scalable approaches for predicting frailty early during hospital admission remain limited. Objective This paper evaluates whether routinely collected electronic medical record (EMR) data available within the first 72 hours of admission can be used to predict frailty in hospitalized patients. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using routinely collected EMR data from the Royal Adelaide Hospital (RAH), including overnight admissions with a length of stay of at least 72 hours between July 2023 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the HFRS (score >4). Predictors were derived from EMR data available within 72 hours of admission, including demographics, medications, laboratory results, nursing assessments, and medical and allied health consult orders. Data were split into training (21,436/26,824, 80%) and test (5388/26,824, 20%) sets. Multiple machine learning models were trained, with the F 2 -score as the primary optimization metric. Model performance was evaluated using the F 2 -score, recall, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, and clinical utility analyses. Results This study included 26,824 admissions, of whom 9427 (35%) were classified as frail. The final XGBoost (XGB) model achieved an F 2 -score of 0.755 (95% CI 0.741-0.768), an AUROC of 0.777 (95% CI 0.764-0.790), and a recall of 0.873 (95% CI 0.857-0.887) on the test dataset, with good calibration and an expected-to-observed ratio close to 1 (0.996, 95% CI 0.963-1.028). Key predictors included polypharmacy, laboratory results (including creatinine, albumin, and sodium), allied health consult orders, and nursing assessment data. Model performance was lower at 24 hours postadmission and improved by discharge. Conclusions An EMR-based frailty prediction model using data available at 72 hours postadmission can identify patients with frailty early in their hospital stay, supporting targeted interventions and operational planning. Reduced performance in Indigenous patients highlights the need for culturally validated frailty indices and ongoing evaluation of equity in predictive modeling.

title: Factors Associated With In-Hospital Mortality and Length of Stay Among Hospitalised Patients Receiving Carbapenem Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Patients receiving carbapenems are clinically heterogeneous and have severe infections and multiple comorbidities. Evidence on factors associated with mortality and length of stay (LOS) in this treatment-defined population remains limited. Methods This retrospective cohort study included adult hospital episodes involving at least one carbapenem dose at Hospital Shah Alam during 2025. Firth penalised logistic regression was used for in-hospital mortality, and median regression with 2000 bootstrap resamples was used for right-skewed LOS. Covariates were selected a priori. Carbapenem continuation beyond 72 h was treated as a postbaseline characteristic and was not included in outcome models. Results Among 112 eligible episodes involving 107 patients, 38 deaths occurred (33.9%); median LOS was 19.0 days (IQR: 10.8-28.0). Older age (adjusted OR: 1.41 per 10 years, 95% CI: 1.07-1.92) and definitive indication at carbapenem initiation (adjusted OR: 0.28, 95% CI: 0.10-0.70) were associated with in-hospital mortality. Hospital-acquired infection was associated with a longer adjusted median LOS (median difference 8.63 days, 95% bootstrap CI: 0.50-14.44). Definitive indication was not clearly associated with LOS after adjustment (median difference -5.54 days, 95% bootstrap CI: -12.00-4.62). Conclusions Older age and definitive indication at carbapenem initiation were associated with in-hospital mortality, while hospital-acquired infection was associated with longer median LOS. The treatment-indication association should not be interpreted causally because residual confounding, particularly by acute illness severity and indication, remains likely.

title: The surgical symphony of human efficiency: a structured intraoperative workflow model for high-volume cochlear implant missions.
abstract: Objective High-volume humanitarian Cochlear Implant (CI) missions require highly organized workflows to maintain efficiency and safety. This study describes the intraoperative model used during a large-scale CI campaign. Methods A descriptive observational design was used to evaluate operative workflow across multiple operating rooms using standardized surgical protocols, structured shift-based assignments, and digital coordination. Operative times, intraoperative findings, ECAP responses, and postoperative radiologic outcomes were analyzed. Results A total of 142 CI surgeries were completed over three days (30-, 66-, and 46-cases). The mean operative time was 57-minutes, with a median of 46-minutes. Unremarkable intraoperative fields were observed in 57.4% of cases, while perilymph oozing occurred in 31.2%. Absent ECAP responses occurred in three patients (2.1%) with inner ear malformations; all demonstrated responses during postoperative fitting. Radiologic assessment confirmed proper intracochlear insertion in all candidates. Conclusion A structured intraoperative workflow enabled the safe and efficient completion of a high surgical volume within a short timeframe. This experience offers practical guidance for centers aiming to enhance operating room efficiency, particularly in high-volume or resource-limited environments. Level of evidence IV.

title: Impact of live music therapy compared with storytelling on maternal depression and psychological distress in mothers of preterm infants: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Introduction Music therapy in neonatology is becoming increasingly important and is now considered an evidence-based intervention that effectively complements standard medical care for preterm infants and their mothers in accordance with family-centered care. This study aimed to compare the effects of live-performed music therapy (MT) and storytelling (ST) in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) on psychological distress and depression among mothers of preterm infants. Methods The study was conducted as a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial (RCT), enrolling 60 preterm infants born between 32+0 to 36+6 weeks of gestation. Infants were block-randomized 1:1 to receive either MT or ST. Both interventions were delivered live to the preterm infants three to four times per week from birth until hospital discharge from hospital. The degree of depressive symptoms, anxiety and acute stress reactions of their mothers were measured using the German version of the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) and the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (IES-R). Assessments were conducted on the first day of delivery prior to randomization (Timepoint 1 [T1]), at infants discharge from hospital (Timepoint 2 [T2]) and around the infants' first birthday (Timepoint 3 [T3]). Results The infants of 30 mothers [mean age 33.8 ± 6.1 years (range 21-47)] received MT and the infants of an additional 30 mothers [mean age 32.9 ± 5.3 years (range 21-45)] received ST. A total of 552 sessions were conducted, including 303 live music therapy sessions with a mean duration of 24 ± 2.5 minutes and 249 live storytelling sessions with a mean duration of 23 ± 4.1 minutes. Mothers whose infants received music therapy demonstrated greater reductions of depressive and stress symptoms between T1 and T2 compared to mothers whose infants received storytelling (MT: CES-D mean difference in total score -22.4, IES-R mean difference of total score -3.9; ST: mean difference in CES-D total score -10.7, mean difference of IES-R total score -1.1). Effect sizes (Cohen's d) for the differences between T1 and T2 were large for total CES-D (1.0) and total IES-R (1.5), but weak for the differences between T1 and T3 (total CES-D 0.4, total IES-R 0.4). The absolute values at T3 did not differ as much as those at T2 between the two groups, but remained slightly more favorable in mothers whose infants received MT (mean total CES-D 6.7, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 5.9-7.6; mean total IES-R -1.8, 95% CI -2.2-(-1.4)) than in mothers whose infants received ST (mean total CES-D 10.8, 95% CI 9.1-12.4; mean total IES-R -1.7, 95% CI -1.9-(-1.2)). Discussion These findings indicate that mothers of preterm infants may benefit from music therapy as a supportive, non-medical intervention in alleviating psychological symptoms and distress during their infants' NICU stay and may continue to support maternal well-being in the longer term, up to the infants' first birthday.

title: Therapeutic Exercise Protocol During Hospitalization in Pediatric Oncohematological Patients: Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy
abstract: Background Leukemias, lymphomas, and central nervous system tumors are among the most common pediatric cancers and may lead to motor deficits, impaired balance, reduced muscle strength, fatigue, and decreased functional capacity. Early physiotherapy during hospitalization may help prevent inactivity and support functional preservation in this population. Objective To evaluate the effects of a therapeutic exercise program on quality of life, muscle strength, fatigue, and functional capacity in hospitalized pediatric oncohematological patients. Methods Thirty participants aged 8-17 years with oncohematological diseases were randomized to an intervention group (IG) or a minimal active physiotherapy comparator group (CG). Assessments included the 6-min walk test, handgrip dynamometry, the PedsQL Multidimensional Fatigue Scale, and the PedsQL Cancer Module at admission and discharge. The IG performed daily 25-min supervised sessions including aerobic, resistance, and breathing exercises with ambulation guidance, whereas the CG received breathing exercises and ambulation guidance. Results No significant group × time interactions were observed for total fatigue or its domains, overall quality of life or its assessed domains, handgrip strength, or six-minute walk test distance. Time-related changes were observed for some outcomes, but these occurred without evidence of differential change between groups and were not interpreted as effects of the structured exercise protocol. No intervention-related adverse events requiring permanent protocol discontinuation were recorded. Conclusion The structured in-hospital therapeutic exercise protocol could be delivered under close clinical supervision without recorded intervention-related adverse events requiring permanent discontinuation. However, the structured protocol did not demonstrate superiority over the minimal active physiotherapy comparator for fatigue, quality of life, muscle strength, or functional capacity. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, clinical heterogeneity, variable intervention exposure, and limited intervention-fidelity data. Trial registration Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC), RBR-8sxnfyd.

title: Predictive Performance of Inflammatory Markers for Severe Disease Progression in Measles: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis.
abstract: The recent European measles resurgence has driven record-high hospitalization, yet objective tools for early risk stratification remain scarce. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of routine admission inflammatory biomarkers for predicting severe disease and prolonged hospitalization. We retrospectively analyzed 509 patients with laboratory-confirmed measles hospitalized during a Romanian outbreak (November 2023-August 2025). Severe disease was defined via a clinical composite endpoint (intensive-care admission, mechanical ventilation, supplemental oxygen, acute respiratory failure, or sepsis). Biomarker discriminative performance was assessed using receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, Youden-optimal cut-offs, and DeLong tests. Multivariable logistic and Cox proportional-hazards regression evaluated independent predictors of severity and time to discharge. The cohort exhibited a pediatric predominance (median age: 3.0 years; 20% infants) with an 82% unvaccinated rate; 33% developed severe disease. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) demonstrated superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.863, 95% CI 0.820-0.898; cut-off ≥ 7 pg/mL, sensitivity 73%, specificity 93%), significantly outperforming ferritin (AUC 0.800) and conventional markers (all p < 0.001). Multivariable modeling established IL-6 and ferritin as the sole independent predictors of severity. All intensive-care admissions occurred exclusively for unvaccinated patients (5.0% vs. 0%). Severe disease, pneumonia, male sex, unvaccinated status and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) independently predicted prolonged hospitalization. Admission IL-6 and ferritin serve as robust, independent prognostic biomarkers that accurately identify high-risk measles patients, providing objective criteria with which to optimize clinical triage and inpatient management during outbreaks.

title: Perioperative Anxiety in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Clinical Consequences, Potential Mechanisms, and Management-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) treats end-stage knee osteoarthritis, yet some patients report persistent pain, incomplete recovery, or dissatisfaction. Perioperative anxiety is a potentially modifiable factor associated with poorer outcomes. This narrative review examines its clinical consequences, mechanisms, and management in TKA. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched without date or language restrictions through 25 September 2026. Evidence was stratified by anxiety-related selection at enrollment: studies of anxiety-selected patients provided direct evidence, whereas studies without such selection provided indirect evidence, regardless of whether anxiety was a primary, secondary, or exploratory outcome. Sixty studies underwent formal risk-of-bias appraisal. Higher anxiety was associated with greater postoperative pain and analgesic requirements and poorer patient-reported recovery and satisfaction, whereas findings for persistent pain and long-term function were less consistent. Proposed pathways include catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, reduced self-efficacy, pain sensitization, and stress-related biological processes. Pharmacological, psychoeducational, cognitive behavioral, digital, and adjunctive interventions may reduce anxiety, but direct evidence remains limited, and improvements do not consistently translate into less pain or opioid use, better function, or higher satisfaction. Anxiety may be considered in preoperative risk assessment, while standardized assessment and higher-quality trials remain needed.

title: Data-Driven Comorbidity Phenotypes and In-Hospital Outcomes Among Patients With Nonvariceal Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Formative Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Existing risk scores for nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding (NVUGIB) may not adequately represent the heterogeneity of coexisting chronic conditions. Routinely collected hospital discharge records may enable data-driven characterization of clinically meaningful comorbidity profiles. Objective This formative study aimed to identify reproducible comorbidity profiles among patients hospitalized with NVUGIB and examine their associations with in-hospital outcomes and health care use. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3193 adults hospitalized with NVUGIB at a tertiary hospital in China between 2015 and 2025. Of 55 prespecified chronic conditions, 33 with a prevalence of at least 1% were included as binary clustering variables. Patients were randomly divided into an 80% training subset and a 20% held-out validation subset. Comorbidity profiles were identified in the training subset using a self-organizing map and Ward hierarchical clustering and then assigned to the validation subset using the fixed clustering solution. Profile reproducibility was evaluated by comparing condition prevalence vectors between subsets. Multivariable regression models assessed associations with severe in-hospital outcomes, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, length of stay, and hospital costs. Results At least 1 selected comorbidity was recorded in 89.7% (2864/3193) of patients. Six profiles were identified: low-burden heterogeneous (cluster 1), non-upper gastrointestinal neoplastic-metastatic (cluster 2), circulatory-renal (cluster 3), cardiometabolic-renal (cluster 4), atherosclerotic-vascular (cluster 5), and rheumatologic-neurological (cluster 6). Profile composition was broadly reproducible between the training and validation subsets (weighted mean Spearman correlation=0.891, SD 0.04; P =.001). The circulatory-renal profile had the strongest associations with severe in-hospital outcomes (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.57, 95% CI 5.39-14.01), intensive care unit admission (aOR 10.38, 95% CI 4.87-25.76), and in-hospital death (aOR 4.66, 95% CI 1.97-13.75). The rheumatologic-neurological and cardiometabolic-renal profiles were also associated with higher odds of these outcomes. All 6 profiles were associated with longer hospital stays and higher hospital costs. Conclusions Using routinely collected hospital discharge records, we identified clinically interpretable comorbidity profiles among patients with NVUGIB. The profiles were broadly reproducible within the study population and showed different associations with clinical outcomes and resource use. Profile-based information may complement established risk assessment and could be examined further as an electronic health record-based approach to clinical management and resource planning.

title: Caregiver Experiences and Resource Gaps Following Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury: A Qualitative Analysis.
abstract: This qualitative study explored caregivers' experiences navigating their child's recovery following pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) and identified barriers and facilitators to accessing healthcare, educational, and community resources after hospital discharge. Semi-structured virtual interviews were conducted with caregivers of children with a history of TBI from Ohio and other U.S. states. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using thematic analysis. Among the 13 caregivers, 69% were female, and 92% were White. Three themes emerged: (1) caregivers as primary navigators of fragmented systems; (2) the impact of recovery on family life and well-being; and (3) the need for personalized, longitudinal support throughout recovery. Caregivers described assuming primary responsibility for coordinating services across healthcare, rehabilitation, insurance, education, and community systems with limited guidance during care transitions. They also reported emotional exhaustion, social isolation, financial strain, and the ongoing demands of advocating for their children's changing needs. Although supportive clinicians, care coordinators, and community organizations facilitated recovery, families continued to face challenges accessing information, coordinating services, and navigating available resources. Findings underscore the need for longitudinal, family-centered models of care that extend beyond current standards. Centralized, technology-enabled navigation may reduce caregiver burden by improving information access, care coordination, and personalized support throughout recovery.

title: Embolization of Thyroid Arteries as a Bridge Therapy Before Thyroidectomy in a Patient With Thyrotoxicosis: Case Report.
abstract: Thyroid artery embolization (TAE) is a minimally invasive technique that induces selective ischemic necrosis of the thyroid parenchyma, thereby reducing thyroid hormone synthesis with few associated complications. Successful cases of TAE as a bridge therapy before total thyroidectomy in patients with refractory thyrotoxicosis are rare. We present the case of a 36-year-old man with a history of Graves' disease and poor adherence to medical therapy who presented with clinical features of thyrotoxicosis. On physical examination, he exhibited active moderate-to-severe orbitopathy (EUGOGO classification; clinical activity score 5/7) and a grade III goiter, reflecting advanced and poorly controlled disease. Paraclinical findings revealed markedly elevated free T4 levels and suppressed TSH. The diagnosis of uncontrolled hyperthyroidism was made, with a Burch-Wartofsky score of 40 points, indicating an impending thyroid storm. Medical therapy at maximally tolerated doses did not result in a complete clinical response; therefore, a total thyroidectomy was planned, preceded by therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE). Due to intolerance to TPE, TAE was performed as a bridge therapy, followed by total thyroidectomy without complications. The patient was discharged with a resolution of symptoms and progressive normalization of thyroid hormone levels. TAE may represent a valuable bridging therapy before total thyroidectomy in selected patients with severe thyrotoxicosis due to Graves' disease who are refractory to or unsuitable for conventional therapies.

title: Clozapine Augmentation Strategies and Clinical Predictors of Prolonged Tertiary Hospitalization in Clozapine-Resistant Schizophrenia: a Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and hypothesis Clozapine-resistant schizophrenia (CRS) remains a major clinical challenge, with persistent symptoms and functional impairment despite adequate clozapine treatment. Real-world evidence is limited, and guidelines recommend a narrow set of augmentation strategies-aripiprazole (D2/3R partial agonist), amisulpride (D2/3R selective antagonist), and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)-without clear guidance on selection or sequencing. This study examined augmentation choice and its association with length of stay (LOS) and symptomatic outcomes. Study design We conducted a retrospective cohort study using BC Psychosis Program electronic records (2012-2025). Symptom severity and functioning scores (PANSS, CGI-S, GAPS, SOFAS) were extracted at admission and discharge. Multivariable Cox models assessed LOS for index and discharge augmentation strategies. ANCOVA compared symptom change across discharge strategies. A machine-learning model examined predictors of ECT versus pharmacological augmentation at discharge. Study results Eighty-eight admissions were included. In adjusted index models, D2/3R selective antagonism was associated with shorter LOS than ECT (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.35-4.62); partial agonism was not (HR 1.41, 95% CI 0.75-2.63). Partial agonist augmentation had the highest inefficacy-related switching. By discharge strategy, ECT was associated with greater reduction in positive symptoms than selective antagonism (MD -3.20, 95% CI -5.65 to -0.75) and partial agonism (MD -3.87, 95% CI -6.57 to -1.16). Greater impairment in psychosis and functioning on admission predicted ECT at discharge (AUC 0.74; balanced accuracy 0.72). Conclusions D2/3R selective antagonism was the most resource-efficient strategy, while ECT produced greater improvement in positive symptoms. Incorporating baseline psychosis severity and functioning into measurement-based care may support more informed augmentation selection.

title: Sodium alginate-based eco-friendly nanocomposites for textile wastewater management.
abstract: Increasing global textile production continues to intensify concerns about the discharge of untreated dye-laden wastewater into the environment. Textile effluents are typically dark in color and characterized by high pH, elevated biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, total dissolved solids, and total suspended solids. Moreover, textile dyes exhibit high levels of toxicity, carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, and mutagenicity toward living cells. In this regard, for environmental sustainability, there is a pressing need to improve the quality of effluents before they are discharged into water bodies. Therefore, various treatment techniques are being explored for textile wastewater, and many studies now use nanomaterials because their unique properties and easy customization make them highly effective for this purpose. Sodium alginate (SA) is an abundantly available, eco-friendly, and cost-effective biopolymer that can be effectively utilized as an adsorbent for wastewater treatment. Moreover, modifying SA or incorporating it into composites with other materials can significantly enhance its functional properties, broadening its potential for advanced environmental applications. In this review, we highlight the development and application of SA-based nanocomposites for effective textile wastewater treatment. Lastly, the review provides insights into the current limitations of SA-based materials and offers recommendations for future research directions to enhance their performance and applicability.

title: Outcomes of Soft-Tissue Reconstruction Around the Elbow Using a Lateral Intercostal Artery Perforator-Based Pedicled Flap.
abstract: Background Soft-tissue defects around the elbow present considerable reconstructive challenges, as effective coverage must be achieved without compromising joint mobility. This study assessed the reconstructive and early functional outcomes of lateral intercostal artery perforator (LICAP)-based pedicled flaps for soft-tissue reconstruction around the elbow. Methods This prospective observational study included 30 consecutively enrolled patients who underwent LICAP-based pedicled flap reconstruction at the Department of Plastic Surgery, Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh, between May 2023 and October 2024. Evaluated outcomes comprised flap survival, flap-related complications, donor-site morbidity, elbow range of motion (ROM), and a predefined composite reconstructive outcome. Elbow ROM was measured with a goniometer at the final follow-up, approximately 30 days after flap division. Results The mean patient age was 27.4 ± 10.97 years, and 26 patients were male. Trauma was the cause of 18 defects. Complete flap survival was observed in 27 patients, whereas marginal and partial flap loss occurred in two and one patient, respectively; no patient experienced significant flap loss. Recipient-site wound dehiscence developed in two patients, and donor-site wound dehiscence occurred in three. Primary closure of the donor site was achieved in 29 patients. At the final follow-up, 26 patients demonstrated full elbow ROM, while four had a residual restriction of 10°-15°. Composite outcomes were classified as good in 22 patients and satisfactory in eight; no poor outcomes were recorded. Conclusions In appropriately selected patients, LICAP-based pedicled flap reconstruction provided favorable early reconstructive and functional outcomes for soft-tissue defects around the elbow. Comparative studies involving larger patient populations and extended follow-up are warranted.

title: HEMIARTHROPLASTY FOR PROXIMAL FEMORAL FRACTURES IN CENTENARIANS: A CASE SERIES WITH 12-MONTH SURVIVAL AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES.
Deep Spinal Infection Caused by <i>Corynebacterium simulans</i>: A Case Report.
abstract: Corynebacterium simulans is a commensal coryneform bacterium that commonly colonizes human skin and mucosal surfaces. Owing to limitations in conventional microbiological identification, it is often regarded as a contaminant, and clinically significant deep-seated infections caused by this organism are rarely reported. Here, we describe a case of lumbar infectious spondylitis caused by C. simulans in a 62-year-old male farmer who presented with a 2-month history of persistent low back pain accompanied by pain in both lower limbs. The patient had several potential predisposing factors including repeated unregulated needle-pricking bloodletting therapy, previously unrecognized hyperglycemia, and a family history of psoriasis. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography revealed destructive infectious lesions involving the L3 and L4 vertebral bodies and L3/4 intervertebral disc. Blood culture initially yielded coryneform bacilli from a single anaerobic bottle, whereas repeated blood cultures were subsequently negative, supporting the possibility of contamination. However, given the compatible clinical manifestations, elevated inflammatory markers, and imaging evidence of spinal infection, percutaneous vertebral biopsy was performed. Routine bacterial culture of the deep-tissue specimen showed no growth, whereas metagenomic next-generation sequencing identified C. simulans with high sequence reads and relative abundance, supporting its etiological relevance in the appropriate clinical context. The patient was treated with intravenous vancomycin combined with glycemic control, followed by oral linezolid as step-down therapy. His symptoms gradually improved, inflammatory markers decreased toward the normal range, and follow-up magnetic resonance imaging showed reduced paravertebral soft tissue edema. No recurrence was observed during the 3-month follow-up period. This case highlights that Corynebacterium species detected in the blood or deep tissue specimens should not be readily dismissed as contaminants in patients with compatible evidence of infection. Deep tissue sampling combined with metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) may improve the detection of rare opportunistic pathogens and facilitate timely targeted antimicrobial therapy.

title: Analysis of Factors Influencing Postoperative Drainage Following Reduction Mammoplasty.
abstract: Aim To explore factors influencing postoperative drainage volume and duration after reduction mammoplasty for perioperative nursing. Design A retrospective analysis was conducted on 83 patients who underwent reduction mammoplasty between January 2023 and October 2025. Methods Patients' characteristics and parameters related to the surgery were recorded. Univariable and multivariable linear regression and correlation analyses were performed to identify the correlation between postoperative drainage and the variables. Data sources Data were extracted from routine de-identified electronic medical records. Results The mean postoperative drainage volume was 81.2 ± 80.4 mL, and the mean drainage duration was 2.5 ± 0.84 days. Preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time, operation time, intraoperative blood loss, and resected tissue weight were independent predictors of drainage volume. Body mass index, operation time, and blood loss independently predicted prolonged drainage duration. Conclusion Multiple perioperative factors jointly affect postoperative drainage outcomes after reduction mammoplasty. These correlational findings offer preliminary references for individualised perioperative nursing management. Implications for the profession and/or patient care High-risk patients may require targeted preoperative education and intensified drainage observation. Further studies are needed to verify the clinical effectiveness of such nursing strategies. Impact This study supplemented comprehensive perioperative predictors for postoperative drainage after reduction mammoplasty. The main findings identified several perioperative factors associated with postoperative drainage outcomes. These preliminary correlational results may provide reference for perioperative nursing and offer hypotheses for future clinical validation. Reporting method This study followed EQUATOR guidelines and the STROBE statement for retrospective observational studies. Patient or public contribution No Patient or Public Contribution. No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or manuscript preparation for this study. This retrospective work solely uses de-identified routine clinical data from medical records for secondary analysis.

title: Association Between Exercise Adherence and Long-Term Quality of Life in Ischemic Stroke Survivors: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Aims This study aimed to investigate factors associated with quality of life within 2 years post-discharge, with a particular focus on exercise adherence. Design A prospective observational cohort study. Methods Participants were enrolled during hospitalisation and followed up at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months post-discharge via questionnaires. Linear mixed-effects models were used to identify factors associated with quality of life. Data sources Data were collected from ischemic stroke patients (discharged from The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, January to August 2021) using structured questionnaires, medical records and validated scales. Results Of 355 enrolled stroke survivors, 242 (68.2%) completed the two-year follow-up. Functional disability, exercise adherence, family history of stroke and prior stroke were independently associated with long-term quality of life. Conclusion Greater exercise adherence is independently associated with better quality of life on average over the 24-month follow-up period among stroke survivors. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Nurses and rehabilitation guidelines should prioritise exercise adherence support during long-term follow-up to sustain post-stroke quality of life.

title: Multidimensional prognostic value of preoperative Prognostic Nutritional Index for postoperative outcomes in older adults undergoing major open abdominal surgery.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the predictive value of the preoperative Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) for multidimensional postoperative outcomes in elderly patients undergoing major abdominal surgery. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 761 patients aged ≥65 years from 2015 to 2025. Patients were stratified into low-PNI ( 45) for dose-response trend analysis. Results Compared to the low-PNI group, the high-PNI group had a significantly lower risk of postoperative delirium (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] =0.21, 95% confidence interval [CI]:0.13-0.35, P P P 1, P Conclusion Preoperative PNI is a robust, independent predictor of multiple postoperative outcomes in elderly abdominal surgery patients. As a simple and cost-effective tool, PNI is well suited for preoperative risk stratification and guiding personalized perioperative management.

title: Acute Care and Rehabilitation After Low-Trauma Hip Fractures in Older Adults-Pathways and Functional Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : This study describes, first, healthcare pathways, including inpatient rehabilitation, and, second, functional outcomes for these low-trauma hip fracture (LTHF) types (femoral neck (FN-F), trochanteric (Tr-F), and acetabulum/periprosthetic (Ac/Pp-F) fractures). Methods : This single-center, retrospective cohort study, 2020-2023, included patients aged ≥65 years, with FN-F, Tr-F, or Ac/Pp-F, admitted to inpatient rehabilitation. Pathways comprised acute care, inpatient rehabilitation, and temporary care homes, bounded by pre-fracture situation and discharge destination. Pairwise Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs) were calculated to determine between-group differences. Results : Of 294 individuals (mean age 81.0 ± 7.4 years; 191 (65%) women; 152 Tr-F, 118 FN-F, and 24 Ac/Pp-F), four main pathways were identified: (1) acute care to inpatient rehabilitation in 208 (70.7%) individuals, (2) temporary care home stays before rehabilitation in 25 (8.5%), (3) temporary care home stays after rehabilitation in 17 (5.8%), and (4) re-hospitalization in 44 (15.0%). Median pathway length was 33.0 days (IQR 26.0-40.0) for FN-F, 35.0 (IQR 29.0-46.0) for Tr-F, and 60.5 (IQR 37.0-86.5) for Ac/Pp-F. Between-group differences in pathway type were moderate to large (SMDs: FN-F vs. Tr-F = 0.47; FN-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 1.25; Tr-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 0.84), and for length, small to large (SMDs: FN-F vs. Tr-F = 0.36; FN-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 1.2; Tr-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 0.69). Overall, 246 (83.7%) returned to a permanent private living setting. A total of 88 (29.9%) required new or increased home support or care. At discharge from rehabilitation, among participants who completed the program, the Functional Independence Measure and the Timed Up and Go test showed small-to-moderate between-group differences. Conclusions: Individuals with FN-F, Tr-F, and Ac/Pp-F fractures follow healthcare pathways in different frequencies and have different pathway durations. The findings may support the identification of future opportunities to improve continuity of healthcare, including orthogeriatric management and specialized rehabilitation.

title: Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy with Intracorporeal Urinary Diversion: Perioperative Management and Operative Technique.
abstract: Radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy and urinary diversion remains the standard of care for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and selected high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease. The procedure carries substantial morbidity, in part because the typical patient is elderly and burdened by cardiorespiratory comorbidity. Robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) was developed to attenuate this morbidity, and RARC with intracorporeal urinary diversion (iRARC) avoids the laparotomy that earlier randomized trials required for extracorporeal reconstruction. In this technical narrative review, we present a single-institution operative approach to iRARC, distinguishing institutional practice from evidence-based recommendations. We describe patient selection, preoperative optimization and enhanced recovery, and provide a step-by-step account of our operative technique for male and female radical cystectomy, pelvic lymph node dissection template, and totally intracorporeal ileal conduit and orthotopic neobladder reconstruction. We also summarize the perioperative, oncological, and functional outcomes of iRARC, which support its role as a safe option with specific perioperative advantages in experienced, high-volume centers.

title: Comparison of qSOFA Score and NEWS for Predicting Hospital Admission and Mortality in the Emergency Department: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study compared the performance of the National Early Warning Score (NEWS) and the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score for predicting hospital admission and in-hospital mortality among adult patients triaged to the high-acuity area of the emergency department (ED). qSOFA was derived and validated in patients with suspected infection, and only 8.1% of this cohort carried a preliminary diagnosis of sepsis; its evaluation here is therefore exploratory. Methods: A total of 270 patients were included in this prospective observational study. Vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale scores, and both scores were recorded at ED presentation. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with the two scores compared using the DeLong test. Sensitivity and specificity were then examined separately at both conventional and data-derived thresholds. Bootstrap internal validation, calibration plots, Brier scores and decision-curve analysis were also performed, all computed using the development dataset. Results: Of 268 patients evaluable for the admission outcome (two ED deaths were excluded as a competing outcome), 35.8% ( n = 96) were admitted, and 7.0% ( n = 19 of 270) died in the hospital. No statistically significant difference was found between the AUCs of the two scores for admission (0.709 vs. 0.695; p = 0.627) or mortality (0.900 vs. 0.862; p = 0.150). At the conventional qSOFA score threshold of ≥2, the expected high-specificity, low-sensitivity profile was reproduced for mortality (96.8% and 52.6%), whereas the cohort-derived qSOFA score threshold of ≥1 favored sensitivity (84.2%). Bootstrap correction showed modest optimism. Calibration assessment was limited by the small number of events, and both score-specific models showed apparent net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across most thresholds examined. Each score was independently associated with mortality in exploratory score-specific models. Conclusions: NEWS and qSOFA showed no statistically significant difference in discrimination in this high-acuity ED cohort.
