With only 19 deaths, the mortality analyses and the cohort-specific thresholds are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts before any clinical use.

title: Womens' experience on barriers and facilitators for implementation with Kangaroo Mother Care at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda: a qualitative study.
abstract: Background Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) is a proven cost-effective intervention for preterm and low‑birth‑weight infants, to provide warmth and secondary health effects. In Uganda, despite a high burden of prematurity, resource constraints limit the delivery of cost-effective interventions. Objective(s) This study aimed to identify barriers and enablers for implementing KMC, explore mothers' experience of KMC and apply the i-PARIHS framework to understand why implementation was, or was not, successful at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital. Methods This study was conducted in a rural referral hospital in Uganda with semi‑structured interviews with mothers ( n = 14) in the KMC ward. Interviews were then translated into English, and the transcripts were subjected to qualitative content analysis using inductive coding. Each code was further grouped into subcategories corresponding to barriers or facilitators. The results were interpreted using the i-PARIHS framework to evaluate why treatment implementation was or was not successful. Results Kangaroo Mother Care was found to be largely acceptable and implemented by most participants. Barriers and facilitators were identified within the areas of i) healthcare system, social support, finances, knowledge and beliefs as well as the health of newborns and motivation. Primary barriers included insufficient healthcare facilities, lack of material resources, lack of education on KMC, and lack of adaptation to twins. Facilitators included supportive healthcare staff, learning tools, and the positive effects of KMC as motivation. Conclusions Barriers and facilitators for Kangaroo Mother Care are multifaceted. To increase implementation for all patients, targeted interventions may need to reach beyond the hospital, addressing social and financial factors.

title: Arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting for Hepple stage V osteochondral lesions of the talus: a retrospective case series.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
abstract: Background Evidence regarding arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting for Hepple stage V osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) remains limited. This study assessed short-term clinical outcomes, postoperative imaging findings, and perioperative characteristics of this technique. Methods This retrospective case series included 23 patients undergoing arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting between March 2020 and July 2024. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) demonstrated subchondral cystic changes in all lesions, which were classified as Hepple stage V OLTs. The primary outcome was the European Foot and Ankle Society (EFAS) score at final follow-up. Secondary outcomes included the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score during walking, the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, Karlsson Ankle Functional Score (KAFS), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) pain domain score, Tegner score and ankle range of motion (ROM). Postoperative radiographs and available CT scans were reviewed to assess graft position and subchondral healing; MRI findings were also evaluated when available. Operative time, concomitant lateral ligament repair, and complications were documented. Paired comparisons were performed using the paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, as appropriate after assessment of normality. Results Mean follow-up was 21.0 ± 8.7 months (median, 18.0 months; Q1-Q3, 13.0-24.0), and mean lesion area was 1.94 ± 0.38 cm 2 . Median operative time was 75.0 min (Q1-Q3, 67.5-86.0), and five patients underwent concomitant lateral ligament repair. The median EFAS score improved from 9.0 (Q1-Q3, 8.0-10.0) preoperatively to 19.0 (Q1-Q3, 18.0-20.0) at final follow-up (P Conclusions Arthroscopic autologous iliac crest cancellous bone grafting was associated with improvements in pain, function, and activity in patients with Hepple stage V OLTs at short-term follow-up. Postoperative CT demonstrated graft incorporation in all patients who underwent CT assessment. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of this technique for appropriately selected cystic lesions, although larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are warranted.

title: Analgesic Efficacy of Ropivacaine-P407 Gel vs. Bupivacaine in Single-Port-Assisted Hysterectomy: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
abstract: Purpose To compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of ropivacaine-poloxamer 407 (P407) gel injection with that of bupivacaine injection in patients undergoing single-port assisted hysterectomy. Materials and methods This retrospective study reviewed medical records from January to December 2023 at Severance Hospital, Yonsei University. A total of 209 patients undergoing minimally invasive hysterectomy with or without adnexal procedures were analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups: 42 received ropivacaine-P407 gel (Welpass), and 167 received bupivacaine alone. Demographic variables, intraoperative parameters, and postoperative pain scores were collected. Propensity score matching was applied to control for surgical complexity and baseline imbalances, yielding 31 matched pairs. Pain levels were assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at multiple time points up to 48 hours postoperatively. Results Before matching, the ropivacaine-P407 gel group demonstrated significantly lower pain scores starting at 12 hours postoperatively compared to the bupivacaine group (NRS difference p =0.005 at 24 hours, p =0.020 at 48 hours). After propensity score matching, this difference remained significant: patients in the ropivacaine-P407 gel group continued to report reduced pain intensity at 24 hours [mean NRS±standard deviation (SD): 1.96±0.35 vs. 2.86±1.35, p =0.003] and 48 hours (1.88±0.49 vs. 2.65±1.12, p =0.014). Both groups showed similar safety profiles, with no severe adverse reactions related to the anesthetic agents reported. Conclusion Ropivacaine-P407 gel injection provides superior early postoperative analgesia compared to bupivacaine alone in minimally invasive hysterectomy.

title: Protocol for a realist evaluation of a COPD clinical pathway in Saskatchewan, Canada.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a complex and common condition with significant health, social, and economic burdens, especially due to frequent hospitalizations and comorbidities. International research shows current care for COPD is limited by delayed diagnosis, poor coordination among providers, and inconsistent adherence to treatment guidelines, which negatively impacts patient outcomes. Clinical pathways offer a promising solution by improving care coordination, aligning treatment with evidence-based guidelines, and enhancing both patient experiences and system efficiency; however, questions remain about how, for whom, and in which contexts they are most effective. Using a realist evaluation approach, our study will evaluate how, for whom, and in which circumstances an integrated clinical pathway for COPD works in Saskatchewan, Canada. First, we will develop initial program theories based on literature and stakeholder input. Second, we will test these theories using administrative data and realist interviews with healthcare staff, managers, providers, COPD patients, and caregivers. Third, we will refine our theories based on data collected. Fourth, we will translate our findings to enhance future implementation. These phases will be repeated over a three-year span to continuously improve pathway implementation processes and monitor improvements in patient outcomes. Findings will be shared through integrated knowledge translation with system decision-makers and patients. Findings will also be disseminated to the broader research community through conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications.

title: Driving the quality of care in publicly financed health insurance: a close look at the accreditation-based incentive policy of AB-PMJAY in India.
abstract: The quality of healthcare delivery, in terms of clinical service standardization and patient satisfaction, remains a persistent challenge for low and middle-income countries (LMIC), including India. Since the launch of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PMJAY)-the world's largest publicly financed health insurance scheme in terms of the numbers of beneficiaries eligible for coverage-the government has undertaken several initiatives to integrate quality-related interventions into the services delivered by empaneled healthcare providers. Among these was the introduction of financial incentives to empaneled healthcare providers linked to the uptake of quality certifications and accreditations in 2019. This policy and practice review examines the design assumptions of the accreditation-linked incentive policy, its early implementation experience and the uptake of quality certification among healthcare providers. It draws on the findings of a mixed-methods study commissioned by the National Health Authority of India, conducted in 2021 and published as a technical report, and extends them with certification uptake data to September 2026. Uptake of certification has been low and concentrated among hospitals that were previously accredited through independent accreditation bodies; providers' responses to the incentive have been varied; and no clear relationship between certification tier and patient satisfaction has been demonstrated, although higher tiers corresponded to better-standardised structures and processes in the facilities observed. We examine the design assumptions that may explain this pattern and suggest the conditions under which the policy could achieve its intended effects. We submit that while the current design is largely an input-driven mechanism to motivate facilities to improve quality standards, it may serve only as a foundational step. For comprehensive quality improvement, we submit that the policy must evolve towards a suitable value-based incentive structure, aligning with international best practices, while providing a value proposition to empaneled hospitals vis-a-vis investments required for accreditation. We suggest actionable recommendations to strengthen the existing policy, spanning value-based incentive design, methods for improving provider value proposition and cross-scheme alignment.

title: Recovery Kinetics and Postoperative Outcomes of Propofol-Based Total Intravenous Anesthesia Versus Sevoflurane in Ambulatory Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Studies.
abstract: Background Optimal anesthetic selection is critical for recovery and patient outcomes in ambulatory surgery. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) with sevoflurane in adults undergoing outpatient procedures, focusing on randomized evidence published since 2014 to reflect contemporary clinical practice. Methods We performed a PRISMA-compliant, random-effects meta-analysis of 15 randomized controlled trials ( n = 1345 randomized participants), published between 2014 and 2025, comparing propofol TIVA with sevoflurane in adults undergoing ambulatory surgery. Primary outcomes were readiness for discharge, postanesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay (LOS), and emergence time. Secondary outcomes included postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) and pain scores, requirement for rescue antiemetics and analgesics, unplanned hospital admissions, and adverse events. All-cause mortality was prespecified for extraction but was not reported in the included trials (PROSPERO: CRD420251151311). Results Fifteen RCTs were included. For the primary outcomes, discharge readiness was shorter with TIVA in a single core trial (not a pooled meta-analytic estimate) (mean difference [MD] -5.8 min; 95% confidence interval [CI] -10.63 to -0.97; p = 0.019), although no significant differences were observed for PACU LOS (MD -1.3 min; 95% CI -7.3 to 4.8; p = 0.56). Emergence times were not pooled due to extreme heterogeneity between studies. Regarding secondary outcomes, TIVA was associated with a lower risk of PONV (risk ratio 0.67; 95% CI 0.47-0.96; absolute risk difference -0.11; approximate number needed to treat 9), with attenuation toward the null under trim-and-fill, and with lower postoperative pain scores (standardized mean difference [SMD] -0.30; among VAS 0-10 trials, MD -0.29 points). Mortality was not reported in any of the included trials. Conclusions Contemporary randomized evidence suggests that propofol TIVA may reduce PONV and yield a small reduction in postoperative pain scores. Evidence regarding discharge readiness, PACU LOS, and emergence is limited or inconsistent and does not support a general claim of faster early recovery with either technique. Anesthetic choice should balance these symptomatic effects against patient factors and institutional resources.

title: A 17-Year Descriptive Analysis of Firework-Related Eye Injuries on Territory Day in Northern Australia.
Changing Case-Mix and Inpatient Rehabilitation Costs in C4/C5 Traumatic Cervical Spinal Cord Injury: A 10-Year Single-Center Study From a National Rehabilitation Center in China.
abstract: Background The case-mix and inpatient rehabilitation costs of traumatic cervical spinal cord injury (TCSCI) may have shifted with population aging and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. We examined decade-long trends in patient characteristics, injury mechanisms, and per-diem rehabilitation costs for neurological-level C4/C5 TCSCI. Methods All patients with C4/C5 TCSCI admitted to the China Rehabilitation Research Center were studied retrospectively, comparing 2013-2017 with 2018-2022, and, in an exploratory analysis, the pre-pandemic (2018-2019) with the pandemic (2020-2022) period. Costs were adjusted for inflation using the medical services Consumer Price Index. Comparisons used the χ 2 , Wilcoxon rank-sum, and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Cost drivers were modeled using multivariable Gamma generalized linear models (log link). Results Among 1063 patients (male-to-female ratio 5.3:1), mean age rose from 43.9 to 49.5 years and the proportion injured by low-level falls increased from 20.7% to 33.8% ( χ 2 = 37.76, p Z = -2.33, p = 0.02) while adjusted daily cost increased ( Z = -10.07, p p Conclusions Admitted patients were increasingly older and frequently injured in low-level falls. Per-diem rehabilitation costs rose despite shorter hospital stays. Changes spanning the pandemic represent an exploratory temporal association rather than causal evidence. Fall prevention strategies for older adults and capacity planning for higher-dependency rehabilitation are warranted.

title: Experiences and needs related to perioperative nutritional management among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A descriptive phenomenological study.
abstract: Objective To explore the lived experiences and needs of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) regarding perioperative nutritional management. Methods This descriptive phenomenological study used purposive maximum-variation sampling at a national medical center in Shanghai, China. Thirty-three patients with HCC (17 preoperative and 16 postoperative) each completed one semi-structured interview between June and September 2025. Recruitment continued until data saturation. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Results Four themes were identified: lack of nutritional management awareness, pressing needs for support, navigating practical challenges, and active engagement in nutritional self-management. Participants described limited understanding, reliance on professional guidance, conflicting advice, unappealing hospital food, financial and emotional burdens, and different levels of involvement in nutritional decisions and self-management. Conclusions Interpreted through Self-Efficacy Theory, the findings suggest that confidence may influence how patients engage with perioperative nutritional care. Clear, individualized guidance and support for patient participation warrant evaluation in future interventional studies.

title: Role and values of Swedish community hospitals through the eyes of general hospital doctors: a qualitative interview study.
abstract: Objective To explore how doctors at general hospitals perceive the role and values of community hospitals (CHs) in rural northern Sweden. Design Interview study, using qualitative content analysis. Setting The study was conducted in Norrbotten and Västerbotten counties in northern Sweden and included three general hospitals. Participants Semistructured interviews were conducted during 2025 with nine doctors at general hospitals. Results Three main themes were developed: Offering care close to home, Providing safe care far from the hospital and Being part of the same organisation. CHs were seen as important in providing not only standard primary care but also both inpatient and emergency care close to patients’ homes. CHs were also regarded as crucial for patient safety, with experienced staff seen as particularly important to achieve this. Healthcare provision in northern rural Sweden was described as a shared mission with a shared patient population and mutual challenges. Conclusion Doctors at general hospitals view CHs as essential in providing healthcare in rural northern Sweden. To provide care safely, CHs are dependent on having both organisational and structural preconditions met.

title: Association Between Pre-Stroke Physical Activity Patterns Assessed by the Baecke Physical Activity Questionnaire and Functional Recovery After First Ischemic Stroke: A Barthel Index-Based Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : This study investigated the association between pre-stroke physical activity (PA) assessed using the Baecke Physical Activity Questionnaire (BPAQ) and functional status after a first-ever ischemic stroke (IS). Methods : This prospective cohort study included 91 patients who had had their first-ever IS and were admitted for inpatient rehabilitation. Functional status was assessed using the Barthel Index (BI) at rehabilitation admission, discharge, and three months after discharge. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were adjusted for age, sex, the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, and the number of comorbidities. Predictors of BI ≥ 91 were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Results : BI improved significantly over follow-up ( p p = 0.021), whereas the time-by-BPAQ interaction was not significant ( p = 0.952). Initial BI was associated with subsequent BI scores ( p p = 0.033 and p = 0.030), whereas the Sport Index was not ( p = 0.089). None of the domain-by-time interactions were significant. Higher BI at rehabilitation admission was associated with higher odds of BI ≥ 91 at discharge and three months after discharge (OR = 1.11, p p = 0.015). Conclusions : Pre-stroke PA assessed using the BPAQ was associated with functional status across the observed time points, but there was no evidence that it was associated with a different longitudinal trajectory of BI recovery.

title: Prognosis Prediction in Adult Intensive Care-A Critical Analysis.
abstract: Background: Prognosis prediction in adult intensive care units (ICUs) guides clinical decision-making, realistic goal-setting with families, and resource allocation, but is challenged by the marked heterogeneity of critically ill patients in multi-speciality wards. Methods: This narrative review critically analyses commonly used prognostic scoring systems by clinical application timeline. Results: Admission prognostic models, including the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE II/III/IV), Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS II/SAPS 3) and Mortality Probability Model (MPM), estimate in-hospital mortality from acute physiological derangement and comorbidity; the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) adds prognostic value. During the ICU stay, organ dysfunction is tracked with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA/SOFA-2), designed for repeated reassessment, and the Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score (MODS), while the Therapeutic Intervention Scoring System (TISS-28) quantifies nursing workload. At discharge, the Barthel Index, Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) and Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) measure functional independence and neurological outcome. Admission-based mortality models use an initial assessment window and may require local recalibration, and discrimination alone does not establish clinical utility. Conclusions: Future directions include trajectory-based models, phenotyping, biomarkers, time-limited trials and machine learning. Prognostic estimates should inform multidisciplinary evaluation and shared decision-making, rather than independently determine treatment intensity or withdrawal.

title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
abstract: Purpose Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs. Methods Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate. Results DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A). Conclusion Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

title: Effect of Buerger-Allen Exercises on Lower Extremity Perfusion in Diabetes Mellitus Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting With Saphenous Vein Harvesting: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy

title: Operational Challenges During Public Health Emergencies in Safety-Net Hospitals.
abstract: Importance Safety-net hospitals (SNHs) serve as essential public health hubs, providing direct clinical care and critical social services to vulnerable populations, yet gaps persist in their ability to reliably deliver these essential services during disasters. Objective To identify common challenges faced by SNHs and actionable approaches described by participants to strengthen future emergency response capacity at these critical institutions. Design, setting, and participants For this qualitative study, from April through November 2025, key informant interviews were conducted with individuals across SNHs selected to represent a spectrum of SNH types. Thematic analysis of site-level case studies was used to identify cross-cutting and context-specific patterns across 5 domains: load balancing, staffing needs, supply chain, crisis standards of care (CSC), and health care coalitions (HCCs). Main outcomes and measures Stakeholder perspectives of pandemic preparedness, response, and recovery were evaluated to understand strategies to mitigate future health care disasters. Results Analysis of interviews with 69 individuals from 10 SNH sites identified systemic vulnerabilities across all 5 domains in SNHs. SNHs rarely succeeded in transferring critically ill patients without extensive staff time spent setting up the transfer. SNHs often experienced severe workforce disruptions from limited staff pools and nurse attrition, leaving them dependent on temporary staff at higher costs. Just-in-time personal protective equipment procurement and constricted manufacturing supply chains created supply crises. Few SNHs implemented full CSC, but many worked to find creative solutions to prevent more extensive changes in care standards. Opinions on written CSC were mixed, with some preferring structured frameworks and others preferring flexibility. Experiences with HCCs varied widely, with SNHs embedded in well-resourced HCCs reporting better coordination and support. Conclusions and relevance In this qualitative study of SNH preparedness and response, findings indicated that SNHs faced challenges with load balancing, supply chain, staffing, CSC, and HCCs. To address such challenges in the future, SNHs, regional coalitions, and the federal government should implement sustainable changes that can be rapidly brought to bear in an emergency. Potential solutions may have outsized benefit for SNHs; however, such solutions must be designed to be accessible to SNHs and feasible in these settings.

title: Association between multiday emergency department boarding and higher in-hospital mortality: evidence from Brazil.

title: Heat and Emergency Department Operations: A Two-Decade Observational Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Emergency department (ED) crowding remains one of the most pressing challenges facing the US healthcare system; environmental factors have received little attention as determinants of ED operational performance, patient behavior, or emergency service utilization. We examined the association between maximum daily heat index and ED throughput metrics, patient behavioral outcomes, and likelihood of EMS arrival. We retrospectively analyzed 485,403 warm-season ED visits from a 22-year period at a large urban academic medical center in New England. The exposure was daily maximum heat index (ERA5-Land) for Suffolk County, Massachusetts. Primary outcomes included four ED throughput time metrics: door-to-doctor time, doctor-to-decision time, boarding time, and total ED length of stay; secondary outcomes included the left without being seen rate, leaving against medical advice rate, and likelihood of EMS arrival. Each 1°F increase in heat index was associated with a 0.41% increase in door-to-doctor time (95% CI: 0.38% – 0.44%). Heat index was not significantly associated with the other three throughput metrics. At the 95°F heat index threshold, patients were 27% more likely to leave against medical advice than on days below the threshold (OR 1.27; 95% CI: 1.02 – 1.58), and had higher odds of arriving by EMS (OR 1.10; 95% CI: 1.06 – 1.15). Higher heat index was associated with longer door-to-doctor time, increased EMS arrival proportion, and higher odds of leaving against medical advice. Health systems and municipalities should characterize how hot weather affects operational performance and integrate this evidence into heat-readiness planning.

title: Impact of overnight boarding in the emergency department on in-hospital mortality and length of hospital stay among older patients.

title: Do Machine Learning–Guided Proactive Full Capacity Protocols Mitigate Emergency Department Overcrowding? A Simulation-Based Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Emergency department (ED) overcrowding threatens care quality. Full Capacity Protocols (FCPs) are often activated reactively, after crowding thresholds have been exceeded. We developed and validated an integrated machine learning–discrete-event simulation framework to answer whether prediction-guided earlier FCP activation improves ED crowding control compared with conventional reactive activation. The simulation model represented ED patient flow, while an embedded machine learning model predicted hourly waiting-room crowding six hours ahead and triggered proactive FCP activation. Using empirically calibrated parameters, we compared proactive and reactive deployment over a 365-day horizon with 10 independent replications. Outcomes included ED length of stay, wait time, time above the crowding threshold, protocol activations, and protocol duration. Proactive deployment produced statistically significant reductions in time above the crowding threshold and average protocol duration across threshold settings, while effects on ED length of stay and wait time were not statistically significant, supporting proactive FCP for crowding control.

title: Orthopaedic Consultation Versus No Consultation for Clavicle, Radial Head, and Proximal Humerus Fractures: Association with Post-Imaging Emergency Department Length of Stay.
abstract: Background/Objectives : To evaluate the association between orthopaedic consultation and Emergency Department (ED) length of stay among patients with clavicle, radial head, and proximal humerus fractures meeting criteria for nonacute management (discharge without orthopaedic consultation). Methods : All adult patients presenting to a single Level 1 trauma centre between 2019 and 2022 with a clavicle, radial head, or proximal humerus fracture that met criteria for nonacute management (discharge without orthopaedic consultation) were identified from an institutional database. Post-imaging ED length of stay, defined as time from radiograph completion to discharge or admission, was compared between patients discharged per protocol without orthopaedic consultation and those discharged after receiving orthopaedic consultation. A mixed-effects linear log regression model with orthopaedic surgery consult, age and sex as fixed effects and year of presentation as a random intercept was used to model the effect of not having an orthopaedic surgery consult on length of stay. A post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding patients who were admitted was performed. Results of the regression model are presented with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Results : This study included 523 patients (average age 57 years, 58% female) with 115 clavicle, 269 proximal humerus, and 139 radial head fractures. Among patients meeting criteria for nonacute management, those who were discharged per protocol without orthopaedic consultation had a 59%, 56%, and 55% reduction in length of stay for clavicle, radial head, and proximal humerus fractures, respectively (all p Conclusions : Discharge without orthopaedic consultation among patients with clavicle, radial head, or proximal humerus fractures meeting criteria for nonacute management was associated with substantially shorter ED length of stay. Adherence to this protocol may aid in reducing overcrowding in the ED.

title: Emergency medicine literature in the Web of Science category "emergency medicine": A bibliometric analysis (1980-2024).
abstract: Objectives The objective is to describe long-term trends in emergency medicine (EM) research output from 1980 to 2024 and to map study designs, conceptual domains, and collaboration structures within the Web of Science (WoS) Category "EM." Methods We conducted a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the WoS Core Collection from January 1, 1980, to December 31, 2024, using the WoS Categories filter "EM." The search was performed on October 3, 2025. Only records with WoS document type "Article" were included. Bibliographic data, including publication year, journal, country, institutions, citations, and indexed keywords/metadata, were extracted. A rule-based text-mining algorithm classified study designs and conceptual domains and was internally validated against a manually reviewed sample of 240 records, showing 75.8% agreement (κ = 0.638) for study design and 86.3% agreement (κ = 0.828) for conceptual domain. Descriptive statistics and VOSviewer-based co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence analyses were performed. Results Of 161,842 records initially identified, 102,561 articles met eligibility criteria. Annual EM publication counts increased after 2000. Health services and systems research and observational clinical studies predominated, whereas randomized controlled trials and qualitative or mixed-methods studies remained uncommon. Trauma, resuscitation, cardiovascular emergencies, and sepsis were longstanding core domains, while digital health, artificial intelligence, point-of-care ultrasound, disaster medicine, and global EM gained prominence after 2010. Collaboration expanded over time, but multinational co-authorship remained limited, and affiliations from low- and middle-income countries were underrepresented. Conclusions EM has evolved into a high-volume, thematically diverse field, but its evidence base remains predominantly observational and geographically imbalanced.

title: Potentially avoidable computed tomography after positive ultrasonography in appendicitis.
abstract: Objective The aim of this study was to determine the frequency of computed tomography performed despite a positive ultrasonography in histopathologically confirmed appendicitis (potentially avoidable computed tomography), and to assess its effects on radiation exposure, cost, and emergency department length of stay. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 887 consecutive patients who underwent appendectomy for suspected appendicitis (January 2023-December 2025). Potentially avoidable computed tomography was defined as computed tomography following a positive ultrasonography result. As length of stay was non-normal, imaging strategies were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, and length of stay predictors were modeled using median (quantile) regression, with a log-link gamma generalized linear model as a sensitivity analysis. Imaging cost used national tariffs; radiation was estimated as ~8 mSv per abdominal computed tomography with age-specific BEIR VII multipliers. Results Computed tomography was used in 87.6% (777/887) of cases. Of the 521 patients who underwent ultrasonography, the results were positive in 35.5%, inconclusive in 30.7%, and negative in 33.8% of cases. Potentially avoidable computed tomography was performed in 81/777 computed tomography examinations (10.4%). Notably, 43.8% (81/185) of patients with positive ultrasonography results subsequently underwent computed tomography scan, corresponding to ~648 mSv of avoidable radiation exposure and an associated cost of 26,667 TL (~US$811), with 49.4% of the affected patients being children. Length of stay did not differ across strategies (p=0.748), and computed tomography was not an independent length of stay predictor (+7.2 min; p=0.23), whereas business-hour arrival was (+15.3 min; p Conclusion Computed tomography remained frequent even after ultrasonography established the diagnosis, with no effect on emergency department length of stay, generating avoidable radiation and costs concentrated in children. Reducing computed tomography after a positive ultrasonography is a feasible opportunity to improve resource utilization while preserving patient safety.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Profile of Homeless Patients Attending the Emergency Department of a Tertiary Care Centre in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, India: A Prospective Observational Study
Associations between psychiatric comorbidity and intensive care unit length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality: A retrospective observational study.
journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
abstract: Aim Psychiatric comorbidities are common among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), but findings regarding their impact on clinical outcomes remain inconsistent. Additionally, existing studies have often included patients admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm, leaving insufficient evidence about the independent effects of psychiatric comorbidity on clinical outcomes. To address this gap, this study investigated the independent association of psychiatric comorbidity with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality among patients admitted to the ICU, excluding those admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm. Methods Of the 2599 patients admitted to the ICU of a university hospital, 2192 were included in the analysis. After adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, admission category, and severity score, generalized linear models were used to evaluate ICU and hospital length of stay, and logistic regression analysis was used to assess in-hospital mortality. Results Among the 2192 patients included in the analysis, 75 had psychiatric comorbidity. In adjusted analyses, psychiatric comorbidity was not significantly associated with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, or in-hospital mortality. Conclusion No participants were admitted to the ICU for suicide attempts or self-harm, and psychiatric comorbidity was not an independent predictor of ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, or in-hospital mortality. Thus, in this ICU population, no statistically significant association was detected between psychiatric comorbidity and short-term clinical outcomes. Therefore, caution is needed when estimating ICU outcomes based solely on the presence of psychiatric comorbidity.

title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
abstract: Background Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED. Methods We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. Results Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P P =0.54). Conclusions Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing. Registration URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

title: Impact evaluation of Lean Healthcare in emergency departments: evidence from a large-scale Brazilian initiative using difference-in-differences
Reliability and Validity of the Australian Mental Health Triage Scale in Children's Hospitals.
journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
abstract: Objective To evaluate interrater reliability and validity of the Australian Mental Health Triage Scale (AMHTS) for children presenting to the emergency department (ED) with behavioral health symptoms. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study of ED visits by children aged 3-17 with a primary behavioral health symptom at two US children's hospitals. Nurses assigned Emergency Severity Index (ESI) and AMHTS Scores. Interrater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) on visits with two independently assigned AMHTS Scores. To evaluate validity, quasi-Poisson regression examined the association of AMHTS Scores and ED resource utilization, adjusted for sociodemographic and clinical factors. Resource use was categorized using the standard ESI definition and an expanded definition incorporating behavioral health-specific resources. Results We included 454 visits (45.4% aged 10-14, 56.2% female) with at least one AMHTS Score, of which 94.1% were ESI 2 and 26.9% were AMHTS 2. Among 221 visits with two AMHTS Scores, ICC was 0.48 (95% CI 0.37, 0.58). Higher-acuity AMHTS Scores were associated with greater resource utilization. Standard resource use was higher for AMHTS Score 1 (Incidence Rate Ratio [IRR] 1.82, 95% CI 1.12, 2.96) and Score 2 (IRR 1.64, 95% CI 1.15, 2.40) versus AMHTS Score 5. When applying the expanded definition, resource use was higher for AMHTS Score 1-4 versus 5. Conclusion Interrater reliability of AMHTS was fair, and higher-acuity scores were associated with greater ED resource utilization. AMHTS Scores were more widely distributed than ESI Scores, suggesting a more responsive approach to pediatric behavioral health triage.

title: Predictors of prolonged emergency department length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients.
Beyond Age: Radiological and Inflammatory Factors Associated with Hospital Stay After VATS in Pediatric Complicated Pneumonia-A 10-Year Single-Center Experience.
abstract: Background/Objectives: We aimed to describe the clinical, laboratory, and radiological characteristics of children with complicated pneumonia/empyema who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and to identify factors associated with length of hospital stay. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 68 children who presented to the pediatric emergency department of a tertiary university hospital and underwent VATS between April 2015 and April 2025. Factors associated with length of stay were assessed using univariable and multivariable negative binomial regression. Results: Median age was 60 months (interquartile range 36-138), and 66% were male. On univariable analysis, C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with length of stay (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.03 per 100 mg/L; p = 0.034), whereas age was not ( p = 0.542). In the multivariable model, CRP remained borderline associated (IRR = 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.06; p = 0.049), whereas performance of computed tomography was not ( p = 0.142). An atypical (gastrointestinal or pain-predominant) presentation occurred in 25%. Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most frequently detected bacterial pathogen, mainly by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction. Conclusions: In this single-center, retrospective cohort, higher CRP at presentation, but not age, was modestly associated with a longer hospital stay; this small association needs confirmation in larger prospective studies, and most children (82%) were managed with VATS alone.

title: Impact of a Nurse-Led, Target-Directed Light Sedation Strategy on the Incidence of Delirium in Septic Patients in the Emergency Intensive Care Unit.
Emergency Department Length of Stay, Employment Status, and Subsequent Risk of Hospitalisation: A survival analysis of linked administrative records in England
abstract: Objectives To investigate the association between time spent in NHS Type 1 emergency departments (EDs, consultant led 24-hour services with full resuscitation facilities) and risk of leaving employment and hospitalisation after leaving the department alive up to two years after attendance. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using linked administrative data from the NHS Emergency Care Dataset, Hospital Episode Statistics, Census 2021, and mortality records. ED length of stay was categorised from under 2 hours to 12 hours or more. Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to estimate the association between ED length of stay and subsequently leaving employment or being hospitalised over a two-year follow-up period, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical characteristics. Results Our study population comprised 3,347,008 individuals aged 25–64 who attended a Type 1 ED in England between April 2021 and March 2023. For leaving employment, adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) increased from 1.04 (95% CI 1.03–1.06) for stays of 2 to Conclusions Prolonged time spent in the ED is associated with poorer outcomes among working-age employees, including reduced labour market participation and increased hospital use. These findings suggest that long ED stays may have wider and longer-term implications beyond immediate clinical outcomes, including potentially for national labour markets and economic growth.

title: Association Between Injury Mechanisms, Hospital Admission, and Length of Stay Among Trauma Patients Aged ≥14 Years in an Adult Emergency Department in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Background Trauma presentations to emergency departments (EDs) encompass a wide range of injury mechanisms and clinical outcomes. Mechanisms of injury may influence both hospital admission and length of stay (LOS). This study examined the association between injury mechanisms and hospital admission as the primary outcome and evaluated LOS as a secondary and exploratory outcome among trauma patients presenting to the ED in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at King Khalid University Hospital, including patients aged 14 years and older who presented with traumatic injuries between January 2019 and April 2025. Hospital admission following the initial ED evaluation was the primary outcome, while LOS among admitted patients was considered a secondary and exploratory outcome. From a database of 10,722 trauma-related records available for screening, patients were randomly selected and assessed against predefined eligibility criteria, with ineligible records replaced by additional randomly selected records until a final sample of 218 eligible ED encounters was obtained. Data were extracted from electronic medical records and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. A pre-specified multivariable logistic regression model was used to assess factors associated with hospital admission. Results A total of 218 patients were included, with a median age of 29.5 years (IQR 22-39); 66.5% were male. Falls were the most frequently documented injury mechanism (49.1%), followed by traffic-related incidents (22.0%). Overall, 32 patients (14.7%) required hospital admission. Among the 30 admitted patients included in the LOS analysis, the median LOS was 5 days (IQR 2-14). Traffic-related injury was associated with higher odds of hospital admission after adjustment for age, sex, and any comorbidity (adjusted OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.49-7.83; p=0.004), whereas age, sex, and the presence of any comorbidity were not significantly associated with admission. Poisoning was associated with longer LOS (median 15 vs 4 days; p=0.042), although this finding was based on only three admitted patients with poisoning. Conclusions Falls were the most frequently documented injury mechanism in this single-center ED cohort, whereas traffic-related injuries were independently associated with higher odds of hospital admission. Poisoning was associated with longer LOS, although this finding was based on a small number of cases and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the distinction between injury mechanisms contributing to ED presentation volume and those associated with greater inpatient utilization.

abstract: Background This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the clinical characteristics, temporal admission patterns, and clinical outcomes of patients with extremity gunshot wounds (GSW) presenting to a tertiary care teaching and research hospital. Methods A total of 123 patients presenting with GSWs affecting at least one extremity between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Injury characteristics, interventions, and clinical outcomes were evaluated. Factors independently associated with hospital length of stay (LOS) and intensive care unit (ICU) admission were identified using negative binomial regression and multivariate logistic regression analyses, respectively. Results Of the patients, 116 (94.3%) were male, with a mean age of 29.9±11.9 years. The lower extremity was the most frequently affected region (69.1%), and 42 of 43 fractures (97.7%) were open fractures. The ICU admission rate was 26.0% (n=32), and in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (n=5). A total of 43.1% of admissions occurred between 18: 00 and 23: 59. In negative binomial regression, concomitant injury (incidence rate ratio [IRR]=6.93; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.82-12.57; p Conclusion Extremity GSWs predominantly affect young males and cluster during evening hours. Concomitant injury and fracture were independently associated with length of hospital stay, whereas reoperation was associated with prolonged hospitalization during the clinical course, while neurovascular injury and concomitant injury independently predict ICU admission.

title: Impact of Pre-Labour Caesarean Delivery for a Low-Risk Indication on Hospital Length of Stay and Costs in Singleton, Nulliparous Women.
abstract: Background Understanding the costs to the healthcare system of caesarean delivery with a low-risk indication ('maternal request') is important for informing policies on its use. Numerous studies have examined hospital length of stay (LOS)-a key driver of hospital costs-by actual mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean). This comparison, however, is misaligned with the information available at the time of antenatal decision-making, as a planned vaginal delivery could result in either an actual vaginal delivery or an emergency intrapartum caesarean. Objectives To compare maternal LOS in hospital and hospital costs for pre-labour caesarean delivery for a low-risk indication with planned vaginal delivery. Methods We conducted a population-based cohort study of all singleton births ≥ 37 weeks from nulliparous pregnancies in British Columbia, Canada, 2013-2023, using the British Columbia Perinatal Data Registry. We identified pre-labour caesarean deliveries for breech presentation (proxies for caesarean deliveries with no medical indication) as well as planned vaginal deliveries. We examined maternal total LOS in hospital, in days, and hospital costs. Differences were estimated using generalized linear models with a gamma distribution and a log link. Results The planned caesarean group comprised 5545 women, and the planned vaginal group comprised 146,270 women (29% emergency caesarean). The total length of hospital stay for the planned caesarean group was 2.9 days and 2.7 days for planned vaginal delivery (absolute difference 0.22 days; relative difference 8.3%, 95% considence interval [CI] -1.75, 19.4). Hospital delivery admission costs were CDN$981 higher (95% CI 886, 1076) for low-risk, pre-labour caesarean delivery than planned vaginal delivery. Conclusion Maternal hospital length of stay for pre-labour caesareans for a low-risk indication was similar to planned vaginal delivery, while hospital costs were 21% higher. These findings provide contemporary evidence to help inform policy development on the use of 'maternal request' caesareans, alongside other clinical, patient, and health system considerations.

title: Hospital capacity and operating room access for emergency general surgery patients : OR access and LOS for short-stay MIS EGS.
Minimally invasive versus open emergency right-sided colectomy for malignant obstruction: a nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study.
journal: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
abstract: Background Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) improves short-term outcomes in elective colectomy, however, the choice of surgical approach in hemodynamically stable patients with obstructing right-sided colon cancer remains unclear in emergency settings. MIS could be considered and the present study aims to evaluate short-term outcomes of MIS in bowel obstructed patients compared with open surgery (OPEN). Methods A retrospective nationwide study including patients from the nationwide Swedish Colorectal Cancer Registry (SCRCR) undergoing emergency right-sided colectomy in Sweden (2017-2023) was conducted. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on sex, age, ASA class, hospital size, and operative timing (on-call vs. daytime). Outcomes included length of stay (LOS), postoperative complications, and surgical quality indicators. Analysis was performed according to intention-to-treat. Results A total of 1147 patients were identified. Of the 1,147 included patients, 99 (8.6%) underwent an initially minimally invasive approach. After matching, 99 patients remained in each group. The conversion rate was 34%. Median LOS was 9 days (IQR 6;14) after OPEN and 6 days (IQR 5;10) after MIS. In quantile regression with bootstrap standard errors, MIS was associated with a 3-day shorter median LOS (median difference - 3.0 days, 95% CI - 4 to - 2, p = 0.002). Postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ 2) occurred in 38.8% after OPEN and in 23.2% after MIS. Logistic regression analysis with robust standard errors showed significantly lower odds of postoperative complications after MIS (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.27-0.83, p = 0.009). No significant differences were observed in re-admission, 90-day mortality, R0 resection, lymph node yield, blood loss or operative time. Conclusion In this nationwide observational cohort, an initially minimally invasive approach was associated with shorter length of stay and fewer postoperative complications. No statistically significant differences were observed in the available short-term surgical and pathological quality indicators. Given the limited number of MIS procedures and potential for residual confounding, these findings support further evaluation of MIS in carefully selected patients.

Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
abstract: Background In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. Materials and methods This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU ® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. Results A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p Conclusion Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

title: Criteria for Safe Hospital Discharge in Bronchiolitis: A Systematic Review.
authors: Paediatric Research in Emergency Departments International Collaborative (PREDICT) Network
abstract: Bronchiolitis is the leading cause of hospital presentation and admission for infants in Australasia. We aimed to synthesise current evidence on the effect of discharge criteria for infants (aged < 12 months) who are presenting to or are admitted to hospital with bronchiolitis, to inform a binational guideline recommendation update. Systematic searches were conducted on MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, Cochrane Library and CINAHL (last search 19 February 2025) for non-randomised studies evaluating hospital discharge criteria in bronchiolitis. The primary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) and readmission rates. The risk of bias (ROBINS-I) and certainty of the evidence (GRADE) were appraised, and findings were narratively synthesised. GRADE evidence-to-decision methodology, expert consensus voting and interest-holder consultation were used to finalise the recommendation update. Two retrospective observational studies were included (N = 2697) (low to very low quality), reporting on unique discharge criteria. In both studies, use of the discharge criteria was associated with a significant reduction in LOS relative to alternative protocols. There was no significant difference in readmission rates observed in either study. There was low to very low certainty evidence across outcomes due to risk of bias, indirectness and imprecision. The review findings informed a recommendation update for safe discharge criteria in the 2025 Australasian Bronchiolitis Guideline update. Updated, prescriptive discharge criteria and flow chart were developed, covering clinical stability, oxygen saturation/support, feeding difficulties, caregiver confidence and education on deterioration, social factors and follow-up. The revised criteria provide clinicians with increased certainty in decision-making in bronchiolitis, albeit with further research needed.

title: General practice follow-up after hospital discharge in older adults: retrospective record analysis in UK primary care.
journal: The British journal of general practice : the journal of the Royal College of General Practitioners
abstract: Background Most hospital admissions are for older patients, who are more likely to be medically complex. Primary care risks after hospital discharge and readmission trajectories are relatively unexplored. Aim To estimate the frequency and nature of errors and harms linked to discharge summary processing in general practice for patients aged ≥65 years; and to explore associations with readmission and healthcare utilisation, using a novel primary care data source. Design and setting Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records (EHRs) from seven purposively sampled general practices in the West Midlands, UK. Method EHRs of patients aged ≥65 years discharged between October 2022 and October 2023 were reviewed. Outcomes included post-discharge healthcare utilisation and costs, frequency and type of discharge actions, error rates (failures to complete requested actions), harms (severity, attribution, and preventability), and 90-day readmissions. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of errors, harms, and readmission. Results Within the cohort of 263 discharged patients, 186 (70.7%) accessed post-discharge care; with 47 out of the 263 patients (17.5%; 95% confidence interval = 13.7 to 23.0) having related readmissions within 90 days. In total, 551 actions were requested in 160 discharge summaries. For those patients who required an action, 20.6% experienced error and 4.4% experienced harm. Most harms resulted in hospital readmission and three out of eight were preventable in primary care. Error and harm disproportionately affected patients who had dementia or a recorded carer. Conclusion General practice should review their processes for responding to patient discharge information in order to improve patient safety post-discharge. Further research into tools to assist practices with transitions is warranted.

title: PHASE-ED: Recorded Emergency Department Stay and Temporal Prediction Across Pandemic Phases at Jordanian Public Hospitals
abstract: Abstract Shorter recorded emergency department stays may reflect changes in care, patient composition or documentation. PHASE-ED characterised recorded stays across pandemic phases, examined recording-period sensitivity and assessed prediction using sparse variables in Jordanian Ministry of Health records. Following a facility and coverage audit of \(\:\text{2017\--2025}\) data, the primary retrospective series comprised \(\:\text{382,018}\) eligible encounters from \(\:\text{85,356}\) patients at one facility during \(\:\text{2018\--2025}\); seven other facility codes contributed separately bounded analyses. Median recorded length of stay was \(\:\text{63.0}\) minutes before COVID, \(\:\text{60.0}\) during COVID and \(\:\text{51.0}\) during recovery. Corresponding \(\:\text{90}\)th percentiles were \(\:\text{317.0}\), \(\:\text{294.0}\) and \(\:\text{156.6}\) minutes, and proportions exceeding six hours were \(\:\text{8.33\%}\), \(\:\text{7.73\%}\) and \(\:\text{1.22\%}\). Recovery medians were already lower before an observed timestamp-precision transition on \(\:\text{23}\) July \(\:\text{2024}\). Historical and recent benchmarks, quantile regression and boosted trees were developed chronologically and evaluated on \(\:\text{191,497}\) later encounters. Test mean absolute error was \(\:\text{49.25}\) minutes for the historical benchmark, \(\:\text{47.66}\) for regression and \(\:\text{48.02}\) for boosted trees; the development simplicity rule retained the historical benchmark. Its nominal \(\:\text{80\%}\) interval covered \(\:\text{91.5\%}\) overall but only \(\:\text{68.7\%}\) within the recorded Resuscitation category. Thus, shorter recovery intervals coexisted with modest predictive gains and uneven uncertainty coverage.

title: Undertriage of Pediatric Major Trauma at a Spanish Pediatric Trauma Center: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Accurate field triage is a cornerstone of an inclusive trauma system, but pediatric undertriage remains poorly characterized outside North America. We aimed to estimate the rate of major trauma undertriage in a Spanish pediatric trauma center, to identify patient factors associated with it, and to explore its relationship with early clinical outcomes. Methods Retrospective cohort study (2016-2025) of children aged 0-14 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of the reference pediatric trauma center for the province of Granada, Spain. Major trauma was defined using a composite of the Cribari Matrix (ISS > 15) and/or the Need for Trauma Intervention (NFTI) criteria. Undertriage was defined as delayed (>2 h) or non-direct transport to the trauma center despite proximity ( Results Out of 1716 PICU admissions during the study period, 157 (9.1%) were due to injury, 131 (7.6%) were eligible traumatic injuries and 94 (5.5%) children met major trauma criteria (median age 8.0 years; 73.4% male; 78.7% blunt trauma; and median ISS 18.5). The undertriage rate was 23.4% (22/94; 95% CI 15.3-33.3). No patient characteristic differed significantly between undertriaged and correctly triaged children. Undertriaged children tended to be older (median 11.0 vs. 7.0 years; p = 0.117), and the overall association between age category and undertriage did not reach significance in the FLIC model ( p = 0.069). One child (1.1%) died in PICU and 75 (79.8%) achieved a good functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale 5). Undertriage was not associated with functional outcome, PICU length of stay or total hospital length of stay in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. Conclusions Nearly one in four children with major trauma who reached this pediatric trauma center met the predefined criteria for undertriage. This rate should be interpreted as undertriage conditional on arrival at the Pediatric Trauma Center and not as a system-level or provincial estimate. Multicenter prospective studies using standardized definitions and incorporating prehospital transport data are needed to better characterize the population-level burden and clinical impact of pediatric undertriage.

Intranasal Dexmedetomidine for Paediatric Procedural Sedation in the Emergency Department: A Single-Centre Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Objectives To describe the use, effectiveness and safety of intranasal dexmedetomidine (IN DEX) for ED paediatric procedural sedation. Method A retrospective cohort study was conducted over 7 months following implementation of an IN DEX guideline at Townsville University Hospital ED. Children aged 1-16 years were eligible if they received IN DEX. Outcomes of interest were sedation depth, ED length of stay (EDLOS), adverse events, procedural success and clinician/carer satisfaction. Results A total of 114 patients were recruited. Median age was 3 years (IQR 2-5), 55.3% were male and 31.6% were Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children. Median IN DEX dose was 3.11 mcg/kg (IQR 2.81-3.93). Common indications included peripheral intravenous cannulation (35.1%), laceration repair (21.1%), burns care (13.2%), foreign body removal (11.4%) and medical imaging (8.8%). Median EDLOS was 395 min (IQR 255-579). Sedation depth was moderate (mean University Michigan Sedation Scale score 2.1 (SD 0.9), a 0-4 scale on which higher scores indicate deeper sedation; documented for 90 of 114 sedations). IN DEX was successful as a sole sedative agent in 78.1% (95% CI 69.6%-84.7%) patients, ranging from 90.0% (9/10) for medical imaging to 53.8% (7/13) for foreign body removal. Adverse events occurred in 13.2% of patients (95% CI 8.1%-20.6%), predominantly mild bradycardia. Younger age was associated with higher success rates (aOR 0.86 per year, 95% CI 0.74-0.998). No dose-response relationship was identified. Clinicians (mean 4.3/5) and parents (mean 4.5/5) reported high satisfaction, although satisfaction was documented for fewer than half of sedations and significantly more often when sedation succeeded. Conclusion In our single-centre study IN DEX is a well-tolerated, moderately effective and safe agent for ED paediatric procedural sedation with higher success rates in younger patients. Large, prospective, multisite studies are necessary to establish IN DEX's safety, effectiveness and predictors of success.

title: The use of a non-invasive neuromonitoring device in the emergency department: comparison with computed tomography results.
journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is widely used to evaluate emergency department (ED) patients with headache, increasing costs, radiation exposure, and workload. Non-invasive intracranial pressure waveform (ICPW) monitoring has been proposed as an adjunctive triage tool. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying abnormal head CT findings in ED patients with red-flag headaches and explored potential resource implications. This retrospective study included 84 patients with red-flag headaches at Hospital Leforte Morumbi, Brazil (June-September 2023). All underwent non-invasive ICPW monitoring (brain4care System) and head CT during the same ED encounter. ICPW was abnormal if P2/P1 ≥ 1.2 or time-to-peak (TTP) ≥ 0.3. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV) were calculated against abnormal CT. CT expenditure and ED length of stay were assessed as exploratory outcomes. ICPW showed 90.0% sensitivity, 66.2% specificity, 98.0% NPV, and 26.5% PPV for abnormal CT. Median P2/P1 ratio yielded an ROC AUC of 0.778 (95% CI 0.640-0.900). Forty-nine patients (58.3%) had both normal ICPW and normal CT; their median ED stay was 3.5 h shorter than that of the overall cohort, though causality cannot be inferred. One patient had normal ICPW despite abnormal CT. Hypothetically, the normal examinations represented a projected gross CT expenditure of US$34,300. The high NPV supports further investigation of ICPW as an adjunctive risk-stratification tool, but the retrospective single-center design, small sample, and few abnormal CTs preclude definitive conclusions. ICPW should not replace clinical assessment or neuroimaging; resource implications remain exploratory hypotheses requiring prospective, multicenter validation.

title: Blood Product Transfusion Patterns in One Lithuanian and Two Polish Academic Emergency Departments: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Blood product transfusion is an important emergency intervention for patients with acute bleeding, severe symptomatic anemia, and selected hematological conditions. Patterns of ED transfusion may differ according to the local case mix, referral pathways, and blood bank processes. We compared transfusion-related characteristics and outcomes among patients treated in one Lithuanian and two Polish academic emergency departments. Materials and Methods : We performed a retrospective comparative study of adults (aged ≥18 years) in whom a blood product transfusion was initiated in the ED between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2024 at one Lithuanian and two Polish academic hospitals. We compared patient characteristics, indication categories, shock index values, time to transfusion, blood product use, adjunctive therapies, laboratory values, ED disposition, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Findings are reported as center-cohort comparisons and are not intended to represent national practice. Results : A total of 670 patients were included: 367 at the Lithuanian center and 303 across the two Polish centers. GI bleeding was significantly more common in the Lithuanian center cohort (48.8% vs. 22.8%; OR 3.22 [95% CI 2.30-4.53]; p p p p p p p p p = 0.002). Hospital admission was significantly more frequent in the Lithuanian cohort than in the Polish cohort (350 (95.4%) vs. 112 (37.0%); p p n = 123) in the Lithuanian cohort and 13.9% ( n = 42) in the Polish cohort (OR 3.13 [95% CI 2.12-4.63]; p Conclusions : Among transfused patients in the three participating academic EDs, the case mix, blood product use, transfusion timing, and unadjusted outcomes differed substantially. These center-specific findings may inform future prospective studies of how referral pathways, clinical populations, and local transfusion processes influence ED blood product utilization. They do not establish differences in national practice, transfusion appropriateness, or causal effects on clinical outcomes.

title: Associations Between Diagnostic Blood-Based Biomarkers and Neuroimaging Findings in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: Study objective Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a prevalent and resource-intensive injury in the emergency department (ED). The blood-based biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have demonstrated diagnostic potential for acute structural brain injury. Our objective was to clinically validate a US Food and Drug Administration-approved plasma test to aid in the identification of intracranial injury in patients with mTBI presenting to the ED and assess its integration with existing protocols. Methods This single-center validation study enrolled 104 adult patients with suspected mTBI undergoing head computed tomography (CT) for evaluation between October 2023 and June 2024 at a Level I trauma center. Peripheral blood draw was completed within 12 hours postinjury and processed at the hospital clinical laboratory. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for the test were calculated and compared with a standard clinical decision rule (Canadian Head CT Rule). ED length of stay and diagnostic turnaround times were examined. Results Within the cohort (n=104), 83 patients had elevated biomarker levels (GFAP >30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 >360 pg/mL), and 11 patients had intracranial injury identified on CT. The combination plasma test demonstrated high sensitivity (0.91 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.59 to 1.00]) but low specificity (0.22 [95% CI 0.14 to 0.31]) for predicting intracranial injury on CT with low positive predictive value (0.12 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.21]) and high negative predictive value (0.95 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.00]). These findings are consistent with prior studies (pooled sensitivity 0.97 [95% CI 0.95 to 0.98]; specificity 0.28 [95% CI 0.23 to 0.34]). False-positive cases (78%) were older than true-negative cases (median 72 years [interquartile range (IQR) 54 to 83] versus 58.5 years [IQR 38.25 to 66]). Median turnaround time for the GFAP/UCH-L1 test was 2 hours faster than head CT (1.09 hours [IQR 0.87 to 1.65] versus 3.28 hours [IQR 2.37 to 4.70]). Conclusions Blood biomarkers for mTBI have potential as an initial rule-out tool for intracranial injury prior to obtaining CT imaging; however, large multicenter studies are needed to clarify its impact on ED resource utilization, length of stay, and acute and long-term costs and benefits to patients and health care systems.

title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Conventional triage relies on clinician judgment and limited information available at first contact. AI and machine learning (ML) may improve early risk stratification, whereas tele-triage and patient-facing tools primarily support remote assessment, access, and care routing. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of AI- and ML-assisted triage systems and summarize evidence on tele-triage, workflow, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes. Methods Comparative studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, evaluating AI-, ML-, natural language processing-, telehealth-, or digitally enhanced triage. At first, clinical contacts were included. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, preprint servers, trial registries, and conference proceedings were searched. Screening and data extraction were performed independently in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Clinically comparable area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) estimates were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis; heterogeneous diagnostic, operational, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes were summarized narratively. Exploratory scenario modeling projected effects per 10,000 emergency department (ED) visits. Results Twenty-seven studies were included, comprising 13 studies in the quantitative evidence stream and 14 in the narrative synthesis. Four adult ED studies evaluating critical care or deterioration outcomes demonstrated high pooled discrimination for AI-assisted triage (AUC 0.874; 95% CI 0.845-0.898; I ²=94.4%; 95% prediction interval 0.803-0.922). Four studies reported directly extractable within-study comparisons favoring AI-assisted models (AUC differences of 0.097, 0.120, 0.108, and 0.065), although these could not be pooled because paired variance estimates were unavailable. Admission/disposition studies reported AI-model AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.93 and were summarized descriptively because extreme heterogeneity precluded meaningful pooling. Two pediatric studies (AUCs of 0.85-0.99) were summarized descriptively. Prediction-model studies were primarily limited by deficiencies in model analysis, calibration reporting, and external validation. Narrative evidence suggested improved front-door operational metrics with tele-triage, including reported reductions of 15%-40% in time to clinical assessment and 2-8 percentage points in left-without-being-seen rates, whereas patient-facing symptom checkers generally favored sensitivity over specificity. Exploratory scenario modeling illustrated that, under specified prevalence and threshold assumptions, AI-assisted triage could be associated with 12-38 fewer missed critical illness cases and 45-120 additional false-positive escalations per 10,000 ED visits. Economic and equity findings were assumption-dependent projections rather than observed clinical, cost-effectiveness, or equity outcomes. Conclusions AI- and ML-assisted triage models demonstrate promising discrimination for adult ED risk stratification; however, AUC-based discrimination does not establish superiority at clinically relevant decision thresholds, improved patient outcomes, or readiness for clinical implementation. Interpretation is limited by substantial heterogeneity, incomplete threshold-level performance and calibration reporting, limited external validation, and sparse pediatric evidence. Prospective multicenter validation, workflow assessment, subgroup calibration and equity auditing, and formal economic evaluation are required before routine implementation.
