title: Association between timely and standardized nursing pain management and outcomes in terminal cancer patients: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Effective pain management is essential for terminal cancer patients in emergency settings, yet nursing protocol adherence remains suboptimal. This study aimed to evaluate the association between key nursing process indicators and pain relief outcomes in terminal cancer patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) and to examine clinical outcomes according to adherence to an optimized nursing pain management workflow. We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 724 terminal cancer patients who visited the ED of the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University between January 2017 and December 2023. Eligible patients presented with pain as a primary complaint and had complete clinical and nursing documentation. Data were extracted on demographics, cancer type, pain scores, timing of analgesic administration, and reassessment practices. The primary outcome was effective pain relief, defined as a ≥2-point reduction on the numeric rating scale within 1 hour of analgesia. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors. Patients were stratified into an optimized care group (completion of pain assessment within 30 minutes, analgesia within 30 minutes, and reassessment within 1 hour) and a routine care group. Of the 724 patients included, 58.2% achieved effective pain relief. Multivariate analysis revealed that timely pain assessment (odds ratio [OR] = 1.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.26-2.69), analgesic administration within 30 minutes (OR = 2.24, 95% CI: 1.57-3.21), opioid use (OR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.06-2.20), and documented pain reassessment (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.22-2.35) were independently associated with improved pain outcomes. Patients in the optimized care group (n = 286) had significantly higher pain relief rates (75.9% vs 46.6%, P < .001), faster relief onset (29.6 ± 11.3 vs 52.7 ± 15.9 minutes, P < .001), shorter ED stays (3.4 ± 1.1 vs 4.7 ± 1.4 hours, P < .001), and lower 72-hour revisit rates (7.3% vs 21.0%, P < .001). Timely and standardized nursing interventions were associated with more favorable pain relief and emergency department care-efficiency outcomes among terminal cancer patients. These findings support the integration of structured nursing protocols into emergency palliative care, although prospective studies are needed to determine their causal effects.

Changes in patient concentration and accessibility across 5 Pediatric Emergency Departments in Daegu, Korea.
abstract: Background The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has substantially altered Pediatric Emergency Department (PED) utilization. However, longitudinal changes across multiple PEDs after major policy transitions remain unclear. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate changes in utilization, patient distribution, accessibility to pediatric emergency care, and clinical characteristics across 5 participating PEDs in Daegu, Korea. Methods This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 140,017 visits among patients aged Results Median monthly population-standardized visit rates were 580.9, 315.8, and 500.1/100,000 child personmonths in the pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID periods, respectively (P Conclusion These findings indicate patient redistribution across the 5 participating PEDs serving Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do. Visit volume recovered after the COVID period, whereas patient distribution became increasingly concentrated with longer door-to-ER distances and greater reliance on emergency medical services, suggesting reduced accessibility.

title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery in Pediatric Urology Patients Undergoing Complex Lower Urinary Tract Reconstruction.
abstract: Importance Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) is a multidisciplinary framework to standardize perioperative care. Pediatric Urology Recovery After Surgery Endeavor (PURSUE) is a multicenter study of ERAS in children undergoing complex lower urinary tract reconstruction. Use of ERAS in children is still relatively uncommon and outcomes are not well understood. Objective To attempt to achieve 70% or more ERAS adherence while reducing length of stay and opioid use without an increase in complications or other balancing measures. Design, setting, and participants This study prospectively enrolled patients who were propensity matched to recent historical controls prior to ERAS implementation and outcomes were compared. From 2017 through 2022, 8 pediatric hospitals implemented ERAS for pediatric patients undergoing catheterizable channel creation, bladder augmentation, and/or bladder neck procedures. Patients aged 4 to 24 years undergoing these operations were prospectively enrolled in the study. Patients with unmanaged neurogenic bowel were excluded. Patients who underwent these operations in the 5 years prior to protocol implementation at each center were used as a comparator group. These data were analyzed from July 2022 to April 2025. Intervention ERAS protocol encompassing 20 evidence-based preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative elements was designed and implemented as standard of care. Patients were followed up postoperatively for a minimum of 1 year. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was compliance with the ERAS protocol. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, opioid usage, pain scores, 90-day complications, and 90-day balancing measures of return to hospital. Results A total of 153 ERAS patients and 153 historical controls were matched with a median (IQR) age of 10.2 (7.6-13.7) and 10.4 (8.0-14.6) years, respectively (P = .47). Median protocol adherence increased from 8 to 16 measures between historical and ERAS cohorts (P Conclusions and relevance In this study, ERAS was highly effective at standardizing perioperative care in pediatric urology patients undergoing complex lower urinary tract reconstruction. ERAS was associated with better outcomes of reduced length of stay, lower postoperative opioid use, and lower complication rates.

title: A Simplified Physiology-Laboratory Score (PLS4) for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Cholangitis.
abstract: Objectives: Acute cholangitis is a common biliary infection in the emergency department (ED) that can progress rapidly to septic shock and multiorgan dysfunction. The Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG2018) is the current reference standard for severity assessment but may be cumbersome during the initial ED encounter. We aimed to develop a simplified physiology-laboratory score (PLS4) computable from four routine bedside variables and to compare its early risk-stratification performance with TG2018. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included 482 adult patients with acute cholangitis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code K83.0) presenting to a tertiary university hospital ED between January 2016 and December 2021. Primary outcomes were ICU admission, vasopressor use, and prolonged hospital stay (length of stay ≥ 14 days); intubation was analyzed as an exploratory outcome. PLS4 assigned 1 point each for albumin Results: ICU admission occurred in 81 patients (16.8%), vasopressor use in 53 (11.0%), and prolonged stay in 111 (23.0%). The areas under the curve (AUCs) for ICU admission were 0.850 for TG2018 and 0.800 for PLS4 ( p = 0.116), and the optimism-corrected AUC of PLS4 was 0.779. For vasopressor use, which is part of the TG2018 grade III definition, the AUCs were 0.936 and 0.843. When PLS4 was added to TG2018, the AUC for ICU admission increased to 0.886. At PLS4 ≥ 3, specificity reached 0.978 for ICU admission and 0.970 for vasopressor use, with event rates rising stepwise from 5.96% to 100% and 2.55% to 90.0%, respectively. Conclusions: In this single-center derivation study, PLS4 showed high specificity and added prognostic information to TG2018. It should be validated in other centers before clinical use.

title: Prehospital management and hospital outcomes of severely injured patients during routine civilian mass casualty incidents: a 1:4 matched cohort analysis of the TraumaRegister DGU<sup>®</sup>.
abstract: Background Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) pose substantial challenges to prehospital emergency medical systems due to limited resources and the need for rapid prioritization. Evidence regarding the impact of routine civilian MCIs on the management and outcomes of severely injured patients remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of MCIs on prehospital care, transport strategies, and clinical outcomes compared with routine individual care. Methods Data from the TraumaRegister DGU ® were analysed for patients treated in Germany between mid-2020 and 2023. Patients with severe trauma (Maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale; MAIS ≥ 3) were included. Mass casualty incident cases were identified based on registry documentation. A 1:4 matched cohort was performed using age group, injury pattern and traffic involvement as matching criteria. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality; secondary endpoints included prehospital time intervals, performed interventions, and transport strategies. An additional multivariable logistic regression was performed as a sensitivity analysis of the primary endpoint. Results A total of 65,152 patients were included, of whom 430 were treated during mass casualty incidents (MCIs). After matching, 423 MCI patients were compared with 1,692 controls. Patients treated during MCIs had slightly higher injury severity (Injury Severity Score (ISS) 24.8 vs. 20.3). Median total prehospital time was significantly longer in the MCI group (85 [IQR 67-100] vs. 67 [IQR 53-83] minutes; p Conclusion Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) were associated with prolonged prehospital care and modified transport strategies. No statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between MCI patients and matched controls. These findings describe outcomes among severely injured patients captured by the TraumaRegister DGU ® but should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and the observational study design.

Digital Health-Enabled Prehospital Notification for Acute Stroke Using the Brain Saver Mobile App in Emergency Medical Transport in South Korea: Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study.
abstract: Background Timely access to stroke care is critical for patient prognosis. Despite the growing use of digital health strategies in stroke management, evidence supporting seamless and timely care coordination from the emergency medical services (EMS) to the emergency department (ED) remains limited. Brain Saver, a newly developed mobile app, addresses this gap by facilitating real-time data sharing between EMS personnel and ED clinicians during stroke transport. Objective This study aimed to examine the potential of the Brain Saver protocol to improve existing EMS-ED workflows in emergency stroke transport by describing its functional components, implementing a pilot intervention in a real-world setting, and exploring its preliminary impact on treatment timeliness. Methods Data were collected in Pohang, South Korea, from December 2023 to April 2024 through collaboration with 2 fire stations, eight 119 EMS and safety centers, 3 hospitals, and SEERS Technology. Preintervention training and postintervention surveys were conducted among EMS personnel (n=80) and clinicians (n=24). In this pilot, patients with stroke (ICD-10 [International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision] codes I60-I63) in the intervention group (n=34) were transported using ambulances equipped with the Brain Saver mobile app, while the comparison group (n=129) was transported by standard ambulances to the same hospitals during the study period. With "needle" defined as any parenteral treatment, onset-to-door time and door-to-needle time were compared by group. After exact matching on age, baseline stroke severity, stroke type, and destination hospital, intervention effects were estimated using generalized estimating equations. Results Participants (N=163) had a mean age of 69.4 (SD 15.2) years, 50.3% (82/163) were male, and 65.6% (107/163) had ischemic stroke. No significant baseline differences, including stroke severity, were observed between groups. The median onset-to-needle time was shorter in the intervention group than in the comparison group (114 vs 204 minutes; P=.03). In the matched analytic sample (n=91), the intervention group showed significant reductions in onset-to-needle time (Exp(β)=0.49; P=.009) and door-to-needle time (Exp(β)=0.67; P=.04) compared with the comparison group. Conclusions Integrating digital health into emergency stroke transport may improve care timeliness by supporting real-time prehospital notification and facilitating prompt in-hospital responses. The Brain Saver mobile app shows potential use for reducing onset-to-treatment time. Further larger-scale studies are needed to evaluate implementation fidelity and scalability.

Heat stroke during the 2025 summer heatwave in Northwestern India: A tertiary care emergency department case series.
abstract: Heat stroke is a life-threatening medical emergency, characterized by a core body temperature above 40°C with central nervous system dysfunction. Population living in arid and northwestern regions are particularly vulnerable during prolonged summer heatwaves. This case series describes the clinical spectrum and outcomes of patients with heat stroke presenting to the emergency department of a tertiary care teaching hospital in such a region during the 2025 heatwaves. We retrospectively reviewed 10 consecutive patients with heat stroke admitted between May 1, 2025 and July 31, 2025. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, cooling methods, laboratory parameters, complications, and outcomes were extracted from the medical records. Ten patients (7 male and 3 female) ranged in age from 22 to 78 years; six had classic (nonexertional) heat stroke; and four had exertional heat stroke (EHS). All presented with hyperthermia (mean 41.2°C) and altered mental status, ranging from agitation to coma. The complications were frequent: acute kidney injury occurred in 70% of patients, severe rhabdomyolysis (creatine phosphokinase >10,000 U/L) in 40% (all EHS), hepatic dysfunction in 80%, and disseminated intravascular coagulation in 20%. Rapid, active cooling was initiated in all cases. The overall in-hospital mortality was 20%. This series highlights the severe, multisystem nature of heat stroke in this setting and underlines the importance of early recognition, prompt cooling, and aggressive supportive care.

title: Age and intensive care unit admissions following opioid overdose.
Physiological reserve and early recovery across oncologic and non-oncologic abdominal surgery: a prospective multicenter interaction analysis.
abstract: Background Frailty and low handgrip strength are established markers of limited physiological reserve, but it is uncertain whether their prognostic meaning differs between oncologic and non-oncologic surgery. We examined whether oncologic indication modifies the associations of preoperative frailty and baseline handgrip strength with early postoperative outcomes. Methods This secondary analysis used a prospective cohort conducted at participating surgical centers between January 2023 and June 2025. Frailty was classified using the Fried phenotype, and handgrip strength was measured at admission. The primary outcome was prolonged length of stay (LOS >10 days); secondary outcomes were any postoperative complication, major complications, and log-transformed LOS. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms in multivariable logistic models adjusted for age and sex. Because no prolonged stays occurred among fit patients in the non-oncologic stratum, categorical frailty models used Firth penalized logistic regression. Results Among 222 clinically characterized participants, 118 (53.2%) underwent oncologic surgery. Prolonged LOS occurred in 41/118 (34.7%) oncologic and 7/104 (6.7%) non-oncologic patients. The complete-case primary analysis included 216 patients and 45 events. In an additional ordinal main-effects model, increasing frailty [odds ratio (OR) 2.91 per category, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.57-5.38], lower handgrip strength (OR 0.95 per kg, 95% CI 0.90-0.99), and oncologic indication (OR 8.97, 95% CI 3.47-23.19) were associated with prolonged LOS. However, categorical frailty-by-oncology interaction was not supported (global p = 0.341), nor was handgrip-strength-by-oncology interaction ( p = 0.739); the joint interaction test was not statistically significant ( p = 0.525). No convincing effect modification was observed for complications or continuous LOS. Conclusions Oncologic surgery was associated with a substantially higher early postoperative burden, while frailty and handgrip strength retained prognostic relevance. No clear evidence of multiplicative interaction by oncologic indication was detected, but clinically meaningful effect modification cannot be excluded. Physiological reserve assessment should therefore be considered across elective abdominal surgery rather than restricted to the oncologic setting.

Factors associated with mortality among critically ill pediatric patients referred to a tertiary hospital in Indonesia.
abstract: Background An efficient referral system is an important but often under-recognized determinant of survival in critically ill children. Previous studies have reported high mortality rates among pediatric patients transferred to tertiary care facilities. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-level referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Material and methods This prospective cohort study was conducted over a 12-month period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024) and included all critically ill children admitted to the PICU following interhospital referral. Demographic, clinical, referral, and transport data were prospectively collected. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PICU mortality. Results A total of 334 children were included, with a median age of 6 years. PICU mortality was 25.4%. The most common referral indication based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was central nervous system dysfunction. Pre-referral management most commonly included oxygen therapy, antibiotic administration, and fluid resuscitation. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher PELOD-2 scores and were more likely to require intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive support before referral. In the multivariable analysis, pre-referral vasoactive support (adjusted OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.20-4.15; P = 0.011) and higher PELOD-2 scores within the first 24 hours after PICU admission (adjusted OR 1.32 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 1.20-1.45; P Conclusion PICU mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-care hospital in Indonesia remains high. Pre-referral vasoactive support and higher PELOD-2 scores at PICU admission were independently associated with PICU mortality. These findings generate the hypothesis that improvements in early stabilization and communication may improve outcomes, warranting prospective evaluation.

title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
abstract: Purpose Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain. Materials & methods Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality. Results The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p Conclusion The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

Frailty is associated with prolonged hospitalization and inferior patient-reported outcomes after acute quadriceps tendon rupture: A multicenter cohort study.
journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
abstract: Background Quadriceps tendon rupture is a functionally devastating injury frequently affecting patients with high comorbidity burden and impaired physiological reserve. Frailty represents an age-independent construct of diminished physiological resilience; its impact on hospitalization and long-term functional outcomes after quadriceps tendon rupture remains poorly defined. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 67 adults who underwent surgical repair or reconstruction for acute quadriceps tendon rupture (≤4 weeks) at four tertiary centers between 2019 and 2023. Pre-operative frailty was quantified using the 5-item modified frailty index (mFI-5) and the 9-point clinical frailty scale (CFS). CFS was assigned retrospectively by two orthopedic surgeons using dual-reviewer consensus (κ=0.82). Primary outcomes were length of hospital stay (LOS) and functional recovery at ≥12 months (Lysholm Knee Scoring Scale); Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score and complications were secondary. Multivariable models were a priori restricted (six predictors for LOS, four for Lysholm; observations-per-predictor ≈11: 1 and ≈17: 1) and adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, comorbidity burden, surgical technique, and follow-up. Results Mean age was 57.5±12.1 years; 79.1% male. Higher mFI-5 scores were associated with prolonged LOS (r=0.404, p Conclusion Frailty is associated with prolonged hospitalization and poorer patient-reported outcomes after surgical repair of quadriceps tendon rupture. Integration of mFI-5 and CFS into routine pre-operative evaluation may refine surgical planning, discharge coordination, and rehabilitation intensity.

Virtual Wards for Acute Care Patients: A Scoping Review.
Prehospital Transfusion With Red Blood Cells and Fresh Plasma in Helicopter Emergency Medical Services.
abstract: Background Prehospital administration of blood products is a growing practice. We aimed to describe clinical parameters and mortality following prehospital blood component therapy with red blood cells (RBC) and/or plasma in patients with traumatic and non-traumatic haemorrhage. Methods An retrospective cohort study was performed on patients receiving prehospital transfusion products at the Danish national Helicopter Emergency Medical service between 2014 and 2020 with addition of a recent period 2023-2024. Data was collected from relevant data bases and electronic patient journals and analysed descriptively and statistically. Results We identified 393 patients who received prehospital transfusion (280 trauma and 113 non-trauma). Prehospital transfusion rate was low (0.9% of missions) with no change during the period studied. Mortality rates for the entire cohort were 13% at 24 h and 26% at 30 days. Trauma patients were significantly younger 49 (IQR; 28-68) vs. 71 (IQR; 60-77)), with lower Glasgow coma score scale; 3 (IQR; 3-14) vs. 15 (IQR; 3-15) and more days on ventilator; 3 (IQR; 1-8) days vs. 2 (IQR; 0-3) days), in intensive care; 5 (IQR; 2-12) days vs. 2 (IQR; 0-4) days) and longer hospital stay 16 (IQR; 6-38) days vs. 8 (IQR; 3-16) days). Lactate trauma-group: 3.2 (IQR; 1.9-5.8), non-trauma: 5.1 (IQR; 2.3-9.4) mmol/L and base excess trauma-group: -4.9 (IQR; -9 to -2.3), non-trauma: -8 (IQR; -15.6 to -4) mmol/L were outside reference range indicating circulatory shock at hospital arrival while standard coagulation parameters were normal or near-normal. Mortality was significantly higher in non-trauma patients as compared with trauma (11% vs. 22%, p = 0.04). Conclusion Prehospital transfusion was uncommon, did not change over time and was associated with biochemical parameters near the normal reference range. Twenty-four-hour mortality was higher among non-trauma patients compared with trauma patients. Editorial comment Some forms of advanced care can be delivered to critically ill or injured patients on their way emergently to hospital, for example in air ambulances. In this cohort of cases which included significant haemorrhage, administration of component blood products was analysed for associations with case conditions and health outcomes.

Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group ( p p = 0.001) and ICU ( p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions : In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
Adjunctive gabexate mesylate with octreotide and clinical outcomes in older adults with acute pancreatitis: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Acute pancreatitis (AP) in older adults is associated with higher risks of systemic inflammatory response, organ dysfunction, and prolonged clinical recovery. Pharmacologic interventions targeting early protease activation and exocrine pancreatic secretion may have therapeutic value in this population; however, evidence in elderly patients remains limited. Methods This retrospective study included 220 adults aged ≥60 years hospitalized with AP between July 2021 and July 2025. Among them, 108 received octreotide plus gabexate mesylate and 112 received octreotide monotherapy. Primary outcomes were times to abdominal pain relief, pancreatic enzyme normalization, and gastrointestinal recovery. Multiple linear and multivariable logistic regression models were used to adjust for prespecified demographic and clinical covariates. Results Combination therapy was associated with shorter times to abdominal pain relief (adjusted mean difference -0.95 days; 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.28 to -0.62), pancreatic enzyme normalization (-1.28 days; 95% CI, -1.67 to -0.89), gastrointestinal recovery (-0.86 days; 95% CI -1.25 to -0.47), and hospital discharge (-1.62 days; 95% CI, -2.47 to -0.77; all P ≤ 0.001). It was also associated with higher odds of radiological improvement among re-imaged patients (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.16-2.86) and lower odds of new-onset or persistent systemic inflammatory response syndrome (adjusted OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.38-0.98) and infectious complications (adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.29-0.99). Drug-related adverse events, composite organ dysfunction, mortality, and readmission did not differ significantly. No treatment-by-severity interaction was identified. Conclusion Adjunctive gabexate mesylate was associated with modestly faster short-term recovery in older adults with acute pancreatitis, without a significant increase in drug-related adverse events. Its effects on organ dysfunction and mortality remain uncertain and require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

title: Obesity and cellulitis: Associations with infection severity, recurrence, and healthcare utilization-A systematic review.
abstract: Background Obesity is a growing global health concern associated with chronic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and impaired skin barrier function, all of which may increase susceptibility to cellulitis and influence clinical outcomes. This systematic literature review synthesized current evidence examining the relationship between obesity and cellulitis risk, infection severity, and healthcare utilization. Methods This PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review and narrative synthesis searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science for English-language primary studies published from January 2015 through December 2025. Eligible studies involved adults with cellulitis or erysipelas-or adult population cohorts reporting a separable cellulitis/erysipelas-specific outcome-evaluating body mass index (BMI) or obesity as an exposure or predictor. Target outcomes comprised cellulitis development or hospitalization, recurrence, treatment response or failure, severity, length of stay, readmission, cost, and mortality. Given the substantial heterogeneity across study designs and outcome definitions, findings were synthesized narratively. When sufficiently complete primary reports were available, risk of bias was evaluated using design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools (Appendix 4). Results Eighteen primary studies met the eligibility criteria. Across population cohorts and cellulitis-specific clinical studies, higher BMI or obesity was generally associated with greater cellulitis risk (e.g., ORs ranging from 1.11 to 4.7) and, in several studies, recurrence or increased healthcare utilization (such as prolonged length of stay). However, associations were not uniform: some studies reported null findings for treatment failure or readmission. The evidence base was predominantly observational and methodologically heterogeneous, so conclusions regarding downstream clinical outcomes are less certain than those regarding cellulitis risk and incidence. Conclusion Obesity is an important risk marker of cellulitis susceptibility and adverse clinical outcomes. Future studies using standardized outcome measures and improved assessments of adiposity beyond BMI are needed to guide prevention strategies and optimize management of this growing population.

title: Comparison of Laparoscopic-Assisted Transversus Abdominis Plane Block and Trocar-Site Local Anesthetic Infiltration After Laparoscopic Appendectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background and objective Abdominal wall blocks are increasingly used for pain control following laparoscopic appendectomy. This study aimed to compare the analgesic efficacy of a transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block performed by the surgical team under direct laparoscopic visualization with trocar-site infiltration using an equal total dose of local anesthetic (LA). Materials and methods Sixty patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy for uncomplicated acute appendicitis between August 2017 and January 2018 were prospectively randomized in a 1:1 ratio into two groups. In the TAP group (n = 30), 15 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine was administered bilaterally under direct laparoscopic visualization before appendectomy. In the LA group (n = 30), 5 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine was infiltrated at each trocar site before incision. The total bupivacaine dose was standardized to 75 mg in both groups. Pain intensity was measured using the visual analog scale (VAS) at postoperative hours 0, 2, 6, 12, and 24. The two groups were compared in terms of rescue analgesic consumption; time to first mobilization, first passage of flatus, and initiation of oral intake; nausea and vomiting; complications; and length of hospital stay. Results The groups were comparable in terms of age, sex, body mass index, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score (all p > 0.05). VAS scores were significantly lower in the TAP group at all measured time points (hour 0, p = 0.005; hour 2, p = 0.022; hour 6, p = 0.020; hour 12, p = 0.020; and hour 24, p = 0.001; effect sizes, r = 0.34-0.49). In the TAP group, 19 of 30 patients (63.3%) required no rescue analgesia during the first 24 hours, compared with 11 of 30 (36.7%) in the LA group (p = 0.039); the total number of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) doses per patient was significantly lower in the TAP group (p = 0.023). Although opioid requirements were numerically lower in the TAP group, the difference did not reach statistical significance (2/30, 6.7% vs. 7/30, 23.3%; p = 0.071). Oral intake was initiated earlier in the TAP group (median, 8.0 vs. 10.0 hours; p = 0.018). The median length of hospital stay was 24.0 hours in the TAP group and 32.0 hours in the LA group (p = 0.002), and the proportions of patients discharged within 24 hours were 16 of 30 (53.3%) and 3 of 30 (10.0%), respectively (p Conclusions A surgeon-performed TAP block under laparoscopic visualization provides lower pain scores and reduces analgesic consumption during the first 24 hours following laparoscopic appendectomy compared with trocar-site infiltration using an equal dose of LA. As it requires neither additional equipment nor ultrasonographic expertise, this technique represents a feasible option in emergency surgical practice.

title: Targeting indocyanine green where it matters most: a CRP-stratified cohort study in acute cholecystitis.
Final Diagnoses and Outcomes After Paramedic-Suspected ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
abstract: Study objective Emergency medical services activate ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) pathways before biomarkers, imaging, or angiography are available. We sought to describe final hospital diagnoses, inhospital care, and outcomes among patients attended by paramedics for suspected STEMI in a statewide ambulance registry. Methods We conducted a retrospective statewide registry cohort study using the Victorian Ambulance STEMI Quality Initiative, with hospital follow-up data from January 2020 to June 2025. Principal International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM) discharge diagnoses were grouped as STEMI; non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome or other coronary syndromes; other cardiac diagnoses; noncardiac diagnoses; and symptom-based diagnoses. Outcomes included out-of-hospital management, coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention, complications, hospital length of stay, inhospital death, 30-day death, and mortality during follow-up. Associations were estimated with multivariable logistic and Cox regression and are reported as odds ratios or hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Results Among 8,077 suspected STEMI visits with hospital follow-up data, 7,205 (89.2%) had a recorded discharge diagnosis and formed the primary analytic cohort; 872 (10.8%) had no recorded discharge diagnosis. Among the 7,205 with a recorded diagnosis, STEMI was confirmed in 4,330 (60.1%); 824 (11.4%) had non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome or other coronary syndromes, 760 (10.5%) other cardiac diagnoses, 613 (8.5%) noncardiac diagnoses, and 678 (9.4%) symptom-based diagnoses. Coronary angiography occurred in 4,836 (67.1%) and percutaneous coronary intervention in 3,200 (44.4%). Inhospital mortality was 8.6%, 30-day mortality 6.5%, and mortality during follow-up 17.5% (median follow-up 2.8 years). Compared with confirmed STEMI, adjusted mortality during follow-up was higher for noncardiac diagnoses (hazard ratio [HR] 1.75, 95% confidence interval [CR], 1.47 to 2.09); other cardiac (HR 1.14, 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.39), NSTE-ACS or other coronary (HR 1.16, 95% CI, 0.98 to 1.38), and symptom-based diagnoses (HR 1.09, 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34) did not differ materially from STEMI after adjustment. Conclusion Within this statewide pathway population, paramedic-suspected STEMI identified a diagnostically heterogeneous, high-acuity group, in which approximately 60% of patients with a recorded discharge diagnosis had confirmed STEMI. These findings describe the suspected STEMI pathway population and should not be generalized to all confirmed STEMI or to all chest pain presentations. Emergency medical services and emergency department STEMI systems should preserve rapid access to reperfusion while supporting early diagnostic refinement and risk stratification for serious alternative diagnoses.

title: Functional Neurological Disorder Management in a Pediatric Hospital: A Retrospective Chart Review.
abstract: Background Functional neurological disorder (FND) is a complex, multinetwork brain disorder that is characterized by the presence of a broad range of neurological symptoms in the absence of neurological disease or damage. For pediatric patients requiring an in-patient stay, misdiagnosis, lack of provider consistency and diagnostic education, frequent testing and work-up, and invasive procedures are often reported. This review will characterize the population, identify current state for receiving diagnosis, detect variability in service delivery, and provide information to evaluate use of resources. Methods This retrospective chart review examined electronic medical records (EMRs) of 59 patients at a pediatric teaching hospital who were admitted following a visit to the emergency department. Records were compiled by the rehabilitation department with inclusion criteria as having a documented diagnosis of FND or as having a similar functional movement related diagnosis such as chorea, panic disorder, and psychogenic nonepileptic seizure (PNES). Extracted data included the following: demographics, patient characteristics, admission characteristics and experience, and discharge recommendations. Results Fifty-nine charts were initially reviewed with 57 meeting inclusion criteria. The subjects in this study had a mean age of 13.7 years (SD: 6.33) and 80.7% were female. The most commonly reported psychiatric diagnoses included anxiety (66.7%), ADHD (29.6%), and depression (22.2%). The most commonly reported FND symptoms at admission were weakness (47.4%), gait instability (28.1%), sensory disturbances (26.3%), and tremor (19.1%). Physical therapy consultations were the most frequently performed (66.7%), followed by occupational therapy (52.6%), psychiatry (38.6%), and psychology (5.3%). No interdisciplinary care conferences were performed. The mean length of stay was 5.13 days (SD: 4.45 days). Readmission rate after 30 days was 16.5%. Conclusions This retrospective EMR review identifies opportunities to improve care for pediatric FND, including reducing unnecessary imaging, testing, and readmissions through strengthened provider, patient, and family education. Findings also highlight inconsistent referrals to physical therapy, occupational therapy, and mental health services. Addressing these gaps may enhance patient experience, support more coordinated interdisciplinary care, and reduce healthcare utilization for this under-recognized population.

title: Role of extended venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in patients with colorectal neoplasia who underwent minimally invasive colorectal surgery within an enhanced recovery after surgery protocol.
Impact of Skin Color on the Clinical Diagnosis and Outcomes of Acute Limb Ischemia.
Machine Learning Prediction of 90-Day Readmission and Mortality in General Internal Medicine: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting post-discharge outcomes in general internal medicine (GIM) is essential for targeted intervention. This study developed machine learning (ML) models to predict 90-day hospital readmission and 90-day all-cause post-discharge mortality using routine clinical data. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 935 adult admissions to a tertiary GIM department (January 2022-December 2023), of which 881 were retained after data quality verification. Six ML algorithms-Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Network, and Voting Ensemble-were evaluated across admission-only (Tier 1) and discharge-augmented (Tier 2) feature sets using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), SelectKBest feature selection, and five-fold cross-validated hyperparameter tuning. Results: The 90-day readmission and mortality rates were 33.4% and 4.8%, respectively. Mortality models substantially outperformed readmission models (best admission-model AUC 0.821 for the Voting Ensemble vs. 0.645 for Logistic Regression in readmission; best discharge-model mortality AUC 0.828 for Logistic Regression, 95% CI: 0.694-0.930). Discharge models did not improve over admission models for either outcome. Key mortality predictors included code status, albumin level, functional dependence, and age. Conclusions: Admission-available clinical variables enabled good discrimination of 90-day mortality but only modest readmission prediction. Given the low events-per-variable ratio and single-centre design, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require external validation before clinical implementation.

title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted PERT-workflow and its association with care processes and budget impact: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Aims Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. In intermediate-high and high-risk PE, timely escalation beyond anticoagulation is critical, yet real-world pathways are often delayed. Pulmonary embolism response teams (PERTs) improve decision-making, but activation remains inconsistent. Whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled triage strengthens PERT and improves acute PE care has not been elucidated so far. Methods and results We retrospectively screened 2500 patients presenting to our university hospital with a symptomatic central or segmental PE between 08/2022 and 07/2024. Clinical and economic outcomes were compared during a 1-year timeframe before and after implementation of an AI algorithm that analyses CT scans, flags suspected PE, and supports PERT triage. 424 patients met inclusion criteria. AI-supported triage increased PERT activation from 9.2% to 84.5% ( P P P Conclusion Implementation of an AI-supported PERT workflow was associated with significant improvements in PE care processes, including higher PERT activation rates and shorter diagnostic and treatment intervals. Numerical reductions in mortality, hospital/ICU length-of-stay did not reach statistical significance. The exploratory budget impact model suggested potential cost savings, mainly driven by trends in reduced resource utilization; however, these findings require prospective validation using adequately powered clinical endpoints.

title: Comparative outcomes of natural orifice specimen extraction surgery versus conventional minilaparotomy-assisted specimen extraction in colorectal cancer: A single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES) has emerged as an advanced minimally invasive technique that eliminates abdominal wall incisions for specimen retrieval; nevertheless, comparative data on its efficacy relative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted extraction in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain limited. This retrospective analysis was conducted on 126 patients who underwent laparoscopic CRC resection at our institution, allocated to either the NOSES group (transanal specimen extraction, n = 49) or the conventional group (minilaparotomy-assisted extraction, n = 77), comparing perioperative parameters, postoperative recovery indicators, complication rates, and pathological outcomes. The NOSES group demonstrated significantly shorter time to first flatus (2.3 ± 0.9 vs 2.9 ± 1.1 days, P = .002), time to first liquid diet (3.1 ± 1.0 vs 3.8 ± 1.3 days, P = .001), and postoperative hospital stay (8.4 ± 3.2 vs 10.1 ± 4.1 days, P = .014). Visual analog scale pain scores on postoperative day 1 were significantly lower in the NOSES group (3.2 ± 1.1 vs 4.5 ± 1.3, P .05). In conclusion, NOSES appears to be a safe and feasible alternative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted specimen extraction in highly selected patients with CRC, offering advantages in postoperative pain control, gastrointestinal function recovery, and wound-related complication reduction without compromising oncological integrity.

title: Secondary Pneumonia Among Non-Communicable Disease Inpatients: A Retrospective Administrative Surveillance Study from a Chinese Tertiary Hospital.
Optimizing Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Cholangiography in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials on Dose, Timing, Route, Efficacy, and Safety.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Near-infrared fluorescence cholangiography with indocyanine green (ICG) has been proposed as an adjunct for improving biliary anatomy recognition during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, uncertainty remains regarding its comparative efficacy, operative value, safety, and optimal route, dose, and timing. Materials and Methods : A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized comparative and dose-finding studies evaluating ICG fluorescence cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Outcomes included visualization of the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, common bile duct, biliary junctions, operative time, time to critical anatomical identification, conversion or bailout procedures, length of stay, bile duct injury, bile leak, and ICG-related adverse events. Clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized descriptively. Results : Eighteen studies were included. ICG improved visualization of selected biliary structures compared with white-light imaging, particularly before dissection, whereas differences versus radiographic intraoperative cholangiography were less pronounced. Operative effects were inconsistent: several studies reported shorter cholangiography duration or earlier anatomical identification, without consistent reductions in total operative time or length of stay. Bile duct injuries and bile leaks were infrequent, but event numbers were insufficient to establish a protective effect or comparative safety. Selected dose comparisons suggested reduced hepatic background fluorescence with lower doses, although findings depended on administration timing and imaging platform. Interpretation was limited by subjective visualization assessment, risk of bias, and heterogeneous patient populations. Conclusions : ICG fluorescence cholangiography improves visualization of selected biliary structures, but improved visualization should not be equated with demonstrated clinical benefit. Evidence remains insufficient to establish reductions in bile duct injury, conversion, or postoperative morbidity, or a universally optimal route, dose, or timing regimen.

title: Application and Evaluation of Whole Process Management Model for Liver Cancer Patients Undergone Yttrium-90 Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (Y-90 SIRT): A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Purpose To construct a standardized whole-process management model for liver cancer patients undergoing Yttrium-90 selective internal radiation therapy (Y-90 SIRT) and evaluate its clinical efficacy, safety and impact on medical resource utilization. Patients and methods This retrospective cohort study included patients with primary or secondary liver malignancies who received Y-90 SIRT at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University between August 2022 and October 2025. Patients were assigned to a control or an intervention group according to the timing of model implementation. Adverse events (AEs), psychological status, satisfaction, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), length of hospital stay (LOS) and hospitalization costs were compared between groups. Results In total, 307 patient episodes were included (144 control, 163 intervention), with balanced baseline characteristics (all P > 0.05). The overall incidence of AEs was significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (14.11% vs 40.27%, P Conclusion In this single-center retrospective cohort, the whole-process management model was associated with fewer adverse events and with better patient satisfaction and emotional well-being in patients undergoing Y-90 SIRT. Because long-term oncological outcomes were not assessed, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

title: Hospitalist perspectives and practices in treating hospitalized patients with alcohol withdrawal syndrome in the era of phenobarbital re-emergence.
abstract: Medication treatment for moderate to severe alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS) is evolving, particularly with renewed phenobarbital use. However, little research has examined how hospitalists manage AWS. We conducted a multiple-methods study involving hospitalists from a national US Hospital Medicine research network. Thirty-three hospitalists from 27 tertiary hospitals completed surveys and participated in seven focus groups on August 8, 2025. Benzodiazepines remained the most common treatment, but phenobarbital use was reported in 67% of emergency departments and 44% of inpatient medical units. Four themes emerged: hospitalists are adaptable in responding to changing practices and drug shortages; a lack of consensus on AWS treatment practices leads to a "wild west approach" to therapy selection; hospitalists prioritize care-delivery outcomes when selecting medications; and patients are minimally involved in shared decision-making. Participants strongly supported additional research to guide evidence-based AWS care. These findings highlight uncertainty and the need for standardized, patient-centered approaches to AWS management.

title: Moderate and Severe Traumatic Brain Injury Outcomes-A 20 Year (2002-2021) Analysis.
abstract: Objective Although recognised as a leading cause of death and disability, it is unclear whether current treatment strategies have improved outcomes from blunt moderate to severe traumatic brain injuries (msTBI) due to a lack of available epidemiological data. This study sought to determine if in-hospital mortality and early functional outcomes of msTBI patients have changed over 20 years. Early functional outcomes were determined through the surrogate measure of the proportion of patients discharged directly to home. Methods A longitudinal cohort study using The Alfred Health Trauma Registry data. Subjects were aged 16-70 years with blunt msTBI (Head Abbreviated Injury Scale 3-5) admitted to The Alfred Trauma Service between 1 January 2002 and 31 December 2021. Results A total of 8222 patients presented with msTBI over the period, with 692 deaths (8.5%). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality decreased from 12.1% in 2002 to 4.0% in 2021 (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.97, p Conclusion There was a reduction in in-hospital mortality and an increase in the proportion discharged home for adults hospitalised with msTBI at The Alfred Hospital over the last two decades. These results foster optimism for the care of neurotrauma patients, but further research is required to identify the modifiable factors associated with these improved outcomes.

title: Management of renal failure in earthquake-related crush syndrome: Multicenter intensive care outcomes.
journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
abstract: Background Crush syndrome (CS) is a clinical condition associated with multisystem organ dysfunction that develops after traumatic rhabdomyolysis and primarily affects the kidneys. The aim of this study was to characterize the incidence, risk factors, and treatment patterns of acute kidney injury (AKI) in earthquake victims with CS, with a particular focus on renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and clinical outcomes. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, 247 adult patients with earthquake-related CS who were admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) in 22 hospitals after the Kahramanmaraş 2023 earthquakes were analyzed. Demographic data, injury patterns, laboratory parameters, treatment protocols, and outcomes were evaluated during the first 15 days following ICU admission. Results AKI developed in 78.5% (n=194) of patients, and RRT was required in 62.4% (n=121) of those with AKI. Multiple logistic regression analysis demonstrated that myoglobin and creatinine levels were associated with an elevated risk of developing AKI (odds ratio [OR]: 1.001; 95% confidence interval CI: 1.000-1.001 and OR: 1.735; 95% CI: 1.151-2.615, respectively). Similarly, creatinine level and reasons for ICU admission were identified as factors influencing RRT administration. (OR: 1.7; 95% CI: 1.28-2.15 and OR: 2.9; 95% CI: 1.26-6.90, respectively). The 30-day mortality rate was higher in patients with AKI than in those without AKI. Mortality rates were similar between patients with AKI who received RRT and those who did not. Conclusion This study demonstrates the high incidence of AKI in earthquake-related CS, underscores the need for improved disaster preparedness with adequate dialysis capacity and early risk stratification using serum myoglobin and creatinine levels for optimal management.

Association of Perioperative Colchicine Use with Morbidity and Inflammation in Heart Valve Surgery.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Valvular heart disease (VHD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and valve replacement surgery performed under cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) with full sternotomy remains an important treatment modality. Colchicine has well-established anti-inflammatory effects in ischemic heart disease and pericardial disease, but its association with postoperative morbidity in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery has not been well studied. This study aimed to investigate the association of perioperative colchicine use with clinical morbidity and inflammatory parameters in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery with CPB. Materials and Methods : In this retrospective study, 82 patients who underwent elective on-pump valvular heart surgery through full sternotomy were divided into a control group ( n = 42) who did not receive colchicine and a colchicine group ( n = 40) who received oral colchicine (0.5 mg once daily) for three days before and ten days after surgery. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, including length of hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) stay, transfusion requirements, sternal wound complication, surgical re-exploration, and inflammatory parameters on postoperative day 5 (C-reactive protein [CRP], white blood cell count, albumin, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR]), were compared between the groups. Results : Length of ICU stay was significantly shorter in the colchicine group than in the control group (4.1 ± 1.6 vs. 5.3 ± 2.4 days; p = 0.009), and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirement was significantly lower in the colchicine group (4.2 ± 2.1 vs. 6.9 ± 3.3 units; p p > 0.05). Conclusions : Perioperative colchicine was associated with a shorter ICU stay and a reduced requirement for fresh frozen plasma transfusion in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery with CPB, suggesting that colchicine may have a potential role in this surgical population. After correction for multiple comparisons, the difference in ICU length of stay was no longer statistically significant. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Stay Alive: The Case for Rural Freestanding Emergency Departments.
