Storage and Disposal of Unused Prescription Opioids for Acute Pain After Emergency Department Discharge.
authors: Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group (OPUM)
on behalf of the Network of Canadian Emergency Researchers
abstract: Importance Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem. Objective To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids. Design, setting, and participants This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months. Exposure Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge. Main outcomes and measures The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months. Results Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered. Conclusions and relevance In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

title: The role of fibrinogen concentrate in the reduction of allogeneic blood product requirements: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Fibrinogen concentrate (FC) has a well-established safety profile and is recommended for treating acquired fibrinogen deficiency. However, its comparative effectiveness vs other treatments regarding transfusions and patient outcomes remains uncertain. Methods Comparative studies from a range of clinical settings in which patients received FC for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia and that evaluated blood product needs, mortality, thromboembolic events, or hospital length of stay were included in a systematic literature review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42024602804). Meta-analyses used pooled data to provide an estimate of the difference in outcome between FC and all other treatments; separate analyses were conducted for adult and paediatric patients. Results Overall, 58 studies (N=13 530 patients) were analysed. Adult FC recipients received significantly fewer red blood cell, fresh frozen plasma, and platelet units than with other treatments: 28% (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.89; P=0.002), 31% (IRR 0.69; 95% CI 0.54-0.89; P=0.004), and 44% less (IRR 0.56; 95% CI 0.33-0.95; P=0.03), respectively. These results were largely driven by cardiac surgery studies. In an RCT subanalysis, the use and quantity of blood products were significantly reduced with FC. No significant difference in mortality or thromboembolic events was found between treatments in adult patients or in any outcomes analysed in paediatric patients. Conclusion This meta-analysis suggests fibrinogen concentrate administered for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia can reduce blood product transfusions in adults, with no obvious safety concerns, compared with other treatments.

title: Preoperative nutritional status defined by GLIM criteria and postoperative delirium in older patients receiving general anesthesia.
abstract: Background Preoperative malnutrition may reflect reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to postoperative delirium (POD) in older surgical patients. However, evidence based on standardized diagnostic criteria remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the association between Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM)-defined malnutrition and POD among older patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia. Methods This retrospective observational cohort study included consecutive patients aged ≥65 years who underwent elective or emergency surgery under general anesthesia between January 2022 and December 2025. Preoperative malnutrition was retrospectively classified according to the GLIM framework using available phenotypic and etiologic criteria. Patients with and without GLIM-defined malnutrition were matched 1:2 using propensity score matching. POD documented during hospitalization was identified from Confusion Assessment Method assessments, Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit assessments, or explicit physician diagnoses. The association between GLIM-defined malnutrition and POD was examined using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were also performed. Results The matched cohort comprised 495 patients, including 165 with GLIM-defined malnutrition and 330 without malnutrition. All propensity score covariates achieved acceptable post-matching balance, with absolute standardized mean differences p p = 0.002). No significant interactions were identified across age, surgical category, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, or immediate postoperative intensive care unit admission subgroups. Comparable associations were observed in the unmatched cohort, alternative matched analyses, fixed observation windows, restricted-length-of-stay cohorts, and analyses using alternative POD definitions. Conclusion GLIM-defined malnutrition was associated with higher odds of POD during hospitalization in older patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia. GLIM-based nutritional assessment may provide clinically useful information for perioperative delirium risk stratification.

title: Outcomes After Major Amputation in Octogenarians.
Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.
Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Corticosteroids vs. No Corticosteroids in Septic Shock Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Septic shock carries a high intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. The role of adjunctive corticosteroid therapy is controversial, with conflicting signals from trial-level meta-analyses, individual patient data syntheses, and large randomized trials. This review aimed to assess the comparative efficacy and safety of systemic corticosteroids versus no corticosteroids in adult ICU patients with septic shock. Methods Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception, supplemented by trial registry and gray literature searches, for randomized trials of systemic corticosteroids versus placebo or standard care in adults with septic shock. Pooling used a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. The Risk of Bias 2 and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) frameworks were used for the methodological appraisal. Heterogeneity was quantified using I 2 , τ 2 , and 95% prediction intervals. Publication bias was assessed using contour-enhanced funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and the Duval-Tweedie trim-and-fill method. Results Eleven randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (n = 6,332; 1,929 deaths) were included. Corticosteroids reduced 28-day all-cause mortality by 8.7% relative to control (pooled risk ratio (RR) 0.91, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86-0.97; P = 0.008; I 2 = 0%; prediction interval 0.84-0.99), corresponding to 27 fewer deaths per 1,000 (10-44 fewer). Time to shock reversal was shortened by 1.25 days (95% CI -2.09 to -0.41), with the standardized mean difference (SMD) sensitivity analysis confirming a robust effect (SMD -0.41, 95% CI -0.51 to -0.32). Shock reversal incidence (RR 1.08, 0.99-1.19) and ICU length of stay (LOS) (mean difference (MD) -2.07 days, -6.50 to 2.36) favored corticosteroids without reaching significance. Hyperglycemia occurred more frequently in the corticosteroid arm of every contributing trial. Egger's test (P = 0.972) and trim-and-fill imputation provided no evidence of small-study effects. GRADE certainty was moderate for mortality and shock reversal incidence, high for time to shock reversal, and low for ICU LOS and hyperglycemia. Conclusion Corticosteroid therapy in adults with septic shock was associated with a reduction in 28-day mortality and with accelerated shock reversal, with no evidence of publication bias. The direction of effect was consistent across pre-specified subgroups but was offset by a consistent excess of hyperglycemia, reinforcing the need for vigilant glucose surveillance during corticosteroid administration.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Complications of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) in Adult Patients With COVID-19 in Central and Eastern Europe: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
abstract: BACKGROUND Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a rescue therapy for severe COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). International datasets do not consistently report Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) separately. We aimed to assess mortality, clinical characteristics, and complications of ECMO-treated COVID-19 patients across the CEE region. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a systematic review with single-arm meta-analyses of observational studies. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from January 2020 to August 2025 for studies reporting ECMO outcomes in adult (≥18 years) COVID-19 patients from CEE countries, with at least 10 ECMO-treated patients. Conference abstracts and overlapping cohorts were excluded. The study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251077593). RESULTS Twelve studies included 802 patients from 6 countries. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 65% (95% CI 0.57-0.72; I²=70.6%; 10 studies; n=691), and ICU mortality was 61% (95% CI 0.47-0.74; I²=85.8%; 7 studies, n=526). Country-level in-hospital mortality estimates were 54% for the Czech Republic and 76% for Poland but were descriptive because of the small number of studies and wide CIs. Mean pre-ECMO mechanical ventilation duration was 4.8 days (95% CI 3.7-5.8; I²=4.4%), ECMO duration was 17.8 days (95% CI 12.8-22.9; I²=79.8%), and ICU length of stay was 23.6 days (95% CI 7.5-39.7; I²=92.6%). Serious bleeding occurred in 40% (95% CI 22-61%; I²=85.7%). Certainty was very low for all pooled outcomes. CONCLUSIONS These CEE-specific estimates provide regional benchmarks, but substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty limit international comparisons and country-level interpretation. Standardized regional registries, prospective multicenter data, harmonized complication reporting, and long-term outcome assessment are needed.

title: Clinical and Economic Outcomes Associated with Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Reporting and Dual-Card Testing in ICU Bloodstream Infections.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the clinical and economic outcomes associated with implementation of an optimized blood culture workflow in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with bloodstream infections. Patients and methods From March 2022 to June 2023, the laboratory implemented a multi-modal workflow optimization including satellite blood culture incubation in the emergency department, upgraded blood culture bottles, rapid MALDI-TOF MS identification, automated rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) reporting, and dual AST cards for Gram-negative bacteria. The pre-optimization group included 107 adult ICU patients with positive blood cultures (March 2021 - February 2022). The post-optimization group included 153 patients (September 2023 - August 2024). Results Compared to the final AST report in the pre-optimization group, the rapid AST report in the post-optimization group was 19.6 hours faster ( P P = 0.055). Use of two broad-spectrum antibiotics, meropenem ( P P = 0.045), decreased significantly. Hospital length of stay was 5 days shorter ( P = 0.006). In unadjusted comparisons, antibiotic and hospitalization costs were reduced by 4871 CNY ([US$ 684], P P = 0.073), respectively. Conclusion This multimodal workflow optimization for ICU patients with BSIs, incorporating automated rapid AST reporting and dual-AST-card-enabled expanded antimicrobial panels, shortened laboratory turnaround time. It was associated with earlier opportunities for targeted antimicrobial therapy and suggests potential clinical-economic benefits, alongside possible mitigation of antimicrobial-resistance risk.

title: General Anesthesia vs Monitored Anesthesia Care With Local Anesthetic Infiltration (MAC-VL) for Ankle Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: Impact on Recovery Metrics and Safety.
Improving Medication Management During SNF-to-Home Transitions.
A Mixed Methods Evaluation of a Model of Care for Domestic Violence Within the Emergency Department
Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Crystalloid fluid is central to pediatric septic shock resuscitation, but the optimal composition is uncertain. Normal saline delivers a supraphysiologic chloride load that may promote hyperchloremic acidosis and renal injury, whereas balanced crystalloids approximate extracellular fluid. Pediatric evidence is mixed, and prior syntheses preceded the large PRoMPT BOLUS trial. We compared balanced crystalloids with normal saline for resuscitation in children with sepsis or septic shock. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts comparing balanced crystalloids with 0.9% saline in children (≤ 18 years) with sepsis or septic shock requiring fluid resuscitation. Co-primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and acute kidney injury (AKI). Data were pooled using random-effects models (risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD); 95% confidence interval (CI)), with trial sequential analysis (TSA) for primary outcomes. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO. Results Nine studies (five RCTs, four observational cohorts) were included. Balanced crystalloids did not reduce mortality (RR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.83-1.06; I 2 = 0%) or AKI (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.61-1.16; I 2 = 73.5%); TSA showed the required information size was unmet, leaving both inconclusive. Balanced crystalloids significantly reduced renal replacement therapy (RR 0.74; 95% CI, 0.56-0.96; I 2 = 23.5%) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; I 2 = 0%). No differences emerged for major adverse kidney events within 30 days (MAKE30) (RR, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.87-1.41), mechanical ventilation (RR, 0.97, 95% CI, 0.85-1.11), or hospital (MD, 1.49 days) and pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) (MD, 0.84 days) length of stay. Conclusions In pediatric sepsis or septic shock, balanced crystalloids consistently reduce hyperchloremia and the need for renal replacement therapy but do not significantly reduce mortality, AKI, MAKE30, mechanical ventilation, or length of stay. Incorporating recent pragmatic randomized data supports cautious interpretation, and TSA confirms that the primary-outcome evidence remains inconclusive. Adequately powered, phenotype-informed trials are needed.

title: Clinical Characteristics of Spontaneous and Recurrent Pneumomediastinum and Risk Factors of Recurrence.
abstract: Background Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (SPM) is rare, and most existing knowledge comes from small case series. Although usually benign, SPM often leads to hospital admission and substantial healthcare resource use. This study aimed to characterize SPM and recurrent spontaneous pneumomediastinum (RSPM) in a large cohort and to explore factors associated with recurrence. Methods Patients with SPM hospitalized at Putian First Hospital between September 2011 and September 2023 were included. Clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. Follow-up was performed to identify RSPM. Patients were divided into nonrecurrence and recurrence groups, and risk factors for recurrence were evaluated using univariate logistic regression. Results A total of 135 patients with SPM were included. Most patients were male (78.1%), with a median age of 20 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 17-32). A bimodal age distribution was observed, with peaks at 15-19 and 50-54 years. The most common symptom was chest pain (51.9%), and 54.0% of the patients had no identifiable trigger. Among the 9 patients with RSPM (6.7%), median age at recurrence was 25 years (IQR: 16-56) and median interval to recurrence was 6.5 months (range: 1-16.5). Dyspnea was the most common symptom at recurrence (66.7%), and 44.4% of the patients showed greater clinical and radiological severity than at initial presentation. Univariate analysis suggested that a history of bronchitis was associated with RSPM (OR: 11.71, 95% CI: 1.68-81.89); other potential factors included silicosis, pneumonia, and upper respiratory infection as a trigger. Conclusion SPM predominantly affects young males and generally follows a benign course. Although recurrence is uncommon (6.7%), it may be more severe than the initial episode in nearly half of the cases. A history of bronchitis may be associated with recurrence, but this finding is exploratory. Age-specific preventive strategies and careful exclusion of secondary pneumomediastinum are essential.

title: Clinical-Histopathological Concordance of Surgical Triage and the Unexpected Acute Phenotype in 773 Consecutive Laparoscopic Cholecystectomies.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Surgical triage and final histopathological classification do not always fully overlap. This study evaluated their concordance, the frequency of unexpected acute pathology among electively scheduled patients, and associated preoperative characteristics. Materials and Methods : This single-center, single-surgeon retrospective cohort included 773 patients whose cholecystectomy was completed laparoscopically between 1 January 2022 and 30 June 2026. Surgical triage was classified as emergency or elective, and histopathology as acute or chronic inflammatory pathology. "Unexpected acute pathology" denoted acute histopathology in electively scheduled patients, irrespective of clinical suspicion. Multivariable logistic regression was performed in 627 elective patients with complete data. Model A included previous biliary attack and preoperative radiological gallbladder wall thickening; Model B additionally included the C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR). Results : Of 773 patients, 138 underwent emergency and 635 elective surgery. Observed agreement was 92.4%, with Cohen's kappa of 0.757 (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.697-0.814). Unexpected acute pathology occurred in 42 elective patients (6.6%). In Model B, previous biliary attack (odds ratio [OR] = 2.76), preoperative radiological gallbladder wall thickening (OR = 4.09), and CAR (OR = 1.52 per 5-unit increase) were associated with unexpected acute pathology. Adding CAR increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.697 to 0.756 and improved model fit ( p = 0.00055). Unexpected acute pathology occurred in 3.8%, 11.9%, and 37.5% of patients with 0, 1, and 2 findings, respectively (n = 477, 126, and 24). Across these strata, documented omental adhesions increased from 23.5% to 62.5% and postoperative hospital stay >1 day from 9.2% to 41.7%. Conclusions : Surgical triage showed high overall concordance with histopathology. The two preoperative findings were associated with unexpected acute pathology and a more complex perioperative profile; CAR provided complementary information. Given the small two-finding subgroup and single-center design, external validation is required before these findings can guide operative planning.

title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Influenza A in Hospitalized Adults, 2019-2024: Exploratory Evidence on Neuraminidase and Polymerase Acidic Protein Mutation-Outcome Associations From a Single Center.
abstract: Background Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period. Conclusions Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.

title: There are No Differences in Early Complications or One-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes Between Single-Stage Bilateral and Unilateral Total Hip Arthroplasty Performed in Patients 70 Years and Older.
Length of stay and nhi-reimbursed expenditures after robotic-assisted surgery in taiwan: a nationwide population-based study.
abstract: Population-level evidence comparing robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with laparoscopic surgery (LS)/video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open surgery (OS) across multiple procedures from a payer perspective remains limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative length of stay (LOS) and insurer-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures among RAS, LS/VATS, and OS across representative procedures following the expansion of RAS reimbursement in Taiwan. This retrospective nationwide population-based cohort study was conducted using claims data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. We identified adults (age ≥ 18 y) who underwent 1 of 12 representative procedures spanning thoracic, hepatobiliary-pancreatic, colorectal, urologic, and gynecologic specialties between September 1 and December 31, 2024. Surgical approaches were classified as robotic-assisted surgery (RAS), laparoscopic or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (LS/VATS), or open surgery (OS) using the corresponding procedure and robotic-assistance codes in the NHI claims database. The outcomes were postoperative LOS and total NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials during the index hospitalization. Procedure-specific stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to each pairwise comparison. This study included 17 549 patients. Of these patients, 2900, 9763, and 4886 underwent RAS, LS/VATS, and OS, respectively. RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS than LS/VATS for lung resection, colectomy, partial nephrectomy, and nephroureterectomy and with lower reimbursed expenditures for lung resection, partial pancreatectomy, nephroureterectomy, and radical prostatectomy. Compared with OS, RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, with the largest difference noted for colectomy (8.38 vs. 14.80 d). Moreover, RAS was associated with lower reimbursed expenditures than OS for lung resection, minor hepatectomy, partial pancreatectomy, colectomy, and malignant hysterectomy. During the early period following the September 2024 expansion of NHI reimbursement for RAS in Taiwan, RAS was associated with shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, whereas differences in NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials varied by procedure and comparator. Given the observational study design, residual confounding, and limited propensity-score overlap in several comparisons, particularly RAS versus OS, these findings should be interpreted as procedure-specific associations rather than evidence of clinical or economic superiority.

title: From Hospital to Outpatient Care After Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotic Initiation in Bipolar Disorder: Nationwide Evidence From Taiwan.
oXiris-Based Blood Purification Efficacy in Adults with Septic Shock and Acute Kidney Injury: The PURE Multicenter Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Randomized evidence for the oXiris adsorptive membrane in septic shock remains limited. We estimated its effect on 28-day mortality and explored short-term physiologic outcomes in adults with septic shock and acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy. Methods: PURE was a multicenter, single-blind, parallel-group pilot randomized trial in Saudi Arabia. Participants were randomized 1:1 to oXiris-based or conventional continuous venovenous hemodialysis. The primary comparison used unadjusted mortality risk estimates. Secondary observations were summarized descriptively; adjusted and post-hoc Bayesian sensitivity analyses are reported in the main text and supplement. Results: Of 204 randomized participants, 202 were analyzed (oXiris, 100; control, 102). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 39.0% (39/100) versus 47.1% (48/102), respectively (risk ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.60-1.14; risk difference, -8.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -21.7 to 5.6; p = 0.247). Reported 72 h norepinephrine dose, lactate, C-reactive protein, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score were lower with oXiris; reported intensive care unit (ICU) stay was also shorter. Secondary descriptive observations are limited by unverifiable time-specific denominators and handling of intercurrent events. Premature filter clotting was reported in 8/100 versus 7/102 participants; no device-related adverse events were reported, but safety ascertainment was limited. Conclusions: This pilot trial did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in 28-day mortality, although mortality was numerically lower in the oXiris group. Consistent protocol implementation and encouraging, hypothesis-generating physiologic observations provide a foundation for a definitive trial with complete longitudinal ascertainment.

title: Outcomes of isolated hip fractures in people with Parkinson's disease: An observational cohort study using propensity score methods.
abstract: BackgroundPeople with Parkinson's disease (PwP) have a high risk of hip fracture and the outcomes of PwP in Australia with hip fractures are unknown.ObjectiveTo describe the characteristics of PwP who present with a hip fracture and to examine the association between Parkinson's with acute hospital outcomes, mortality and discharge destination.MethodsWe conducted a cohort study of individuals with an isolated proximal femur fracture using the Victorian Orthopaedic Trauma Outcomes Registry (Australia) from 2016 to 2022. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, fracture types, acute hospital length of stay, discharge destination and 30-day and 12-month mortality data were extracted. Inverse-probability weighting with estimated propensity scores determined the association of Parkinson's with outcomes, using a logistic regression model that included covariates and injury characteristics.ResultsOf 5,553 patients, 208 (4%) had PD, with a mean age of 79.9 years (SD 12.9). After propensity score adjustment, there was no association between Parkinson's and ICU admission (OR 1.89; 95% CI 0.67, 5.34), acute length of stay (adjusted median 6.9 vs 7.7) and 12-month mortality rates (OR 1.25; 95% CI 0.85, 1.82). PwP were more likely to be discharged to rehabilitation than home (RR 2.04; 95% CI 1.12, 3.74).ConclusionsWe did not observe a statistically significant difference in acute hospital outcomes between the two cohorts, including length of stay. This is encouraging as avoiding prolonged hospitalisation reduces health care costs and risk of hospital-related harms. However, these findings may reflect limited statistical power and differences between groups cannot be excluded. Further research is also indicated to explore post-care discharge pathways and longer-term functional outcomes of this group.

title: Colchicine Use Is Associated with Shorter ICU Stay and Lower FFP Transfusion Requirements After CABG.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
abstract: Background Colchicine has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular benefits in patients with coronary heart disease. However, evidence regarding its effects on postoperative inflammation and early clinical outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains limited. Objective We aimed to evaluate the association between perioperative low-dose colchicine use and postoperative clinical outcomes, transfusion requirements, complications, and inflammatory markers in patients undergoing elective on-pump CABG. Methods This retrospective study included 151 patients who underwent elective on-pump CABG: 81 received colchicine (0.5 mg once daily for 3 days preoperatively and 10 days postoperatively) and 70 did not receive colchicine in the past period. The primary clinical outcomes included ICU and total hospital length of stay, erythrocyte and fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion requirements, wound complication, and surgical revision. Postoperative day 5 laboratory parameters included C-reactive protein, white blood cell (WBC) count, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and albumin. Between-group comparisons were performed using Student's or Welch's t tests and Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, as appropriate. Results Baseline age and sex distribution were similar between the groups. The colchicine group had a significantly shorter ICU stay than the control group (4.28 ± 1.95 vs. 5.83 ± 3.04 days; mean difference, -1.54 days; 95% CI, -2.38 to -0.71; p p 9 /L; p = 0.027). Total hospital stay, erythrocyte transfusion requirements, other inflammatory parameters, wound complication rates, and surgical revision rates did not differ significantly between the groups. Conclusions Perioperative low-dose colchicine was found to be in relation with shorter ICU stays, lower FFP transfusion requirements, and reduced postoperative WBC counts following elective on-pump CABG according to this retrospective study. Prospective randomized studies are required to confirm these findings and to determine whether colchicine improves early postoperative outcomes.

title: Chest pain in the emergency room: value of the new HEAR score identifying patients with low risk of acute coronary syndrome without troponin testing.
abstract: Background Chest pain is a frequent reason for Emergency Department (ED) visits, although only a minority of patients ultimately present an Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). Current diagnostic strategies rely heavily on troponin testing, but a new clinical tool requiring no blood sampling, the HEAR score, has recently been proposed. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the HEAR score for identifying low-risk patients presenting with chest pain, using 45-day Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) as the primary outcome. Methods All patients presenting with chest pain to the ED of Dijon University Hospital in 2019 were retrospectively analyzed in this single-center study. Patients were stratified as "low risk" (HEAR Results Among 2177 patients presenting with chest pain, 1807 met inclusion criteria. Of these, 653 (36%) were classified as low risk (HEAR Conclusion A HEAR score < 2 identifies a substantial proportion of ED chest pain patients at very low risk of short-term adverse cardiovascular events. However, given the limitations of retrospective follow-up and potential under-ascertainment of events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. The HEAR score may contribute to early clinical risk stratification rather than replace troponin-based strategies.

title: Brain tumor surgery outcomes in rural America: a cross-sectional statewide study.
Totally single-incision laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction in children: clinical outcomes and learning curve.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the feasibility, perioperative outcomes, and learning curve of totally single-incision laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction in children. Methods We retrospectively reviewed children who underwent laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision between January 2018 and December 2024. Thirty-five children underwent totally single-incision laparoscopic intracorporeal hand-sewn reconstruction (TSILC), and 40 underwent conventional single-incision laparoscopic-assisted reconstruction (SILC). Baseline characteristics, operative outcomes, recovery, complications, and follow-up were compared. Multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors was used to adjust continuous outcomes for baseline differences. The TSILC learning curve was assessed using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis of jejunojejunostomy time. Results TSILC patients were older (29.86 ± 12.99 vs. 19.60 ± 13.62 months, P = 0.001), heavier (14.90 ± 5.07 vs. 9.22 ± 4.40 kg, P P = 0.030). After adjustment, total operative time did not differ significantly (adjusted β =8.75 min, 95% CI -12.10 to 29.60; P = 0.411), whereas jejunojejunostomy time remained longer with TSILC (adjusted β=12.02 min, 95% CI 3.02 to 21.02; P = 0.009). TSILC was associated with less blood loss, a shorter incision, and earlier first flatus and defecation (all adjusted P P = 0.568). Early complications occurred in 3/35 TSILC and 5/40 SILC patients. Thirty-three TSILC procedures were completed without an additional port or open conversion; one required an additional port and one required open conversion. Median follow-up was 40.0 months (IQR 21.5-59.5) for TSILC and 46.5 months (IQR 27.2-66.2) for SILC. The CUSUM curve peaked at case 17, suggesting relative stabilization after case 18. Conclusion TSILC with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction was technically feasible in selected children and showed a measurable learning curve. The findings suggest that TSILC may offer perioperative advantages in appropriately selected older and larger children.

title: Impact of Surgical Airways on Location of Death, Healthcare Utilization, and Costs Among Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Population-Based Study.
Association between cachexia-associated diagnoses, health care resource utilization, and costs in patients with pancreatic, lung, and colorectal cancers: A US insurance claims database analysis.
journal: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy

title: The effect of case-based payment reform on hospitalization rates: evidence from China.
abstract: Background Rising medical expenditure has posed a major governance challenge worldwide, prompting health systems to replace fee-for-service reimbursement with case-based payment models to realign provider incentives. China has also implemented the case-based payment reform nationwide, adopting both the DRG-based payment and a domestically developed alternative model known as the Diagnosis-Intervention Packet (DIP). Using a county-level panel dataset from Sichuan Province covering 2011-2022, this study examines how this reform is associated with changes in hospitalization rates, an outcome that remains insufficiently understood in the existing literature. Methods This study employs an imputation-based staggered difference-in-differences design to examine the impact of case-based payment reform on public hospital hospitalization rates. Results The case-based payment reform increases public hospitals' hospitalization rates by 0.72% points, a 6.7% increase relative to the pre-reform mean of 10.68%. Additional analyses offer suggestive evidence on factors that may be related to this pattern. On the supply side, the reform is associated with improved hospital efficiency, which is consistent with the possibility that hospitals are able to accommodate more inpatient admissions. On the behavioral side, changes in hospitalization rates may also reflect hospitals' strategic adjustment to the new reimbursement scheme. Heterogeneity analyses further show that the effect is more pronounced in areas with more abundant medical resources, higher per capita health insurance revenue, and a lower share of beds in primary care institutions. Conclusions Case-based payment reforms can trigger unintended volume expansion, which could partly weaken their expected cost-containment effects. These findings highlight the importance of designing provider payment systems with more carefully aligned incentives and strengthening regulatory frameworks to monitor hospitals' behavioral responses. The evidence also offers policy-relevant lessons for China and other low- and middle-income countries seeking to reform provider payment systems while balancing cost control, service capacity, and access to care.

title: Management and Prognosis of Sustained Ventricular Tachycardia in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective, Observational, Single-Centre Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia requiring prompt Emergency Department (ED) assessment and management. However, data on its frequency, real-world treatment, and prognosis in the ED remain limited. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, acute management, and short- and long-term outcomes of patients presenting with VT. Methods: We retrospectively included consecutive patients presenting to the ED between January 2018 and December 2024 with a primary diagnosis of sustained VT with a pulse. We collected baseline characteristics, hemodynamic status, underlying cardiac disease, and acute treatment. In-hospital events and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were assessed. Results: A total of 103 patients were identified, accounting for approximately 0.025% of all ED visits during the study period; 84.5% were male. Chest pain (31.1%) and palpitations (25.2%) were the most common presenting symptoms. Structural heart disease was present in 90% of the cases, predominantly of ischemic origin (61%). Nearly half of the patients (49.5%) had a prior history of VT. Electrical cardioversion was performed in 28.2% of the cases. The majority of the patients (95/103; 92%) required hospitalization. Mortality was 4.9% at 30 days and 17% at 1 year. After adjustment for age, a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and in-hospital arrhythmic recurrence were independently associated with 1-year mortality. Conclusions: Sustained VT is an uncommon but high-risk ED presentation, mainly affecting patients with ischemic structural heart disease. A discrepancy was observed between real-world clinical practice and guideline recommendations. The substantial mortality observed, particularly among patients with impaired left ventricular function or in-hospital arrhythmic recurrence, highlights the need for prompt risk stratification and optimized, guideline-concordant acute management.

title: Patient outcomes and healthcare utilisation following implementation of an advanced therapy care pathway for inflammatory bowel disease: a multicentre, prospective quasi-experimental preimplementation/postimplementation study in the Netherlands.
abstract: Objective Care pathways have the potential to decrease treatment variation and improve patient outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the effect of an advanced therapy care pathway (ACP) on patient outcomes, healthcare utilisation and treatment variation among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in the Netherlands. Methods A multicentre, prospective quasi-experimental preimplementation/postimplementation study was conducted, with a preimplementation (December 2020-December 2021) and postimplementation period (March 2022-March 2023). Outcomes were collected from electronic medical records and validated questionnaires according to the International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement standard set. The effect of the ACP was analysed using difference-in-differences (DiD) analysis. Results 1173 patients were included; the majority was female (55%) with a median age of 45 years (IQR 33-58 years). Most patients had Crohn's disease (64%). Patients reported a high level of disease control and this did not change postimplementation (DiD-estimate: 0.12, 95% CI -0.74 to 1.01). Number of emergency room visits and hospital admissions decreased significantly 6 months postimplementation; however, the effect attributable to the ACP was only maintained for admissions (DiD-estimate visits: -0.05, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.01; DiD-estimate admissions: -0.06, 95% CI -0.11 to -0.03). Conclusion Implementation of an ACP, in which a minimum of care is defined, can achieve outcomes comparable to standard practice, highlighting the value of prioritising structured care pathways, especially given the current burden of IBD on healthcare systems. An ACP can guide healthcare providers and policymakers in standardising treatment and improving quality of care in chronic disease management. Study registration NL8276/NL-OMON21751 (https://onderzoekmetmensen.nl/en/trial/21751).

title: Receipt of needed care coordination and emergency department utilization among US children with chronic physical pain: a pooled analysis of the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health.
abstract: Background Children with chronic physical pain often require complex, multidisciplinary services across medical, behavioral, and community systems. However, whether receipt of needed care coordination is associated with acute healthcare utilization and care access in this population remains poorly characterized. Methods We conducted a pooled cross-sectional analysis of the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH). The analytic cohort included US children aged 6-17 years with caregiver-reported chronic physical pain who had an identified need for care coordination. The exposure was receipt of needed care coordination. The primary outcome was all-cause emergency department (ED) utilization (≥1 visit) in the prior 12 months. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used, with a minimally adjusted model (sociodemographic factors) and a fully adjusted model (additionally including insurance status, anxiety, depression, and functional difficulties) reported side by side. Results Among 6,326 eligible children (representing an average of 878,491 children annually), weighted 12-month ED visit rates were 29.0% (95% CI, 25.4%-32.5%) for those who received needed care coordination versus 40.0% (95% CI, 36.4%-43.7%) for those who did not. In the minimally adjusted model, receipt of needed care coordination was associated with lower odds of ED utilization (adjusted OR [aOR] 0.61; 95% CI, 0.48-0.76; P n = 6,310). This association persisted in the fully adjusted model (aOR 0.69; 95% CI, 0.54-0.87; P = .0019; n = 6,145) and was consistent for recurrent ED visits (≥2 visits: aOR 0.54; 95% CI, 0.36-0.79; P = .0015). Receipt of care coordination was also associated with substantially lower odds of unmet healthcare needs (aOR 0.32; 95% CI, 0.23-0.45) and forgone mental health care (aOR 0.21; 95% CI, 0.13-0.33). The estimate for hospital stay was imprecise and included the null (aOR 0.61; 95% CI, 0.37-1.01; P = .053). Conclusion Among US children with chronic physical pain who needed care coordination, receipt of needed care coordination was associated with lower odds of all-cause ED use and reported healthcare access gaps. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporal ordering or causal effects and should be evaluated in prospective studies.

title: Wearable-measured early postoperative mobility is associated with recovery after elective colorectal cancer surgery: a prospective pilot study.
abstract: Purpose Early mobilization is a key component of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways following colorectal cancer surgery; however, objective postoperative mobility quantification remains limited. We evaluated whether early postoperative step counts measured using a wearable device could be associated with the achievement of ERAS-based discharge eligibility. Methods In this prospective pilot study, adults undergoing elective colorectal cancer resection at a single tertiary academic referral hospital wore a consumer wearable device (Galaxy Watch 5) from the day of surgery. Cumulative step counts on postoperative days (PODs) 1 and 2 were recorded. Discharge readiness was assessed daily by predefined ERAS criteria. The patients were dichotomized according to the median cumulative step count (3,781 steps). The primary endpoint was the achievement of ERAS-based discharge eligibility by POD 3, and the secondary endpoints included time to discharge readiness and postoperative length of stay. Results Between August 2023 and December 2024, 38 patients were evaluated. Discharge readiness by POD 3 was more frequent in the active group (68.4% vs. 26.3%; odds ratio, 6.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.49-24.76; P=0.009), which achieved discharge readiness earlier (median, POD 3 vs. POD 4; P=0.003) and had a shorter postoperative stay (median, 5 days vs. 6 days; P=0.041) than did the inactive group. Early diet tolerance differed between the groups (P=0.013). Conclusion Higher early postoperative step counts were associated with earlier ERAS-based discharge readiness and shorter hospitalization. Wearable-derived mobility might provide an objective marker of recovery and target for postoperative mobilization strategies.

title: Emergency Hold Use in Youth With Mental Health Concerns Presenting to the Emergency Department.
Work Engagement in the Association Between Emotional Intelligence and Intent to Stay Among Registered Nurses in Riyadh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Research on nurse retention in Saudi Arabia has focused mainly on turnover intention, and little is known about how emotional intelligence and work engagement relate to nurses' intent to stay. This study examined these associations among registered nurses in Riyadh, including the indirect association involving work engagement. Methods: A cross-sectional survey used convenience sampling to recruit 299 registered nurses from two tertiary referral hospitals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Emotional intelligence, work engagement, and intent to stay were measured using the WLEIS, UWES-9, and McCain's Intent to Stay Scale. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapping indirect-association model (5000 samples) were used, adjusting for sociodemographic and work-related characteristics. Results: Emotional intelligence, work engagement, and intent to stay were moderately and positively correlated ( r = 0.43-0.48). After adjustment, work engagement (β = 0.38) and emotional intelligence (β = 0.24) remained independently associated with intent to stay (both p B = 0.365, of which the statistical indirect association involving work engagement was B = 0.148 (95% bootstrap CI [0.090, 0.226]). Conclusions: Emotional intelligence and work engagement were each associated with greater intent to stay in this convenience sample. Because the data are cross-sectional and drawn from two Riyadh hospitals, these associations do not establish causality or temporal ordering.

title: Urgent versus scheduled resection in high-grade glioma: patient selection and healthcare utilization in a single-center cohort.
abstract: Purpose Patients with high-grade glioma reach surgery during the initial, index hospitalization (urgent), or through scheduled/outpatient pathways. There is a paucity of literature examining what patients require expedited versus elective surgery. This single-center retrospective study describes complications, utilization, and survival by pathway. Methods Adults with WHO grade 3-4 gliomas undergoing primary resection (2021-2026) were classified as urgent (admitted without a planned resection date) or scheduled (discharged and readmitted for planned surgery, or managed exclusively as an outpatient). Primary outcomes were 30-day complications and days alive at home within 30 days of admission for resection (DAH-30). Secondary outcomes were progression free and overall survival. Survival was analyzed with propensity-score overlap weighting and Cox regression. Results Of 166 patients, 122 underwent urgent resection and 44 scheduled resections; 40 of 44 (91%) proceeded as planned. Urgent patients more often had midline shift (62% vs. 32%), less often seizure (15% vs. 39%), and lower Karnofsky scores (70 vs. 80); all p ≤ 0.002. They had longer index hospitalizations (median 8 vs. 3 days, p Conclusions Scheduled resection identified a distinct population, recognizable at initial evaluation by preserved performance status and the absence of midline shift. These patients spent more days at home and required shorter hospitalizations; no harm signal was observed. These data suggest that a substantial proportion of patients with newly diagnosed presumed high grade gliomas can be managed effectively in an expedited, outpatient basis.

title: Prognostic value of modified thrombelastometry for thromboembolic risk stratification in neurosurgical patients: protocol for a prospective, multicenter, observational study (TENS).
abstract: Background and objectives Neurosurgical patients, particularly those with intracranial tumours such as glioma or meningioma, face a markedly elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), with reported rates of deep vein thrombosis between 15% and 70% depending on tumour entity and surgical extent. Current prophylactic strategies rely predominantly on pharmacological and mechanical measures and do not account for the individual complexity of coagulation dynamics. Modified thromboelastometry, employing a low-dose tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) test, enables functional assessment of both fibrinolytic capacity and prothrombotic states at the point of care. We hypothesize that preoperative and perioperative thromboelastometric parameters - in particular lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test - are associated with the occurrence of thromboembolic events in neurosurgical patients. Methods TENS is a prospective, multicenter, observational prognostic factor study targeting 350 evaluable participants (up to 369 enrolled to account for attrition) across four university hospitals in Cologne, Munich (two centres), and Oldenburg. Eligible patients are adults (≥ 18 years) scheduled for neurosurgical procedures involving intracranial tumour resection or with an anticipated operative duration of ≥ 4 h. Thromboelastometric measurements (EXTEM, INTEM, FIBTEM, low-dose TPA test) are performed at three defined time points: before surgery, at the end of surgery, and on postoperative day 1. The primary objective is to assess the prognostic association between lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test and objectively imaging-confirmed venous thromboembolic events occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints comprise further thromboelastometric parameters, standard coagulation laboratory values, and clinical outcomes including length of hospital stay, duration of surgery, ICU stay, and days at home at day 30. Conclusions Modified thromboelastometry has the potential to improve individualised risk stratification for thromboembolism in neurosurgical patients. If lysis time in the low-dose TPA test demonstrates prognostic value for thromboembolic events, this could inform the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for high-risk surgical populations. Trial registration, date Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien (DRKS), No. DRKS00034388, registered October 8, 2024. Anonymised participant-level data and the statistical analysis code will be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author following publication of the primary results, subject to applicable data protection regulations and the terms of the institutional data sharing agreement (see chapter The full study protocol will be publicly accessible via the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS, No. DRKS00034388). Trial status The study is currently in active recruitment. Recruitment was initiated at the coordinating centre in Cologne on 19 December 2024, with additional centres opening after completion of their local approval and site-initiation processes. As of March 2026, fewer than 50% of the target sample of 350 evaluable participants had been enrolled. Recruitment is expected to be completed by March 2027.

title: After-hours on-site radiologist availability and emergency CT reporting: a roster-based cohort with staffing-boundary analysis.
Prospective, Population-Based Evaluation of Costs and Outcomes of Status Epilepticus According to the New Definition.
abstract: Background To address the paucity of data on outcomes and costs of status epilepticus (SE) following the updated 2015 International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) definition and changes in clinical practice guidelines in Germany. Methods This prospective population-based study (October 2018-March 2020) included adult patients from postal code area prefix 35, representative of Germany, diagnosed with SE according to the 2015 ILAE definition. Costs were calculated using German Diagnosis-Related Groups (G-DRG). Results In total, 181 patients were included. Mean inpatient costs were €10,543 (median €6376; range €845-€133,267), corresponding to €939 per hospital day (median €580.8; range €76.8-€12,115). Mean length of stay (LOS) was 11 days (median 9; range 1-67). In univariable analyses, super-refractory SE was associated with higher costs and longer LOS (both p Conclusions This study provides population-based data on costs and outcomes of SE in Germany, serving as a basis for future cost-effectiveness analyses. Compared with earlier studies, lower direct costs and shorter LOS were observed. Identification of high-risk constellations may support clinical decision-making and optimize monitoring, treatment escalation, and allocation of intensive care resources.

title: Circulating cell-death-associated biomarkers and inflammatory severity in Hymenoptera sting envenomation: a single-center retrospective study.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Background Severe Hymenoptera sting envenomation can cause systemic inflammation, shock, and multi-organ injury. Gasdermin D cleavage and RIPK3 phosphorylation are associated with inflammatory cell-death pathways, but circulating measurements cannot by themselves establish a specific cellular death mechanism. We therefore evaluated the clinical associations of serum GSDMD-p30, p-RIPK3, IL-1β, and IL-18 with illness severity in patients with Hymenoptera sting envenomation. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 142 adults admitted between January 2023 and December 2025. Clinical severity was categorized at admission using a four-level institution-specific scheme: Grade I, local/minimal systemic manifestations without organ dysfunction; Grade II, systemic allergic manifestations without organ dysfunction; Grade III, single-organ failure; and Grade IV, multi-organ failure and/or anaphylactic shock. Archived serum was available for 98 patients (Grade I/II/III/IV: 30/33/22/13). Serum GSDMD-p30, p-RIPK3, IL-1β, and IL-18 were measured by ELISA-based assays. Associations with severity grade and SOFA score and exploratory same-cohort ROC performance for Grade III-IV disease were assessed. Results The cohort included 42 Grade I, 48 Grade II, 34 Grade III, and 18 Grade IV patients. Sting count, time to hospital presentation, inflammatory indices, organ-injury markers, SOFA score, ICU admission, and length of stay increased with clinical severity. In the serum subset, mean GSDMD-p30 increased from 0.82 ± 0.21 ng/mL in Grade I to 9.43 ± 2.18 ng/mL in Grade IV, and p-RIPK3 increased from 0.64 ± 0.18 to 7.84 ± 1.87 ng/mL (global p Conclusion Circulating GSDMD-p30, p-RIPK3, IL-1β, and IL-18 were associated with clinical severity and organ-failure burden in this retrospective cohort. These findings support further evaluation of these proteins as candidate severity-associated biomarkers, but they do not demonstrate PANoptosis, establish cell-specific origin, or validate a clinical triage tool. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized assays and adjusted analyses are required.

title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Introduction Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting. Methods and analysis The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively. Ethics and dissemination This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication. Clinical trial registration identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

title: Safety of in-hospital delay of appendectomy in complicated appendicitis - a propensity score-matched analysis of 1027 patients.
abstract: Introduction Appendectomy is one of the most frequently performed emergency surgical procedures worldwide. Current guidelines recommend surgical intervention within 24 h for uncomplicated appendicitis; however, the optimal timing for patients with complicated appendicitis remains unclear. Recent studies suggest that in-hospital delay may be safe in uncomplicated cases, yet patients with clinical or radiological signs of perforation are usually excluded. This study aims to identify clinical and laboratory risk factors for perforation and to evaluate whether it is safe to delay surgery by 6 to 9 h in patients presenting with signs of complicated appendicitis. Methods This retrospective single-center study included patients who underwent emergency surgery for complicated appendicitis between January 2008 and June 2023. Perforation was defined histopathologically, and complications were recorded perioperatively. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors for perforation and complications. Propensity-score (PS) matching was performed to control confounding factors. Results A total of 1,027 patients with suspected complicated appendicitis were included. PS matching yielded two cohorts of 327 patients. No significant differences were observed in perforation rates (46.5% vs. 47.1%; p = 0.88) or complication rates (23.5% vs. 21.4%; p = 0.51). Logistic regression analysis of the PS matched groups confirmed that a delay of surgery of > 6 h was not associated with increased risk of perforation (OR 1.03; 95% CI 0.75-1.41; p = 0.87) or complication rate (OR 0.87; 95% CI 0.59-1.27; p = 0.47). A 9-hour threshold to surgery showed no significant differences in perforation rates (50.0% vs. 44.9%; p = 0.34) or complication rates (24.7% vs. 19.7%; p = 0.25). Logistic regression analysis did not demonstrate an association between a surgical delay of > 9 h and either perforation (OR 0.79; 95% CI: 0.51-1.22; p = 0.28) or complication rate (OR 0.68; 95% CI: 0.39-1.17; p = 0.16). Age > 65 years, higher BMI, symptom duration > 48 h at the time of admission, elevated inflammatory markers, and suspected perforation on imaging were identified as independent risk factors for perforation. Higher ASA scores, male sex, suspected perforation on imaging, and elevated CRP levels were associated with increased complication rates. Interpretation A delay in surgical intervention of 6-9 h may be acceptable in patients with suspected complicated appendicitis without increasing the risk of perforation and / or complications.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
Fishbone-Induced Gastrointestinal Perforation: A 21-Case Series from Vietnam.
journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) perforation caused by fishbone ingestion is rare but potentially life-threatening. Because symptoms are nonspecific and most patients do not recall or are unaware of ingesting the bone, diagnosis is often delayed. This study presents a series of 21 patients with fishbone-induced GI perforation and highlights the importance of early surgical intervention. We retrospectively reviewed 21 patients treated at a tertiary referral hospital in southern Vietnam, from June 2022 to August 2024. Data included demographics, symptoms, imaging findings, surgical approach, perforation site, complications, and outcomes. Thirteen patients were female (61.9%), and the mean age was 57.7±13.2 years (range, 39-85). Computed tomography (CT) was performed in 12 patients, and a fishbone was identified in 10 cases (83.3%). Diagnostic laparoscopy was attempted in 17 patients (81%), and the perforation site was identified in all attempted cases. Laparoscopic surgery was completed in 8 patients (47.1%), whereas 9 of 17 patients (52.9%) required conversion to open surgery. Four patients (19.0%) underwent primary open surgery. The most common perforation site was the colon (13 patients, 61.9%), followed by the small intestine (6 patients, 28.6%) and the stomach (2 patients, 9.5%). Postoperative complications occurred in 5 patients (23.8%), and one patient (4.8%) died. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 8.7±5.1 days (range, 3-26). Fishbone-induced GI perforation should be considered in patients with unexplained peritonitis, especially in regions with high fish consumption. CT and laparoscopy are key diagnostic tools. Early surgical intervention reduces morbidity and improves outcomes.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Intravenous Flecainide Within an Early, Electrophysiologist-Guided Rhythm-Control Strategy for Atrial Fibrillation in the Emergency Department (HEROMEDICUS Study)
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Atrial fibrillation accounts for approximately 0.5–1% of emergency department visits. Contemporary ESC and ACC/AHA guidelines address acute pharmacological cardioversion, anticoagulation before cardioversion, and delayed “wait-and-see” strategies; however, real-world implementation of an early, specialist-guided pathway in the emergency department remains incompletely described. In the HEROMEDICUS study we implemented a protocol for acute management of patients presenting to the emergency department with atrial fibrillation as their main complaint. The present analysis reports the safety and efficacy of intravenous flecainide within that pathway. Methods: All patients who visited the emergency department from 8 September 2023 to 10 October 2025 with a primary diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia were screened. Patients with known heart failure (left ventricular ejection fraction 300 mg propafenone or >200 mg flecainide were eligible for intravenous flecainide 2 mg/kg (maximum 150 mg) infused over 10 minutes. Follow-up at the outpatient atrial fibrillation clinic was scheduled through the application. Results: Of 277 patients screened (15 atrial tachycardia, 28 atrial flutter, 234 atrial fi-brillation - mean age 68.5±12.3 years, heart rates 122.9±25.1 bpm and CHA2DS2-VASc 2.3±1.5 points, 53% females), 85 fulfilled criteria for intravenous flecainide administration; of them, 83 had atrial fibrillation on both the triage and recruitment electrocardiograms and 2 had atrial flutter on the triage but atrial fibrillation on the recruitment electrocar-diogram – thus all patients receiving flecainide effectively had atrial fibrillation. A first-diagnosed episode was recorded in 130 patients. Sinus rhythm was restored with flecainide alone in 61/85 patients (71.8%; 95% CI 61.4–80.2%). Of the remaining 24 patients, 22 were subsequently electrically cardioverted in the emergency department and 2 failed both strategies and were discharged after rate control. Among the 26 successful pharmacological conversions with available timestamps, median time from start of in-fusion to sinus rhythm was 13 minutes. No patient developed ventricular proarrhythmia or atrial flutter with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction, at least during their stay in the emergency department. Also, no thromboembolic events occurred in the same period. None of the 85 flecainide-treated patients was admitted. Conclusions: Intravenous flecainide was safe and effective as the initial pharmacological option within the HEROMEDICUS emergency department pathway for selected patients with atrial fibrillation. Subsequent electrical cardioversion rescued most pharmacological failures. These findings apply to atrial fibrillation; they should not be extrapolated to atrial flutter or atrial tachycardia. In the absence of a control group, we report the observed absence of admissions following implementation of our protocol.
