Positive results regarding cost-effectiveness were reported (n = 11), including cost-savings (n = 1), as well as implementation determinants (n = 11). However, evidence on sustained implementation was limited. Barriers included innovation design, complexity, workflow compatibility, work and IT infrastructure, and costs. Conclusion Included studies suggest most prehospital stroke triage tools are cost-effective, but implementation remains largely context-dependent. Barriers, including innovation complexity, role delineation, workflow fit, design, and costs, highlight the need for future studies to integrate health economics into an implementation science framework alongside clinical outcomes.

title: Efficiency evaluation of secondary public general hospitals in Shandong Province, China based on three-stage data envelopment analysis.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the operational efficiency of secondary-level public general hospitals in Shandong Province, thereby providing scientific evidence for optimising the allocation of hospital healthcare resources. Methods A sample of secondary public general hospitals across 16 prefecture-level cities in Shandong Province, China, was selected. The first stage employed the Super-Efficiency SBM model to measure overall technical efficiency (TE), pure technical efficiency (PTE), and scale efficiency (SE). The second stage constructed an SFA regression model to analyse the impact of external environmental factors on input slack variables. The third stage recalculated efficiency using adjusted inputs and original outputs, comparing efficiency differences before and after adjustment alongside regional characteristics. Results The TE and PTE of Shandong Province's secondary public general hospitals topped 1 in the majority of the first stage, while the SE often fell short of 1. The greatest mean values for TE (0.952), PTE (0.983), and SE (0.971) were found in the Lunan Economic Circle. PTE variations were the main factor influencing TE stability, and the provincial capital economic circle (TE = 0.808) and Jiaodong economic circle (TE = 0.851) displayed comparatively lower averages. Second-stage SFA regression results indicate that fiscal allocations positively correlate with hospital practising (assistant) physicians, actual bed capacity, fixed assets, and total cost redundancy ( p p Conclusion Secondary-level public general hospitals in Shandong Province demonstrate relatively high overall efficiency, yet remain significantly influenced by external environmental factors, indicating considerable scope for improvement. This study reveals that differentiated improvement strategies should be implemented across distinct regions based on their actual developmental circumstances, thereby propelling hospitals towards high-quality development.

title: Strategies towards designing visible and near-infrared light driven molecular motors.
abstract: Light is one of the most powerful and versatile stimuli for controlling molecular motion, serving as a key driving force in the development of photoresponsive molecular systems. Among these architectures, artificial molecular motors represent a unique class of molecules capable of converting light energy into chirality-controlled unidirectional rotary motion. However, the majority of reported examples are operated under ultraviolet excitation, which restricts their practical applicability especially in biomolecular systems and sensitive responsive materials. To address these limitations, major recent effort has been devoted to extending photoresponsiveness of molecular motors into the visible and near-infrared (NIR) regions which enables milder and more efficient operation. This review summarizes the principal molecular design strategies that have been developed to achieve such red-shifted photoactivation of molecular motors. Moreover, we highlight the current challenges and outline future directions toward the realization of high-efficiency, multifunctional, and programmable visible/NIR-light-driven molecular motors for integration into responsive materials, catalysis, and biological systems.

title: Robust mask-based appointment scheduling in primary care practices.
abstract: In most health care systems, a primary care physician (PCP) is both the first instance consulted by patients with medical concerns and the instance coordinating patients' continued access to medical care. Due to the PCP's pivotal role, we address challenges of a high-quality primary care service by interday appointment scheduling on a tactical decision level. In addition to patients who seek medical care by appointments, we also consider patients who complicate the PCP's schedule planning by seeking immediate care as walk-ins without prior notice or failing to show up to their appointments. We study appointment scheduling systems based on so-called masks and focus on the balanced workload of the PCP in form of the mask design problem. To account for different uncertainties in demand for treatment, we extend the mask design problem to the robust mask design and the robust multimask design problem. For all three problems, we provide a combinatorial interpretation by a network flow and design model. We develop a solution approach that combines binary search with compact formulations (of extensions) of minimum cost flow problems. Finally, we conduct an extensive case study by agent-based simulation. We evaluate the mask-based appointment scheduling systems and compare them with five appointment scheduling systems from the literature on the basis of key performance indicators such as the PCP's overtime and idle time as well as the number of unsuccessful treatment requests or rejected walk-ins.

title: Addressing Physical Therapy Access Gaps: Impact of Embedded Scheduling Tools on Patient Language Preference.
abstract: Importance Patients with Non-English language preference (NELP) face barriers accessing outpatient rehabilitation services, with disparities at the referral-to-scheduling stage. Despite decades of Federal mandates to provide meaningful access, patients with NELP remain operationally invisible in high-volume scheduling workflows, contributing to lower completion rates and delays compared to patients identified as English-proficient (EP). Objective The objective was to evaluate whether implementing an electronic health record (EHR)-integrated language filter and visible language preference field improves referral scheduling for patients with NELP. Design This was a quasi-experimental study using interrupted time-series analysis. Setting This study took place in outpatient rehabilitation clinics at an urban academic medical center. Participants We studied 19,260 physical therapy referrals, including 985 (5.1%) patients with NELP and 18,275 (94.9%) patients with EP, from September 2024 to May 2025. Intervention We used a sortable "Preferred Language" field and toggle filter in the EHR referral workqueue enabling schedulers to identify and proactively schedule patients with NELP. Main outcomes Our primary outcome was the proportion of referrals scheduled within 10 days of referral. Secondary outcomes included overall scheduling rates, time from referral to scheduling, scheduling to visit, and referral to visit; no-show and unscheduled referral rates; and Press Ganey patient satisfaction scores related to appointment scheduling. Results Patients with NELP demonstrated a larger increase in the likelihood of scheduling within 10 days following the intervention (adjusted RL = 2.86, 95% CI = 1.82-4.48) relative to patients with EP. Scheduling within 10 days improved from 27.4% to 31.3% pre- and post-intervention. However, baseline disparities persisted, with patients with NELP experiencing a longer median time to scheduling throughout the study period (7 days vs 6 days). Implementation fidelity varied, with 22% of schedulers regularly using the tool. Conclusions An EHR-integrated language visibility intervention improved 10-day scheduling rates among patients with NELP (adjusted RL = 2.86), yet baseline disparities persisted. Low implementation fidelity suggests that visibility intervention requires pairing with capacity enhancement and accountability structures for sustained, equitable access to rehabilitation services. Relevance Language-visibility EHR tools improve but do not eliminate scheduling disparities, pointing to the need for implementation infrastructure alongside technical solutions.

title: Patient preferences for treatment‑free intervals in multiple myeloma: mixed‑methods insights on monitoring trade‑offs and supportive care improvements.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Purpose Continuous and maintenance therapy remains central to multiple myeloma (MM) care, but repeated treatment-related healthcare encounters may impose physical, psychosocial, and logistical burden. We explored patient preferences regarding intervals between active treatment contacts, monitoring trade-offs, and opportunities to improve inpatient and outpatient care. Methods A 12-month, single-center mixed-methods survey was conducted among 100 patients with MM at a German tertiary center. The survey assessed the perceived importance and preferred length of treatment-free intervals (TFIs), monitoring perceptions, relapse-risk trade-offs, inpatient stressors, and care-improvement proposals. Quantitative responses were summarized with item-specific denominators and exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Free-text responses underwent inductive content analysis by two independent raters and mixed-methods integration. Results Intervals between inpatient treatments were rated 10/10 by 49/100 participants (49.0%; 95% CI 38.9-59.2) and 0/10 by 9/100 (9.0%; 95% CI 4.2-16.4). The most frequently reported inpatient stressors were separation from family (27.0%), treatment-related symptoms or side effects (23.0%), and fatigue (17.0%). Regular check-ups were reassuring for 77/100 (77.0%; 95% CI 67.5-84.8) and burdensome for 13/100 (13.0%; 95% CI 7.1-21.2). Seven of 100 participants (7.0%; 95% CI 2.9-13.9) explicitly accepted higher relapse risk for longer TFIs. Preferred minimum interval length was heterogeneous; 39/99 (39.4%; 95% CI 29.7-49.7) preferred > 8 weeks. Qualitative narratives emphasized recovery, autonomy, restoration of routines, and modifiable care-process factors. Conclusion Patients frequently valued intervals between active treatment contacts for recovery, while monitoring was predominantly reassuring. These descriptive findings do not establish the safety or clinical appropriateness of longer TFIs but support prospective evaluation of preference-sensitive scheduling and monitoring.

title: Gender differences among board-certified general surgeons in Israel: demographics, professional advancement, and leadership.
journal: Israel journal of health policy research
abstract: Background Women remain underrepresented in general surgery leadership and academic roles globally, yet specialty-specific data from Israel are limited. This study examines gender differences among board-certified general surgeons in Israel across demographic, professional, and leadership domains. Methods A cross-sectional, confidential questionnaire was distributed electronically to all board-certified general surgeons registered with the Israeli Surgical Association in 2026. A total of 105 surgeons responded (15.2%). Participants were stratified by gender and compared across demographic characteristics, employment patterns, operative scope, fellowship training, academic activity, and management roles. Results Of 105 respondents, 78 (74.3%) were men and 27 (25.7%) were women. Women had a longer residency duration (median 7 vs. 6 years, p = 0.024). Women were less likely to hold full-time public hospital positions (63.0% vs. 84.6%, p = 0.029), participate in on-call (44.4% vs. 80.8%, p = 0.0009) or senior on-call duties (7.4% vs. 38.5%, p = 0.003), and had a substantially narrower operative scope (median 3 vs. 5 surgery types, p = 0.0002). Women were significantly more likely to practice breast surgery (48.1% vs. 16.7%, p = 0.002) and less likely to have completed a fellowship (59.3% vs. 84.6%, p = 0.013) or trained abroad (25.9% vs. 62.8%, p = 0.0015). Academic productivity was also lower among women: fewer taught students (74.1% vs. 91.0%, p = 0.044), published articles (29.6% vs. 65.4%, p = 0.002), or held academic appointments (25.9% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.042). Women were less likely to hold any management role (25.9% vs. 51.3%, p = 0.026). Conclusions Significant gender disparities exist among board-certified general surgeons in Israel across all domains examined. Women bear a systematically different professional burden, with less call coverage, narrower operative scope, fewer fellowships, lower academic output, and reduced leadership representation. These findings highlight structural barriers that persist beyond training completion. Of particular concern is the leadership gap: in the Israeli hospital system, senior positions are long-tenured and turn over infrequently, meaning that generational change in the trainee demographic alone will not close this gap within any reasonable timeframe. Mandatory, policy-level structural intervention is required alongside broader institutional efforts to promote gender equity in Israeli general surgery.

title: Leveraging Primary Care Resources Through Quality Improvement to Increase Follow-up After Mental Health Emergency Department Visits.
abstract: Introduction Timely follow-up after mental behavioral health (MBH) crises can improve health outcomes; moreover, it is a national quality metric. We aimed to improve the completion of 7-day follow-up after emergency department (ED) discharge for youth with an MBH concern from 28.7% of discharges to 50.0% within 12 months. Methods We used quality improvement methods from November 1, 2024, to October 31, 2025, across 3 primary care sites and 2 ED sites. Baseline data, literature reviews, and lived experience identified key drivers and failure modes. We developed 2 interventions: (1) direct phone outreach after discharge and (2) increased access in pediatric primary care (PPC). The primary outcome measure was the percentage of ED MBH discharges with a completed follow-up appointment within 7 days of discharge. Process measures included the percentage of patients who received a postdischarge outreach call and who followed up within PPC. The balancing measure was return ED MBH visits within 30 days. Results The mean follow-up percentage increased from 28.7% (n = 258) to 40.3% (n = 334). Follow-up for Medicaid-insured patients increased from 24% to 35% and remained stable for commercially insured patients (42%), decreasing our equity gap by 11%. Outreach calls occurred following 52.4% of discharges. Follow-up visits within PPC increased from 3.5% of discharges to 10.7% of discharges. There was no change in return ED visits within 30 days of ED discharge. Conclusions Increasing access to pediatric primary care and implementing timely postdischarge follow-up calls can improve follow-up within a large healthcare system for patients discharged from the ED for MBH concerns.

title: Patient Satisfaction With a One-Stop Service Center in a Tertiary Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Objective To investigate the current status of outpatient satisfaction and its key influencing factors under the "One-Stop" service model, providing an empirical basis for optimizing outpatient service processes and enhancing operational efficiency. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2025, selecting 1016 outpatients (or their family members) from 15 departments in our hospital. The Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire (PSQ) was used for investigation, covering basic patient information, appointment experience, quality of doctor-patient communication, and overall satisfaction. One-stop service convenience (11 items) and communication quality (4 items) were extracted as composite scores. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27.0, employing descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, and hierarchical linear regression to identify independent predictors of satisfaction. Results The overall satisfaction level among outpatients was relatively high, at 89.17% (906/1016). Pearson's correlation analysis revealed that both one-stop convenience ( r = 0.992, p r = 0.934, p β = 0.767, p β = 0.254, p R 2 = 0.999). In contrast, demographic variables (age, gender) and binary waiting time (on-time vs. delayed) were not significant in the multivariable model (all p > 0.05). Among the respondents, 94.69% (962/1016) expressed high recognition of the environmental convenience, and within this group, the excellent satisfaction rate reached 96.67%. Conclusion The "One-Stop" service model can effectively enhance outpatient satisfaction. Service process efficiency (one-stop convenience) is the dominant driver of satisfaction, while the quality of doctor-patient communication serves as a distinct and complementary contributor. Environmental convenience remains a foundational element. These three factors should be key focuses in the continuous improvement of healthcare quality.

title: Unmet social needs in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease linked to increased risk of missed appointments.
abstract: Objectives Health-related social needs (HRSNs) are associated with worse health outcomes. This study aimed to identify unmet HRSNs in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate their association with missed medical and biologic infusion appointments. Methods This study was conducted in an ambulatory pediatric gastroenterology program and infusion center from December 2021 to December 2024. Patients with IBD or guardians completed a standardized HRSNs screen. The primary outcome was the number of missed medical and infusion appointments in the year prior to screening. Bivariate and multivariable models without and with adjustment for socio-demographic characteristics were used. Results A total of 191 patients with IBD were screened (median age 16 years, 68.59% male). Overall, 17.8% screened positive for HRSNs. Among patients with at least one completed medical appointment ( n = 184), 54% had one or more missed appointments. Patients with HRSNs had a 63% (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 1.63, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11, 2.38, p = 0.0121) higher rate of missed medical appointments, which remained significant after adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, and sex (IRR: 1.56, 95% CI: 1.07, 2.28, p = 0.0212). Inadequate housing (8.38%), followed by food insecurity (6.81%) were the most prevalent HRSNs in our pediatric population. Unmet needs related to utilities ( p = 0.0013), transportation ( p = 0.0014) and healthcare cost ( p = 0.0282) were significantly associated with missed appointments. Positive HRSNs were not associated with missed biologic therapy infusions ( p = 0.155). Conclusion HRSNs were significantly associated with missed medical appointments. Future research should aim to develop strategies that address specific HRSNs, along with personalized interventions to the individual circumstances.

title: Patient and carer perceptions and experiences of technology-facilitated appointment reminders in healthcare: a scoping review.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
abstract: Background and aim Missed healthcare appointments, or "Did Not Attends" (DNAs), pose challenges for healthcare systems. Technology-facilitated reminder systems, such as SMS and phone calls are often implemented to improve attendance. This scoping review aimed to map the evidence on patient and carer perspectives and experiences of technology-enabled appointment reminders in healthcare and, secondly, examine how equity-relevant characteristics were reported. Methods A scoping review which searched EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus, and EBSCO from September to October 2025 for studies published between 2010 and 2025. Studies examining patient or informal/unpaid carer perceptions and experiences of technology-based reminder systems were included. Equity-relevant dimensions were examined using the PROGRESS-Plus framework. Data were extracted and summarised using a structured form; with findings synthesised thematically. Results A total of 45 studies were included. Most focused on patient perspectives, with comparatively fewer centered specifically on carers. The majority were cross-sectional surveys, with fewer longitudinal and theory-informed designs. SMS reminders were the most studied modality, followed by phone calls and app-based notifications. Patients and carers reported high satisfaction. Recurring barriers included digital exclusion, language challenges, confidentiality concerns, and socio-economic inequalities. Equity reporting across studies was inconsistent, with many studies describing sociodemographic characteristics without examining how they influenced engagement with reminder systems. Conclusions Technology-enabled appointment reminders are widely perceived as useful. Digital exclusion, privacy, language, and trust-related barriers limit engagement and access. Greater user involvement is needed to ensure reminder systems support, rather than reproduce, healthcare inequalities. Future research and implementation efforts should prioritise equity-informed design and evaluation.

title: Preventing Avoidable Amputations in Somalia: Building a Diabetic Foot Care Pathway for Somali Hospitals [Commentary].
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
abstract: Diabetes-related foot disease requires coordinated prevention, timely assessment, and access to treatment. Two hospital-based studies in Mogadishu reported foot ulcer prevalence of 15.0% and 17.9% among adults with diabetes; neither provides a national estimate or establishes the effectiveness of a care pathway. This commentary proposes a six-function pathway for Somali hospitals: screening, risk stratification, triage, initial treatment, coordination, and recurrence prevention. The proposal draws on International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot guidance, the World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions, Somali hospital studies, and implementation experience elsewhere. Established clinical recommendations are distinguished from author-proposed responsibilities, pilot arrangements, and operational targets. The pathway has not undergone formal stakeholder review, feasibility testing, or validation in Somali hospitals. A proposed 12-month pilot would begin with assessment of staffing, competencies, supplies, referral access, patient costs, and data governance. It would then test a clinical algorithm, supervised training, referral coordination, and a small set of defined process and clinical measures. Emergency care must not wait for routine review or completion of a treatment bundle. Expansion should depend on demonstrated readiness, affordable recurrent financing, and evaluation across different hospital settings. The intended contribution is a locally testable organization of established care, with explicit responsibilities and measurable transitions, rather than new clinical guidance or a proven amputation-reduction intervention.

title: Impact of Primary Health Care Reforms in Quebec's Health Care System: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Introduction Primary health care (PHC) reforms in Quebec between 2000 and 2023 aimed to improve accessibility, continuity, efficiency, and equity through organisational transformation, notably the Family Medicine Groups (FMGs), centralised waiting lists (Guichets d'accès), the advanced access model, and legislative instruments such as Bill 20. The evidence on their cumulative impact remains fragmented across disciplines, outcome domains, and study designs. Objective To systematically identify, appraise, and synthesise the empirical evidence on the association between PHC reforms implemented in Quebec during the 2000-2023 reform cycle and organisational transformation, accessibility, health outcomes, costs, and equity, with mental health service organisation treated as a distinct policy stream outside the scope of this review. Methods This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 statement and a protocol registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023421145). PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched on 7 November 2023 and the searches were rerun on 3 September 2026, complemented by structured searches of Quebec governmental and institutional repositories and reference-list checking. Screening, extraction, and appraisal (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, MMAT 2018) were performed in duplicate. Reports were analysed for policy documents, implementation, descriptive and qualitative studies, and comparative evaluative studies, and synthesised narratively by reform mechanism and outcome domain, following SWiM guidance for quantitative evidence. Results 192 reports were included (171 from the original search and 21 from the update), corresponding to 26 policy, institutional, review, or commentary documents, 131 implementation, descriptive, or qualitative studies, and 35 comparative evaluative studies, including one pragmatic randomised trial with reported results. Policy documents and implementation studies consistently describe organisational transformation and rising attachment rates. Comparative evaluative studies report that FMG enrolment and centralised-waiting-list attachment were associated with modest reductions in avoidable emergency department use and improvements in guideline-concordant care processes, whereas quasi-experimental evaluations of enrolment incentives found no meaningful population-level gain in affiliation. Evidence on health outcomes and costs is limited and largely proxy-based; socioeconomic and geographic gradients in access persisted across the period. Early evaluations of the Primary Care Access Points (2024-2026) report high patient-reported unmet needs when no physician appointment is obtained. Conclusions The reforms were accompanied by substantial structural change and by limited, uneven, and mostly modest associations with patient-level access, outcomes, and equity. Confidence in these conclusions is moderate for organisational and attachment-related findings, low for health outcomes and costs, and constrained throughout by incomplete reporting and the scarcity of counterfactual designs.

title: Preoperative inspiratory muscle training for patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy: a randomized feasibility study.
abstract: Background Patients undergoing surgery due to peritoneal metastases (PM) are at high risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). While several studies have provided promising results regarding the positive effects of preoperative inspiratory muscle training (IMT) regarding length of hospital stay and PPCs after other types of major abdominal surgery, its feasibility in the preoperative management of patients with PM is still unclear. The aim of the study was to evaluate the feasibility of preoperative IMT for patients scheduled for cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). Methods A single-blinded randomized controlled feasibility study was conducted in Uppsala, Sweden, between 2016 and 2020. Inclusion criteria were age ≥ 18 years, surgery scheduled ≥ 2 weeks after inclusion, and proficiency in Swedish. Patients were randomized 1:1 to either IMT or positive expiratory pressure (PEP). Feasibility was evaluated using two domains: process feasibility (recruitment, intervention adherence, and patient acceptability) and scientific feasibility (ability to perform pre- and postoperative respiratory muscle and lung function assessments, reproducibility of assessments, and adverse events). Preliminary treatment effects and incidence of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) were also evaluated. Results Thirty participants were enrolled, with a recruitment rate of 11%. The median training period was 24.5 days, with adherence of 77% in the intervention group and 98% in the control group. Acceptability was high, with 87% rating the training program ≥ 5 on a scale of 1-10. Two participants withdrew due to discomfort at the postoperative assessments, and the reproducibility of assessments was 57-100%. One IMT participant withdrew due to a dry cough. The intervention group showed a larger increase in maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) from baseline to follow-up and faster recovery of vital capacity (VC) than controls. PPCs were more frequent in the control group. Conclusions Preoperative IMT was acceptable to patients and safe, but recruitment and attrition were identified as obstacles to address in a future full-scale RCT. Trial registration NCT05665257 . Registered 23 December 2022-retrospectively registered.

title: Stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Stroke health literacy refers to the ability of non-medical individuals to recognize stroke symptoms and make timely decisions, which is critical for improving outcomes. However, data on stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior in Bogotá, Colombia, remain limited. Objective To assess stroke symptom knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes and to identify sociodemographic predictors of limited knowledge and suboptimal response. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2023 and April 2024 in Bogotá, Colombia. A structured questionnaire was administered to 5,402 adults with hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes. Participants were recruited using a non-probabilistic sampling strategy, primarily from individuals under routine follow-up within the Bogotá public health network, and were identified through multiple recruitment strategies, including institutional databases. Surveys were conducted either by telephone or in person. Continuous variables were summarized using descriptive statistics, differences in categorical variables were assessed using chi-square tests, and binomial logistic regression models were applied to evaluate adjusted associations. Results Of 6,050 respondents, 5,402 met inclusion criteria (median age 67 years; 46.3% male). Although most participants recognized that ischemic stroke can cause disability (89.6%) and death (91.1%), 32.5% reported no knowledge of stroke symptoms. Limited symptom knowledge was independently associated with male sex (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12-1.42), low educational attainment (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.38-1.82), and low socioeconomic status (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.85-2.60). Regarding intended response, 26.6% would not activate emergency medical services, and 52% reported they would schedule an outpatient appointment instead. Lower educational attainment was associated with greater likelihood of reporting non-emergency responses (all p Conclusions Despite high awareness that stroke can cause disability and death, substantial gaps in symptom recognition and intended response persist, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to improve stroke literacy in high-risk populations.

title: Haitian Mamas: The Development and Two-Year Implementation of an OB/GYN-Based Preventive Behavioral Health Group in a Safety-Net Hospital Setting.
abstract: Perinatal mental health conditions are among the leading causes of maternal mortality in the United States. However, 50% to 70% of perinatal mental health cases go undiagnosed, and of those diagnosed, fewer than 30% receive treatment. At Boston Medical Center, a large safety-net academic medical center in the northeastern United States (US), this treatment gap became apparent when new Refugee Women's Health Clinic patient visits increased by 138% following an influx of Haitian forced migrants starting in 2021. In response, we developed and implemented Haitian Mamas, a same-day access preventive behavioral health group within the Obstetrics and Gynecology department. This quality improvement study evaluates the development of Haitian Mamas from August 2023 to 2025, using four Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles. We evaluated the feasibility of this program across six domains: reach, engagement, integration of measurement-based care, financial viability, adaptability, and provider-perceived acceptability. Over two years, 196 women participated in the group, with an average of eight members per group, and there was a progressive improvement in integrating measurement-based care, which rose from 11.5% in Cycle 1 to 67.4% in Cycle 4. 35% screened positive for moderate to server mental health concerns. A thematic analysis of qualitative data from providers' weekly post-group reflections identified implementation barriers and facilitators for Haitian Mamas. Our findings suggest that the development and implementation of a same-day access, OBGYN-based preventive behavioral health group for perinatal patients in a safety-net hospital setting is operationally feasible.

title: Reengineering the Concept of Emergency Care.
journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) absorb most acute unscheduled care (AUC) in the United States. Routing all of this care through one high-intensity system serves no one well: crowding delays care for time-critical patients; visits that turn on evaluation and coordination, and routine and chronic care defined by longitudinal needs, are delivered episodically and at high cost in a setting built for resuscitation and stabilization; and clinicians trained for emergencies spend much of their time on work the category does not fit. I argue that this is not only a capacity or workflow problem but a conceptual one. In practice, "emergency care" is defined by arrival: crossing the ED threshold, not clinical risk, triggers the legal duties, insurance protections, and workflows attached to the label. This was no one's mistake; routing everything through the one door always open was a rational adaptation to a fragmented system. But the adaptation no longer merely persists; it forecloses alternatives. Using conceptual engineering, I trace how history, regulation, payment, public scripts, and lexical entrenchment stabilize this system, and situate it against the social drivers that make ED-as-default ethically necessary and operationally costly. I then propose an ameliorated concept of emergency care: a risk- and time-sensitive, expert-mediated, priority-conferring subset of AUC, determined by structured triage wherever it occurs. Because a definition changes nothing by itself, I outline a phased implementation pathway, show how it applies across delivery settings, including rural and safety-net systems where the ED should remain the local acute care hub, and describe the workforce implications for emergency medicine. The choice posed to the specialty is whether to keep treating crowding, mismatched care, and clinician dissonance as operational problems to optimize within the ED, or to recognize them as properties of what we mean by emergency care and of the system that enacts it.

title: Mental Health and Addiction Care Professionals' Views on Artificial Intelligence Integration in Oman: A Descriptive Qualitative Study.
abstract: Aim To explore mental health and addiction care professionals' views on integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice at a tertiary psychiatric hospital. Design A qualitative descriptive study. Methods Purposive sampling recruited 17 nurses, psychiatrists, psychologists, and social workers. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated from Arabic into English, and analysed through codebook-based thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke's six phases. Results Four themes were identified: variable familiarity with artificial intelligence (AI); actual experience with artificial intelligence and non-artificial-intelligence digital technologies, with telemedicine and electronic health records more common than AI-specific tools; anticipated benefits involving efficiency, clinical decision support, communication, data management, and service access; and anticipated barriers concerning infrastructure, resources, training, clinical suitability, therapeutic relationships, and ethics. Conclusion Participants were cautiously optimistic but had limited direct clinical experience and sometimes conflated AI with other digital technologies. Safe implementation requires a shared understanding of AI, reliable infrastructure, role-specific education, ethical governance, accountable human oversight, and protection of therapeutic relationships. Patient or public contribution No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting of this study. The participants were healthcare professionals.

title: The COVID-19 Pandemic Experience of Families With Children With Developmental Disorders in Northeastern Germany.
abstract: Background Developmental disorders are associated with considerable challenges for affected children and their families. During the COVID-19 pandemic, families faced additional stress, including challenging decisions regarding COVID-19 vaccination for their children. This exploratory study therefore examined the experiences of families with children with developmental disorders during the pandemic and their attitudes towards vaccination, including the perceived benefits and disadvantages of their decision. Methods This exploratory study was conducted from April to June 2022 at a university hospital in Northeastern Germany. The semi-structured interviews included open and closed questions, as well as 5-point Likert scales. Results We interviewed 65 parents of children aged 3-17 years (median age: 6; Q25/Q75: 4/11). Among them, 69% reported a negative impact on their child, most frequently emotional and behavioural changes (45%), followed by developmental and educational setbacks (26%) and social and communication difficulties (14%). Seventy-three percent of parents perceived the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on the parent-child interaction as very, rather or partly burdensome. Governmental support was judged as 'not adequate' or 'rather not adequate' by 64% of parents. Among the 44 children eligible for COVID-19 vaccination, 59% were not vaccinated. Fear of adverse events was the main reason against vaccination (81%), whereas fear of COVID-19 infection was the main motivation for those who chose to vaccinate (89%). Vaccination was associated with perceived benefits in daily life, whereas nonvaccination was associated with reduced participation and increased infection-related worries. Conclusions Most parents of children with developmental disorders perceived negative effects of the pandemic on the lives of their child and themselves. Among children eligible for COVID-19 vaccination, more than half of the parents decided against vaccination, despite reported benefits of vaccination and reported disadvantages associated with nonvaccination. Future research is needed to develop tailored vaccination campaigns and safety-focused communication strategies for children with developmental disorders.

title: Real-Time Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Digital Triage and Care-Team Integration in Early Breast Cancer: ENABLE Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background Electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) can support patient-centered oncology care, but in early breast cancer, it is unclear whether real-time ePRO-triggered triage adds benefit beyond lower-intensity app-based support and scheduled ePRO collection. Objective We tested whether adding weekly ePRO screening, rule-based triage, and care-team escalation to app-based support improves health-related quality of life (HRQoL) during systemic therapy for early breast cancer. Methods ENABLE was a multicenter, open-label, parallel-group randomized controlled trial at 2 German university hospitals. Adults with early (stage I-III) breast cancer initiating systemic therapy were randomized 1:1 to reactive patient-reported outcome assessment (RPA) or control. Both arms received the ENABLE app with educational and organizational support and scheduled HRQoL assessments at 6 fixed time points; only RPA received weekly EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale screening (trigger: score Results Of 605 randomized patients, 487 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis (RPA: n=242; control: n=245). End-of-treatment between-group differences (RPA minus control, T -score points, 95% CI, and adjusted P ) were: fatigue -3.90 (95% CI -5.77 to -2.03; P =.004), social participation +2.84 (95% CI 1.18 to 4.49; P =.01), anxiety -2.10 (95% CI -3.65 to -0.55; P =.049), depression -1.95 (95% CI -3.25 to -0.65; P =.10), sleep disturbance -1.82 (95% CI -3.43 to -0.20; P =.051), pain interference -1.44 (95% CI -3.38 to 0.49; P =.18), physical function +1.33 (95% CI -0.22 to 2.88; P =.18), and pain intensity -0.26 (95% CI -0.73 to 0.21; P =.32; 0-10 scale). All T -score differences were below the 5-point minimally important difference (MID). Exploratory time-to-deterioration analyses favored RPA for fatigue (hazard ratio [HR] 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.89), social participation (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59-0.97), and depression (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44-0.98). Of 209 monitored RPA patients, 160 (76.6%; 95% CI 70.4-81.8) triggered at least 1 alert. No intervention-related harms were identified. Conclusions ENABLE tests real-time, rule-based ePRO triage with care-team escalation against an active digital comparator rather than usual care, isolating the response pathway itself; it extends this design from metastatic disease into early breast cancer and escalates to the care team rather than to the patient alone. Benefits were domain-specific and sub-MID, in anxiety, fatigue, and social participation, tempering the expectation of a global HRQoL effect. For practice, symptom-triggered triage is a supportive-care workflow tool worth embedding where alerts reach a team that acts and documents, not a stand-alone remedy for treatment-related morbidity.

title: Temporary Nurse Staffing in the Context of Nursing Shortages: A Narrative Review of Workforce Flexibility, Organizational Trade-Offs, and Patient Safety.
abstract: Nursing shortages require hospitals to balance staffing adequacy with flexibility in responding to vacancies, fluctuating demand, and unexpected service pressures. This focused narrative review examines temporary nurse staffing in acute hospitals, with primary emphasis on agency, travel, and contract registered nurses, and integrates evidence on workforce demand, operational flexibility, economic and workforce consequences, clinical integration, and patient safety. Evidence was identified through targeted PubMed and Scopus searches, citation tracking, and supplementary literature discovery. Temporary staffing can provide adaptive capacity by redistributing available nursing labor and reducing exposure to unfilled staffing requirements, but it does not eliminate underlying workforce scarcity. The evidence does not support treating temporary nurses as intrinsically less competent or inherently unsafe. Outcomes instead vary with the intensity and persistence of temporary staff use, baseline staffing adequacy, work environment, familiarity with local systems, orientation, and organizational integration. Limited supplementation may be operationally and economically useful in some contexts, whereas recurrent high reliance may increase coordination demands, workforce strain, and costs and may be associated with selected adverse outcomes. Temporary staffing is therefore best evaluated as one component of the overall staffing configuration and against realistic alternatives, including permanent staffing, overtime, flexible internal staffing, reduced capacity, or unresolved understaffing.

title: Temporary Nurse Staffing in the Context of Nursing Shortages: A Narrative Review of Workforce Flexibility, Organizational Trade-Offs, and Patient Safety
Fair and Efficient Nurse Scheduling With Answer Set Programming in Hospital Practice: From Rules to Rosters.
A Blueprint for Effective Succession Planning Using a Structure-Process-Outcome Framework.
Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Efficiency of Nurse-Led Interventions: Insights From a Critical Systematic Review.
abstract: Healthcare systems worldwide face mounting pressure to deliver high-quality care while enhancing efficiency and sustainability. Nurse-led interventions have emerged as promising strategies to optimize care delivery, particularly within value-based health systems. However, a comprehensive understanding of their clinical impact and economic value remains limited. This systematic review conducted following PRISMA guidelines, searched nine international databases to identify and synthesize formally evaluated nurse-led interventions, programs, and strategies. Twenty-eight studies were included, encompassing diverse care settings and patient populations. Most studies reported improvements in clinical outcomes, including reduced hospital readmissions, enhanced quality of life, and improved chronic disease management. Several interventions analyzed effectiveness, particularly those involving advanced nursing roles such as nurse practitioners and case managers. Findings suggest that clinical effectiveness does not necessarily translate into increased professional authority: nurse-led interventions consistently generate value across patient, organizational, and systemic dimensions, yet nursing leadership remains structurally subordinate within healthcare governance. A systematic agenda for rigorous economic evaluation embedded in nursing research programs is urgently needed, alongside structural reforms that redistribute authority-not merely develop competencies-within healthcare organizations.

title: Policies to address Israel's physician workforce challenges.
journal: Israel journal of health policy research
abstract: Background Israeli policymakers have four key concerns about Israel's future physician workforce: an insufficient number of physicians, an uneven quality of training, a geographic maldistribution, and a sub-optimal specialty mix. Recently, Israeli policymakers have launched a multi-year, multifaceted effort to address those workforce challenges. This comprehensive review of the policy responses seeks to fill a gap in the English-language literature, making it possible for scholars worldwide to contribute to the development of effective Israeli workforce policies and their evaluation. Methods This integrative article was written by a group of senior and mid-level professionals based at the Ministry of Health, all of whom are significantly involved in healthcare workforce issues. In writing the article, the authors drew on a wide range of official government reports, internal government memos, journal articles, OECD reports, Israeli and OECD databases, and Israeli committee reports. Findings The policy responses fall into the following six clusters: 1. Implementing strategic workforce planning and data-informed workforce regulation. 2. Increasing the number of students trained annually in Israeli medical schools. 3. Increasing the supply of well-trained physicians from non-Israeli medical schools. 4. Streamlining and modernizing post-graduate medical education. 5. Increasing the number of young people from the geographic periphery who successfully pursue medical careers. 6. Expanding training and employment opportunities for advanced practice professionals. The multi pronged workforce modernization agenda that Israel is now implementing-at remarkable speed and with substantial budgetary resources-is similar to that which many OECD countries have been building gradually over the past decade. It has also been adapted to Israel's unique demographic pressures, reliance on foreign trained physicians, and longstanding geographic disparities. Conclusions Successfully addressing Israel's many workforce challenges will require a stepping up of the analysis, creativity, resourcefulness, cooperation and budgetary expansion that have characterized recent efforts to meet Israel's medical workforce needs. To maximize the impact of Israel's multi-faceted workforce reform, it will also be important to solicit ongoing input from national and international workforce experts.

title: Turkish Adaptation, Psychometric Validity and Measurement Invariance of the Reasons for Implicit Rationing of the Nursing Care Scale.
abstract: Aim This study aimed to adapt the Reasons for Implicit Rationing of Nursing Care Scale into Turkish and evaluate its validity, reliability and measurement invariance among nurses in Türkiye. Background Implicit rationing of nursing care may compromise care quality and patient safety and is influenced by organizational, resource-related and communication factors. A culturally valid instrument is needed to identify the factors contributing to implicit rationing of nursing care within the Turkish healthcare context. Design A methodological, cross-sectional psychometric validation study. Method Data were collected between July and December 2025 from nurses working in a public hospital in Türkiye. The source population comprised 900 nurses and 411 nurses were included in the final sample using convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form and the Reasons for Implicit Rationing of Nursing Care Scale. Construct validity was examined using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses on randomly divided samples. Convergent and discriminant validity and gender-based measurement invariance were assessed. Reliability was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha, McDonald's omega and the intraclass correlation coefficient. Results The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin value was 0.936, indicating that the data were suitable for factor analysis. Exploratory factor analysis revealed a two-factor structure consistent with the original scale, explaining 74.30% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated acceptable model fit. Convergent validity was supported, whereas the heterotrait-monotrait ratio value indicated borderline discriminant validity. Measurement invariance across genders was largely supported at the configural, metric and scalar levels. The scale demonstrated high internal consistency and temporal stability, with a Cronbach's alpha value of 0.941, a McDonald's omega value of 0.932 and an intraclass correlation coefficient value of 0.873. Conclusion The Turkish version of the Reasons for Implicit Rationing of Nursing Care Scale is a valid, reliable and gender-invariant instrument. It can be confidently used in Turkish clinical settings to assess factors contributing to implicit rationing of nursing care.

title: Optimization of the organization of a hemodialysis center.

Community Mental Health Workers' Experiences of Care-Coordinating Hospital Discharge of Patients With Diagnosis of Mental Health Condition Into Community Mental Health Integrated Services in the Northwest of England.
journal: International journal of mental health nursing
abstract: The significance of community mental health workers in coordinating hospital discharge of patients with diagnosed mental health conditions is globally recognised, yet research on their experiences is scarce. This study contributes to knowledge through a qualitative empirical intrinsic case study of community mental health workers' experiences. This study aimed to explore community mental health workers' experiences of care-coordinating patients diagnosed with mental health conditions discharged from the hospital into community mental health integrated services. Guided by constructivist inquiry, the qualitative study focused on co-constructing meaning to understand community mental health workers' experiences in care coordination. Two theoretical lenses informed the study: Ecological Systems Theory, to understand multi-level influences, and Normalisation Process Theory, to explore how care coordination practices are embedded in discharge processes. Fourteen community mental health workers aged 18 and above were recruited from one NHS Trust in Northwest England from October 2021 to June 2022. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using reflective thematic analysis, generating themes and subthemes. Analysis identified 13 subthemes grouped into four major themes: (1) Experiences of collaborative working; (2) Challenges and enablers to care coordination; (3) Experiences of organisational system and culture; and (4) Community Mental Health Workers' personal experiences of professional growth. Findings highlight poor communication, staff shortages, high caseloads, limited community mental health services, and challenges in care coordination. The study provides valuable insights for improving community mental health workers' clinical practice and informs future research and policy development in community mental health care.

title: Integration of oral health into primary health care in Somalia: opportunities, barriers, and system-level implications for universal health coverage.
abstract: Background Oral diseases are among the most common noncommunicable conditions globally, yet oral health remains poorly integrated into primary health care (PHC) and universal health coverage, especially in fragile, low-limited settings. As Somalia rebuilds its health system through the Health Sector Strategic Plan III 2022-2026, the Essential Package of Health Services 2020, the Investment Case for the Somali Health Sector 2022-2027, and community health reforms, this study examined the place of oral health within national health policies. It identified barriers to integration and explored feasible pathways for strengthening PHC-based oral health. Methods The study used a qualitative policy and health-systems analysis combining documentary review with 13 key-informant interviews. Participants represented national policymakers, health-system technical advisers, regulators, academics, professional associations, and providers at public hospital, and private dental settings. Data were analyzed thematically and mapped against the WHO health-system building blocks, PHC principles, and the WHO Global Strategy and Action Plan on Oral Health 2023-2030. Results Somalia's policy environment offers opportunities for oral health integration, but stakeholders highlighted a persistent gap between policy recognition and implementation within routine PHC. Seven interrelated themes were identified: (1) policy recognition without operationalization; (2) fragmented governance, weak regulation, and limited coordination; (3) reliance on out-of-pocket financing and private-sector; (4) workforce, education, and task-sharing constraints; (5) predominantly curative, urban, hospital-based service with weak linkage to maternal and child health (MCH) and PHC; (6) limited oral health data and evidence generation; and (7) opportunities for phased integration through PHC, MCH, school health, community health workers, and NCD platforms Policymakers emphasized the need for stronger policy implementation, financing, regulation, standards, and data systems, while service providers highlighted unaffordable care, delayed care-seeking, workforce and infrastructure shortages, and missed opportunities for prevention. Conclusion Oral health integration in Somalia is a broader health system challenge rather than solely a dental-service issue. The most feasible approach is a phased, system-based model that prioritizes strengthened governance, a defined minimum oral health within PHC, workforce task-sharing, screening, counselling, referral pathways, private-sector regulation, essential commodities, and oral health indicators in District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2), followed by the gradual expansion of curative and rehabilitative services.

title: Low Pay, High Risk: The Nursing Pay Gap in Italy as a Systemic Health Policy Vulnerability.
Anticipated Determinants and Strategies Supporting Same-Day HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis Implementation During Emergency Care Encounters in Kenya: A Qualitative Study.
journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
abstract: Background Same-day HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) implementation remains challenging, especially in high-volume settings such as emergency departments (EDs). To guide program design and implementation efforts, we qualitatively explored anticipated implementation determinants and accompanying strategies facilitating same-day PrEP implementation in an urban Kenyan ED. Methods In 2024-2025, we conducted a cross-sectional qualitative study involving key informant interviews (N = 20) with physicians, nurses, pharmacists, HIV counselors, and administrators at Kenyatta National Hospital in Nairobi, Kenya. Using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), we explored theorized determinants of ED-based PrEP implementation and subsequently mapped identified determinants to requisite implementation strategies, articulated in the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC) taxonomy, using a CFIR-ERIC matching approach. Results The most salient barriers to same-day, ED-based PrEP implementation emerged within the Inner Setting domain, including space limitations, staffing shortages, and suboptimal capacity and provider competency to deliver PrEP in emergency care settings. Some providers perceived HIV services and emergency care as incongruous, impeding integration of PrEP into ED-based clinical workflows. Anticipated patient stigma, perceived incompatibility of PrEP services with status-neutral care environments, and opaque clinical/practice guidelines also constrained ED-based PrEP implementation. Identified facilitators included existing leadership involvement in clinical decision making, existing interdepartmental collaborations, and provider enthusiasm to reach younger persons and key populations with PrEP in the ED. ERIC strategies mapping to all 5 CFIR domains included: conducting ongoing training , promoting network weaving , and tailoring strategies . Conclusions Findings indicate strategies such as longitudinal training, standardizing screening with integrated systems, and configuration of setting-specific guidelines/protocols may enhance same-day, ED-based PrEP programming.

title: Leadership-Driven Risk Management for Radiation Protection in Iodine-125 Seed Wards: A Quality Improvement Study.
abstract: Purpose Iodine-125 seed implantation requires coordinated radiation protection after patients return to inpatient wards. However, ward-based radiation safety depends on more than individual knowledge; it also requires risk identification, leadership accountability, standardized workflows, and continuous quality monitoring. This study evaluated a leadership-driven, risk-based radiation protection management intervention for iodine-125 seed wards. The intervention was developed and structured using failure mode and effects analysis and the Donabedian structure-process-outcome framework. Methods Baseline failure mode and effects analysis informed a leadership-driven intervention structured using the Donabedian framework. Total quality-management scores from 33 inspections before and 33 after implementation were analyzed using regression with separate within-period linear trends and heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent covariance estimates. Post-implementation patient and nurse satisfaction were also assessed. Results Baseline FMEA identified two critical risks related to nurses' protective practices and two high risks related to nurses' knowledge and patient education. The mean total quality-management score was 75.27 ± 3.42 before implementation and 90.42 ± 3.80 afterward, with a period-mean difference of 15.15 points (95% CI, 13.11-17.19; P Conclusion A leadership-driven radiation protection management intervention was associated with improved routine ward-level radiation protection quality management in iodine-125 seed wards. The findings provide a practical model for translating radiation protection requirements into coordinated ward management processes.

title: Examining the academic physician workforce in the United States: work patterns, demographic characteristics, and COVID-19 effects.
journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges

title: Nurses' perspectives on perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation for patients with lung cancer in the pre-implementation phase: a CFIR 2.0-guided study.
abstract: Background Despite strong evidence supporting perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery, little is known about factors that may influence implementation prior to program rollout, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Guided by the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0), this study aimed to identify anticipated barriers and facilitators to inform program refinement and future implementation strategies. Methods A descriptive qualitative design was used. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nurses from the thoracic surgery department of a tertiary hospital in China (September-November 2025). Guided by the four CFIR 2.0 domains (innovation, outer setting, inner setting, individuals), directed content analysis was performed based on nurses' perspectives. Results Sixteen nurses were interviewed, representing diverse roles: Ward/ICU frontline staff nurses, charge nurses, unit secretaries, administrative nurses and nurse managers. Relevant constructs included 22 of the 29 CFIR 2.0 constructs and 8 subconstructs. Facilitators spanned: innovation (source, evidence base, relative advantage, trialability); outer setting (financing, policy, external pressure); inner setting (relational connections, communication, culture, incentive systems); and individual factors (team needs, leadership/practitioner capability, motivation). Barriers comprised: innovation (adaptability, complexity, cost); outer setting (local condition, partnerships and connections); inner setting (structural characteristics, compatibility, access to knowledge and information); and individuals (recipient needs, capability). Notably, implementation concerns differed across nursing roles, reflecting role heterogeneity and underscoring the need for tailored implementation strategies. Conclusion Implementation of perioperative PR for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery is influenced by multilevel factors spanning innovation, outer setting, inner setting, and individuals determinants. Differences in concerns across nursing roles highlight the importance of role-tailored implementation strategies. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing implementation approaches and may facilitate the sustainable integration of evidence-based PR into routine practice, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

title: Allergology Specialty Development and Talent Cultivation in China (2022-2025).
journal: Advances in medical education and practice
abstract: Introduction To analyze the status of allergology specialty development across seven regions of China from 2022 to 2025, evaluating institutional scale, workforce, service capacity, and regional equity, and to compare with international levels. Methods Two national cross-sectional surveys were conducted in 2022 and 2025, covering 502 and 520 hospitals, respectively, across all 31 provinces (seven regions) of mainland China, using the same structured questionnaire. Of these, 87 hospitals (2022) and 139 hospitals (2025) with independent allergology departments were identified as the primary analytical sample. Descriptive statistics with 95% confidence intervals (Wilson method), the population-weighted Gini coefficient, and the coefficient of variation were used to assess development trends and regional disparities. Results Independent allergology departments increased from 87 to 139 (+59.8%), and allergists from 371 to 770 (+107.5%), while the growth rates of nurses (+62.3%) and technicians (+44.8%) were considerably lower than that of physicians. Resources were concentrated in East and North China, which together accounted for 46.8% of departments and 56.8% of physicians. The national tertiary hospital coverage rate was 3.4% (95% CI 2.9-4.0), ranging from 5.8% in Northeast China to 1.1% in Southwest China. The physician-to-nurse ratio was 1:0.68, and the physician-to-technician ratio was 1:0.31. Technical readiness reached 82.7% (93.9% in East vs. 50.0% in Southwest). Master's or doctoral programs were available in 27.3% of departments. Discussion China's allergology specialty has grown rapidly in department numbers and workforce size, yet marked regional disparities persist. The low tertiary hospital coverage (3.4%), the decline in the proportion of departments with master's or doctoral programs (33.3% to 27.3%), and an allergist density far below European levels (approximately 0.055 vs. 1.81 per 100,000 population) highlight the need for regionally tailored workforce planning, expanded tertiary hospital coverage in underserved regions, and strengthened local training capacity.

title: Extubation in anesthetic practice: A systematic integrative review of anesthesiologists' and nurse anesthetists' experiences.
abstract: Background Extubation is a crucial component of anesthesia practice, requiring clinical expertise and effective communication among anesthesia personnel to ensure patient safety. In situations of insufficient spontaneous respiration, the anesthesia personnel assume control of ventilation using appropriate airway management techniques and anesthetic equipment. Objectives To explore the experiences of nurse anesthetists and anesthesiologists regarding extubation. Methods A systematic literature review with an integrative approach was conducted in PubMed, MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, including both qualitative and quantitative studies. Literature searches were performed in electronic databases and via web-based sources. Thirteen articles published between 2006 and 2022 were included. Results Experience was identified as a key factor in optimizing extubation outcomes. Challenges such as poor communication, time constraints, and lack of mutual respect were detrimental to the performance of the anesthesia personnel during extubation. Furthermore, adequate planning and preparation were highlighted as essential components for improving the management of extubation. Conclusion Experience, effective communication, and structured planning are fundamental to safe extubation practices. Addressing interpersonal and organizational barriers may enhance both health care professionals' performance and patient safety.

title: From Plan to Practice: Embedding Safety Planning in Inpatient Mental Health Care.
journal: International journal of mental health nursing

title: Gender-transformative action as a strategy for health system strengthening: a framework for advancing equity, accountability, and resilience.
journal: International journal for equity in health
abstract: Gender inequity is embedded in the organisation, financing, leadership, and everyday practice of health systems. It shapes who receives care, who provides it, who advances into decision-making roles, whose labour is undervalued, and whose safety is treated as negotiable. While health systems are often presented as neutral institutions, they frequently reproduce the gendered hierarchies of the societies in which they operate. This viewpoint argues that gender-transformative action should be treated as a core strategy for health system strengthening rather than as a peripheral equity concern. It proposes a three-domain framework for understanding and addressing gender inequity in health systems: capacity, institutional structures, and contextual barriers. Capacity refers to the ability of health workers, managers, educators, and policymakers to recognise and respond to gender bias in policy and practice. Institutional structures refer to the formal and informal rules that shape leadership, pay, career progression, workplace safety, budgeting, and accountability. Contextual barriers refer to the wider social conditions that influence whether people can access services and whether workers can participate equitably in institutional life, including restrictive gender norms, unpaid care burdens, violence, insecurity, and economic dependence. Drawing on purposively selected evidence from diverse settings, the paper examines how inequity is reproduced across these domains and outlines four practical areas for action: gender-sensitive training and mentorship, equitable governance and workforce reform, community engagement and norm change, and strengthened digital gender data systems. It argues that isolated or symbolic interventions are unlikely to produce durable change unless they alter the distribution of power, resources, and institutional recognition. Gender-transformative action is therefore not an optional addition to health policy, but a practical requirement for building health systems that are more equitable, accountable, resilient, and capable of advancing universal health coverage and the Sustainable Development Goals. As a viewpoint, the framework is offered as an analytic and planning aid rather than as an empirically validated model. Evidence on how gender-transformative reforms interact across domains remains limited, and the claims made here about what such reform can achieve should be read as arguments for a direction of travel rather than as established effect estimates.

title: How is practitioner-led quality and safety improvement sustained across a whole hospital? A process evaluation of a practice development programme.
abstract: Background Building frontline workforce capability to sustain quality and safety improvement across whole hospitals is a strategic priority for healthcare leadership. The principles are well established; how to enact and sustain them at scale is not. Practice development, a participatory approach to workforce transformation, has not been evaluated at hospital-wide scale. Objectives To develop and refine programme theories explaining how and why a hospital-wide practice development programme for quality and safety produces its effects in different settings, and to identify the conditions under which practice development mechanisms work, and fail to work, at hospital-wide scale. Methods This study was a qualitative process evaluation at a major Australian tertiary referral hospital where nursing leaders implemented a Quality Safety Culture Framework across all 41 acute-care units over 6 years. Practice development theory provided the sensitising framework; the empirical material was used to challenge rather than confirm its assumptions. Fieldwork comprised 27 interviews with nursing, medical, allied health, and executive staff; 6 half-day workshops with 49 frontline staff; a multidisciplinary focus group; and approximately 20 h of observations. Four tentative programme theories were developed prior to analysis. Abductive analysis foregrounded theoretical surprise through sustained dialogue between fieldwork and existing theory; within-programme variation provided the analytical structure. Findings The same programme simultaneously produced sustained participatory quality and safety improvement in some settings and directive compliance in others. Five refined programme theories specify the conditions for enactment: how data are used for learning rather than accountability; whether communicative space is sustained as an organisational precondition; what facilitators actually do; whether leadership creates organisational enablement without prescribing what fills it; and how collaborative prioritisation prevents project proliferation from undermining engagement. Implementation drift from participatory towards directive processes was concentrated in the facilitation pipeline, driven by governance logics that systematically favour measurable quality improvement outputs over relational and cultural processes. Conclusions Organisational enablement is necessary but insufficient to sustain participatory practice. Even with genuine participatory design intent, governance infrastructure built to reward measurable outputs can systematically displace participatory processes. The five theories specify the conditions required to sustain participatory approaches at scale and offer practical guidance for hospital leadership teams.

title: Work Demands, Burnout, and Withdrawal Behaviors Among Healthcare Workers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to determine whether work demands-specifically work overload and mental workload-are associated with burnout and withdrawal behaviors among healthcare workers, and to estimate the magnitude of these associations. Method A systematic review with meta-analysis and exploratory structural meta-analytic modeling was conducted, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The search covered Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed/MEDLINE with no restrictions on publication year, yielding 34 studies. Of these, five studies providing six independent samples with comparable data were included in three bivariate random-effects meta-analyses using REML and Fisher's z-transformation, as well as a two-stage TSSEM to explore the statistical indirect association involving burnout. Results This review identified heterogeneity in the constructs and instruments used, as well as consistent associations between the variables of interest. The meta-analyses showed positive associations between work overload and burnout, work overload and turnover intention, and burnout and turnover intention. Work overload showed comparatively more homogeneous associations with both burnout and turnover intention, whereas the burnout-turnover intention association showed greater between-study heterogeneity. The exploratory TSSEM showed an indirect association between work overload and turnover intention through burnout, alongside an association between work overload and turnover intention conditional on burnout. Conclusions Work demands are associated with burnout and withdrawal behaviors. The findings suggest that work overload shows comparatively more consistent associations with burnout and turnover intention, whereas the burnout-turnover intention association appears more sensitive to contextual and measurement-related factors. Burnout may be a relevant correlate within the association between work overload and turnover intention, although longitudinal evidence is needed to establish temporal relationships.

title: Development and Validation of a Next-Generation Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing Model for Quantifying Uncertainty: An Empirical Study of Fuzzy-Logic Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing Using Surgical System Data.
abstract: Background/objectives Under fixed-fee reimbursement such as Japan's Diagnosis Procedure Combination/Per Diem Payment System (DPC/PDPS), hospitals bear the cost of operations that run longer than planned, yet conventional time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) reports a single cost per case. This study developed and validated a fuzzy-logic TDABC (FL-TDABC) model that expresses case-level time uncertainty as interpretable intervals. Methods Data from 4674 gastrointestinal surgeries at a Japanese acute-care hospital (fiscal years 2020-2024) were analyzed. Four pre-operative attributes (surgical index rank, technical grade, number of anesthesiologists, and urgency) define 96 possible rules; for each rule, triangular fuzzy numbers for surgical, anesthesia, and room occupancy times were built from the observed minimum, mode, and maximum and defuzzified by the centroid method. Estimates were validated against realized costs in a temporal hold-out (rules from FY2020-2022 applied to FY2023-2024) and 5-fold cross-validation, and 21 alternative specifications were tested. Results The FL-TDABC centroid exceeded realized cost by ¥36,080 per case (10.2%; Cohen's d = 0.558). The premium arose entirely from the maximum-time vertex, vanished under percentile bounds, and did not improve point accuracy out of sample. The intervals were informative: the observed range of each rule covered the recorded room occupancy time of 97.5% of hold-out cases and the α = 0.5 cut 76%, interval width increased with surgical complexity, and planning room time at the α = 0.5 upper bound reduced overruns from 44% to 10% of cases. Conclusions The value of FL-TDABC lies in interval information that can inform scheduling buffers, staffing, and risk assessment, not in a higher or more accurate point estimate.

title: Out-of-hours general practice consultations and emergency department referrals from 2013-2022 in the Republic of Ireland: a retrospective observational study.
Florence Nightingale's Contemporary Legacy for Patient Safety: Implications for Nursing and Public Health.
abstract: This paper critically examines Florence Nightingale's legacy and its ongoing relevance to contemporary patient safety. Drawing on Notes on Nursing, the study highlights Nightingale's emphasis on hygiene, cleanliness, environmental factors, and systematic care as foundational to reducing harm and improving patient outcomes. Her insights laid the groundwork for infection prevention and control practices that remain central to modern nursing and healthcare safety protocols. Nightingale's principles align closely with current patient safety frameworks and global initiatives, such as the World Health Organization's Global Action Plan, emphasizing the social responsibility of healthcare professionals. Despite scientific advances and evolving healthcare systems, her legacy continues to influence nursing practices by reinforcing systematized, ethical, and patient-centered care. This enduring relevance underscores the critical role of nursing in safeguarding health and promoting safety in diverse clinical settings. This study advocates for ongoing recognition and integration of Nightingale's principles to enhance patient safety and care quality in modern healthcare. Her legacy remains an epistemological and practical resource for advancing nursing theory, patient-centered care, and critical reflection in healthcare. Trial Registration: Not applicable.

title: The role of outreach workers in care coordination for teenagers and young adults with cancer: The BRIGHTLIGHT_2021 programme.

title: Improving the Documentation of Clinical Frailty and Resuscitation Status on a Psychiatric Older Adult Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
Artificial Intelligence Readiness in Nursing: A Scoping Review of Knowledge, Attitudes, Practice, and Emerging Evidence on Patient Safety Culture.
abstract: Background : Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into nursing practice, yet nurses often demonstrate low to moderate AI knowledge, mixed attitudes, and inconsistent practice behaviors.
