Although individual studies have examined these domains, no review has comprehensively examined AI-related knowledge, attitudes, and practice (KAP) together with the emerging evidence on patient safety culture among nurses. This gap is significant because safe AI adoption in nursing depends on both technical competence and a strong safety culture across diverse clinical settings. Objective : To systematically map international evidence on nurses', nursing students', and other included participants' AI-related KAP, and to examine how these factors may relate to patient safety culture. Because several eligible studies included multidisciplinary samples in which nurse-specific quantitative data were not reported separately (China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and three studies from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia [KSA]), only studies with extractable nurse-specific results were used to inform nurse-focused conclusions, and multidisciplinary findings were not attributed solely to nurses. Methods : This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework and adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2021-2026) identified studies examining AI-related perceptions among nurses and other healthcare participants when nurse-specific data were reported separately or extractable. Data extraction and narrative synthesis were conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute guidance. Results : Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final review. Studies from China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, the KSA, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates showed variable AI knowledge but predominantly positive attitudes. Ethical concerns-privacy, job displacement, and reduced empathy-were common. Younger age, higher education, and prior AI exposure were associated with more favorable perceptions. Nurses across regions emphasized the need for structured AI training. Only one study examined patient safety culture, and it reported that AI knowledge and attitudes significantly predicted patient safety culture, with attitude showing the stronger effect. However, because this evidence comes from a single cross-sectional study conducted in a multidisciplinary sample without nurse-specific results, it is insufficient to establish causal conclusions, and its findings cannot be generalized specifically to nurses. Conclusions : Nurses are generally receptive to AI but lack sufficient knowledge, training, and organizational support for safe implementation. Preliminary evidence suggests a positive association between AI-related knowledge, attitudes, and patient safety culture, but this relationship remains uncertain due to the extremely limited evidence base and the reliance on evidence that is not exclusively nurse-specific. Available studies indicate generally favorable attitudes toward AI alongside variable knowledge, limited formal training, and persistent ethical and organizational concerns, with only one eligible cross-sectional study linking these factors to patient safety culture. The conclusion regarding this association should not be attributed exclusively to nurses because the patient safety culture evidence was derived from a multidisciplinary sample. Future research should explore how AI competencies may interact with safety-related behaviors and organizational systems. Strengthening AI training, ethical guidance, and organizational support remains essential for safe adoption.

title: Resilience, Well-Being, and Professional Practice Capabilities in New Graduate Nurses: A Longitudinal Mediation Study.
Sustaining nursing practice in Greenland: insights from a positive deviance study on motivation, resilience, and holistic care in arctic healthcare.
abstract: Health disparities in the Arctic remain substantial, with Inuit populations experiencing shorter life expectancy and higher morbidity than global averages. Nurse shortage exacerbates these challenges, and Greenland continues to rely on nurses from other countries. Despite these constraints, health outcomes have improved over time, including increased life expectancy, enhanced diabetes care, and better child growth indicators. To sustain professional well-being and retention in the Greenlandic nursing workforce, this study explores how nurses deliver high-quality care under constrained conditions, and what motivates them to remain in healthcare using a positive deviance framework. Ethnographic fieldwork was conducted across five Greenland regions, involving participant observations and interviews with nurses and students across professional roles. Across backgrounds and seniority, nurses demonstrated a shared passion for their work, with patient encounters central to practice. Resilient communities, shaped through collaboration and humour, supported creative problem-solving and a strong sense of responsibility, extending from individual patients to healthcare and society. Nurses sustain their practice through patient-centred values, community resilience, improvisational competencies, and commitment to societal well-being. Using a positive deviance perspective, insights from effective nursing practices can inform nursing education and Arctic healthcare, improving patient care, job satisfaction, staff retention, and long-term cost efficiency.

title: Artificial Intelligence and AI-Adjacent Digital Technologies in Nursing Practice Within Gastroenterology: A Scoping Review of Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into clinical gastroenterology, with emerging applications in nursing contexts. However, the extent and nature of these applications in gastroenterology nursing remain under-explored. This scoping review aimed to map the current landscape of AI and closely related AI-adjacent digital technologies in gastroenterology nursing. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guideline, PubMed, Medline, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed, English-language studies published since 2000, and the findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Of 184 records identified, 11 studies were included, highlighting the potential of these technologies in clinical decision support, workflow optimization, patient education, and endoscopy assistance. Reported benefits include gains in workflow efficiency, technical accuracy, and reduced administrative workload; direct evidence of improved nursing-led patient outcomes was reported in only a minority of studies. Challenges encompass limited nurse-led research, insufficient external validation, implementation gaps, and ethical concerns. Conclusions: Greater nurse involvement in AI development is essential to drive paradigm shifts in clinical practice. This review synthesizes evidence to inform future applications, research, and policy in AI-enhanced gastroenterology nursing.

title: Fight, flight, freeze, fawn: mapping emergency department staff stress responses to workplace violence - a mixed-methods study.
abstract: Background Workplace violence and aggression are escalating in emergency departments (EDs) globally, yet the self-reported psychological and behavioural responses in clinicians to such stressors remain underexplored. Trauma theory conceptualises stress responses as fight, flight, freeze, and fawn (4Fs); but how these responses manifest in ED staff before, during and after violent incidents has received limited empirical attention. Methods This mixed-methods study analysed data collected between 2019 and 2023 across four emergency departments within one Australian local health district. Data sources included semi-structured interviews (2019; n = 20), focus groups (2021; n = 30 participants), a cross-sectional survey (2023; n = 61), and follow-up interviews (2023; n = 12). Qualitative data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, applying a deductive framework informed by the 4Fs. Quantitative survey data were integrated to examine the distribution of stress responses across reported incidents. Results Across all data sources, 123 ED staff described 145 coded instances of the 4F stress responses: fight (n=94); flight (n=24), freeze (n=15), and fawn (n=12). Four overarching themes that underpinned these responses were identified: 1) Moral and emotional impact on clinicians, 2) Safety systems interface, 3) Organisational constraints and environment and 4) Patient Complexity. Participants described sustained hyperarousal, anticipatory vigilance, moral distress, emotional withdrawal, and appeasement behaviours arising from repeated exposure to violence. While Code Black responses were viewed as a structured and effective "organised fight" mechanism, this was compromised by inconsistent training, role ambiguity, and limited post-incident support which contributed to burnout, disengagement, and workforce attrition. Conclusion Emergency department clinicians operate in persistently threatening environments that drive recurrent activation of fight, flight, freeze, and fawn responses with cumulative individual and system-level consequences. Behavioural emergencies warrant the same level of preparation, standardisation, and organisational support as other high-risk clinical events, such as a Code Blue - a life-threatening medical event with a responding Medical Emergency Team. Trauma-informed education team-based training, and embedded post-incident support are critical to safeguarding staff wellbeing and sustaining the ED workforce.

title: Construction of an evaluation index system for nurse-led discharge planning competence in patients with chronic heart failure based on the iceberg model.
abstract: Objective To construct an iceberg model-based competency evaluation index system for nurse-led discharge planning in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), providing a scientific foundation for the cultivation and management of nurses' discharge planning competencies. Methods A preliminary item pool was established through a literature review. The Delphi method was employed to conduct three rounds of expert consultation with 17 experts. Following the three Delphi rounds, the same 17 experts were invited to complete pairwise comparison questionnaires based on the Saaty 1-9 scale, independently evaluating the relative importance of indicators at each hierarchical level. The research team aggregated all pairwise comparison matrices and computed indicator weights using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Results The effective response rates for all three rounds were 100%. The rates of experts proposing modifications were 64.70%, 29.41%, and 11.76%, respectively. The authority coefficient (Cr) was 0.93. Kendall's W coefficients for the first-, second-, and third-level indicators across the three rounds were 0.430, 0.308, and 0.158; 0.431, 0.321, and 0.292; and 0.365, 0.204, and 0.203, respectively. Moderate coordination was observed for first- and second-level indicators, while third-level indicators showed relatively weaker coordination; all differences were statistically significant (all P Conclusion The competency evaluation index system demonstrates strong scientific rigor, reliability, and practical utility. It provides a reference for the training, evaluation, and instructional design of nurse-led CHF discharge planning competencies, and offers an evidence-based foundation for healthcare institutions to develop relevant training programs and assessment criteria.

title: Implementation of a Preoperative Nursing Consultation in Elective Paediatric Surgery: An Implementation Science Perspective.
abstract: Aim To analyse the role of standardized protocols and nurse-led preoperative consultations in elective paediatric surgery and the factors influencing their implementation. Design Perspective article guided by the integrated Promoting Action on Research Implementation in Health Services framework. Data sources Structured search of Dialnet, PubMed, SciELO and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2018 and 2025, conducted between January and March 2025. Of 547 records identified, 40 sources were eligible and 17 inform this article. Conclusion Available studies suggest that non-pharmacological interventions, family involvement and nurse-led preoperative preparation may reduce anxiety and improve the surgical experience. However, implementation remains inconsistent because of workload, limited training and resources and insufficient institutional support. Nurses are well placed to facilitate the translation of evidence into practice, while organizational culture and leadership determine sustainability. Implications for nursing practice Nurses can operationalize preoperative consultations through structured, developmentally appropriate assessment of child and parental anxiety and of pain; child- and family-centered education; non-pharmacological preparation; escalation of high anxiety or pain through agreed referral pathways; and local adaptation of evidence-based protocols with the multidisciplinary team. Impact This article addresses the gap between evidence and practice in paediatric preoperative care. It identifies barriers and facilitators related to the innovation, its recipients, the context and facilitation, and proposes nurse-led implementation strategies that require evaluation. It is relevant to perioperative nurses, managers and policymakers in paediatric surgical services. Reporting method No EQUATOR reporting guideline applies to perspective articles; the literature search is reported in the Methods. Patient or public contribution This perspective article is based on a structured literature search and on theoretical implementation frameworks. No primary data were collected, and no patients, caregivers, service users, or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or preparation of this manuscript.

title: Nurse-led rehabilitation after total hip or knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of functional recovery, self-efficacy, and quality of life.
abstract: Background Nurse-led rehabilitation is increasingly embedded in postdischarge care after total hip or knee arthroplasty, but its effect on patient-reported recovery has not been quantified through meta-analysis. Objective The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of nurse-led rehabilitation versus usual care on functional recovery, self-efficacy, and quality of life after total hip or knee arthroplasty. Methods PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched (2010-2026; English only) for randomized controlled trials comparing nurse-led rehabilitation with usual care. Standardized mean differences (Hedges g ) were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 and prediction intervals, robustness with leave-one-out and subgroup analyses, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Results Eleven trials (1,107 participants) were included. Nurse-led rehabilitation improved functional recovery (10 trials; g = 1.11, 95% confidence interval 0.42-1.81; I 2 = 94.5%), self-efficacy (five trials; g = 1.10, 0.00-2.20; I 2 = 93.8%), and quality of life (four trials; g = 0.77, 0.08-1.46; I 2 = 81.7%). The certainty of evidence (GRADE) was rated low for all three primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes were directionally favorable but imprecise. The functional recovery effect was robust to leave-one-out analysis, whereas self-efficacy was statistically fragile. Quality of life showed a homogeneous benefit after knee replacement ( g = 1.12, I 2 = 0%) but not hip (between-subgroup p = 0.032), and functional recovery differed by delivery model ( p = 0.012, largest for digital). Heterogeneity was substantial throughout, all prediction intervals crossed the null, and funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible small-study effects. Conclusions Nurse-led rehabilitation after hip or knee arthroplasty was associated with improved function, self-efficacy, and quality of life, consistently favoring nurse-led care in direction but with evidence of low certainty, substantial between-study heterogeneity, prediction intervals that crossed the null, and possible small-study effects. Therefore, the magnitude of benefit remains uncertain. Adequately powered, outcome-blinded trials are needed. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261425216, PROSPERO CRD420261425216.

title: Influences of Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Transmissible Infections Among Operating Room Team Members: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Aim To synthesise evidence on the influences of infection prevention and control practices for transmissible infections among operating room team members. Design Systematic review. Data sources PubMed, CINAHL, APA PsycInfo, Web of Science and Scopus, supplemented by manual searches using Google Scholar and citation tracking. Review methods Databases were searched between March and April 2025, with an updated search undertaken in August 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data were synthesised using a convergent integrated approach. Results Thirteen studies across quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods methodologies were included. Factors influencing infection prevention and control practices for transmissible infections among operating room team members included resource accessibility, organisational infrastructure and leadership support, alongside variation in knowledge and training. Precaution use differed across professional groups, whereas communication and teamwork were identified as important to coordinating infection prevention efforts. The practical demands of personal protective equipment also created challenges for communication and the delivery of surgical care. The four overarching themes were organisational support and resources; professional and team dynamics; knowledge and training; and the practical challenges in implementing precautions. Conclusion Given the heterogeneity and predominantly observational nature of the evidence, the findings provide conceptual insight into factors influencing practice, although certainty regarding the effectiveness of specific strategies remains limited. Supporting infection prevention practices for transmissible infections in the operating room therefore requires attention to influences beyond individual knowledge, to include the wider team and organisational conditions in which precautions are implemented. Implications for nursing practice Throughout a patient's operating room journey, perioperative nurses play a central role in coordinating patient care and infection prevention activities. They communicate infection risks, prepare the clinical environment, implement precautions, and coordinate care across professional groups. Support from nurse managers and clinical nurse educators through appropriate resources, continuing education, and interprofessional learning is important to sustain this role and promote consistent infection prevention practice for patient and staff safety. Impact This review highlights the factors influencing infection prevention and control practices for transmissible infections among operating room team members. As transmissible infections continue to persist in healthcare settings, these findings may assist perioperative nurses and multidisciplinary teams to identify barriers and facilitators and inform locally relevant strategies that support consistent infection prevention practice and safer surgical care. Reporting method This systematic review was reported in accordance with the relevant EQUATOR guideline, the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. No patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution was required as this systematic review synthesised data from previously published studies. Prospero registration CRD420251168178.

title: Global Landscape of Telehealth Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Self-Care: A Scoping Review of Nursing Roles, Care Models, and Outcomes.
abstract: Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) requires ongoing self-care support to minimize preventable complications. Telehealth interventions have the potential to extend diabetes self-management education and support beyond conventional face-to-face care. However, the specific contributions of nursing roles, conceptual frameworks, and digital care architectures have not been comprehensively synthesized. Objective This scoping review aimed to map global evidence on telehealth interventions for T2DM self-care. Methods The review was conducted in accordance with Arksey and O'Malley's framework, JBI scoping review guidance, and the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Electronic databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Taylor AND Francis Online, ScienceDirect, and Sage Journals, were systematically searched for empirical studies published between January 1, 2021, to June 26, 2026, examining telehealth, mHealth, telenursing, or digital self-care interventions for adults with T2DM involving nursing or nursing-relevant digital care component. Data were charted using the systematic table and synthesized through descriptive and thematic analysis. Results A total of 26 studies were included, representing diverse models such as app-based self-management, messaging platforms, telemonitoring, virtual education, EHR-supported discharge pathways, virtual group visits, and comprehensive telehealth. Nursing roles were categorized as digital education, clinical monitoring, care coordination, behavioral coaching, medication and follow-through support, peer-support moderation, and digital onboarding. Of the 26 included studies, nine (34.6%) were classified as nurse-led, five (19.2%) as nurse-supported, seven (26.9%) as multidisciplinary/team-based, and five (19.2%) had insufficient reporting to isolate a nurse-specific intervention role. Interventions featuring structured nurse involvement, individualized feedback, theory-informed behavior-change strategies, and escalation pathways demonstrated the most consistent improvements in self-care behaviors and selected glycemic outcomes, particularly HbA1c and fasting blood glucose. Conclusion Telehealth interventions for T2DM self-care should be regarded as hybrid care models rather than solely technology-based tools. The synthesized evidence supports nurse-mediated, theory-informed, and equity-sensitive digital diabetes care, while underscoring the need for improved reporting on nursing scope, digital engagement, clinical escalation, fidelity, cost, and implementation context.

title: Intensivists' Perspectives and Practices on Palliative Care in the ICU: A Nationwide Survey in Korea.
abstract: Background While many countries have made progress in integrating palliative care into intensive care units (ICUs), implementation remains highly context-dependent. In Korea, palliative care integration within ICUs remains limited, and intensivists' perspectives on its role and applicability have not been well studied. Methods We conducted a nationwide, cross-sectional online survey of certified intensivists and fellows registered with the Korean Society of Critical Care Medicine between April and May 2024. The questionnaire explored knowledge and confidence in palliative care, current ICU practices, referral patterns, perceived barriers, and preferred strategies for integration. Results A total of 241 intensivists responded (response rate, 23.9%). Most agreed that palliative care should be incorporated into ICU care (97.1%) and were willing to make referrals (98.3%). Advance care planning, symptom management, and family decision-making were the most expected domains of support. However, fewer reported involvement in psychological support, end-of-life care, or bereavement services. Referral practices were more frequent in institutions with palliative care teams, while lack of resources, unsupportive institutional culture, and unclear processes were commonly cited barriers. Clinical guidelines, professional education, and reimbursement reform were identified as priority strategies for integration. Conclusion Korean intensivists widely recognize the need for palliative care in the ICU but apply it within a limited scope. To strengthen integration, consensus on definitions, clear referral criteria, and supportive institutional and policy frameworks are required.

title: Discharge Planning in Children With Cancer: Components, Strategies, and Outcomes-A Scoping Review (2021-2025).
Strengthening data-driven primary health care delivery in Rajasthan, India.
abstract: Digital health information systems have the potential to improve data-driven decision-making and strengthen primary health care delivery in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study examines Rajasthan's public health information systems with an aim to describe data processes and identify key barriers and opportunities for improvement. Using a qualitative approach, we conducted in-depth interviews with 39 stakeholders, including frontline health workers and state health officials. Our findings highlight inefficiencies in parallel paper and digital reporting systems, leading to high health worker burden, redundant data entry, delays in patient care, and poor data accountability. While digital platforms have improved data accessibility and care coordination, challenges such as poor design, interoperability, IT infrastructure limitations, and gaps in digital literacy remain. Lessons from successful digital health implementations in other LMICs suggest that integrated, human-centered, and interoperable systems are critical for sustainable digital transformation. We propose a "5I Framework" for policymakers to streamline Rajasthan's digital health ecosystem: (i) Integrated platforms, (ii) Implementable systems co-designed with health workers, (iii) Ink-free transitions away from paper-based systems, (iv) Insights from geospatial and real-time data, and (v) Incentives aligned with workforce needs. Strengthening Rajasthan's digital health systems through these strategies can enhance service delivery, improve public health outcomes, and serve as a model for other LMICs.

title: 'Let's work alongside it': healthcare professionals' perspectives of generative AI in supporting care at home in paediatric rheumatology.
abstract: Objectives Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly explored in healthcare, yet its potential to support care at home remains largely unexamined. In paediatric rheumatology, where families frequently undertake complex tasks to manage treatment plans between appointments, safe and effective guidance is essential. The aim of the current study was to understand healthcare professionals' (HCPs') views on adopting GenAI tools to help families manage their child's care. Methods Utilising a vignette-based methodology, paediatric rheumatology HCPs were invited to focus groups and presented with 3 hypothetical scenarios: (1) injection administration, (2) flare assessment, and (3) physiotherapy exercises. Following the principles outlined by Braun and Clarke, data were analysed using thematic analysis. Results A total of 37 HCPs from the wider multidisciplinary team from 14 different hospitals participated in this study. Six main themes were identified: (1) opportunities of GenAI to benefit patient care; (2) disadvantages and challenges; (3) risks, safety netting, and evaluation; (4) different approaches of utilising GenAI; (5) role of HCPs in the world of GenAI; and (6) ensuring inclusivity and accessibility. Conclusions HCPs recognised opportunities for how GenAI could support caregivers in managing their child's healthcare or young people's self-management, particularly through guidance support rather than clinical interpretation. However, concerns were raised regarding the accuracy, reliability, privacy, and data governance of currently existing GenAI tools. The perspectives of HCPs are critical to ensuring that the application of GenAI in healthcare aligns with clinical expectations, ethical standards, regulatory processes, and the needs of patients and families.

title: Operationalizing clinical artificial intelligence through secure FHIR pipelines: a zero-trust cloud reference architecture for EHR interoperability
Establishing Welfare Evacuation Shelters for Children With Medical Complexity: A Prefecture-Wide Policy Shift Driven by Simulation in Tottori, Japan.
journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
abstract: Objective Children with medical complexity (CMC) are highly vulnerable during disasters, yet few Japanese welfare evacuation shelters accept them, leading to hospital-dependent planning. We aimed to assess the key issues hindering the establishment of welfare evacuation shelters for CMC. Methods In Tottori Prefecture (2020-2024), the government, municipalities, a university hospital, and device partners used facility assessments, staff education, and tabletop/field simulations (weekday earthquake with power outage and ventilator-dependent 5-year-old model) to identify gaps and iteratively revise manuals. Results Key issues included space underestimation, difficult mobility, power insecurity, unreliable verbal information, unclear deterioration pathways, and undefined public health nurse (PHN) roles. Revisions established PHN-led reception/triage, standardized information collection, specified power sourcing, and set escalation/transport flows. A section on "Persons Requiring Medical Care" was added to prefectural policies, and the disaster medical guidance was updated, shifting preparedness from hospital-centered to shelter-based welfare. Conclusion This simulation-driven intersectoral model appears scalable; however, it was performed in a single prefecture with limited follow-up, impairing generalizability.

title: Reducing Serious Hospital-acquired Pressure Injuries in Pediatric Intensive Care Units through Proactive Interdisciplinary Rounding.
abstract: Introduction Hospital-acquired pressure injuries (HAPIs) contribute to significant morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs). Critically ill children are at increased risk due to immobility, complex comorbidities, and frequent use of medical devices. Despite stable rates of adherence to prevention bundles, an increase in serious HAPIs (sHAPIs)-defined as stage 3, stage 4, or unstageable injuries-was observed at our institution. This quality improvement initiative aimed to reduce the rate of sHAPIs by 10% through the implementation of proactive interdisciplinary rounding. Methods Weekly interdisciplinary pressure injury rounds were implemented across the cardiac intensive care unit, neonatal intensive care unit, and PICU at a freestanding 364-bed children's hospital. Rounding teams included physicians, nurses, certified wound ostomy nurses, clinical quality coordinator nurses, and rehabilitation therapists. High-risk patients were identified using the Braden QD Scale and unit-specific criteria. During rounds, teams discussed prevention strategies and implemented targeted interventions, including device optimization, mobility promotion, nutrition assessment, skin protection measures, and bedside education. Outcome, process, and balancing metrics were tracked. Results Within 1 year of implementation, the ICU sHAPI rate was reduced by 39% from 0.564 to 0.343 per 1,000 patient-days. The time between events increased in the PICU and cardiac intensive care unit. More than 1,400 proactive interventions were implemented. Rates of non-sHAPI hospital-acquired conditions decreased from 4.8 to 2.8 events per month. Conclusions Proactive interdisciplinary rounding was feasible, reproducible across ICUs, and associated with fewer sHAPIs.

title: Caregiver Perspectives on Implementation of Discharge Plans for Children With Medical Complexity.
Stakeholder Perspectives on Barriers and Facilitators to Implementing Nurse-Led Diabetic Plantar Pressure Assessment and Management: A Multicentre Group Concept Mapping Study.
Occupational injury patterns in a hospital-based cross-sectional study in Türkiye: sectoral characteristics, injury profiles, and determinants of multiple injuries (2019-2023).
journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
abstract: Background Occupational accidents remain a major public health and economic burden, particularly in middle-income countries. While healthcare workers and high-energy industrial sectors are often examined separately, hospital-based injury data derived from forensic medical records provide a structured opportunity to compare sector-specific injury patterns within a unified analytical framework. Methods This retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study included all occupational injury cases presenting to a tertiary emergency department and systematically documented through forensic medical records between 2019 and 2023 (n = 402). Sociodemographic characteristics, sector, accident mechanism, injury location, and injury count were analysed. Associations were assessed using chi square tests and Cramérs V. Independent predictors of multiple injuries were examined using binary logistic regression, and sector- and mechanism-specific within-sample relative risks were calculated. Results The study population was predominantly male (66.9%) and young (45.5% aged 18-29 years). Construction, healthcare, and logistics were the most represented sectors. Physical trauma accounted for 95.3% of cases, while infectious exposure risk was identified in 21.4%, mainly from needlestick injuries and body-fluid splashes in healthcare. Multiple injuries occurred in 35.8% of cases and were disproportionately concentrated in high-energy sectors, including electrical-mechanical work (OR = 44.43; 95% CI = 3.72-531.12), manufacturing (OR = 12.82; 95% CI = 2.91-56.50), construction (OR = 4.64; 95% CI = 1.58-13.62), and logistics. Traffic incidents and falls were the strongest contributors to multi-region trauma. Upper-extremity injuries, particularly hand and finger trauma, predominated in healthcare workers, mainly nurses and healthcare technicians, and were more frequent among females. Conclusions Among workers presenting to a single tertiary hospital, injury patterns differed by sector, with infectious exposure predominating in healthcare and high-energy mechanisms in industrial sectors. These within-sample patterns identify potential targets for sector-specific prevention; however, without workforce denominators, they do not establish which sectors or age groups carry the highest injury risk, and broader prioritization requires population-level evidence.

title: Specific interventions as part of a quality improvement collaborative enhance care for ischemic stroke patients.
abstract: Introduction Adherence to guidelines for stroke care varies, despite evidence that managing fever, glycemia (sugar), and conducting swallowing screening (FeSS) reduces mortality and disability. We established a quality improvement collaborative to improve care processes for ischemic stroke, with a focus on these three recommendations. We then added two additional care process activities: screening for activities of daily living (ADL) and depression, collectively defined as FeSS + . Methods In this multicenter intervention study ( n = 24), we retrospectively analyzed 30 consecutive patient records per center of ischemic stroke patients in 2019, pre-intervention (measurement period 1 [MP1]), and in 2022, post-intervention (measurement period 2 [MP2]). All hospitals received feedback on their MP1 performance, and an optional e-learning tool on FeSS + was also offered. We compared adherence between MP1 and MP2 and assessed the impact of the e-learning tool. Results Data were collected from 580 patients during MP1 and 588 patients during MP2. E-learning tools were delivered to teams at 18 hospitals (75%). Adherence improved for temperature measurement (18 to 25%, p = 0.004) and swallowing screening (36 to 59%, p p = 0.01, p = 0.03). Discussion We observed improvements in measuring temperature and swallowing screening after receiving feedback. The dissemination of the e-learning tool was associated with increased adherence to glycemic measurement, swallowing screening, and depression screening, underscoring the role of specific interventions. However, overall adherence remained low, highlighting the need for continued quality improvement.

title: Factors affecting women's disclosure of domestic abuse and healthcare professionals' preparedness to identify and respond: a systematic literature review.
abstract: Purpose Domestic abuse (DA) is a significant public health and human rights issue with profound physical, psychological, and social consequences. Healthcare settings provide important opportunities for identification and support; however, disclosure by women remains inconsistent, and healthcare professionals' readiness to identify and respond varies widely. This qualitative systematic review synthesised evidence examining factors influencing women's disclosure of DA within healthcare contexts and healthcare professionals' preparedness to respond. Methods A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between 2000 and 2023. Additional studies were identified through reference searching. The review followed PRISMA guidance and was informed by the SPIDER framework. Qualitative and mixed-methods studies with extractable qualitative findings were included. Methodological quality was appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme checklist. Findings were synthesised narratively and interpreted using a socio-ecological model to capture multilevel influences on disclosure and response. Results Disclosure emerged as a relational and socially mediated process shaped by trust, perceived safety, validation, confidentiality, and continuity of care. Forms of "borrowed trust," mediated through social networks, influenced women's willingness to engage. Healthcare professionals' preparedness was determined by competence, confidence, emotional readiness, clarity of safeguarding responsibilities, and access to referral pathways. Structural factors, including limited consultation time, workload pressures, and organisational ambiguity, constrained effective response. Importantly, disclosure alone did not ensure improved outcomes where system readiness was inadequate. Conclusion Improving responses to DA requires multilevel strategies extending beyond individual training. Sustainable progress depends on organisational leadership, protected time, clear referral systems, and alignment across relational and structural domains to support safe disclosure and meaningful intervention.

title: Development of a phased discharge planning for patients undergoing airway stenting: a Delphi study informed by the timing it right framework
Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as an important energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering tissue selectivity and procedural efficiency while introducing specific anaesthetic and sedation requirements. This narrative review examines the rationale for anaesthesia and sedation during PFA, the mechanisms underlying pain, involuntary movement, and neuromuscular stimulation, and the implications of catheter design, waveform characteristics, and patient-related factors for peri-procedural management. Available evidence indicates that both deep sedation and general anaesthesia can provide safe and effective procedural conditions when supported by appropriate monitoring, airway rescue capability, and experienced multidisciplinary teams. Deep sedation may offer advantages in workflow, recovery, and patient-centred care, particularly for standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures using contemporary biphasic systems with reduced muscle activation, whereas general anaesthesia remains appropriate for complex procedures, patients with substantial comorbidity, or settings in which complete immobility and airway control are essential. Current real-world practice is highly heterogeneous across regions and institutions, reflecting differences in regulations, staffing models, procedural complexity, and local expertise rather than a universally accepted standard. Overall, anaesthetic strategy in PFA should be individualised according to patient risk profile, expected procedural demands, and device-specific stimulation burden. Further prospective comparative studies are needed to define optimal sedation depth, standardise monitoring and outcome measures, and clarify how emerging technologies may enable lighter yet still effective sedation pathways.

title: Evaluating the Holistic Value of Family-Centred Care in Paediatric Intensive Care Units: A Mixed Methods Study.
abstract: Aim This study aimed to explore the perceived holistic value of family-centred care (FCC) in Ghanaian paediatric intensive care units (PICUs) from the perspectives of nurses, doctors, and families. Design This is a four-phase mixed-methods study that incorporates literature control, qualitative, instrument development, and quantitative survey. Methods The researchers purposely conducted 12 individual interviews with six PICUs nurses and doctors (three nurses and three doctors) and six families (three fathers and three mothers) with sick children in two PICUs. Thematic analysis was employed to manage the qualitative data. Qualitative findings were used to develop a questionnaire for an electronic survey (n = 100), and the data were analysed using exploratory factor analysis, Principal Component Analysis, and commonalities. Results The study demonstrates the perceived holistic value of FCC in promoting family-child bonding, reducing family anxiety, reducing workload, promoting recovery, providing timely information, and educating families on childcare processes in intensive care units. Most respondents (95%) agreed with the identified FCC value, indicating broad acceptance. The internal consistency of the holistic value of FCC, as measured by the Cronbach alpha coefficient (> 0.82), further validated the results. The primary contextual value identified by Principal Component Analysis was the FCCs role in promoting family education, with a significant Eigenvalue of 3.200 and accounting for 53.337% of the cumulative variance. Conclusion FCC practices empower families to continue providing appropriate childcare after discharge, which has been perceived as reducing anxiety, promoting bonding, and fostering good parenting for critically ill children. Participants perceived a high level of agreement that the FCC also shortens hospital stays and reduces workload. To improve the quality of paediatric care in resource-constrained settings, healthcare professionals and policymakers should prioritise implementing FCC practices. Implication for practice Our findings suggest that FCC integration into PICU could improve quality health outcomes, particularly for children and their families. As such, nurses and doctors may require additional in-service training on FCC integration into the PICU setting. It is proposed that heads of PICUs could modify the set-up to create space for easy FCC integration. Reporting method This study is reported using Mixed Methods Reporting in Rehabilitation and Health Sciences. Patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution. Clinical trial number The authors have nothing to report.

title: Relationship Between Nurses' Second Victim Experience and Professional Identity: The Mediating Role of Psychological Resilience.
abstract: Background/objectives The second victim phenomenon is increasingly recognized in patient safety, yet the pathways connecting second victim experience to nurses' professional outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationships among second victim experience, psychological resilience, and professional identity, and to examine the mediating role of psychological resilience. Methods This study used convenience sampling to recruit nurses who had experienced nursing adverse events at a tertiary Grade-A hospital. Participants were assessed using the Second Victim Experience and Support Tool, the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and a Professional Identity Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS 25.0, with Pearson/Spearman correlation and mediation analyses performed. Results A total of 368 nurses who experienced nursing adverse events were included in the study. Scores for second victim experience, professional identity, and psychological resilience were 55.03 ± 12.42, 113.82 ± 21.42, and 28.04 ± 7.33, respectively. The mean second victim experience distress and support dimension (reverse-scored) scores were 34.33 ± 10.21 and 20.70 ± 6.84, respectively; their correlation was small and non-significant (r = 0.023, p = 0.722). In the total-score model, the indirect effect of second victim experience on professional identity through psychological resilience was significant (indirect effect = -0.308, 95% CI [-0.400, -0.223]), whereas the direct effect was not (direct effect = -0.080, p = 0.158). In the support-dimension model, both the indirect effect (indirect effect = -0.211, 95% CI [-0.290, -0.143]) and the direct effect (direct effect = -0.341, p p = 0.012), resulting in a non-significant total effect (total effect = -0.099, 95% CI [-0.222, 0.023]). Conclusions The Second Victim Experience and Support Tool composite score reflects multiple facets of the second victim experience, encompassing both distress-related and support-related components. Perceived support deficit was consistently associated with lower professional identity, partly through psychological resilience, whereas distress showed a more complex indirect association through resilience. These findings suggest that psychological resilience may be a potential intervention target and that both distress- and support-related aspects of second victim experience warrant attention. However, because this was a cross-sectional mediation analysis, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than causal relationships.

title: Review research progress, critical reflections and future prospects of digital care for chronic diseases.
abstract: The global prevalence of chronic diseases is becoming increasingly severe, and traditional care models are confronted with multiple challenges, including uneven distribution of medical resources, insufficient continuity of care, and inadequate patient self-management capacity. The rapid iteration of digital technologies and the catalyst of the COVID-19 pandemic have driven chronic disease care into a new phase of digital transformation. Based on relevant studies published from 2021 to 2026, this paper structures its analysis around a core logical framework: evidence-based evidence, care models, population adaptability and practical implementation. It systematically reviews the core technical systems and innovative characteristics of care models in digital chronic disease care, deeply analyzes the adaptive differences across diverse populations and disease types, and conducts critical reflections from the perspectives of evidence quality, health equity, clinical applicability, and homogeneity in intervention design. Finally, it puts forward future development directions centered on precision, localization, equity, and integration. The study reveals that digital chronic disease care has formed four core technological systems in application: intelligent sensing, digital behavioral intervention, immersive technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) and big data. Care models demonstrate innovative trends of nurse leadership, multi-dimensional collaboration, and caregiver empowerment. Nevertheless, prominent issues persist, such as insufficient high-quality evidence, a striking digital divide, difficulties in clinical integration, and a lack of personalized design. In the future, deep integration of technological innovation with clinical demands, enhanced targeted interventions for vulnerable populations, implementation of localized long-term studies, and improvement of policy and ethical guarantee systems are required. These efforts will promote the shift of digital chronic disease care from technology-driven to evidence-driven and demand-driven models, ultimately improving the overall efficiency of chronic disease management and health equity.

title: Clinical and diagnostic factors associated with 72-h unscheduled return to high-priority pediatric emergency care: a health services retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Seventy-two-hour unscheduled return visits reflect short-term emergency care reutilization, discharge-transition safety, and disease progression in children. Evidence is limited for children managed through high-priority pediatric emergency care pathways, where triage acuity, observation needs, and disease-specific care processes differ from standard emergency department care. This study examined clinical and diagnostic factors associated with 72-h unscheduled return to such a pathway and assessed whether these associations differed between red-zone and yellow-zone encounters. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 30,170 pediatric visits from 24,479 children managed through an institutionally defined high-priority pediatric emergency care pathway at a tertiary women's and children's hospital in China in 2025. The primary outcome was unscheduled return to the same pathway within 72 h after the index visit. Visits were ordered chronologically within each child. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a patient-level random intercept was used to account for repeated visits. Zone and triage level were not included together because they were structurally linked in the institutional workflow. Results Overall, 1,507 index visits were followed by a 72-h return (5.0%). In the primary model, yellow-zone encounters had higher odds of return than red-zone encounters (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34-3.87). Oncologic conditions showed the strongest association with return (aOR, 6.48; 95% CI, 3.54-11.87), followed by hematologic diseases (aOR, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.06-5.89). The zone-by-diagnosis interaction model indicated that the oncologic risk signal was amplified in the yellow zone (interaction aOR, 5.10; 95% CI, 1.25-20.84; p = 0.023). The oncologic association remained stable across sensitivity analyses. Conclusion In this high-priority pediatric emergency care pathway, 72-h unscheduled return was more closely related to the underlying diagnostic category than to initial vital-sign abnormality. Yellow-zone children with oncologic conditions may require strengthened discharge assessment, explicit return precautions, and short-interval follow-up to improve care-transition safety and support risk-informed use of high-priority emergency resources.

title: Short courses on maternal mental health provided by healthcare providers in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review.
abstract: Introduction Maternal mental health (MMH) conditions are increasingly alarming yet remains under recognized and poorly integrated into healthcare services, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Nurses, midwives, and other frontline healthcare providers are well positioned to identify, support, and refer women with perinatal mental health conditions. However, the content and delivery of short MMH training courses for healthcare providers in LMICs are not well documented. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on short MMH training courses for healthcare providers in LMICs. Methods This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and was registered with the Open Science Framework. Reporting adhered to the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A comprehensive literature search was conducted from PubMed, CINAHL EBSCO Host, Web of Science, Scopus, African Journals online (AJOL) and Sabinet with EndNote and Rayyan used to manage records, screening, and study selection. Results Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Most training programmes targeted nurses, midwives, primary healthcare workers, or community health workers and were implemented after 2020. Course content focused primarily on two areas: (1) clinical knowledge and screening for perinatal mental disorders using validated tools such as the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7); and (2) counselling and psychosocial support, including psychoeducation, empathic communication, problem-solving, and family-centred care. Evaluation methods predominantly assessed knowledge, competence, and self-efficacy through pre- and post-training assessments. Nine studies reported significant improvements in participants' knowledge and skills, four demonstrated improved screening and referral practices, three reported positive clinical outcomes for women, and three showed successful integration of MMH training into routine health services. Conclusion Short MMH training courses in LMICs primarily strengthen healthcare providers' knowledge, screening, and counselling competencies. Although evidence suggests improvements in provider capacity and service delivery, more research is needed to evaluate long-term behavioural, clinical, and health system outcomes.

title: "Okay, you're moving to the adult world": perspectives on transitioning users of home mechanical ventilation to adult care.
journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
abstract: Rationale Children requiring long-term home mechanical ventilation (HMV) increasingly survive into adulthood. However, structured processes to support their transition from pediatric to adult care are lacking. Understanding the perspectives of patients, caregivers, and health and social care providers (HSCPs) is critical to improving transition experiences and outcomes. Objectives To explore the experiences, perceptions, and priorities of patients, caregivers, and providers involved in the transition of young people using HMV from pediatric to adult care, and to identify practical targets for improvement. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews and focus groups with the following participant groups: pediatric and adult HSCPs (n = 14) and patients aged 17 to 21 years with experience of HMV (n = 7) and their caregivers (n = 9). Iterative inductive thematic analysis was performed. Patient partners with lived experience contributed to study design, development of data collection tools, and analysis. Results Four key themes emerged: (1) The absence of a formal transition framework left patients and caregivers unclear about expectations, timelines, and responsibilities; (2) care continuity and coordination were often disrupted, with prolonged gaps between pediatric and adult care and confusion over roles of providers; (3) patients were insufficiently prepared for differences in adult care, including greater self-management expectations; and (4) providers reported systemic barriers, including lack of institutional support, insufficient resources, and overreliance on individual "transition champions" to drive processes. These challenges were consistently reported across participant groups. Conclusions Young people using HMV face significant challenges during and after their transition to adult care. Priorities for improvement include the need for structured transition protocols, early planning, education about adult care expectations, and formalized handovers between services. Sustainable improvements require operational support and integration of transition planning into routine care from early adolescence. Future research should evaluate the impact of formalized transition models on patient experiences and outcomes.

title: Advances in assessment systems and non-pharmacological intervention strategies for cancer-related fatigue following transarterial chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma: a narrative review.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Purpose Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a primary treatment for intermediate to advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a prevalent and distressing symptom following TACE that significantly impairs patients' recovery and health-related quality of life. This review aimed to systematically summarize the current evidence on CRF screening, assessment, and non-pharmacological interventions specifically tailored to the post-TACE HCC population, and to propose an integrated, nurse-led clinical management framework. Methods A narrative review was conducted by systematically searching PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI for literature published up to April 2026. The search encompassed peer-reviewed original research articles (including randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, cross-sectional studies, and meta-analyses), clinical practice guidelines, and expert consensus reports. The level of evidence for each intervention category was evaluated using the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (OCEBM) grading system. The literature search focused on CRF epidemiology, pathophysiology, validated assessment tools, non-pharmacological interventions (including exercise, psychosocial support, nutritional management, and traditional Chinese medicine therapies), and nursing management models in HCC patients following TACE. Results CRF following TACE is a multifactorial symptom driven by treatment-induced inflammation, hepatic dysfunction, and psychological distress. Validated screening tools, including the Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI), Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS), and EORTC QLQ-C30 fatigue subscale, are recommended for routine use, though to the best of our knowledge, no CRF assessment tool developed specifically for the post-TACE HCC population has been validated to date. A structured screening pathway encompassing baseline assessment, perioperative monitoring, and long-term follow-up was identified as essential for early detection. Among non-pharmacological interventions, individualized exercise prescriptions (aerobic and resistance training) have been most consistently supported across randomised trials and meta-analyses for alleviating CRF, followed by cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and nutritional support. Traditional Chinese medicine approaches, including acupoint massage, auricular acupressure, and moxibustion, showed preliminary potential but require further high-quality validation. A nurse-led multidisciplinary care model integrating assessment, individualized intervention planning, and continuous coordination has been proposed as a promising operational framework for CRF management, endorsed by international CRF practice frameworks. Conclusions Effective management of CRF after TACE requires a comprehensive, evidence-based approach spanning standardized screening, multimodal non-pharmacological interventions, and a nurse-coordinated multidisciplinary care model. Integrating routine CRF assessment into standard TACE clinical pathways and developing TACE-specific assessment tools are priorities for future research and clinical practice.

title: Evaluation of Nurses' Intent to Leave: Italian Translation, Cultural Adaptation, and Initial Psychometric Assessment of the Anticipated Turnover Scale.
abstract: Aim The aim of this study was to translate, culturally adapt, and preliminarily validate the Italian version of the Anticipated Turnover Scale (ATS). Design Cross-sectional validation study. Methods The Italian version of the ATS instrument was evaluated in a non-probabilistic sample of 168 nurses working at a Northeastern Italian Public University Hospital. Content validity was assessed by expert evaluation and statistical significance analysed using a binomial test. Construct validity was explored through Principal Axis Factoring analysis and internal consistency was measured using Cronbach's alpha. Results In a sample of 168 Italian nurses, the Italian 12-item (complete) version of the ATS showed an Item-Level Content Validity Index of 0.68, an internal structure with three main factors explaining 57.82% of the variance, and an internal consistency of 0.828. A reduced 10-item version showed an Item-Level Content Validity Index of 0.78, an internal structure with two main factors explaining 59.16% of the variance, and internal consistency increased to 0.901. Conclusions The Italian version of the ATS was preliminarily evaluated for its validity and reliability. In the current form, it is not ready for practical application yet and further studies should deepen its psychometric properties, as well as perform a confirmatory factor analysis on the factor structures reported here. They should also examine its temporal stability and establish a cut-off point to estimate actual turnover. Implications for nursing practice After implementing the questionnaire validation process, as reported above, ATS may help nursing managers to assess intention to leave and plan targeted and personalized interventions for improving retention, engagement, and well-being among nursing professionals. No patient or public contribution No patients, service users, caregivers, or members of the public were involved in this study, as it focused on the psychometric validation of a scale among registered nurses.

title: Advanced Practice Providers in Spinal CSF Leak Programs: A Multi-Institutional Study of Current Roles and Perceived Impact on Patient Care.
Challenges and opportunities with adapting international health care quality indicators to local contexts: a descriptive case study.
journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
abstract: Background International quality of care indicators provide a common framework for interoperability among different health care systems. We aimed to demonstrate the challenges and opportunities with adapting such quality indicators through the case of adapting the International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement (ICHOM) set of patient-centered outcome measures for older persons to the context of Canada. Methods In this descriptive case study, we purposefully recruited diverse stakeholders. Adapting a nominal group technique, we conducted group discussions to identify additional aspects deemed important for the context and needed to be added to the ICHOM. Transcripts were thematically analyzed to describe challenges and opportunities with adapting the ICHOM. Results Four older persons, seven clinicians, five health managers, and four decision-makers participated. Four emerging themes indicated that the ICHOM set for older persons was: (i) focusing on the negative aspects of care, suggesting an opportunity to have a positive perspective and strength-based approach; (ii) omitting equity in care delivery, which should be across all domains; (iii) disease-centered while a holistic approach was preferable; and (iv) primarily descriptive although it is key to generating action plans. Ageing in place-helping older persons remain in the communities through integrated care-was viewed as the optimal outcome. Conclusion International quality of care indicators are excellent starting points, but care must be taken to adapt them for use in local contexts. Social norms, relationships between users and health care providers, trust in health and social care systems, and contextual values are important factors to situate the quality indicators in an action-oriented context.

title: Determination of Managerial Competence Levels and Training Requirements of New Nurse Managers for Role Transition: Empirical Research Quantitative.
abstract: Aim The aim of this study was to identify managerial competencies and training needs of new nurse managers to improve their role transitions and inform the design of structured training programmes. Nurse managers significantly influence patient outcomes and organisational effectiveness. However, they are often appointed based on clinical expertise rather than managerial skills, creating challenges in leadership roles. Design A descriptive cross-sectional study design was used. Methods Data were collected from 185 new nurse managers using an online survey that assessed various domains of managerial competencies, including unit management, personnel management and care management. Results New nurse managers demonstrated high overall managerial competency scores. However, most participants reported limited formal managerial training before their appointments. Structured training programmes are essential for effectively developing managerial competencies in new nurse managers. Orientation and ongoing training programmes, including mentoring and coaching by experienced nurse managers and academic staff, will facilitate smoother role transitions and improve organisational outcomes. Patient or public contribution No patıent or publıc contribution.

title: Narrative nursing for prolonged myelosuppression after autologous stem cell transplantation in multiple myeloma: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Myelosuppression after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) exposes patients with multiple myeloma to substantial infection and bleeding risks and may be accompanied by marked psychological distress during protective isolation. Although supportive care is central to posttransplant recovery, reports describing how narrative nursing can be integrated into routine transplantation care remain limited. Patient concerns A 46-year-old married man with multiple myeloma was admitted 7 months after ASCT because of fever for half a day and erosive oral-labial mucosal lesions. He presented with febrile neutropenia, oral mucositis, severe pancytopenia, anxiety, hopelessness, and concern about his family role as the main financial provider. Diagnoses The patient was diagnosed with multiple myeloma after ASCT complicated by prolonged myelosuppression, febrile neutropenia, oral mucositis, and severe pancytopenia. Delayed hematopoietic reconstitution and infection, including possible fungal infection, were considered during the clinical course. Interventions The patient received protective isolation in a laminar airflow room, empiric broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, hemostatic prophylaxis, blood component support, meticulous oral and skin-mucosal care, nutrition and hydration support, and dynamic monitoring. A supplemental infusion of autologous hematopoietic stem cells was administered on hospital day 2. Individualized narrative nursing was provided through repeated one-to-one conversations, emotional validation, misconception correction, achievable daily goal setting, family communication, and discharge planning. Outcomes During the 16-day hospitalization, fever and mucositis resolved, leukocyte and neutrophil counts gradually recovered, inflammatory markers declined, and no new infection or major bleeding occurred. The patient reported reduced fear, improved sleep, and greater willingness to participate in care and follow-up. Lessons This case suggests that structured narrative nursing can be feasibly embedded in routine ASCT supportive care during prolonged myelosuppression and may support emotional adjustment, treatment engagement, and family-centered coping.

title: Age-Friendly Telegeriatrics: Evidence and a 5M-Based Framework for Hybrid Geriatric Care in Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Population ageing is increasing demand for accessible, coordinated, and person-centered care, while many older adults face barriers to conventional services related to frailty, multimorbidity, cognitive or sensory impairment, functional dependency, and travel burden. Telehealth can extend specialist expertise beyond conventional clinical settings, but geriatric care cannot be reduced to transferring a standard outpatient consultation to video. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on telegeriatrics, including virtual comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), cognitive and functional assessment, medication review, chronic-disease monitoring, rehabilitation, home-based care, and caregiver-supported models, with particular attention to Saudi Arabia. Evidence supports the feasibility and acceptability of several telegeriatric applications, although clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and long-term outcomes remain heterogeneous. Important limitations include digital exclusion, sensory and cognitive barriers, restricted physical examination, interoperability challenges, and the risk of shifting additional work to family caregivers. Emerging Saudi evidence demonstrates both rapid expansion of virtual-care infrastructure and growing experience with telehealth among older adults, including multidisciplinary tele-CGA through Seha Virtual Hospital, but geriatric-specific outcome evidence remains limited. Based on the narrative synthesis, an author-proposed, evidence-informed conceptual framework is presented to illustrate how the Geriatric 5Ms may inform the integration of virtual and in-person geriatric care. This framework has not undergone formal consensus development, prospective validation, or effectiveness testing. It is intended to support discussion, inform future research, and provide a starting point for prospective feasibility and implementation studies rather than serve as a clinical practice recommendation.

title: AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance with ABC-structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms after gastrointestinal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Background Postoperative nutritional management is critical for gastrointestinal cancer surgery patients, yet discharge advice is often standardized and lacks individualization. Whether an AI-facilitated individualized and quantified strategy improves short-term dietary intake compared with standard generic advice remains unclear; this trial does not isolate the independent effect of AI. Objective To determine whether AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance using structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms versus standard discharge advice. Methods In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 90 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastric or colorectal cancer surgery were assigned 1:1 to AI-facilitated individualized guidance generated by DeepSeek v3.2 using an ABC-structured prompt plus clinician review or standard discharge dietary advice (standard care group). The intervention combined AI, individualization, quantified targets, written guidance, and clinician review; the trial cannot isolate AI alone. Primary outcome was energy intake adequacy (≥ 90% of target) at 30 days post-discharge. Secondary outcomes included protein intake adequacy, nutritional status, patient-reported outcomes, process measures (expert-rated quality scores, provider time), and 30-day complications. Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment. Results Baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups. The AI-guided group achieved significantly higher energy adequacy (66.7% vs. 40.0%, OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1, P = 0.01) and protein adequacy (62.2% vs. 35.6%, OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.8, P = 0.01) at 30 days. Expert-rated quality scores were superior in the AI-guided group for completeness (4.6 vs. 3.2), individualization (4.8 vs. 2.8), and actionability (4.5 vs. 3.5) (all P Conclusion AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance improved short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms and reduced provider time compared with standard generic advice. These findings do not show that AI itself is superior to similarly individualized non-AI counseling and do not establish longer-term nutritional or clinical benefit. Clinical supervision remains essential.

title: Patient-Centred Quality of Nursing Care: A Cross-Sectional Study of the Level and Associated Factors as Perceived by Patients.
abstract: Aim To produce evaluative knowledge on the patient-centred quality of nursing care and factors related to it from the perspective of hospitalized patients in Finland. Design A cross-sectional explorative study. Review methods Survey instrument included the structured, internationally validated Good Nursing Care Scale (40 items) (Leino-Kilpi 2025), General Evaluation of the Quality of Nursing Care (5 items) and background factors (15 items). The data were statistically analysed. Data sources Data were collected between May and July 2025 from hospitalized adult patients (N = 861), from two wellbeing services counties in Finland. Results Patients evaluated the quality of nursing care high: subcategories of Good Nursing Care Scale (Median 3.80-3.00, Scale 1-4), The General Evaluation of the Quality of Nursing (Median 9, Scale 4-10) and Patient educational support (Median 3.46, Scale 1-4). Lowest ratings were in the collaboration with the family/significant others. Identified statistically associated factors were patients´ work status and health status on the day of discharge, and sufficient information prior hospitalization. Conclusion The results both confirm existing knowledge and identify development needs in conceptual, methodological and clinical fields. Implications for the profession and patient care The research has implications both on the patient and organizational levels, including role of the patients and leadership of nursing quality. Impact The public social and healthcare reform underscores the need for quality evaluation in Finland. The research showed the patient-centred quality of nursing care in hospital being high, but identified areas for development. The findings may impact on nursing practice, nursing education and healthcare organizations. Reporting method Reported in accordance with the STROBE guidelines. Patient or public contribution Patients were voluntary respondents in the study.

title: From Gendered Diagnosis to Community Care: How Borderline Personality Disorder Organizes Community Mental Health Nursing Practice.
abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a contested diagnosis that has been criticized for pathologizing women's responses to trauma, adversity, and relational harm. This paper examines how BPD, as a gendered, historically situated, and institutionally mediated diagnostic category, shapes community mental health nursing (CMHN) practice. Using a critical conceptual analysis, it synthesizes historical, feminist, psychiatric, nursing, and Mad studies literature, combining genealogical, critical feminist, and social-structural perspectives. The paper argues that BPD functions not only as a clinical description of symptoms but also as an institutional category that influences documentation, referral pathways, eligibility criteria, and service design. Through these processes, the diagnosis shapes clinical visibility, therapeutic relationships, service access, and continuity of care. Moving beyond explanations of stigma that focus solely on individual clinician attitudes, the analysis demonstrates how diagnostic meanings are reproduced through organizational and health system structures, contributing to forms of structural stigma that constrain relational and trauma-informed care. The paper concludes with implications and recommendations for nursing practice, education, service delivery, and policy, including trauma-informed and relational approaches to assessment, non-stigmatizing documentation practices, transparent referral and eligibility processes, investment in community-based services, and strengthened clinical supervision and workforce supports.

title: Development and Feasibility Evaluation of a Nurse-Led ePRO System for Home-Based Post-Chemotherapy Symptom Management in Patients With Cancer.
abstract: Background Electronic patient-reported outcome (ePRO) systems support symptom monitoring after chemotherapy; however, their integration into structured nurse-led oncology workflows remains limited. In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate the short-term feasibility and usability of a nurse-led ePRO system for home-based postchemotherapy symptom monitoring and structured nursing triage for cancer patients. Methods This single-arm feasibility study was conducted at a cancer center in Taiwan between April and September 2024 among adult patients requiring home-based symptom monitoring after hospital-based chemotherapy care. The nurse-led digital system was designed to support weekly self-reporting of 12 chemotherapy-related symptoms using the Chemotherapy Toxicity Self-Assessment Questionnaire. The system incorporated rule-based triage categorization using green, orange, and red risk levels and predefined nurse response protocols. Feasibility outcomes included report adherence, triage alert management, and system performance. Usability was evaluated using the System Usability Scale. Results Forty-two patients submitted 306 symptom reports during the 8-week monitoring period, corresponding to an overall adherence rate of 91.1%. Among all reports, 16.3% generated orange alerts requiring nurse follow-up and 6.5% generated red alerts requiring urgent review. Fatigue, pain, and hand-foot syndrome were the most frequently reported abnormal symptoms. All orange and red alerts had documented nursing review. The system met the predefined technical performance indicators during simulated load testing, and achieved a mean System Usability Scale score of 92.6 ± 6.46. Conclusions This nurse-led ePRO system demonstrated favorable short-term feasibility and usability for home-based postchemotherapy symptom monitoring and structured nursing triage. These findings support the practicality of integrating structured ePRO monitoring into postchemotherapy nursing care. Further multicenter and comparative studies are warranted to evaluate long-term engagement, scalability, and clinical outcomes.

title: 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN).
authors: On Behalf Of The Italian Society Of Nephrology Nurses Sian Board Of Directors
abstract: The 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN), held in Bologna, Italy, from 4 to 6 May 2026, provided a national forum for discussion on the evolving role of nursing in nephrology.
