METHODS: We conducted a retrospective machine learning-based study using weekly pharmacy usage data from a large tertiary hospital in Beijing, China, from January 2021 to December 2024. Data were split into a training set (2021–2023) and a testing set (2024). Stock keeping units were classified by the Syntetos–Boylan average demand interval/coefficient of variation squared framework into smooth, erratic, lumpy and intermittent demand. The LightGBM-Tweedie model was compared with naïve, autoregressive integrated moving average, random forest and long short-term memory models. Performance was assessed using weighted mean absolute percentage error (wMAPE) on the 2024 test set and stratified by demand pattern. Financial impact was evaluated by comparing model forecasts with historical manual procurement orders using overstock and shortage cost proxies. RESULTS: In the targeted analysis of complex demand patterns, our model achieved a wMAPE of 21.4%, with approximately 3% improvement on the baseline naïve model. Financially, the analysis revealed a critical operational insight: while manual procurement led to minimal overstock but shortage costs significantly higher than overstock costs, the model substantially reduced estimated shortage-related financial losses while moderately increasing holding costs. By implementing a strategic inventory buffer, the model reduced the estimated financial impact of stockouts by approximately 70% for erratic-demand drugs compared with manual practices. CONCLUSION: The developed framework may support more balanced inventory decision-making by mitigating systematic under-ordering behaviours. Rather than replacing professional judgement, it functions as a risk-stratification tool that provides a quantitative basis for balancing holding costs and availability. Integrating such decision-support systems into hospital policy potentially offers a scalable pathway to reduce clinical shortages and enhance the financial resilience of the pharmaceutical supply chain.

title: Availability and Access to Cardiovascular Medicines in Mozambique: A Scoping Review
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. In Mozambique, non-communicable diseases account for approximately 28% of deaths, with CVDs contributing substantially to this burden. Despite the country’s hierarchical health system and the World Health Organization target of 80% availability of essential medicines, access to cardiovascular medicines remains poorly documented. This scoping review mapped the availability, prices, affordability, physical access, and health-system barriers affecting access to essential cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O’Malley framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies assessed the availability, stock-outs, prices, affordability, or health-system barriers related to cardiovascular medicines and diagnostics in Mozambique. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by multiple reviewers. Consistent with the scoping review design, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not undertaken. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Essential cardiovascular medicines showed persistently low availability, with mean availability of approximately 21% across public hospital pharmacies, private retail outlets, and private hospitals, substantially below the WHO 80% target. Public facilities consistently provided only a limited range of older first-line medicines, while second- and third-line medicines, statins, digoxin, direct oral anticoagulants, and diagnostic reagents were frequently unavailable. When public stocks were depleted, patients relied on private-sector purchases, where generic medicines cost an average of 4.51 times international reference prices. Long-term secondary prevention could require 14.0–17.8 days of wages per month for low-income workers. These barriers were associated with low hypertension awareness, treatment, and control, substantial target-organ damage, high stroke case-fatality, and poor anticoagulation control. Access to cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique is severely constrained by low availability, frequent stock-outs, and unaffordable private-sector prices. Strengthening medicine selection, supply-chain management, financial protection, and decentralized protocol-based care is essential to improve equitable access to cardiovascular treatment.

title: Ceftriaxone-by-default in surgical prophylaxis across the East African community: a measurement problem.
abstract: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis across the East African Community is dominated by ceftriaxone, a WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve (AWaRe) Watch-group third-generation cephalosporin not recommended for routine prophylaxis. The practice recurs across regional point prevalence surveys, yet consumption surveillance cannot distinguish prophylactic from therapeutic use. Drawing on antimicrobial-use surveys, surgical-prophylaxis studies, resistance surveillance, and medicine-availability reports, we argue that four interacting failure modes sustain it: substitution of first-line agents, prolongation of postoperative prophylaxis, unnecessary combination, and empirical spillover from ward prescribing. Resistance among surgical-site isolates is already high enough to threaten the value of prophylaxis itself. Prophylaxis is measured for duration, documented indication, and guideline concordance, and agent choice is captured in point-prevalence surveys, but none of this reaches the national consumption totals that govern procurement, and no indicator records the supply constraint determining the agent or the resistance it selects. We propose four measures, one requiring routing rather than building and three genuinely absent, that would convert an ungoverned practice into a governable one.

title: Operational Workflows and Decision Making Processes in Hospital Pharmacy Services During Drug Shortages: A Scoping Review.
Contextual conditions shaping the upward referral of obstetric emergencies from community health centres in the Eastern Cape: a Straussian Grounded Theory study
From Gaps in Maternity Care to Maternal Rescue: An Interprofessional Implementation Agenda for Anesthesia and Maternal Critical Care in Somalia.
abstract: Somalia's maternal health system faces a dual challenge: limited access to skilled maternity care and insufficient capacity to rescue women who deteriorate during or after obstetric emergencies. Hemorrhage, hypertensive emergencies including eclampsia, sepsis, obstructed labor, and urgent cesarean delivery require coordinated maternity, anesthesia, nursing, resuscitation, postoperative surveillance, and critical-care functions. This evidence-informed commentary shifts the discussion from documenting gaps to an interprofessional implementation agenda. We propose five linked priorities: a regulated and supported maternity and obstetric-anesthesia workforce; an evidence-based cesarean safety bundle; step-up maternal high-care capacity; early-warning, crisis resource management, escalation, and referral pathways; and routine measurement through maternal and perioperative quality systems. The approach emphasizes actions that referral maternity hospitals can introduce progressively, with named local accountability, team training, minimum resource requirements, and measurable indicators, while avoiding unsupported assumptions about national critical-care capacity. Somalia does not need to wait for a fully developed intensive-care system before improving maternal rescue. The immediate opportunity is to connect five functions that are too often fragmented: competent anesthesia provision, reliable cesarean safety processes, early recognition of deterioration, monitored maternal high care, and accountable review of outcomes. Strengthening these functions as one interprofessional maternal-rescue pathway offers a practical route to reducing preventable severe maternal morbidity and mortality in Somalia.

title: Logistics of clinical xenotransplantation: from donor pig production to global organ distribution.
journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
abstract: The shortage of transplantable organs remains one of the most significant unmet challenges in modern medicine. Despite advances in donor management, organ preservation, surgical techniques, and immunosuppression, organ demand continues to exceed supply worldwide. Xenotransplantation using genetically engineered porcine organs has emerged as a promising strategy to address this gap. Recent clinical pig-to-human heart and kidney transplantations have demonstrated the feasibility of clinical xenotransplantation and shifted attention from immunological barriers toward practical implementation. This review examines the logistical requirements for clinical xenotransplantation, with particular emphasis on donor herd management, biosafety, organ preservation technologies, and future distribution networks. The integration of donor production with advanced machine perfusion technologies may ultimately transform transplantation medicine from a donor-dependent emergency service into a predictable and scalable therapeutic platform.

title: Fatty acid oxidation impairment in diabetic kidney disease: a bidirectional feedback network from mitochondrial quality control to systemic regulation.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes with complex metabolic pathogenesis and limited therapeutic options. Defective fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and consequent lipotoxicity are central to renal fibrosis, but their systematic integration with other DKD pathologies remains incomplete. This Review examines the molecular links between FAO impairment and mitochondrial quality control, metabolic reprogramming, ferroptosis, ER stress, and gut dysbiosis. Based on current evidence, we propose that in diabetic kidney disease, defective fatty acid oxidation and impaired mitochondrial quality control form a self-amplifying bidirectional positive feedback loop. Hyperglycemia and lipotoxicity suppress PGC-1α-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis, promote excessive mitochondrial fission, and lead to impaired PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy, thereby reducing fatty acid oxidation efficiency. The resulting ATP deficiency and lipid accumulation, in turn, elevate mitochondrial ROS levels and further exacerbate mitochondrial quality control dysregulation. This energy crisis then drives aberrant lipid accumulation, compensatory glycolytic enhancement, and blocked branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and amplifies injury signals through pathways such as ferroptosis and ER stress, ultimately establishing a systemic vicious cycle via the gut-kidney axis that promotes tubular injury and interstitial fibrosis. We also summarize emerging FAO-targeted interventions, including natural compounds, modern drugs, Chinese patent medicines, and lifestyle strategies. Although FAO impairment is now recognized as a key node in DKD progression, most evidence remains preclinical. Future integration of multi-omics and dynamic metabolic tracing is needed to establish causality and stage-specific roles, while dissecting the FAO regulatory architecture across renal cell types may offer new early diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

title: The Knowledge‐Practice Gap in Prescribing: A Study of Perceptual and Experiential Predictors at Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital, Ethiopia—A Cross‐Sectional Study
Strengthening public health programmes and the antivenom ecosystem: strategic policy priorities to combat envenomation by animal bites and stings in Latin America and the Caribbean.
authors: Latin American Network of Public Antivenom Manufacturing Laboratories (RELAPA) Collaboration
Latin American Network of National Programs for Venomous Animal Accidents (REDPEVA) Collaboration
abstract: Background Envenomation by snakes, scorpions, spiders, and caterpillars remains a major but unevenly addressed public health challenge in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). Environmental change, urbanisation, and ecological disruption are changing the distribution of medically important species, while persistent gaps in surveillance, clinical management, and antivenom availability limit prevention and care. In this study, we analysed epidemiological trends, health system capacity, and the regional antivenom ecosystem to inform strategic public health priorities. Methods We analysed secondary data from regional surveys coordinated by Pan American Health Organization networks for the period 2019-2024. We used negative binomial regression models to assess temporal trends in total cases and deaths from four major envenomations and to generate projections up to 2030. We used spatial analyses to examine heterogeneity in incidence, mortality, and case-fatality rates, and evaluated antivenom production, procurement, and use with indicators standardised to epidemiological burden. We complemented the quantitative findings with qualitative content analysis of regional and meeting reports. Results The incidence of all envenomations showed an increasing trend over time, with particularly marked increases in spider bites and caterpillar contacts. We observed spatial heterogeneity across countries. Overall mortality remained low for most envenomations, while the case-fatality rate for spider envenomation was projected to increase by 2030 if the observed trends continued. We identified weaknesses in surveillance quality, risk mapping, clinical preparedness, and follow-up of sequelae. We also identified mismatches between antivenom production, procurement, and therapeutic use, varying by envenomation type. Regional initiatives have strengthened coordination but have not fully resolved inequities in access and preparedness. Conclusions Envenomation in LAC remains an expanding and evolving public health challenge requiring coordinated, forward-looking responses. While acknowledging limitations in data quality and the need for longer-term evidence, our findings provide a system-level analysis and generate scientifically and policy-relevant evidence, supporting a targeted action framework to advance progress toward the World Health Organization 2030 targets for reducing envenomation-related morbidity and mortality.

title: Clinical efficacy and safety of medicines procured through China's national volume-based procurement policy: a systematic review of 81 studies.
abstract: Background China's National Volume-Based Procurement (NVBP) policy, launched in 2018, has sharply cut drug prices through competitive bidding among manufacturers of quality-consistent generics. Concerns persist that reductions sometimes exceeding 90% may compromise efficacy or safety, and this evidence has not been systematically synthesised. Objective To evaluate the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of NVBP-selected medicines. Methods Six sources (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP) were searched in two arms for reports published between January 2018 and January 2026; CENTRAL records could not be exported. Titles and abstracts were screened by one reviewer with a second checking; all 862 full-text reports were screened in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed in eight domains, three specific to this policy setting, and certainty with GRADE. Results were synthesised without meta-analysis by effect direction within comparator strata. PROSPERO: CRD420261303351. Results Eighty-one studies were included, 72 from the database searches and nine from citation searching; 72 were retrospective or before-and-after and 62 single-centre. Sixty-eight studies plus one comparison from a six-arm study formed the main analysis against the originator. There, 60 of 62 counted efficacy comparisons and 55 of 65 safety comparisons found no significant difference, and no efficacy comparison carries an assigned direction. Four safety comparisons favoured the originator (moxifloxacin tablets, olanzapine, paediatric ceftriaxone, atorvastatin) and three favoured the selected product (linezolid tablets, ceftriaxone, bortezomib); no direction could be assigned in three. Acquisition costs were 44% to more than 90% lower wherever reported. The median smallest detectable fall in response rate was 16.5 percentage points and the median smallest detectable relative risk for harm 2.67, reflecting the sample sizes available. Certainty was very low for efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics, and low for economic outcomes. Conclusion The available evidence does not show that NVBP-selected generics perform worse than their comparators, but its certainty is very low and the concordance of null findings cannot be read as demonstrated equivalence. Most studies reported no effect estimate, many were small and single-centre, and six reported statistics irreconcilable with their own data. Prospective, adequately powered studies reporting estimates with confidence intervals remain necessary. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261303351; Identifier: CRD420261303351.

title: Anticipating El Niño-related health risks in Latin America and the Caribbean: from climate information to public health preparedness.
abstract: El Niño is a recurrent mode of tropical Pacific climate variability with major public health implications for Latin America and the Caribbean. Its development is partly driven by the Bjerknes feedback, a coupled ocean-atmosphere process in which weakened equatorial trade winds reduce coastal upwelling and allow warm surface waters to shift eastward. Warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific can reshape regional rainfall and temperature patterns, increasing the likelihood of floods, droughts, wildfires, food-system disruption, and health-service interruption in locations with established ENSO teleconnections. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the environmental and health pathways through which El Niño may affect populations in Latin America and the Caribbean. We distinguish evidence directly linking health outcomes to ENSO or Coastal El Niño from evidence derived from floods, droughts, wildfires, and other hydrometeorological disasters without formal attribution to ENSO. The latter is used to characterize plausible health pathways and preparedness needs rather than ENSO-specific causal effects. Potential consequences include immediate mortality and injury, waterborne and vector-borne infections, disruption of chronic disease care, food insecurity, undernutrition, toxic exposures, psychological distress, and prolonged health-system burden. The timing and persistence of these effects are context-dependent; preparedness and response priorities are therefore organized by operational needs rather than fixed post-event intervals. As of August 2026, authoritative forecasts indicated that El Niño was present and strengthening, providing a current illustration of why anticipatory preparedness is necessary while not guaranteeing any specific regional impact. Early warning, flood-risk mapping, water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions, epidemiological and entomological surveillance, continuity of health services, and community-centered risk communication should therefore be adapted to local forecasts, vulnerabilities, and surveillance data.

title: Surveillance Data Use Through the Fleming Fund: Informing Action on Antimicrobial Resistance in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
abstract: Background Drawing on the Fleming Fund's work to strengthen antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance across Africa and Asia during 2018-2026, this article provides one of the first syntheses of AMR surveillance data use in low- and middle-income countries. Methods A participatory synthesis for narrative review was conducted to summarize experience across administrative levels (facility, subnational, national, and regional). Results Data use was most evident at the facility level, in human health systems where resistance patterns, antimicrobial use, and clinical data increasingly informed antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention and control, and other quality improvement initiatives. Data use in other sectors required different approaches. At the national level, Fleming Fund investments were associated with revisions of treatment guidelines, updates of essential medicines lists, and regulatory measures, primarily through improved governance and policy communities. Regional platforms supported member country data use at the national level. Subnational data use was undertaken in countries with decentralized health systems. Across levels, data use pathways driven by local priorities helped surveillance inform action. Conclusions Fleming Fund experience suggests that surveillance is more likely to inform action when data use is built into system design. Continued investment will be needed if AMR surveillance is to improve policy and practice in low- and middle-income countries.

title: CE Mark Is Not Enough: Medical Device Safety in African Healthcare Systems.
abstract: Across African health systems, CE marking is often used as an important regulatory or procurement screening criterion for imported medical devices. Yet the CE symbol is not, by itself, a safety certificate issued by a regulator; it is a manufacturer's declaration of compliance with applicable European Union requirements, supported by technical documentation and, depending on device classification, notified-body assessment. This commentary examines the risks that arise when a CE claim is accepted without verifying the supporting documentation, device identity and configuration, or post-market performance. Drawing on regulatory literature and published African evidence, it discusses documented equipment and device-management failures while noting that direct evidence attributing such failures to false or unsupported CE claims remains limited. It reviews emerging regulatory responses, including Uganda's National Drug Authority framework, South Africa's Health Products Regulatory Authority requirements, and continental initiatives. It argues that strengthening medical device safety in Africa does not require abandoning regulatory reliance, but does require verifiable documentation, risk-based oversight, stronger post-market surveillance and regulatory cooperation. CE marking should be treated as an important input into verification, not the end of the process.

title: Client, health care provider, and policymaker perspectives on point-of-care/near-point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections in community pharmacies in Uganda.
abstract: Introduction Point-of-care or near-point-of-care (POC/near-POC) tests for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are often unavailable and unaffordable in low-resource settings, despite the World Health Organization's (WHO) recommendation that such testing be offered, leading to empiric treatment. Private community pharmacies (CPs) are often the first point of contact for people with symptoms of STIs, where pharmacists dispense treatment without diagnostic testing or prescriptions. This study evaluated clients,' providers,' and policymakers' perspectives on POC/near-POC STI testing in community pharmacies for targeted management. Methods Between June and September 2022, we nested a qualitative study into a prospective cohort of clients seeking both STI and non-STI treatments in community pharmacies in Kampala and Wakiso districts in Uganda. They were tested for HIV, syphilis, trichomonas, chlamydia, and gonorrhea using POC/near-POC tests. A purposive sample of 50 participants consented to participate in in-depth and key informant interviews. Data were analyzed thematically using NVivo version 14 with an inductive approach, with results reported according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ). Results Clients (n = 35), health care providers (n = 9), and policymakers (n = 6) described the benefits of POC/near-POC tests for HIV/STIs at community pharmacies, citing affordability, accessibility, and convenience. Participants noted that such testing could promote behavioral change, shorten turnaround time for results, speed access to treatment relative to conventional laboratory methods, and support sustainable antimicrobial resistance control. Reported barriers included limited awareness among clients and health workers, inadequate privacy and space, long waiting times, unclear self-sample collection instructions, stigma around HIV testing, and reluctance to test for non-HIV STIs. Participants recommended raising STI awareness, offering clearer explanations of test results, expanding test access, reducing stigma, provider training, and ensuring a sustainable supply chain for testing kits. Conclusions POC/near-POC testing for HIV/STIs was highly acceptable to both pharmacy clients and providers in this study. Integrating such testing into community pharmacy settings could strengthen national HIV/STI management programs, and addressing the identified barriers could improve access to HIV/STI diagnostics and strengthen linkage to care.

title: Viral Hepatitis, Potential Aflatoxin B1 Exposure, and Projected Metabolic Risk Factors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Somalia: A Call for Integrated Prevention, Surveillance, and Research.
abstract: This commentary is a narrative synthesis of Somali, regional, and global evidence on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in Somalia; it does not report new epidemiological data, and claims are graded according to whether they are directly demonstrated in Somalia or inferred from broader African or global literature. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality globally and presents a particularly difficult challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, hepatitis C virus (HCV), food-borne aflatoxin exposure, limited surveillance, and restricted access to curative treatment intersect. Somalia has no mature population-based cancer registry, yet available hospital-based evidence indicates that liver cancer is an important component of the national cancer burden. Directly documented Somali evidence is limited to hospital case series and to donor-, hospital-, and laboratory-based HBV studies: a Somali series of 268 patients with HCC documented a predominantly male population, a relatively young mean age, large tumors, and portal-vein thrombosis associated with poor prognostic features, and recent Mogadishu studies have shown continuing HBV transmission and important gaps in vaccination, testing, and linkage to care. By contrast, the contribution of aflatoxin B1 exposure and of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to HCC in Somalia is not directly documented. No Somali biomonitoring, dietary-exposure, or MASLD-prevalence data exist; the discussion of these pathways in this commentary is therefore inferred from regional and global literature and should be read as a precautionary, hypothesis-generating projection of future risk rather than an established local driver of current disease. This commentary argues that Somalia should nonetheless not address viral, toxic, and metabolic exposures through isolated programs. An integrated, phased HCC prevention strategy should combine timely HBV birth-dose vaccination, maternal screening and antiviral prophylaxis, adult testing and treatment, HCV diagnosis and cure, precautionary food-safety surveillance for aflatoxins, metabolic-risk assessment embedded in liver care, risk-based liver ultrasound surveillance with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) used only as an adjunct, strengthened diagnostic imaging and pathology, and a national liver-cancer registry. Locally led epidemiological and implementation research, including population-attributable-fraction scenario modelling and representativeness analyses of existing hospital series, is urgently needed to quantify the relative contribution of viral, toxic, and metabolic pathways and to identify feasible models for surveillance and referral in a resource-constrained setting.

title: Improving Medication Management in Indonesian Aged Care Homes: Research Priority Setting With Stakeholders.
abstract: Indonesia and other Southeast Asian nations are experiencing rapidly aging populations. The Indonesian Government recently announced a national initiative of aged care homes to support older people not able to live independently or receive family care. Medication-without-harm is the topic of the World Health Organization Third Global Patient Safety Challenge. The objective of this study was to prioritize research questions for improving medication management in public and private aged care homes in Indonesia. In April 2025, a 20-person expert consensus panel was convened comprising general practitioners, geriatricians, neurologists, nurses, pharmacists, physiotherapists, nutritionists, public health practitioners, aged care home managers, Ministry of Health representatives, ASEAN organization representatives, and a family caregiver. The panel used modified nominal group technique to identify and prioritize research for improving medication management in aged care homes in Indonesia. The panel identified 47 research priorities that were consolidated into 15 policy and 20 practice priorities for voting. The highest ranked policy priorities focused on necessary regulations and clinical guidelines; essential medication lists for older people; and policies to support development and use of drug formulations acceptable for residents of aged care homes. The highest ranked practice priorities emphasized digital health technologies; medication safety monitoring; and enhancing communication among families, aged care home staff, and prescribers. The findings lay the groundwork for a culturally- and context-specific research roadmap for improving medication management in Indonesian aged care homes. This will guide researchers and research funding organizations in aligning future studies with policy and practice priorities.

title: Hereditary angioedema in Latin America: international recommendations, expert consensus, and reported implementation barriers.
abstract: Background Current international hereditary angioedema (HAE) guidelines and treat-to-target recommendations emphasize accurate diagnosis, early on-demand treatment, procedure-related short-term prophylaxis, individualized long-term prophylaxis (LTP), and routine assessment of disease control and quality of life. Evidence on implementation in Latin America remains limited. We aimed to assess concordance between international guidance and the consensus of a selected Latin American expert panel and to identify expert-reported implementation barriers. Methods A scientific committee developed and externally validated a 74-item questionnaire (domains summarized in Supplementary Table S1) and conducted a two-round Delphi process among Latin American HAE experts. Consensus items were rated on a nine-point agreement scale, with consensus defined a priori as at least two-thirds of respondents scoring within a three-point band in the agreement or disagreement range. Descriptive items captured expert-reported diagnostic testing, treatment patterns, monitoring practices, and perceived implementation determinants. Consensus findings are summarized as meeting the prespecified threshold; descriptive findings are reported with item-specific n/N when available. Instrument validation (July-November 2024) showed high inter-rater agreement (Kendall W = 0.84; p Results Thirty experts from 10 countries completed the process (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela). The prespecified consensus threshold was met for core biochemical diagnostic work-up, selective genetic evaluation, first-line targeted LTP (pdC1-INH, lanadelumab, and berotralstat), continued availability of on-demand therapy, routine monitoring, and management of special populations. The principal expert-reported implementation signal was limited feasibility: frequent or constant prophylaxis-supply interruptions were reported by 19/30 experts (63%), including 13/23 (57%) practicing in settings where public or insurance coverage was reported. Cost (19/30; 63%) and medicine availability (8/30; 27%) were the most frequently reported barriers. These reports were not independently verified against reimbursement, procurement, formulary, or inventory data. Conclusion Within this selected panel, expert consensus was broadly concordant with international HAE guidance. Panelists reported barriers involving diagnostic testing, financing, medicine availability, and continuity of supply; however, these findings are perceptions and reported practices, not representative national or regional estimates or audited health-system data. They identify candidate implementation priorities that require confirmation through patient-level registries and objective access data.

title: An evaluation experiment on the causal effects of differentiated medical insurance reimbursement on medical choice and medical expenses.
abstract: Introduction Uneven distribution of health-care resources and rising medical spending have kept medical-insurance reform high on China's policy agenda. This study examines whether differentiated reimbursement can redirect patients toward lower-level providers and moderate the cost of care. Methods We used provincial health-insurance claims, institutional operating records, and a patient-behavior survey covering December 2022 to August 2024. A difference-indifferences model was used to estimate policy effects, followed by mechanism and heterogeneity analyses. Results Higher reimbursement rates for primary and secondary institutions increased the probability of choosing these providers. The association operated mainly through a lower out-of-pocket share and improved primary-care service capacity. Responses were stronger among patients with chronic conditions, older patients, and lower-income groups, whereas acute and severe cases continued to rely largely on tertiary hospitals. The policy also reduced average per-visit costs and individual payment burdens, although provider responses at some tertiary hospitals may attenuate the cost-control effect. Discussion Differentiated reimbursement appears useful for supporting hierarchical care, but it is unlikely to establish a mature hierarchical medical system by itself. It should be combined with primary-care capacity building, clearer referral pathways, and payment-system reform.

title: Fleming Fund Implementation in Kenya: What Have We Learned About Strengthening One Health Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance for Decision-making?
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
abstract: Background Kenya has moved from fragmented, pilot-based antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance toward a coordinated One Health system, and its experience, pathways of change, and remaining gaps are relevant for other low- and middle-income settings working to operationalize One Health AMR surveillance. Methods Here, we report a narrative overview of programmatic learning using 2018 as the pre-Fleming Fund baseline, drawing on national and global surveillance reports, monitoring frameworks from the Quadripartite indicators, qualitative evidence on governance, implementation and policy evolution across the One Health sectors, and Fleming Fund documentation. Results Since 2018, AMR surveillance expanded from 2 human health sites to 30 human, animal, and environmental sites by 2025. National reports evolved to integrate AMR, antimicrobial consumption, and antimicrobial use data; routine reporting to global platforms matured; and outputs such as dashboards, reports, and policy briefs informing stewardship, Infection Prevention and Control, regulatory action, and policy decisions. External benchmarks showed improvement in AMR-related capacity, with World Health Organization Joint External Evaluation scores moving from limited to demonstrated capacity for surveillance and multisectoral coordination. Conclusions Kenya's experience suggests that sustainable progress depends on embedding AMR surveillance within government-led governance structures, technical systems, and coordinated partner support, but sustaining gains will require predictable financing and routine data use.

title: Generating Actionable Data From Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance: Insights From the Fleming Fund's International Experience.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, with the greatest burden falling on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) also challenged with limited surveillance capacity. The UK Government's Fleming Fund was established in 2015 to strengthen AMR surveillance across Africa and Asia through a One Health approach. This paper draws on program experience, country implementation evidence, and published literature to describe how the Fleming Fund operationalized AMR surveillance, assess its contribution to the quantity and quality of surveillance data, identify key implementation challenges, and consider implications for future global surveillance strategies. The Fleming Fund combined investments in laboratory infrastructure, workforce development, quality assurance, data systems, governance, and data use. Across supported countries, these investments enabled substantial growth in routine bacteriology and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, strengthened reference and surveillance laboratory capacity, increased participation in external quality assessment, and expanded reporting to the World Health Organization's Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System. The program also supported complementary surveillance approaches, including antimicrobial use and consumption data and, in some settings, burden-of-disease and genomic surveillance. Progress, however, has been uneven and remains vulnerable to fragile infrastructure, procurement and supply chain bottlenecks, workforce turnover, fragmented data systems, weak clinical-laboratory interfaces, limited representativeness, and uncertain long-term financing. The Fleming Fund experience shows that strengthening AMR surveillance in LMICs is feasible, but requires sustained, system-wide investment. Future strategies should prioritize integration with clinical care, stronger digital and analytical capacity, broader diagnostic access, and domestic financing to ensure that high-quality AMR data are generated, shared, and translated into action.

title: Pharmacological treatment, adversities, and mobile-based post-discharge follow-up of mucormycosis survivors in Central India: strengthening patient care.
abstract: Introduction Mucormycosis, a significant post-COVID-19 complication, is stimulated by uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (DM), prolonged corticosteroid exposure, or immunosuppression. Despite clinical advancements, survivors experience long-term challenges; however, follow-up is often missing from treatment strategies, highlighting a critical gap in safeguarding survivors' long-term well-being. Objective To analyze pharmacological management, adverse events, and post-discharge outcomes among rhino-orbital cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM) patients using medical records and Mobile-Based Post-Discharge (MBPD) follow-up, to inform future clinical and follow-up practices. Method Clinical data of confirmed ROCM inpatients (2021) at two COVID-19-dedicated hospitals in Central India were extracted from medical records and analyzed. Mucormycosis survivors were followed up in 2023 using the MBPD questionnaire to explore overall treatment, post-discharge adversities, and outcomes. The clinical findings and patient-reported experiences were summarised descriptively. Factors associated with adversities were examined using multivariable Firth-penalized logistic regression. Results Among 108 mucormycosis patients, DM was present in 32% of inpatients. Liposomal amphotericin B (71%) and posaconazole (75%) were predominantly prescribed. Access (40%), Watch (39%), and Not Recommended antibiotic combinations (13%) were most prescribed. An average of 1.3 adverse drug reactions were recorded among 73 inpatients. Of 97 survivors, 36 were non-responders. Eighty could be contacted, and 61 (76%) consented to participate in MBPD follow-up. Fifty-two of 61 respondents reported 123 post-discharge adversities, averaging 2.4 adversities per patient, including 9 (7%) deaths confirmed by family members. Antifungal prescription was significantly associated with adversities (aOR 5.82, 95% CI 1.56-21.71; p = 0.009), whereas older age (>60 years) showed a borderline association. Respondents appreciated the follow-up calls and emphasized regularizing them. Conclusion Liposomal amphotericin B, posaconazole, and antibiotics were the most prescribed drugs. DM was the most common comorbidity, highlighting the need for careful monitoring. Antifungal prescriptions were significantly associated with adversities, suggesting the need for implementation of a contextual drug-use policy. The MBPD follow-up was well received and may help monitor recovery, identify health needs, and support the care of survivors of chronic diseases in the future. Survivor-centred care models are suggested to support post-discharge recovery and multidimensional challenges.

title: The potential of a "next generation" of community health workers to accelerate progress in reaching Universal Health Coverage and Health for All.
abstract: Many health systems, particularly in low- and lower middle-income countries (LMICs), are lagging in their progress in achieving Universal Health Coverage and delivering on the promise of Health for All, constrained by workforce shortages, fiscal ceilings, and inadequate outreach to those lacking basic and essential services. Stark inequities in coverage of services and in health status persist. Strengthening community health worker (CHW) programs provides the fastest and most cost-effective route for health systems to achieve their full potential. CHWs should become the backbone of primary health care (PHC) and the foundation of health systems. Evidence from more than a decade of national-scale experience demonstrates that CHWs who are appropriately trained, paid, equipped, and supervised can extend high-quality essential services to the last mile while improving the overall efficiency of the health system. We are at a point in time when donor strategies and private investment are captivated by the promise of digital health and artificial intelligence. The most reliable approach to saving more lives is still a paid, supported CHW empowered with digital tools. At the same time, the contraction of Official Development Assistance (ODA) creates both risk and opportunity. ODA must pivot from supporting services to catalytic capital: time-bound, matching investments that accelerate governments' own proCHW policy. A "next generation" of CHW programs in LMICs would enable CHWs to visit every home monthly and provide a broad array of PHC services as a result of adequate remuneration and appropriate training, supervision, logistical support, and integration into the health system. This could yield a highly favorable economic return-through productivity gains from better health, reduced health-care expenditures, and pandemic-risk mitigation. A "next generation" of CHW programs is our best bet for accelerating progress in achieving Universal Health Coverage and Health for All sooner rather than later.

title: Cancer and Hypertension: Shared Mechanisms, Treatment Interactions, and Clinical Management.
abstract: Cancer and hypertension (HTN) frequently coexist, and their relationship is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant intersection between oncology and cardiovascular medicine. However, the extent to which this association reflects shared risk factors, common biological mechanisms, or treatment-related effects remains incompletely understood. In this narrative review, we focus specifically on the cancer-HTN interface and summarize epidemiological evidence while considering the potential influence of age, obesity, metabolic syndrome, dietary patterns, and psychosocial factors. We further discuss overlapping mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activation, calcium signaling abnormalities, activation of the sympathetic nervous system, metabolic dysregulation, dysbiosis of the gut microbiota and genetic and epigenetic alterations. Particular attention is given to the bidirectional interactions between cancer therapies and HTN, as well as the heterogeneous evidence concerning potential associations between antihypertensive medications and cancer outcomes. We also summarize the clinical assessment and management of cancer therapy-related HTN, including Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grading, blood pressure monitoring, cardiovascular risk assessment, and current recommendations from the European Society of Hypertension (ESH) and American Heart Association. Emerging issues, including immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cardiovascular toxicity, the potential role of cardiac biomarkers such as troponin and natriuretic peptides, and the prognostic significance of treatment-induced HTN across different tumor types, are also discussed. Overall, the available evidence supports an important clinical interplay between cancer and HTN but does not establish a uniform causal relationship. Future prospective studies integrating tumor biology, cardiovascular risk factors, treatment exposure, and longitudinal blood pressure (BP) assessment are needed to clarify these interactions and improve individualized cardio-oncology care.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare in Cambodia: Enhancing Access and Patient Outcomes.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping healthcare globally and may offer opportunities to strengthen health systems in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Cambodia. AI-enabled technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, predictive analytics, computer vision, wearable devices, and generative AI, could help address persistent health-system challenges such as shortages and maldistribution of healthcare professionals, limited specialist services, unequal access to care, and constrained resources, particularly in rural and underserved communities. However, translating these technological opportunities into meaningful health benefits requires more than access to AI tools. Cambodia faces important barriers related to digital infrastructure, health-information systems, data quality and availability, workforce capacity, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, affordability, and regulatory and ethical governance. At the same time, ongoing digital transformation, the expansion of electronic health information systems, emerging AI research capacity, and national efforts toward AI governance provide an evolving foundation for responsible adoption. This perspective examines the current and potential role of AI in Cambodia's healthcare system, focusing on applications in disease diagnosis, clinical decision support, telemedicine, public health surveillance, healthcare administration, and health-system management. Particular attention is given to the gap between technological feasibility and sustainable health-system implementation, including local validation, interoperability, economic evaluation, workforce preparedness, and long-term financing. AI should therefore be introduced through a phased, evidence-based, and patient-centered approach in which technology complements rather than replaces healthcare professionals. Investments in digital infrastructure, human capacity, locally relevant research, ethical governance, and sustainable implementation will be essential to ensure that AI contributes to improved healthcare access, quality, equity, and patient outcomes in Cambodia.

title: Retatrutide as a Unimolecular GIP/GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Tri-Agonist: Molecular Design, Pharmaceutical Development and Critical Interpretation of Emerging Phase 3 Evidence.
abstract: Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational, once-weekly, lipidated 39-residue peptide that activates the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors. Its molecular design combines incretin activity with glucagon receptor engagement while maintaining glycaemic efficacy. This critical narrative review examines molecular engineering, pharmacokinetics, dose escalation, pharmaceutical development, and clinical evidence available through 11 September 2026. Five phase 3 trials have reported positive primary outcomes, but only TRANSCEND-T2D-1 has a full peer-reviewed report; the obesity trials are currently available as sponsor topline disclosures. In those disclosures, efficacy-estimand mean weight reductions of 28.3% at 80 weeks (TRIUMPH-1) and 28.7% at 68 weeks (TRIUMPH-4) were reported, with a TRIUMPH-1 treatment-regimen estimate of 25.0%; these values remain provisional pending full published trial reports. The peer-reviewed TRANSCEND-T2D-1 report supports glycaemic efficacy in early type 2 diabetes. Interpretation requires attention to estimands, population differences, treatment discontinuation and selection into trial extensions. Gastrointestinal adverse events, dysaesthesia, heart-rate changes and the functional consequences of lean-mass loss require further evaluation. Pharmaceutical priorities include scalable synthesis, impurity and potency control, formulation stability, immunogenicity and reliable dose delivery. Retatrutide provides a clinically advanced example of unimolecular poly-agonism, but comparative effectiveness, long-term outcomes and regulatory review remain essential to defining its therapeutic role.

title: Fruquintinib: Mechanism of Action, Clinical, and Translational Science.
abstract: Fruquintinib is a highly selective, oral inhibitor of all three vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (-1, -2, and -3) that was approved, including in China, the United States, and the European Union, for the treatment of previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). The efficacy of fruquintinib for mCRC has been consistently demonstrated in randomized, double-blind, Phase 3 clinical studies, including FRESCO (NCT02314819), which enrolled patients in China, and FRESCO-2 (NCT04322539), which enrolled patients across 14 countries in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. In both studies, patients were randomized 2:1 to receive oral fruquintinib 5 mg or a matching placebo once daily, 3 weeks on, 1 week off, in 28-day cycles, plus best supportive care, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Both FRESCO and FRESCO-2 met their primary endpoints, demonstrating significant improvements in overall survival (OS) with fruquintinib versus placebo: in FRESCO (fruquintinib: n = 278; placebo: n = 138), median OS was 9.3 with fruquintinib versus 6.6 months with placebo (hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51-0.83; p < 0.001); in FRESCO-2 (fruquintinib: n = 461; placebo: n = 230), median OS was 7.4 with fruquintinib versus 4.8 months with placebo (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55-0.80; p < 0.001). The most common any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events with fruquintinib (incidence ≥ 20% in either study, excluding laboratory abnormalities) were hypertension, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, proteinuria, dysphonia, diarrhea, asthenia, decreased appetite, hypothyroidism, and fatigue. This mini-review summarizes the mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, key clinical trials, and clinical efficacy and safety data for fruquintinib.

title: Synthetic gatekeeping in health chatbots: configured answer systems as the unit of AI evaluation and governance for medical information.
abstract: Two health chatbots can give the same clinically appropriate advice and still constitute different interventions: one stops at a clinician referral, the other places an affiliated booking one click away. In this Hypothesis and Theory article we argue that the appropriate unit of health-AI evaluation is therefore not the model output alone, but the configured answer system - the large language model (LLM) together with source selection, retrieval, interface, action routing and downstream data return. We call this organizationally configured mode of mediation synthetic gatekeeping. Its necessary core comprises source selection and generative synthesis, with personalization and action routing as extending dimensions; its observable manifestations are content and pathway traces, and its proposed mechanism is infrastructural steering. Content parity does not guarantee pathway parity: two systems can name the same options while making only one easily actionable. Organizational position, revenue architecture and integration depth are treated as exposures that may shape these functions, not as elements of the construct, and owner-linked advantage is an empirical outcome to be demonstrated rather than assumed. Direct health evidence of owner- or revenue-linked steering remains sparse, and one comparative study found LLM answers less commercially biased than conventional search; the mechanisms nonetheless appear in adjacent domains, and health outputs are configurable at deployment level. We advance three core propositions - organizational alignment (P1), pathway asymmetry (P2) and behavioural mediation (P4) - with one conditional moderator hypothesis on conversion-linked funding (P3) and a measurement corollary on surface-pathway divergence (M1), each stated with its weakening condition. The framework yields a practical audit model based on configuration anchoring, paired content-pathway comparison, organizational disclosure and proportionate governance triggers. The unit of evaluation should move from the model output to the configured answer system in which information becomes action.

title: Erdi Bazhen decoction for cancer-related fatigue due to qi and blood deficiency in prostate cancer patients receiving androgen deprivation therapy: an exploratory randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot clinical trial protocol.
abstract: Background Prostate cancer is the most common male genitourinary malignancy in China. Long-term androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) causes severe cancer-related fatigue (CRF), which impairs patients' physical function and quality of life. Currently, there is a lack of safe, long-term specific pharmacological agents for this condition in Western medicine. From the perspective of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), qi and blood deficiency is the core pathogenesis underlying the occurrence and progression of CRF. Erdi Bazhen Decoction (EBD) has shown favorable clinical effects on fatigue after ADT in routine practice, but high-quality clinical evidence remains scarce, and key parameters for large-scale confirmatory trials remain undetermined. This exploratory pilot trial aims to investigate the preliminary efficacy and safety of EBD granules for CRF in prostate cancer patients receiving ADT, and to estimate critical trial parameters including effect size, recruitment rate, adherence and dropout rate to inform the design of a future large-scale confirmatory RCT. Methods This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel pilot trial will enroll 50 eligible patients from a single hospital. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups at a 1:1 ratio. Both groups will receive routine supportive care for 4 weeks. The intervention group will receive EBD granules, and the control group will receive matched placebo granules. The primary exploratory efficacy endpoint is the change in total score of the revised Piper Fatigue Scale (PFS-R) from baseline to week 4. Secondary outcomes include quality of life, physical performance and TCM syndrome scores; hemoglobin and C-reactive protein levels will be assessed as exploratory biomarkers. Trial feasibility parameters such as recruitment rate, medication adherence and dropout rate will also be descriptively analyzed to inform future trial design. Safety indicators and adverse events will be fully recorded. Variable block randomization without stratification and full double-blinding will be implemented. The primary analysis will be conducted in the intention-to-treat population; a per-protocol analysis will be performed as a sensitivity analysis. All efficacy estimates are exploratory. This protocol was designed in accordance with the SPIRIT 2025 statement; trial results will be reported in accordance with the CONSORT 2025 statement. Conclusion This standardized pilot controlled trial will provide preliminary clinical evidence and essential methodological parameters for EBD in relieving ADT-related fatigue. The results may offer preliminary support for a safe TCM regimen to improve patients' fatigue, physical status and quality of life, and lay a methodological foundation for integrated Chinese and Western medicine management of prostate cancer-related fatigue. As an exploratory pilot study, the single-center design, small sample size and short intervention period limit the generalizability of confirmatory conclusions. Further large-scale, multi-center, long-term confirmatory trials are needed to verify the long-term effects and population applicability of EBD. Clinical trial registration https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier [ITMCTR2026001527].

title: Climate Change as a Chronic Stressor: Biological and Psychological Pathways Linking Environmental Change to Human Well-Being.
abstract: Climate-related hazards are associated with adverse mental and physical health outcomes, but exposure-specific human findings are often discussed together with general stress mechanisms without clearly distinguishing their evidentiary strength. This narrative review addresses that gap by examining climate change as a context for recurrent thermal, disaster-related, and psychosocial stress, rather than as a single measurable exposure. Evidence is organized around three interacting biological domains: neuroendocrine regulation, inflammation and oxidative stress, and neuroplasticity. Human observational studies support associations between heat, extreme events, and mental health outcomes; short-term human experiments and animal models provide mechanistic insights but do not establish a chronic biological mediation pathway from climate change to psychiatric illness. Indirect pathways include displacement, livelihood disruption, loss, and anticipatory distress. Air pollution is treated as an interacting exposure with both climate-related and independent determinants. Eco-anxiety, climate anxiety, eco-distress, and ecological grief are distinguished from diagnosable disorders, with clinical relevance assessed through functional impairment and individual context. The review's contribution is an evidence-qualified framework linking exposure timing, biological plausibility, psychosocial appraisal, and unequal adaptive capacity. Practical implications include contextual mental health assessment, continuity of psychiatric care during heat and disasters, and incorporation of psychosocial support into adaptation planning. The proposed framework remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective testing with repeated exposure, biomarker, and clinical assessments.

title: Actions, recommendations, and public policy solutions for the management of dermatological diseases in Latin America: a systematic review.
abstract: Introduction Dermatological diseases impose a substantial health burden and contribute to health inequalities across Latin America. However, data regarding regional public policies has not been systematically synthesized, limiting the identification of approaches, gaps, and best practices. Objective To conduct a systematic review aimed at synthesizing the available literature and documents on public policy actions, recommendations, and solutions related to dermatological diseases in Latin America. Methods Electronic databases and official government websites were searched. Documents published in Spanish, English, and Portuguese between 2015 and 2026 were included. When applicable, methodological quality was assessed according to study design. Data were narratively synthesized according to the identified groups of dermatological conditions. Programs or policies, implementation characteristics, and reported outcomes were described. Results After screening 6,533 references identified through database searches, 74 scientific studies were included; additionally, the grey literature search identified 140 eligible documents. The analyzed documents on public policy solutions primarily focused on infectious diseases and neglected tropical diseases, particularly leprosy (15.4%) and leishmaniasis (11.2%), with most documents originating from Brazil (24.3%). The main actions identified included vaccination programs, early detection and transmission control strategies, strengthening of health surveillance and information systems, diagnostic decentralization, teledermatology, workforce training, implementation of guidelines and protocols, and community-based and intersectoral interventions. Implementation faced structural barriers such as territorial inequalities, limited problem-solving capacity at the primary care level, shortage of specialists, and weaknesses in health information systems. Implementation could potentially be facilitated through the integration of technological innovation, strengthening of primary care, community participation, and intersectoral approaches incorporating the social determinants of health. Conclusion In Latin America, public policies in dermatology have primarily focused on disease control and reducing access gaps, with greater emphasis on infectious and neglected tropical diseases. The persistence of structural inequalities and the limited availability of data onchronic dermatological conditions highlight the need for more comprehensive, context-specific, and sustainable responses aimed at strengthening health systems and reducing inequities in dermatological care across the region. Systematic review registration CRD420261322767 https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261322767.

title: Nano-/Nanobiotechnology-Augmented Pyroptosis in the Treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: An Updated Review.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), a breast cancer subset defined by the absence of estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 expression, faces persistent clinical challenges including narrow first-line treatment choices and inferior long-term survival rates. Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed clinical management across multiple malignancies, yet unselected TNBC patients exhibit only modest and heterogeneous clinical responses. This therapeutic resistance is primarily attributed to an immune-excluded tumor microenvironment (TME) with suppressed anti-tumor immunity, the hallmark of the so-called immunologically "cold" tumor phenotype. Pyroptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death characterized by asdermin-mediated membrane pore formation and pro-inflammatory mediator secretion, triggers potent tumor immunogenic cell death and reverses the immunosuppressive TME state. Rationally designed nanoscale delivery vehicles enable tumor-localized delivery of pyroptosis agonists, minimizing off-target activation in normal tissues; this targeted induction boosts intratumoral cytotoxic CD8 + T cell infiltration, drives the immunophenotypic shift from "cold" to "hot" tumors in TNBC, and ultimately sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. This review catalogs and contextualizes current preclinical progress on pyroptosis-triggering biomaterials for TNBC intervention, organized around three interconnected themes: design rationales for diverse nanoplatforms, molecular cascades of canonical and non-canonical pyroptosis signaling, and the immune-sensitizing roles of nanomediated pyroptosis in TNBC. Furthermore, this work highlights underaddressed translational barriers in the field: the mismatch between tumor tissue accumulation and intracellular pyroptosis activation efficiency, the lack of precise spatiotemporal control over pyroptotic magnitude, and the unmitigated risk of systemic inflammatory adverse events. Addressing these remaining knowledge gaps in the field, this review defines core priority research directions, namely subcellular-targeted delivery platforms, switchable pyroptosis modulation strategies, and combined therapeutic modalities that exert synergistic anti-tumor effects. Overall, this work establishes a structured, translational pathway for advancing pyroptosis-based nanotherapeutic strategies and improving clinical immunotherapy outcomes in patients with TNBC.

title: Strengthening post-market COVID-19 vaccine safety surveillance and research: An interpretive description study from Kenya, South Africa, and Canada.
abstract: Post-market vaccine safety surveillance and research are essential to detect and evaluate rare adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) not identified in pre-licensure clinical trials, such as myocarditis post-COVID-19 vaccination. AEFI surveillance infrastructure varies between jurisdictions. Factors that enable or hinder vaccine safety evaluation across diverse settings are not well understood. The study objective was to examine clinical, social, and structural/system factors that enable AEFI case identification, reporting, data and biosample collection in high-income countries (HICs) and low-and middle-income countries (LMICs). We conducted a qualitative study informed by Interpretive Description in Kenya, South Africa, and Canada. Three participant groups were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling: (1) key informants with leadership roles in AEFI surveillance and research, (2) healthcare workers, research and laboratory staff involved in vaccine safety evaluation, and (3) past participants in COVID-19 vaccine safety studies. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis was conducted. Eighteen key informants, 37 healthcare workers and research staff, and 27 past research participants were enrolled. Facilitators and barriers were identified across two domains: AEFI surveillance and investigation, and vaccine safety research participation. AEFI surveillance and investigation were shaped by trust in system responsiveness, beliefs and awareness around AEFI reporting, digital innovation, and implementation gaps. Research participation was shaped by altruism and social influence, logistics and research infrastructure, and institutional policies and privacy. Facilitators for AEFI surveillance and research included established policies and procedures for surveillance, digital tools, empathic communication about AEFIs, and convenient research processes. Barriers included limitations in workforce capacity, diagnostic testing and funding (especially in LMICs), and cumbersome research approval processes. Findings underscore the need for globally harmonized standards and locally tailored strategies to support AEFI surveillance and research in LMICs and HICs that are patient/participant-centered and include sustainable investments in infrastructure and workforce capacity.

title: Artificial intelligence for medication recognition and safety: a systematic review of detection, classification, OCR, and digital health applications.
abstract: Introduction Medication errors and adverse drug events remain causes of patient harm, underscoring the need for technologies supporting medication identification, verification, and medication safety. Artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, optical character recognition (OCR), and digital health technologies are applied to medication recognition. Objective To systematically review AI-based medication recognition systems and characterize recognition tasks, computational approaches, datasets, evaluation, validation, generalizability, deployment, applications, and emerging directions. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed/MEDLINE were searched for publications from 1 January 2016 to 4 September 2026, using two conceptual blocks covering medication recognition and AI methods. Of 895 retrieved records, 136 duplicates were removed, and 759 records underwent screening. After full-text assessment, 14 reports were excluded, and 91 studies were included. Title-and-abstract screening yielded 84.72% observed agreement (Cohen's κ=0.527 ). For methodological assessment, both reviewers independently applied D1-D8 to the 91 included studies before consensus resolution. Across 728 domain-level assessments, observed agreement was 97.66%, with an aggregate Cohen's κ of 0.959; domain-specific κ values ranged from 0.857 to 1.000. Evidence was synthesized through cross-study analysis and four evidence maps. Results Evidence shows use of detection, classification, OCR/imprint recognition, hybrid and multimodal architectures, alongside few-shot, low-shot, zero-shot, and incremental learning. Applications extend to assistive, mobile, and IoT-enabled systems, medication verification, and clinical decision support. Heterogeneity in datasets, imaging conditions, evaluation protocols, and validation strategies limits comparison and generalizability. External validation, cross-dataset testing, unseen-medication evaluation, prospective deployment, and clinical testing remain limited. Conclusion AI-based medication recognition is evolving from a computer vision task into a digital informatics component supporting medication safety, accessibility, verification, and patient care. Future research should prioritize diverse datasets, leakage control, independent multicenter validation, unseen-medication evaluation, explainable and privacy-preserving AI, interoperability, and resource-efficient deployment. Evaluation should extend beyond accuracy to clinical utility, safety, usability, trust, and patient-centered outcomes.

title: Immune checkpoints: cross-disease insights and clinical dilemmas.
abstract: The immune checkpoints and their inhibitors are revolutionary advances in tumour immunotherapy. Immune checkpoints, however, have a broad spectrum effect. They not only contribute to tumour immune escape, but also are involved in the regulation of the pathopathological processes of numerous inflammatory illnesses, such as sepsis, autoimmune diseases, organ transplant rejection, and viral infections, among others. Today, a considerable gap in knowledge remains regarding immune checkpoints and immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-tumour inflammatory diseases, which remains largely unaddressed. At the same time, the emergence of immune-related adverse events and resistance challenges related to the clinical use of immune checkpoint inhibitors is becoming increasingly prominent, posing a significant obstacle to their application across various diseases. To overcome such issues, this narrative review establishes a systematic framework that links immune checkpoints to various inflammatory diseases and explores the associated therapeutic and clinical challenges. These diseases pose therapeutic and clinical challenges of immune checkpoint inhibitors, which we explore. The paper not only thoroughly describes the clinical picture, pathophysiology, and interventions in immunologic adverse events but also suggests a prospective strategy to confront the existing problems with immune checkpoint inhibitors in 3 dimensions: evaluation, management, and prevention. It will attempt to present a new conceptual framework for a comprehensive understanding of the dual role of immune checkpoints (in maintaining immune homeostasis and facilitating disease progression) and to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of safer and more effective cross-disease immunotherapy.

title: Barriers and Priorities for Strengthening Prehospital Trauma Care in Hawassa, Ethiopia.
A review of radiotherapy linear accelerator quality control techniques.
abstract: This study provides a review of recent publications on different quality control (QC) techniques for radiotherapy linear accelerators (linacs). QC in radiotherapy is essential to ensure patient safety, deliver optimal quality treatments, monitor equipment performance over time, and to satisfy statutory or recommended testing. While conventional QC methods are still widely used and valuable, there have been advances in QC methods and approaches which aim to improve efficiency and keep pace with the rapidly advancing complexity of clinical equipment and treatment delivery methods. Existing reviews of QC concepts mainly focus on single QC techniques. There are limited reviews that explore and compare the variety of techniques to QC, which is the aim of this report. QC techniques were separated into 7 domains: conventional QC, automated and manufacturer integrated QC, risk, statistical, artificial intelligence (AI), end-to-end and patient-specific QC (PSQC), external dosimetry audits and clinical trial credentialing audits. An overview of each technique with example studies from literature is presented.

title: Health systems and climate change mitigation through an applied health informatics and sustainability perspective.
abstract: Climate change poses a growing threat to U.S. healthcare systems, which are uniquely positioned to mitigate its impacts while addressing their own greenhouse gas emissions from energy use, supply chains, clinical operations, and waste. Clinical informaticists can advance mitigation by integrating environmental data into health system operations and decision-making. Tracking emissions across scopes enables data-informed strategies, while frameworks such as I-CLIMATE and One Digital Health can help coordinate disparate data streams and reduce healthcare's environmental impact. Integrated dashboards can support renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, and operational decision-making, while telehealth can reduce transportation-related emissions. Artificial intelligence may also reduce resource use when applied judiciously through narrowly scoped, task-specific models, with frameworks such as SAHAI guiding sustainable implementation. Financial approaches such as New York University's Return on Sustainability Investment framework can quantify the financial value of decarbonization initiatives. Effective governance, including vertical alignment and horizontal integration, is essential to operationalizing these strategies. Emerging opportunities include climate-conscious hardware design and carbon accounting applications. Ultimately, informatics can provide the data, tools, and governance infrastructure needed to translate climate mitigation goals into measurable health system action and establish carbon neutrality as an organizational performance priority.

title: Spatio-temporally modulated fluorescence imager for intraoperative nerve identification.
abstract: Significance Fluorescence-guided surgery (FGS) based on nerve-labeling agents has the potential to enhance nerve identification during various operational procedures including orthopedic, craniofacial, and otolaryngological surgeries that involve complex and delicate nerve structures. A major challenge in FGS is the adverse impact of strong ambient light, which interferes with weak fluorescence signals, especially at visible wavelengths. Currently, this issue is mitigated by dimming or turning off the operating room (OR) lights during the fluorescence imaging procedure. However, this causes substantial disruption to the surgical workflow and reduces the potential for clinical adoption of FGS technologies. Aim In this work, we develop a novel intraoperative fluorescence imager that is based on a spatio-temporal modulation (STM) approach to suppress interference from strong OR lights. Approach The STM technology employed a line-scan imaging scheme that encodes the fluorescence signal into a distinctive spatial frequency within a narrow time window. By applying spatial frequency demodulation and time-gating methods, the imager effectively extracted the fluorescence signals by rejecting temporally constant and spatially uniform background OR lights. Results The performance of the imager in detecting nerve structures in realistic OR lighting conditions was validated during in vivo animal studies. Additional evaluation using ex vivo human nerve tissue specimens and perfused amputated human limbs further supported the clinical suitability and readiness. Conclusions This innovative imaging technology enables high-contrast fluorescence visualization of nerve tissue under standard OR lighting and represents a significant step toward practical clinical implementation of FGS for enhanced nerve identification.

title: A Novel Informatics-Driven Model for Proactive Radiation Safety Management: Lessons from a Tumor Specialist Hospital in China.
abstract: Background Tumor hospitals face intensive radiation equipment, large radiation worker groups, and inefficient paper-based radiation safety management. Suitable and targeted informatization solutions are lacking in Southwest China. Methods Based on a tertiary tumor hospital in Southwest China, we designed, implemented, and evaluated a full-process informatized radiation safety management system with requirement analysis, functional module design, and real-world application assessment. Results After system implementation, the personal dose monitoring rate increased from 95% to 99%, training completion rate rose from 70% to 99%, occupational health examination implementation rate improved from 80% to 90%, and new project approval time was shortened from a typical range of 30-60 days to approximately 15 days. Conclusion This informatics-driven proactive radiation safety model improved institutional management efficiency, standardization, and risk control. It offers a replicable scheme for regional radiation protection informatization and public health security. Trial registration Not applicable.

title: Beyond Resource Expansion: Building Resilient Hospital Surge Capacity for Sustained Crisis Response.
abstract: Background: Hospital surge-capacity assessment has traditionally emphasized the expansion of beds, staff, equipment, and medical supplies, but provides limited insight into how these resources are transformed into sustained operational capabilities under uncertainty. This study develops a resilience-oriented function-capability framework to assess hospital surge capacity from a systems perspective. Methods: Hospital surge capacity theory and hospital resilience theory were integrated to define 5 capability dimensions: functional reconfiguration, resource configuration, operational continuity, regional coordination, and collaborative optimization.
