FRAM was used to model 24 operational functions and their couplings under 4 synthesized surge scenarios. An improved K-shell algorithm quantified structural importance, while Monte Carlo derived functional-performance uncertainty was represented by truncated-normal prior distributions. Bayesian network was then used for performance assessment, propagation, sensitivity, and robustness analyses. Results: The estimated overall surge-capacity performance was 0.5479, 0.5631, 0.5723, and 0.5867 for S 1 - S 4 , respectively. Influential functional nodes differed across scenarios, whereas operational continuity capability consistently showed the greatest sensitivity to overall performance. Cumulative 50% degradation of structurally important functions reduced overall surge capacity by 23.54%, 16.91%, 20.51%, and 19.75% in S 1 - S 4 , respectively. Robustness analyses showed that the main scenario ordering and principal influential nodes remained generally stable under alternative modeling assumptions. Conclusions: Hospital surge capacity depends not only on resource availability but also on the coordinated performance of interconnected operational functions. The proposed FRAM-K-shell-BN framework separates structural importance from functional-performance uncertainty and links function level variability to capability level and overall system performance, providing a structured approach for assessing hospital surge capacity under uncertain emergency conditions.

title: Semiconductor Technologies for Predictive, Preventive, and Personalized Healthcare.
abstract: Purpose This narrative review investigated how semiconductor technologies contribute to predictive, preventive, and personalized healthcare and considered their clinical value, technological maturity, and implementation challenges. Methods A structured narrative-review search of literature published from January 2015 through August 2026 was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect. Eligible publications had to describe a semiconductor-based technology with a clear or potential healthcare application related to prediction, prevention, personalization, diagnosis, monitoring, or therapeutic decision-making. Forty-seven publications met the eligibility criteria and were critically appraised and synthesized thematically. Results The evidence set included 47 publications published from 2016 to 2026. Major technology categories included wearable and flexible physiological sensors, biosensors and lab-on-chip systems, implantable devices, complementary metal oxide semiconductors and application-specific integrated-circuit platforms, edge processing hardware, and semiconductor imaging detectors. Across the evidence, semiconductor platforms supported continuous physiological monitoring, rapid biochemical and molecular detection, early risk identification, individualized treatment management, and local processing of health data. Signal instability, calibration drift, limited external validation, power constraints, biocompatibility, interoperability, cybersecurity, affordability, algorithmic bias, and unequal access remained important barriers. Conclusion Semiconductor technologies can strengthen predictive, preventive, and personalized healthcare, but technical performance alone is insufficient. Near-term translation is strongest for established sensing, imaging, and implantable platforms linked to defined care pathways, whereas flexible biochemical sensors and in-sensor computing platforms require stronger clinical validation. Wider adoption requires representative validation, long-term safety evidence, interoperable systems, equitable design, clear regulation, sustainable lifecycle planning, and demonstrated improvements in patient outcomes.

title: Assessing digital factors influencing AI-led asset information management in hospital facilities.
abstract: Purpose This study examines the digital factors influencing AI-led Asset Information Management (AIM) in hospital facilities. The study focuses on the extent to which digital factors related to data governance, operational efficiency, resource optimisation, and predictive capabilities are perceived to be present in healthcare facilities. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered to relevant professionals involved in hospital asset management. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics in SPSS, including mean scores, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis to evaluate the distribution and significance of responses. Reliability testing was conducted, yielding a high Cronbach's Alpha value of 0.95, confirming strong internal consistency of the measurement instrument. Findings A two-factor structure of digital factors was identified through an exploratory factor analysis. Although the statistical evidence points to a dominant one-factor structure, the two-factor solution was retained on theoretical grounds. Respondents rated foundational digital services, particularly access control and security protocols, mostly highly. One-way ANOVA comparing item-level mean scores across six groups of professionally experienced individuals showed no statistically significant differences. Suggesting that perceptions of these digital factors do not vary meaningfully by years of professional experience in this sample. Practical implications The study highlights the need for healthcare institutions to invest in digital infrastructure, data integration, and capacity development to leverage AI capabilities fully. Emphasis should be placed on transitioning from basic automation toward predictive and intelligent asset management systems. Originality/value This study provides empirical evidence on the layered adoption of AI in hospital asset management, demonstrating that current implementations are largely efficiency- and security-driven, while advanced predictive capabilities remain underdeveloped. It contributes to the growing body of knowledge by identifying a critical gap between AI potential and its practical realisation in healthcare infrastructure.

title: Protecting the invisible health workforce: experiences and occupational safety challenges of facial protective equipment use among central sterile supply department workers.
abstract: Background Central sterile supply department (CSSD) personnel may be exposed to blood, body fluids, splashes, and aerosols while reprocessing contaminated medical devices. Evidence remains limited on how CSSD personnel experience facial personal protective equipment (facial PPE) during routine work and what shapes their reported protective practices. This study explored CSSD personnel's experiences of facial PPE use and the factors they perceived as influencing these practices. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted from January to February 2026 in the CSSD of a tertiary hospital in Chongqing, China. Purposive sampling was used to recruit frontline personnel who had worked in the CSSD for at least 1 year and routinely used facial PPE. Data collection ceased after two consecutive interviews produced no new themes. Individual semi-structured interviews lasting 30-45 min were audio-recorded and transcribed. Data were analyzed using an inductive thematic approach with NVivo 12. Two researchers independently reviewed and coded the transcripts, compared their interpretations, and developed and refined the themes through discussion. Results Twenty CSSD personnel participated in the study. Six themes were identified: ① perceptions of facial protection as a means of safeguarding personnel, medical devices, patients, and others; ② protective decisions shaped by perceived risk, work context, comfort, and emergency conditions; ③ policies, multilevel training, supervision, and peer feedback supporting standardized facial protection; ④ discomfort, poor fit, fogging, and communication difficulties associated with facial PPE; ⑤ the influence of heat, inadequate ventilation, repetitive workflow, and prolonged continuous work on sustained use; and ⑥ differences in risk perception, workplace relationships, and passive responses to mandatory requirements. Participants recognized the value of facial protection, but reported facial PPE practices were shaped by the interaction between equipment characteristics, physical working conditions, organizational arrangements, and interpersonal dynamics. Conclusion Participants' reported facial PPE practices reflected the interaction of perceived risk, equipment usability, working conditions, workflow, institutional support, and workplace relationships. The findings suggest that task-based protective requirements, well-fitting and tolerable equipment, practical training, supportive feedback, and environmental and workflow adjustments may support appropriate and sustained facial PPE use in CSSDs.

title: Strengthening patient safety through biosafety and infection prevention measures during COVID-19: a policy and practice review
A deep learning model for detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head on x-ray images: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study in China.
Designing a hybrid surgical ICU to avoid intrahospital transport in selected critically Ill patients: the CUHK-SZ institutional concept.
journal: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
abstract: Background Intrahospital transport for surgery exposes critically ill patients to equipment failure, displacement of tubes and lines, interrupted monitoring, and physiologic instability. Although transport protocols can reduce these hazards, they do not address the underlying physical decoupling of surgical infrastructure from the critical care environment. Objective This institutional perspective describes the rationale and design of a hybrid surgical ICU planned for the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-SZ) Medical Center: a dedicated clinical space designed to function as both a critical care unit and a procedural suite, bringing surgery to the patient rather than transporting the patient to the operating room (OR). The model is presented as an illustrative, hypothesis-generating concept rather than a validated clinical pathway. Design concept The design concept, which is a patient-centered approach, should guide healthcare delivery in modern medicine by placing the patient at the forefront of all decisions and mobilizing all available resources to serve them. This approach addresses all three domains: personnel, environment, and equipment. Overlapping anesthesiology and critical care competencies support integrated staffing. Connectable ICU rooms, adequate space and electrical capacity, anterooms, and switchable HEPA-filtered positive-pressure ventilation meet environmental requirements. Total intravenous anesthesia, portable surgical platforms, and minimally invasive or robotic techniques reduce dependence on fixed OR infrastructure. At CUHK-SZ, the concept is planned as a prototype in the trauma building using two adjacent ICU rooms with an openable partition and switchable ventilation. Candidate patient groups, procedural levels, and implementation requirements are presented as provisional, expert-derived proposals, and engineering testing and simulated drills are planned before any clinical use. Conclusions The hybrid surgical ICU is a technically plausible option for carefully selected patients at high risk from transport, but its clinical effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness remain unproven. The CUHK-SZ concept is intended to generate hypotheses for prospective evaluation, and its transferability to existing hospitals is likely to depend on incremental adaptation rather than direct replication.

title: Subpicogram-Level Quantification of Trace Biomarkers Using an Automated High-Sensitivity Chemiluminescence Immunoassay Technology Based on a Novel Substrate Enhancement Strategy.
A passive thin-film mechanical device for visual respiratory monitoring during oxygen mask use: development and bench validation.
abstract: Continuous respiratory monitoring during transfer from the operating theatre to the post-anaesthesia care unit is frequently unavailable despite this being a period of recognised patient vulnerability. Existing electronic respiratory monitors introduce cost, complexity and set-up that may limit use in fast-paced clinical environments. We developed Flow-Bag, a fully passive mechanical breath-indicating device consisting of a thin heat-sealed high-density polyethylene film bag that attaches externally to an oxygen mask. Preliminary film-thickness screening was undertaken using a programmable breathing simulator (PEMDx Pty Ltd, Australia). A 6 µ m (per ply) prototype was assessed across respiratory rates (RRs) of 5-60 breaths min -1 and tidal volumes of 50-600 ml. Three blinded observers positioned 5 m from the device counted visible inflation-deflation cycles over 60 s intervals, with counts compared against simulator-delivered breaths. Performance was additionally assessed across four commercially available oxygen mask models. In screening, the lowest detected tidal volume fell from 400 ml with 20 µ m film to 150 ml with 6 µ m film, the thinnest film that could be reproducibly manufactured using the processes available to us. The final prototype produced observable breath indications in 42 of 56 tested conditions (all tidal volumes ⩾150 ml) but not at 50 or 100 ml. Within these detectable conditions, observer counts agreed 100% with simulator-delivered breaths. Performance was maintained across four oxygen mask models. However, sensitivity was reduced by incomplete sealing at either the mask-to-face or device-to-mask interface. Flow-Bag is a fully passive mechanical breath indicator. Under controlled bench conditions using a mechanical breathing simulator, it provided reliable visual indication of simulated breathing across RRs of 5-60 breaths min -1 and tidal volumes of 150-600 ml. Subject to clinical validation and safety testing, this device may offer a potentially low-cost adjunct alongside standard monitoring.

title: Reducing Peripheral Intravenous Catheter Use in Adult Acute Care: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVCs) are the most frequently inserted invasive device in acute care, yet up to 52% remain unused, exposing patients to avoidable risks and increasing healthcare costs. Despite growing awareness of inappropriate PIVC use, unnecessary insertion persists, driven by cultural and organisational norms and risk-averse practices. Interventions to reduce PIVC use have been implemented, but their effectiveness and sustainability have not been systematically synthesised. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251033201). Searches of CINAHL, MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies reporting interventions to reduce PIVC insertion, unused PIVCs, and common complications. Data were extracted for intervention characteristics and PIVC outcomes. Implementation strategies were mapped to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research domains for summative analysis. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when appropriate. Twelve studies were included from emergency departments and inpatient settings across high-income countries. Most reported reductions in PIVC insertion and unused catheters, with improvements in secondary outcomes including phlebitis and bloodstream infections. Sustainability of practice change was demonstrated in two multi-year follow-up studies. Interventions showed a significant trend for increasing complexity over time, with recent strategies incorporating multi-modal, theory-informed approaches. Meta-analysis showed substantial heterogeneity, limiting pooled estimate interpretation, while methodological limitations restricted causal inference. Multi-modal interventions addressing behavioural, organisational, and contextual determinants appear most effective for reducing PIVC insertion rates and unnecessary PIVC use. Future research should evaluate sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and scalability using implementation science frameworks.

title: Global stakeholder preferences for point-of-care HIV nucleic acid amplification tests: A conjoint study.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to assess global stakeholder preferences for key attributes of point-of-care (POC) HIV Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAAT), with the aim of informing product development to support progress toward UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. Methods A web-based conjoint survey was conducted in August through November 2024 among HIV clinicians, laboratory professionals, and researchers. Participants were asked to evaluate hypothetical POC HIV NAAT profiles varying by six attributes: sensitivity / limit of detection (LOD), sample-collection method, turnaround time (TAT), result format, price, and power source. Relative importance and part-worth utilities were calculated to assess trade-offs in decision-making. Results One hundred three respondents from 33 countries, primarily in Africa (75%), completed the survey. The relative importance placed on the attributes in the conjoint task varied based on the setting. In community and home-based settings, participants prioritized fingerstick sample collection (25.90%) and faster TATs (28.8%), even at the expense of sensitivity (15.70%). By contrast, respondents from hospitals and health centers valued tests with high sensitivity (42.6%, 40.9%) and faster TATs (31.5%, 22.6%). Across all respondents, price (7.0%), result format (3.30%), and power source (7.25%) were less influential. Conclusions Stakeholders were willing to make trade-offs among desirable attributes, prioritizing rapid turnaround time, strong sensitivity, and fingerstick sampling over affordability, power requirements, and result format in the conjoint task. These preferences vary by level of care and by use case, underscoring the importance of aligning product features with contextual needs. Engaging stakeholders early in the design process is critical to ensure new POC HIV NAAT technologies are both acceptable and scalable in low-resource settings.

title: First-in-human evaluation of real-time pixel-level AI-assisted anatomical segmentation in neurosurgery: pituitary surgery as an exemplar.
abstract: Introduction Precise anatomical navigation is fundamental to safe endoscopic pituitary surgery, a high-stakes procedure characterised by a challenging learning curve. While traditional navigation systems often rely on workflow-disrupting probes or static preoperative imaging, advancements in computer vision AI (CVAI) now enable dynamic, real-time pixel-level anatomical segmentation directly from live surgical video. Our group has previously conducted a series of preclinical human-computer interaction studies to refine the system's design, alongside digital and high-fidelity physical simulations demonstrating the potential benefit of AI assistance in improving surgical performance, training, and safety. Building on this foundation, the current study represents a first-in-human evaluation of real-time pixel-level CVAI anatomical segmentation in the neurosurgical operating room - assessing feasibility, human factors and clinical outcomes, while iteratively improving the system. Method Guided by the DECIDE-AI and IDEAL frameworks, this single-centre evaluation comprises an initial proof-of-concept of CVAI anatomical segmentation in endoscopic transsphenoidal pituitary surgery. The AI model utilised a DINOv3-derived vision transformer architecture, deployed via a high-performance edge computing unit to achieve low-latency real-time inference without reliance on cloud infrastructure. Feasibility and functionality were assessed via structured questionnaire, prospective observation, and blinded retrospective review of the recordings of the endoscopic surgical video feed and wider operating room environment. Continuous multi-stakeholder feedback through validated human factors surveys drove iterative technical refinements between cases. Routine clinical outcomes, aligning with the standard pituitary surgery core outcome set, were collected. Results Eight patients with pituitary adenomas were enrolled. The CVAI system was successfully deployed in six cases, demonstrating acceptable real-time pixel-level sella segmentation accuracy. Deployment failed pre-operatively in two cases owing to a single platform-level boot-configuration issue. Iterative refinement between cases was driven by our experience and surgical team feedback. This resulted in the integration of additional anatomical structure segmentations (e.g., carotid arteries), enhanced model accuracy via training dataset expansion, and hardware firmware upgrades. Multi-stakeholder surveys demonstrated satisfactory system feasibility, usability, and acceptability among the surgical team. Both prospective observation and retrospective video review confirmed the absence of adverse events, including no significant distraction to the primary surgeon, and there were no AI-related clinical complications. Conclusion This first-in-human early clinical evaluation (IDEAL Stage 1) of real-time pixel-level AI anatomical segmentation in live neurosurgery demonstrates feasibility, showcases iterative system evolution, and reports clinical and human factors outcomes. Future work will include a larger single-centre case series (IDEAL Stage 2a) with more surgical teams to further iterate the system and explore its impact on safety, training and workflow. As the underpinning AI models improve and integrate with other intra-operative navigational technologies, such tools will likely be the cornerstone of intra-operative surgical decision support systems.

title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy.
Patient safety culture in dental clinics: A cross-sectional study in Afghanistan.
abstract: Healthcare safety is a major global concern since unsafe and low-quality services can lead to poor health outcomes and even harm to patients. Promoting a strong patient safety culture is a prerequisite for improving patient safety. The present study aimed to assess patient safety culture in dental clinics in Herat, Afghanistan in 2024. This cross-sectional study included 210 dental team members selected by random cluster sampling from 7 regions. The assessment tool was the Medical Office Survey on Patient Safety Culture (MOSOPS) modified for use in dentistry. A pilot study confirmed content validity and reliability (Cronbach's alpha > 0.70). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests (t-tests and ANOVA), and multiple linear regression to examine associations with patient safety culture. The total patient safety culture score was (0.70 ± 0.10) (on a 0-1 scale), indicating a moderate level. The strongest mean scores were for organizational learning (0.78 ± 0.14) and teamwork (0.77 ± 0.17). The lowest score was observed for office processes and standardization (0.62 ± 0.13). Multiple linear regression revealed that being female (B = 0.031, p = 0.049) and holding a managerial position (B = 0.073, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with higher patient safety culture scores. Overall, patient safety culture was generally favorable, although important organizational gaps remain. Future improvement efforts should focus on standardizing office processes and strengthening information exchange with external healthcare providers. In resource-limited settings such as Afghanistan, feasible interventions including locally adapted protocols, and ongoing managerial support and supervision may further strengthen patient safety culture.

title: Acceptability of Wearable Digital Devices for Remote Continuous Mobility Monitoring in People With Parkinson Disease and Carers: Qualitative Study.
abstract: Background Parkinson disease (PD) impairs mobility and motor function, making accurate mobility assessment important for effective management and treatment planning. Traditional clinical assessments often rely on periodic clinical evaluations, which may not capture day-to-day symptom fluctuations. Wearable devices offer a promising alternative with continuous, objective tracking of mobility (eg, gait). However, although these tools provide valuable insights for patients and clinicians, their successful implementation depends on their acceptability to users. Objective This study aimed to explore the acceptability of wearable devices for remote continuous mobility monitoring in PD from the perspectives of people with PD and informal carers. Methods This international qualitative study used purposive sampling to recruit a diverse sample of 72 people with PD and 20 informal carers from the United Kingdom, Ireland, Belgium, Germany, Spain, and the United States. Participants were recruited between June 2023 and February 2026 through multiple community-based routes. One-to-one semistructured interviews, conducted online, via telephone, or in person, explored views on wearable devices for digital mobility assessment. Interview data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's 6-phase reflexive thematic analysis. Results Most people with PD were generally open to wearable monitoring when it could capture motor fluctuations between "on" and "off" periods that were difficult to convey during clinical appointments, reduce reliance on memory, provide objective evidence to support treatment and medication discussions and self-advocacy, and track changes in mobility over time, which some felt could be reassuring. Acceptability depended on devices having a clear purpose, requiring minimal effort, and being easy to use. Tremor, reduced dexterity, and "off" periods could make fastening straps, navigating menus, and charging devices difficult. Carers valued wearable monitoring for the reassurance and safety it offered, particularly fall detection, and for support with both clinical and everyday decision-making but emphasized that devices must operate passively and integrate into daily caregiving without adding burden. Conclusions Wearable mobility monitoring was generally acceptable to people with PD and carers when it offered clear clinical value, fit easily into everyday life, and provided reassurance that remote monitoring would complement rather than replace clinical care. As PD mobility was experienced as a shared concern within the care relationship, the value of monitoring depended on how well it supported the wider care dyad rather than the person with PD alone. These findings suggest that successful implementation will require co-design with people with PD and carers, alongside thoughtful clinical integration, to ensure that wearable technologies are both acceptable and effective in practice.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in long-term care facilities: a scoping review across planning, design, operation, and assessment.
abstract: Introduction Improving the quality of long-term care facilities (LTCFs) is critical to safeguarding the health, safety, dignity, and quality of life of older adults amid global population aging. However, traditional design methods for LTCFs rely heavily on static codes and empirical judgment, limiting their ability to respond to dynamic care needs and balance multiple objectives across lifecycle stages. To address these limitations, artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution through dynamic optimization and intelligent decision-making. Methods A scoping review was conducted to systematically map the applications of AI in LTCFs across four lifecycle stages: planning and site selection, architectural design, operation and management, and assessment and retrofit. Searches were performed in Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, SAGE Journals, and CNKI for literature published between January 2010 and December 2025, resulting in the inclusion of 38 eligible publications. The review was guided by the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. Results Four main application pathways were identified, including prediction and evaluation, generation and evolution, sensing and recognition, and simulation and modeling. Specifically, AI was applied to site-selection evaluation and demand forecasting during planning; spatial layout generation and intelligent equipment integration during design; safety monitoring, behavior recognition, and environmental control during operation; and comfort and safety assessment and retrofit optimization during assessment. Research was concentrated in operation and management, whereas evidence on assessment and retrofit remained limited. Discussion Overall, AI shows potential to shift LTCFs from static, fragmented, and experience-based practices toward more data-informed, adaptive, and person-centered care environments. However, implementation remains constrained by data quality and standardization, facility heterogeneity, system integration, equitable access, privacy, and ethical concerns. This review provides planners, architects, engineers, care providers, facility managers, and public health decision-makers with a technology roadmap and identifies priorities for using AI-enabled built environments to support high-quality older adult care and sustainable long-term care systems.

title: Effects of Dynamic Neck Sensorimotor Biofeedback Training in Individuals With Mechanical Neck Pain: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy
abstract: Mechanical neck pain (MNP) is commonly accompanied by pain-related functional limitations, sensorimotor disturbances, and fear of movement, which together may contribute to persistent disability. This preliminary randomized controlled trial study investigated the short-term effects of dynamic neck sensorimotor-based biofeedback training in individuals with MNP. 20 MNP patients from outpatient clinics were assigned to a biofeedback training group or a control group. The training group underwent dynamic biofeedback exercises twice weekly for 2 weeks, whereas the control group performed repeated cervical movements without biofeedback. Outcomes included cervical kinematics as repositioning errors (RPE), movement units (MU), maximal range of motion (ROM), and subjective measures, including pain intensity, Neck Disability Index (NDI), and Fear-Avoidance Beliefs Questionnaire (FABQ). All participants completed post-intervention assessments; adherence in the training group was 100%, with no missing data and no adverse events reported. Within the biofeedback training group, participants receiving biofeedback training demonstrated greater improvements in cervical repositioning accuracy during flexion (51.95%, p = 0.04) and extension (46.67%, p = 0.02), along with reductions in fear-avoidance beliefs related to physical activity and work (p < 0.05); these changes were less apparent in the active control group. Exploratory regression analyses suggested associations between improvements in repositioning accuracy and pain reduction, and between increased cervical range of motion and improvements in fear-avoidance beliefs related to physical activity. These pilot findings suggest that dynamic sensorimotor biofeedback training may improve proprioceptive acuity and fear-avoidance beliefs in individuals with MNP, supporting further evaluation in an adequately powered randomized trial.

title: The osteoporosis-fracture paradox in older Taiwanese men: lower osteoporosis prevalence but comparable fragility fracture burden.
abstract: Despite a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women, older men experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures, demonstrating a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fracture burden. Purpose Although osteoporosis is less common in men than in women, male fragility fractures carry substantial morbidity and post-fracture mortality. Whether the lower prevalence of osteoporosis translates into a proportionally lower fracture burden remains unclear. We compared the prevalence of osteoporosis and fragility fractures between age-matched Taiwanese men and women. Methods This retrospective cohort study evaluated 2093 men undergoing clinical dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) between 2021 and 2023, of whom 2031 met eligibility criteria and were compared with 2031 age-matched women selected via 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching. Osteoporosis was defined as a T-score ≤-2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck and/or total hip. Vertebral and hip fractures were identified from radiographs and electronic medical records. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of fracture. Results The prevalence of osteoporosis in men was approximately half that in women (32.4% vs. 51.4%; P Conclusions Older Taiwanese men exhibited a substantially lower prevalence of osteoporosis than age-matched women but experienced a relatively comparable burden of fragility fractures. These findings demonstrate a marked dissociation between osteoporosis prevalence and fragility fracture burden in older men and reinforce the importance of comprehensive fracture risk assessment integrating BMD with clinical risk factors.

title: Co-exposure to planned power outages and wildfire PM2.5 and acute healthcare utilization in California: A time-stratified case-crossover study.
abstract: Background To prevent wildfires, electric utilities may preemptively de-energize power lines (public safety power shutoffs [PSPS]). These PSPS events may unintentionally harm health, particularly for those with pre-existing conditions like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or who rely on electricity-dependent medical equipment. Health impacts may worsen further if a wildfire occurs despite the power shutoff. To assess the effect of PSPS events, wildfire fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure, and their co-occurrence on cause-specific healthcare utilization. Methods and findings We identified PSPS events in California from 2013 to 2019, categorizing magnitude based on number of people without power by zip code. We leveraged zip code-level average daily wildfire PM2.5 estimates and respiratory, COPD-specific, cardiovascular, and psychiatric emergency department visits and unscheduled hospital admissions among adults aged 20+ from the California Department of Health Care Access and Information. Using a time-stratified case-crossover design, we estimated the impact of same-day and lagged PSPS events alone, wildfire PM2.5 alone, and their co-occurrence on healthcare utilization, adjusting for daily temperature. Severe PSPS events were associated with elevated odds of same-day respiratory encounters (OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.11) and lag0-3 effects were similar. These associations were stronger for COPD. Compared to no PSPS or wildfire exposure, joint PSPS and 10 μg/m3 higher wildfire PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of respiratory encounters (1.16 [95% CI: 1.10, 1.22]), with evidence of multiplicative interaction. Associations were null for cardiovascular and psychiatric encounters. Limitations include exposure misclassification, because we assigned exposure at the residential zip code level, aggregating circuit-level data and not accounting for individual behavior or the potential for PSPS events to impact wildfire PM2.5 exposure. Conclusions PSPS events may increase risk of respiratory events requiring acute care utilization, especially when they co-occur with wildfire PM2.5.

title: Self-powered bioelectronics for peripheral nerve regeneration: Electroactive materials, energy transduction, and therapeutic mechanisms.
abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries remain difficult to treat because axonal regeneration is slow, incomplete, and highly dependent on timely biochemical, structural, and electrical cues. Self-powered electroceuticals offer an emerging route to deliver localized electrical stimulation with reduced dependence on bulky batteries and percutaneous leads. This review summarizes recent advances in self-powered bioelectronic systems for nerve repair, with emphasis on three representative platforms: self-electrified galvanic devices, triboelectric nanogenerators, and piezoelectric nanogenerators. From a materials and interfacial engineering perspective, we discuss how redox reactions, contact electrification, and piezoelectric polarization convert physiological or externally applied energy into therapeutic electrical outputs. Key design factors, including biodegradable metals, electroactive polymers, piezoelectric composites, conductive interfaces, encapsulation strategies, and nerve-guidance architectures, are critically examined in relation to output stability, degradation behavior, tissue compatibility, and regenerative efficacy. We further highlight preclinical evidence that self-powered electrical cues influence Schwann cell activity, axonal elongation, neurotrophic factor secretion, immune modulation, and downstream signaling pathways to enhance myelination, suppress muscle atrophy, and improve functional recovery. Finally, current limitations and future opportunities are discussed, including stimulation-dose standardization, degradation-byproduct management, scalable fabrication, closed-loop integration, and large-animal validation. This review provides a unified-materials-interface-device-biology framework for developing clinically translatable self-powered electroceuticals for nerve regeneration.

title: A real-time, gamified approach for optimizing intra-hospital transport of time-critical biospecimens.
abstract: Intra-hospital transport of biological specimens is a time-critical, preanalytical step. However, especially for diagnostic or scientific critical biospecimens it remains largely manual, poorly tracked, and decoupled from performance feedback. Existing solutions commonly address isolated parts of the logistics chain but fall short in engaging the personnel who perform it. Therefore, we propose a mobile-first, gamified concept for real-time specimen tracking that combines QR-based documentation with behavioral incentives. Each transport is recorded automatically through start and end scans, closing a gap in the pre-analytical record without adding documentation effort. Beyond external rewards, the concept emphasizes determinants of intrinsic motivation such as task significance to support sustainable engagement. By combining technological and behavioral optimization, this perspective outlines a strategy for time saving, transparent and efficient specimen logistics.

title: Conductive hydrogel bioelectronics for chronic neuromodulation: From biomimetic design and bioactive interfaces to integrated neural platforms.
abstract: In biomedical engineering, hydrogel bioelectronics brings together the interface between flexible electronic devices and biological systems, opening up a new way for chronic neural regulation. Here we focus on the recent progress in this field, from material design to system integration. The design of high-performance conductive hydrogels is an entry point. The multi-level structure engineering strategy, such as the introduction of carbon nanotubes or conductive polymers, can raise the conductivity and mechanical toughness together. When biomimetic adhesion molecules such as polydopamine or tannic acid are added, the hydrogel has the ability of wet tissue adhesion, and anti swelling and active anti-inflammatory functions are also embedded in the material system. As a result, the resulting neural interfaces are not only more durable in practical applications but also ensure excellent biocompatibility. Turning to applications. How does this kind of material promote the development of chronic neuromodulation technology? Peripheral nerve repair, brain computer interface, spinal cord injury, autonomic nervous system regulation can be seen in several scenes. The long-term and high-precision recording and regulation of neural signals is exactly the most important link in these applications. Hydrogel electronics does have its own uniqueness in this regard. However, there is still a long way to go between laboratory research and clinical transformation. How to ensure long-term stability? Can controllable degradation be achieved in practice? Will the signal fidelity drop with time? How to optimize wireless operation and system integration? Large scale manufacturing is an unavoidable reality test. These directions are probably the worthy areas for follow-up research. Looking forward, if the lines of intelligent response materials, closed-loop sensing and control, and advanced micro processing technology can be screwed together, hydrogel bioelectronics may truly move towards the next generation of personalized, dynamic and adaptive neural diagnosis and treatment platform.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Ocular Surface Oncology: A Narrative Review of Multimodal Imaging, Smartphone-Based Screening, and Clinical Decision Support.
abstract: Ocular surface malignancies include ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), con-junctival melanoma, and conjunctival lymphoma. These rare disorders may threaten vi-sion and, in some cases, life. Early identification may be difficult because malignant le-sions can resemble benign ocular surface conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a potential aid to detection, classi-fication, and referral. This structured narrative review, organized with reference to SANRA principles, synthesizes PubMed/MEDLINE literature on AI applications in ocular surface oncology available through 29 August 2026. We examine slit-lamp photography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, in vivo confocal microscopy, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and smartphone imaging. Deep-learning models have shown promising performance in selected binary OSSN tasks, whereas multiclass studies report lower sen-sitivity for rare malignancies such as conjunctival melanoma and lymphoma. Smartphone-based screening has also been evaluated in a prospective referral pathway, although the reference standard and verification process limit interpretation of popula-tion-level sensitivity. Dataset imbalance, image-acquisition variability, limited external and prospective validation, explainability, and workflow integration remain barriers to implementation. Future work should prioritize multicenter datasets, standardized acquisition, calibrated thresholds, and prospective human-AI evaluations. Current evidence supports further evaluation of AI as an adjunct for detection and referral, not as a re-placement for specialist assessment or histopathology.

title: The Current Status and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer: Clinical Applications and Research.
abstract: Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.

title: Molecular evidence of a dominant multidrug resistant <i>Acinetobacter baumannii</i> lineage in a tertiary hospital in northern Peru.
abstract: Background Acinetobacter baumannii is a major nosocomial pathogen because of its genomic plasticity and capacity to acquire multidrug resistance (MDR), particularly resistance to carbapenems. The World Health Organization classifies carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii as a critical-priority pathogen. Molecular epidemiological data from Latin America remain limited, especially for northern Peru. Methods Drug-resistant A. baumannii isolates collected between 2015 and 2021 at a tertiary referral hospital in northern Peru were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, BOX-PCR, ERIC-PCR, REP-PCR, and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS). Results All seven isolates met the criteria for MDR, and Ac-4268 showed an extensively drug-resistant phenotype. Repetitive-element PCR identified a group of six isolates with similar banding profiles and a divergent isolate, Ac-4268. Several isolates in the six-isolate group retained susceptibility to one or more aminoglycosides, whereas Ac-4268 was resistant to all antimicrobials tested. The combined molecular and phenotypic findings are consistent with the possible persistence of a dominant related lineage, but they do not establish transmission without whole-genome sequencing and epidemiological linkage data. Conclusion This study provides additional molecular epidemiological evidence on MDR A. baumannii in northern Peru. The findings suggest that a dominant related lineage may have persisted in the hospital alongside a genetically divergent isolate with an extensively drug-resistant phenotype. Confirmation of clonal transmission requires higher-resolution genomic and epidemiological analyses.

title: Triage misalignment and early neonatal death in regionalized perinatal care.
abstract: Background Regionalized perinatal systems aim to align maternal-infant risk with facility capability, yet most evidence focuses on extremely preterm and very low birth weight infants and evaluates delivery hospital or NICU outcomes in isolation. How triage alignment across the full perinatal care continuum relates to early neonatal mortality, including in lower-risk infants and in settings with declining obstetric capacity, is not well understood. Methods We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of 428,717 live births (2013-2024) in Arkansas, including 1,511 early neonatal deaths (0-6 days). Triage alignment at birth, NICU admission, and interfacility transfer was classified as risk-appropriate, under-triaged, or over-triaged based on concordance between required and actual facility level within a regionalized system. Matched case-control analyses with conditional logistic regression used a sequential modeling strategy distinguishing pre-delivery confounders (gestational age, birth weight) from post-delivery clinical indicators (Apgar score, ventilation, seizures, congenital anomalies), with a nested sensitivity analysis to assess mediation. Results Under-triage at birth was associated with five-fold higher early neonatal mortality than risk-appropriate care (56.89 vs. 10.70 per 1,000; P Conclusions Within a regionalized perinatal system, under-triage at birth and inadequate prenatal care are major determinants of early neonatal death across the risk spectrum. Prenatal risk identification, sufficient engagement with prenatal care, triage alignment at birth, geographic access, and coordinated referral should be treated as core system-level targets for reducing preventable early neonatal mortality.

title: Modeling Factors Associated with Smoking Dependence Severity Using Binary Classification-Based Machine Learning: Prediction with Hematological and Demographic Patient Data.
abstract: Background/Objectives : The Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence (FTND) is a subjective, self-report-based instrument used to grade the level of nicotine dependence. Complete blood count (CBC) parameters reflect markers of smoking-related systemic inflammation. In the present study, we aimed to develop a leakage-free and interpretable machine learning approach for classifying FTND level using demographic data, CBC parameters, and duration of smoking exposure. Methods : In this retrospectively designed study, the records of 660 patients with complete data who had presented to the Smoking Cessation Outpatient Clinic of Malatya Training and Research Hospital were included. Because one of the six FTND items directly scores the number of cigarettes smoked per day, the number of packs and the features related to it constitute data leakage and were therefore excluded from the data pool. Smoking duration (years), which is not an FTND item, was retained as the sole predictor of smoking exposure. Feature engineering generated 49 candidate features. Six base learners (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, SVM, LightGBM, XGBoost) and a stacking ensemble were evaluated with an 80-20% training/test split and 10-fold stratified cross-validation. To prevent optimism bias, feature selection and scaling were performed only within the training folds, and class imbalance was addressed through class weighting. The models were interpreted with SHAP and LIME, and the contribution of each feature family was quantified by ablation analysis. Results : In leakage-free 10-fold cross-validation (the primary performance estimate), discrimination was modest, with the highest AUC (0.652) obtained by both SVM (RBF) and logistic regression; on the single hold-out test set, the stacking ensemble reached an AUC of 0.749 (95% CI 0.667-0.831). The full model did not significantly outperform smoking duration alone (DeLong p = 0.22), and extensive feature engineering did not provide a measurable gain (ΔAUC = -0.015). In the SHAP analysis, smoking duration and the age-based interaction terms made the largest predictive contributions. Conclusions : Routine CBC parameters do not by themselves constitute an independent diagnostic tool for determining dependence severity; they carry only weak, complementary information and should not be regarded as a screening biomarker. This exploratory study classifies FTND-based nicotine dependence severity at the individual patient level by combining CBC parameters with machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence; the model is not ready for clinical use.

title: Delayed Silicotuberculosis Diagnosis in a Young Worker: The Importance of Dust Control and Occupational Surveillance.
abstract: Silicosis is an irreversible occupational lung disease caused by inhaled crystalline silica and is a known risk factor for tuberculosis. We report a 26-year-old male construction worker with more than 10 years of unprotected silica dust exposure who presented with worsening dyspnea, chronic productive cough, and weakness. He had been diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis by GeneXpert and was receiving continuation-phase antituberculosis treatment. Chest imaging showed bilateral fibroinfiltrative changes, fibroconsolidation, bronchial dilatation, pleural thickening, and calcified nodules in the right upper lobe, suggesting silicotuberculosis. Bronchoscopy was deferred due to high anesthetic risk, and open lung biopsy with wedge resection was performed. Histopathology showed chronic nonspecific inflammation, dust-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and fibrosis, without alveolar proteinosis or classic silicotic nodules. Given his more than 10 years of unprotected occupational exposure to silica-containing dust, confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis, and overlapping radiological and pathological abnormalities, the overall presentation was interpreted as silicotuberculosis with an accelerated clinical course. The patient received oxygen therapy, continued antituberculosis treatment, antibiotics, bronchodilator nebulization, mucolytic therapy, and chest physiotherapy. His symptoms improved, but he remained oxygen-dependent during mobilization at discharge. He was subsequently readmitted in May 2024 with worsening respiratory symptoms and died during hospitalization. This case emphasizes the importance of occupational history and further evaluation for silicosis in young tuberculosis patients with persistent respiratory abnormalities and silica exposure.

title: Working together to achieve greater quality and safety in healthcare; interweaving Quality Improvement, Lean Six Sigma and Human Factors Ergonomics: a viewpoint paper
journal: International journal of health care quality assurance

title: Individual-level health effects of living near a gas-fired "Peaker" power plant.
journal: The journal of climate change and health
abstract: Introduction "Peaker" electrical power plants operate only during periods of peak energy needs. Rapid fossil-fuel combustion ramp-up produces high emissions, and peaker plants are significant sources of CO 2 and particulate air pollution. We evaluated whether residents living near a gas-fired peaker plant experienced increased pollution-associated emergency department/urgent care (ED/UC) visits associated with air pollution related to the "on" phases of peaker operation. Methods ED/UC visits for patients in a primary care practice serving the neighborhoods surrounding a peaker plant in Massachusetts were analyzed for 5 years (2017-2021) for visit diagnoses including respiratory and cardiovascular conditions, headache, and pregnancy complications. Daily exposure to peaker-related emissions using HyADS, an air-parcel trajectory model-derived unitless measure of exposure magnitude, was assigned by the zip code of each patient's residential address. A case-crossover design evaluated the association between daily peaker exposure and cause-specific ED/UC visits, adjusting for heat index, PM 2.5 from other sources, holidays, and seasonality. Results Average daily peaker plant exposure was 1.4 (unitless); large variability reflected plant intermittency (SD=16). Background PM 2.5 exposure was 8.5 μg/m³ (SD=6.4). Analyses included 2,310 ED/UC visits for assessed diagnoses among patients residing ≤ 30 km from the plant. Main analyses showed a positive association between short-term peaker emissions and increased risk of ED/UC visits for respiratory conditions (OR 1.044; 95 % CI 1.001-1.090). In addition, we found respiratory disease-related visits were elevated among the non-white group (OR 1.347; 95 % CI 1.034-1.755). There was no association noted between peaker emissions and visits for cardiovascular, headache, or pregnancy diagnoses. Conclusion The peaker plant worsened air quality when turned on. Although we did not observe consistent associations across all assessed ED/UC visit categories, there was a positive same-day association between modeled peaker-plant exposure and respiratory-related visits. Replacing combustion-driven peaker plants with renewable energy in densely populated neighborhoods could yield measurable global and local air quality-related health benefits.

title: Mobile AI-Assisted Oral Lesion Triage for Community Oral Cancer Screening: Prospective Field Evaluation Study.
abstract: Background AI-based tools for oral cancer screening have shown promising performance in curated image datasets, but their performance in real-world mobile community screening workflows remains less clear. Objective This study evaluated the prospective field performance of a parameter-locked, mobile AI-assisted oral lesion triage system embedded in a human-supervised community oral cancer screening workflow. Methods We conducted a prospective community-based field evaluation in eastern Taiwan from June 17 to December 31, 2025. Trained nonspecialist personnel acquired standard white-light intraoral images using handheld mobile devices during routine screening. The AI system incorporated on-site image quality assessment and lesion-level risk stratification into green, yellow, and red triage categories. Technically inadequate images after repeated acquisition attempts were classified as ungradable and excluded from performance analysis. Three board-certified oral and maxillofacial specialists established an operational clinical reference standard through structured image review and consensus adjudication. The primary outcome was lesion-level identification of high-risk lesions requiring specialist referral, defined as red versus nonred triage. Diagnostic performance was estimated with Wilson 95% CIs; precision-recall performance and preconsensus specialist agreement were also assessed. Results Among 602 screened participants, 4283 interpretable intraoral images were included in expert adjudication and lesion-level analysis. The AI system flagged 68 red lesions; 12 (17.6%) were confirmed as high risk, and 4 additional high-risk lesions were identified during expert review, yielding 16 high-risk events for the primary red-triage analysis. For high-risk lesion identification, sensitivity was 75% (12/16; 95% CI 50.5%-89.8%) and positive predictive value was 17.6% (12/68; 95% CI 10.4%-28.4%); specificity, negative predictive value, and accuracy were 98.6% (3928/3984), 99.9% (3928/3932), and 98.5% (3940/4000), respectively. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values were 0.957 for red, 0.931 for yellow, and 0.964 for green triage; precision-recall analysis showed area under the precision-recall curve values of 0.8235, 0.9052, and 0.9476, respectively. Preconsensus specialist agreement was high, with a Fleiss κ of 0.921 and a Gwet AC1 of 0.981. Conclusions This mobile AI-assisted oral lesion triage system was feasibly integrated into a real-world community screening workflow operated by trained nonspecialist personnel. In this low-prevalence field setting, red triage showed moderate sensitivity and modest positive predictive value, supporting its use as human-supervised referral-prioritization support rather than autonomous diagnosis. Further multicenter studies with blinded assessment, participant-level outcomes, workflow-efficiency measures, and longitudinal follow-up are needed before clinical impact and scalability can be determined.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Microbial Colony Analysis: Plate-Reading Challenges, Method Selection, and Validation.
abstract: Microbial colony analysis is routinely used in clinical microbiology, pharmaceutical quality control, food safety, and environmental monitoring. Colony enumeration remains challenging because real-world plates frequently show crowding, size variation, background debris, and plate-rim interference. Low contrast on membrane or filter media, weak colony boundaries, and ultra-dense or too-numerous-to-count (TNTC) growth further complicate analysis. These conditions increase counting variability and limit rule-based counters. This review examines artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled colony analysis and links recurrent plate-reading challenges to method selection and validation requirements. We examine traditional threshold- and morphology-based pipelines, object detection, semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and density- or keypoint-based estimation. Current evidence is stronger for plate-level triage and semi-quantitative interpretation than for direct colony enumeration. However, evidence supporting routine quantitative colony-forming unit (CFU) reporting across laboratories remains limited. Reliable deployment requires methods suited to plate format, organism, imaging conditions, and intended use, with validation in the target workflow.

title: Mapping the research landscape of UAV- and eVTOL-enabled emergency medical services: a bibliometric analysis, scoping review, and policy tool assessment.
abstract: Background Electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly recognized as transformative technologies for emergency medical services (EMS). Despite a growing body of evidence on drone-delivered automated external defibrillators (AEDs), blood product logistics, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations, no study has comprehensively mapped this interdisciplinary research landscape while simultaneously analyzing the policy frameworks that govern its implementation. Methods We conducted a triple-method study integrating bibliometric analysis, a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and quantitative policy text analysis. Bibliometric mapping covered 2015 to 2026. The scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology with the PAGER (Patterns, Advances, Gaps, Evidence, Recommendations) synthesis framework, including 168 studies. Policy analysis applied the Rothwell and Zegveld policy tool classification and the Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) Index to 62 Chinese policy documents related to low-altitude economy and emergency medical rescue (2020-2025), yielding 526 codable policy provisions. Results The bibliometric analysis identified 683 publications across five thematic clusters, with exponential growth from 2022 onward. The scoping review of 168 studies synthesized evidence showing drone-delivered AEDs arrived before ambulances in 67% of cases (median lead time 3 min 14 s), blood product drone delivery reduced transport time by 61%, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations halved advanced life support response times. All 964 modeled drone networks were cost-effective under model assumptions, improving OHCA survival by 21%-46%. Policy analysis of 62 Chinese documents revealed structural imbalance: supply-side and environmental tools constituted 75.3% of provisions while demand-side tools accounted for only 24.7%. The mean PMC Index was 7.46 (SD = 0.89), with timeliness (0.73) and policy measures (0.72) as the weakest dimensions. Conclusion The evidence base for UAV/eVTOL-enabled emergency medical services is approaching the consistency needed to inform health systems planning, although no formal risk-of-bias appraisal was undertaken, and a critical disconnect persists between technological readiness and policy infrastructure. We propose a "dual-wheel drive, four-chain integration" framework encompassing scenario implementation and ecosystem cultivation across infrastructure, industrial innovation, institutional policy, and human capital dimensions. This framework offers a roadmap for translating fragmented pilot programs into sustainable, equity-enhancing emergency medical service systems.

title: Micro/Nanostructured Materials and Microfluidic Diagnostic Platforms Enable Multimodal Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), as pivotal targets in liquid biopsy, offer dynamic, multidimensional insights into tumor heterogeneity and metastatic progression. However, their extreme rarity, pronounced heterogeneity, and the complexity of the blood microenvironment severely constrain detection accuracy. Advances in micro/nanomaterials and functional device engineering have enabled substantial improvements in CTC enrichment efficiency by refining the topographical and chemical properties of capture interfaces. These innovations also provide a compatible foundation for multimodal molecular profiling. This review systematically outlines the structure-function relationships of functionalized nanomaterials, microfiltration substrates, and biomimetic microfluidic devices, highlighting how material parameters-such as nanoscale architectures and membrane pore sizes-govern CTC capture performance. We further explore the integration of micro/nanomaterials with functional platforms for multidimensional molecular analyses across DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Coupled with emerging digital PCR technologies, these systems show promise in overcoming the sensitivity barriers associated with rare mutation detection and protein quantification, enabling multi-omics data fusion. We also discuss how artificial intelligence (AI)-driven feature selection, clustering, and prediction integrate multidimensional data to decode tumor heterogeneity and guide disease monitoring. Despite rapid progress, key challenges remain-including the lack of standardization, limited integration of multi-omic datasets, and the need for robust clinical validation. Future directions may lie in the convergence of microfluidic-integrated materials, single-cell multi-omics, and AI-driven analytics to establish dynamic, high-resolution monitoring platforms that bridge the gap between fundamental research and clinical precision oncology.

title: Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Background Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (IS) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the clinical and laboratory data of 12,213 hospitalized stroke patients (including 3,251 with ICH and 8,962 with IS) and 2,893 hypertensive controls at Xijing Hospital between 2013 and 2023. A temporal validation cohort comprising 153 ICH and 342 IS patients admitted from January to December 2024 was also established. To address class imbalance, BorderlineSMOTE-2 (BS2) was applied. Candidate variables were screened using three feature selection strategies, including RFECV-ADA, Lasso, and Boruta. Six supervised machine learning models were trained using ten-fold cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Feature importance was interpreted using SHAP analysis. Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses were performed as exploratory complementary analyses. Results Ten routine laboratory parameters were retained for model construction: white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, uric acid, total protein, potassium, sodium, chloride, fibrinogen degradation product, and D-Dimer. In the test cohort, the final model (BS2_LightGBM_V10) achieved AUCs of 0.926 for discriminating ICH from IS, 0.979 for discriminating ICH from controls, and 0.923 for discriminating IS from controls. For the three-class classification task (ICH, IS, and controls), the overall accuracy reached 79.07%. SHAP analysis indicated that neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, D-Dimer, and total protein were the most influential predictors. Mendelian randomization analysis suggested that uric acid had a potential causal association with the risk of ICH (OR = 1.309), whereas uric acid (OR = 1.0008), cystatin C (OR = 1.0011), and potassium (OR = 1.0040) had potential causal associations with the risk of IS. Colocalization analysis identified 18 genes linked to uric acid in the context of ICH. Conclusion A diagnostic model based on ten routine laboratory indicators accurately differentiated ICH from IS. Uric acid may also play a causal role in the pathogenesis of both disorders.

title: Rethinking Postoperative Pain in the Era of Robotic Thoracic Surgery: A Surgeon's Perspective on Functional Recovery and Potential Oncologic Implications.
abstract: Persistent postoperative pain remains an incompletely resolved problem after minimally invasive thoracic surgery, despite expectations that robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) would meaningfully outperform video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) in analgesia. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from randomized trials, cohort studies, and meta-analyses comparing acute and chronic pain outcomes between VATS and RATS, examines mechanisms and surgically modifiable risk factors underlying intercostal nerve injury and pain chronification, and evaluates the emerging concept of Return to Intended Oncologic Treatment (RIOT) as a perioperative endpoint linking pain control to oncologic recovery. Across randomized and propensity-matched comparisons, RATS has generally failed to demonstrate superior pain outcomes relative to VATS, and several studies suggest multiport robotic platforms may produce greater early pain than uniportal thoracoscopic approaches. Port number, operative time, and drainage duration emerge as modifiable surgical predictors of chronic pain, while inadequately controlled acute pain compromises functional recovery and is associated with delayed RIOT; direct evidence that pain independently influences RIOT or long-term survival remains limited, and this link should currently be regarded as a plausible, testable hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. We conclude that, on the comparative evidence available to date, robotic instrumentation has not shown a consistent, clinically meaningful reduction in pain burden relative to VATS, and that pain management should be reframed as a shared surgical-anesthetic target relevant to oncologic recovery rather than a comfort-oriented endpoint alone. Emerging robotic platforms warrant evaluation against this expanded outcome set.

title: A systematic review of non-contact medical IoT systems for physiological biomarker monitoring.
abstract: Introduction Non-contact medical Internet of Things systems measure physiological biomarkers such as heart rate (HR), respiration rate (RR), temperature, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and blood pressure (BP) without physical contact with the patient. These systems combine sensing modalities including cameras, radar, Wi-Fi, acoustic, and infrared sensors with signal processing and learning algorithms to deliver comfortable, non-invasive monitoring. Prior reviews have largely examined individual sensing modalities or signal processing techniques in isolation, leaving cross-modality system architecture and privacy-preserving design underexamined. Methods We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and analyzed 88 recent studies of non-contact monitoring systems. Studies were characterized by sensing modality, system architecture, target physiological parameter, validation setting, and reported performance. We additionally assessed each study for methodological quality and examined the extent to which privacy-preserving mechanisms were incorporated into system design. Results Radar and vision-based systems dominate the corpus, together accounting for approximately three-quarters of included studies, while sound, Wi-Fi, embedded sensor, and mixed-modality designs remain at an earlier stage of validation. Research effort is heavily concentrated on two parameters: RR appears in 83% of studies and HR in 67%, while no other parameter exceeds 11%. BP, SpO₂, and temperature therefore remain largely unaddressed by contactless methods. Heterogeneous reporting metrics across studies prevent direct statistical comparison of performance between modalities. Discussion The findings indicate that modality selection should be driven by deployment context rather than headline accuracy. Radar suits wards and intensive care units where patients are covered or moving, vision and sound suit structured clinical spaces with stable conditions, embedded sensor designs suit eldercare beds and chairs, and mixed radar and vision systems suit precision-critical settings such as neonatal and postoperative monitoring. Persistent challenges include signal reliability in uncontrolled environments, limited benchmarking due to the absence of standardized datasets, privacy and ethical concerns, and poor integration with existing healthcare infrastructure. Building on these insights, we propose a conceptual federated, edge-based learning framework, presented as a design proposal for future implementation rather than a validated system, and outline research directions to accelerate clinical translation.

title: From safety science to operational reality: competing institutional logics in the translation of national patient safety recommendations.
journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
abstract: Background National patient safety investigation bodies conduct system-level investigations and produce recommendations intended to drive improvement. Evidence that such recommendations translate into meaningful improvement is weak, and the reasons for this are poorly understood. This paper examines how recommendations produced by the Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB), England's independent national patient safety investigation body, are produced by investigators and received by the national organizations to whom they are directed. Methods A qualitative multimethod design was used including documentary analysis of 22 investigation reports produced by the Healthcare Safety Investigation Branch (HSIB), predecessor to HSSIB, two focus groups with HSSIB patient safety investigators (n = 12) and semistructured interviews with 11 senior representatives of national organizations, recipients of HSSIB recommendations. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, guided by institutional logics. Results Documentary analysis showed that HSIB recommendations were nondirective, clustering at the weakest level of the hierarchy of risk controls and favouring administrative measures. Two competing institutional logics were constructed using reflexive thematic analysis. HSSIB investigators deploy a safety science logic focusing on systems thinking, collaborative engagement and nonpunitive learning, while recipient organizations enact a managerial-operational logic prioritizing resource management and operational feasibility. Four consequences follow: (i) recommendations are attenuated through nominal coproduction; (ii) recipients navigate priority thickets in which political salience, strategic fit, and resource availability govern implementation; (iii) accountability among recipients is diffuse; and (iv) HSSIB's transparency carries limited traction within the managerial-operational logic. Conclusions These conditions produce a paradox: HSSIB's structural separation from the organizations it investigates, while central to its legitimacy as a learning body, can distance it from the operational realities that govern whether recommendations are acted upon. Overcoming this paradox requires deliberate logic-building strategies that address how recommendations are framed, how accountability is constructed, and how the governance landscape is coordinated.

title: Tendinopathy: Types, Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, and Future Precision-Oriented Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Tendinopathy represents a heterogeneous spectrum of tendon disorders characterized by persistent pain, impaired function, and progressive disruption of tissue homeostasis. Rather than a single degenerative entity, tendinopathy reflects the interaction between mechanical adaptation failure, immune dysregulation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and systemic metabolic influences. However, its pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Tendinopathy can affect multiple anatomical sites, such as the rotator cuff, Achilles tendon, and patellar tendon, and has a high prevalence in both the general population and athletes. Despite decades of research, there is currently a lack of targeted therapies capable of effectively reversing the pathological process, and clinical management is primarily limited to empirical symptomatic treatment. This review systematically synthesizes the epidemiology and risk factors of tendinopathy and proposes a "multidimensional tendinopathy remodeling network" model encompassing mechanotransduction, inflammatory cascades, pathological angiogenesis, and matrix turnover. Furthermore, we discuss emerging approaches for molecular stratification through multimodal imaging and biomarkers, and evaluate precision-oriented therapeutic strategies, including mechanomodulation, immunomodulation, regenerative medicine, and nano delivery systems. This framework provides a conceptual foundation for understanding the heterogeneity of tendinopathies and facilitates a shift from symptom-oriented treatment to mechanism-oriented approaches, potentially leading to precision treatment strategies. At the same time, it highlights the challenges in current translational research and points to future research directions for personalized tendon repair strategies.

title: An agentic AI- and n8n automation-powered maternal care framework with predictive pregnancy monitoring and continuous learning.
abstract: Conventional maternal remote patient monitoring has relied upon using immutable ranges for detection of conditions on maternal telemetry. However, this has created extreme alert fatigue in clinicians. The newly proposed Agentic AI Maternal Triage Framework combines patient-reported outcome data with quantitative telemetry values to deliver real-time, context-aware decisions regarding risk stratification to both the clinician and patient. The triage workloads are processed in an orchestrated manner via n8n, utilizing light gradient boosting machine models to determine the likelihood that the maternal telemetry is showing that the patient is developing cardiovascular or metabolic risks. The models produce continuous risk scores that are consumed by a retrieval-augmented generation-powered Google Gemini large language model to yield structured triaged outputs. The triage outputs are delivered to a conversational agent for low-risk patients and a physician for high-risk patients using a triage model of escalation. To allow for continued learning, expert validation is captured via stateless webhooks. In the simulation-based evaluation, the predictive models achieved classification metrics above 99.8%; however, these results reflect the controlled synthetic data-generating environment and do not establish clinical validity. The framework therefore represents a technical proof of concept for integrating predictive modeling, retrieval-grounded generative reasoning, context-aware routing, and human-in-the-loop feedback, with external clinical validation required before real-world deployment.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Tidal Breathing Patterns in Assessing Airflow Obstruction Compared with Spirometry.
journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
abstract: Purpose Spirometry is the standard for assessing airflow obstruction in COPD, but low-burden screening tools may support primary care in identifying patients needing referral, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and timely disease management. A novel, easy-to-use device (AMES BV, the Netherlands) estimates obstruction from nasal pressure variation during tidal breathing and may support referral decisions. This study aimed to assess the ability of nasal pressure analysis to identify airflow obstruction compared with spirometry. Patients and methods Cross-sectional study at a hospital pulmonary function laboratory. In a convenience sample of participants referred for routine spirometry, nasal pressure variation was measured via a nasal cannula and converted into an obstruction index, expressed as an estimated Forced Expiratory Volume in the first second/Forced Vital Capacity ratio (FEV 1 /FVC). The ability to identify spirometry-derived obstruction (FEV 1 /FVC 1 /FVC ratio (derived from nasal pressure variation) and spirometry-defined FEV 1 /FVC ratio.
