Results Both procedures were performed in 192 participants (median age 66 (IQR 56-74) yrs; 39% male). Nasal pressure analysis showed moderate performance in detecting obstruction (sensitivity 66%, specificity 63%, accuracy 64%). The Bland-Altman plot showed variability between both measurements, consistent with moderate classification performance, with a mean difference of -0.016 and 95% limits of agreement ranging from -0.43 to 0.40. Conclusion Nasal pressure analysis showed moderate performance in detecting spirometry-defined airway obstruction, suggesting limited potential as a non-invasive tool. Further research is needed to establish its possible clinical utility.

title: Pulsed field ablation: from concepts to technology.
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract: Aims Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a transformative approach for treating cardiac arrhythmias by exploiting irreversible electroporation to preferentially injure myocardium while limiting collateral damage. Translating this biophysical principle into safe and effective clinical systems requires careful integration of waveform design, catheter engineering, computational and experimental modelling, safety testing, and procedural workflow. Objective This review summarizes the fundamental physical and engineering principles that govern cardiac PFA and examines how these principles influence efficacy, safety, lesion formation, and clinical usability. Biophysical and technical considerations Electroporation is governed primarily by the local electric field and waveform-dependent lethal thresholds rather than generator voltage alone. Key waveform variables include monophasic vs. biphasic pulses, microsecond vs. nanosecond pulse widths, duty cycle, and total application duration. Catheter design further determines electric field distribution, lesion geometry, current density, and applicability across anatomic targets, with important distinctions between bipolar and monopolar configurations. Modelling and safety Experimental and computational approaches used to investigate PFA include finite element simulations, cell culture systems, vegetal substrates, and in vivo animal models, each with distinct strengths and limitations. High-voltage pulse delivery can also produce unintended effects, including Joule heating, electrochemical reactions, bubble formation, arcing, and interactions with implanted electronic devices. These phenomena highlight the importance of optimized waveform design, electrode configuration, and safety monitoring. Clinical usability Clinical adoption depends not only on biological efficacy and safety but also on workflow efficiency, catheter versatility, procedure duration, mapping integration, anaesthesia requirements, and adaptability to differing clinical practices and geographic settings. Conclusions The performance of a PFA system reflects the interaction of biophysics, waveform characteristics, catheter design, modelling, safety controls, and procedural usability. Understanding these interconnected principles is essential for developing PFA technologies that are effective, safe, predictable, and practical for contemporary electrophysiology laboratories.

title: Exhaled Breath Analysis for Lung Cancer Detection: From VOCs Signatures to EBC-Based Liquid Biopsy and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Although low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is the current standard for early screening, its high false-positive rates and cumulative radiation exposure create a pressing clinical need for complementary, non-invasive diagnostic tools. Exhaled breath analysis represents an accessible strategy for early detection and risk stratification. Early breathomics primarily focused on gas-phase volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, as volatile metabolites, VOCs are chemically unstable and highly susceptible to background ambient air and physiological confounders. Distinct from gas-phase analysis, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) offers enhanced biomarker stability and functions as a lung-proximal liquid biopsy. By capturing non-volatile, high-molecular-weight analytes, including tumor-derived nucleic acids and proteins, EBC more closely reflects the underlying molecular mechanisms of the respiratory microenvironment. Nevertheless, the clinical translation of EBC remains constrained by severe sample dilution, unstandardized collection device architectures, and pre-analytical inconsistencies. This review summarizes the progression from VOCs profiling to EBC-based platforms, detailing recent advances in sample harvesting, ultrasensitive detection technologies, and multi-omics integration. Advancing EBC toward routine clinical use requires consensus-driven standard operating procedures and the application of machine learning algorithms to high-dimensional datasets. Future efforts should prioritize large-scale, multicenter prospective trials to validate specific EBC signatures, thereby establishing this technology as a reliable liquid biopsy for precision pulmonary oncology.

title: Generative enhancement of suboptimally opacified cerebral CT angiography for large-vessel occlusion detection: a multireader study.
abstract: Background Rapid identification of proximal anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion (LVO) on CT angiography (CTA) is essential for thrombectomy triage. Suboptimal arterial phase timing can obscure the intracranial arteries, prompting repeat CTA, additional contrast exposure, and treatment delay. We evaluated whether deep-learning-generated vascular images from a single suboptimally opacified acquisition improved LVO detection. Methods This retrospective study included 626 patients. RescueCTA, a paired 2.5D conditional generative model, was developed in 391 patients using last-frame CT perfusion (CTP) as the simulated acquisition-failure input and same-session CTA as the target. Evaluation included 194 primary cases with simulated inputs and 41 exploratory cases with genuinely underopacified CTA. RescueCTA was compared with three generative baselines. Two radiologists assessed image quality. Four readers compared source images alone with source images plus RescueCTA for target LVO detection in the primary cohort; two also evaluated the exploratory cohort. The primary endpoint was the multireader multicase (MRMC) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); exploratory analyses were descriptive. Results In the primary cohort, RescueCTA image quality was higher than that of all three baselines (3.90 ± 0.81). Combined reading improved AUC from 0.850 to 0.933 (ΔAUC = 0.083 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.025-0.141]; p = 0.007), while paired CTA reached 0.948 ( p = 0.594 vs. combined reading). Strict AUC improved from 0.756 to 0.880 ( p p = 0.019). In the exploratory cohort, combined reading yielded a higher AUC than underopacified CTA alone (0.981 vs. 0.889). Conclusion Deep-learning-generated vascular images improved LVO detection under simulated underopacification and showed preliminary feasibility in genuinely underopacified CTA. Larger real-world cohorts are needed to establish diagnostic performance after suboptimal arterial phase CTA.

title: Precision oncology at speed: workflow design determines clinical utility in rapid molecular testing for lung cancer.
abstract: Purpose Matching patients with effective targeted therapies requires timely molecular results; however, the challenge today how to embed it into routine clinical workflows in ways that meaningfully affect patient-level treatment decisions. Methods Building on prior work, the authors systematically reviewed laboratory operations, interdepartmental coordination, and administrative processes from two distinct healthcare settings: a US-based academic tertiary care center and a Canadian community hospital. We identified shared themes, context-specific challenges, and operational elements that distinguished successful integration from assay availability alone. Results Across both environments, the comparison revealed that rapid testing consistently accelerated treatment decisions and facilitated biomarker-informed patient management, but its successful implementation depended on re-engineering laboratory workflows, aligning personnel competencies, and establishing turnaround time monitoring; technical availability alone did not ensure clinically meaningful rapid testing. While the academic context integrated rapid testing within comprehensive molecular pipelines and research frameworks, the community hospital context focused on pragmatic adoption for frontline care, especially in urgent clinical settings and based on the organization of the Canadian health system. Conclusion Implementing rapid molecular testing in NSCLC is fundamentally an implementation and systems-engineering challenge rather than a technical challenge. Clinical speed depended more on system design than assay availability alone and is influenced, in part, by the larger national healthcare context. Addressing laboratory, operational, and administrative barriers is essential to ensure that rapid testing improves outcomes. Lessons learned from both academic and community practice provide a practical, implementation-focused roadmap for broader adoption and equity in access to precision oncology.

title: Turnaround time in diagnostics, analysing delays and strategic improvements in a tertiary care hospital
abstract: Abstract Background: Turnaround time (TAT) is an important indicator of laboratory efficiency and can influence clinical decision-making. Delays may occur during the pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical stages. This study assessed laboratory TAT and identified factors associated with delays in biochemistry and haematology investigations. Methodology: A Descriptive, cross-sectional, single-centre study was conducted from January to March 2026 in a multispeciality tertiary care hospital in New Delhi. Hospital Information System (HIS) records for routine biochemistry and haematology investigations from outpatient (OPD) and inpatient (IPD) settings were reviewed. Of 4,552 retrieved records, 2,505 complete records met the predefined eligibility criteria, including 1,598 (63.8%) biochemistry and 907 (36.2%) haematology samples. Collection, sample assessing, acceptance, result reporting, and validation timestamps were extracted. Pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical, and TAT were calculated. Median TAT with 10th and 90th percentiles was assessed. Operational factors were evaluated using structured questionnaires among 238 OPD patients and 80 healthcare workers from inpatient settings. Results: The overall median total TAT was 138 minutes, with 139 minutes for biochemistry and 137 minutes for haematology. The analytical phase contributed the highest proportion (57%), followed by pre-analytical (26%) and post-analytical (17%) phases. Significant differences were observed among the TAT phases (Kruskal–Wallis H = 5897, p Conclusion: Laboratory TAT was influenced by multiple workflow-related factors. Although the analytical phase accounted for the largest proportion of TAT, administrative processes, specimen transportation, HIS-related delays, and result validation also contributed to it. Targeted workflow redesign, adequate staffing, improved transport systems, clear patient navigation, and optimized HIS processes may help reduce delays and improve diagnostic service efficiency.

title: AI-Generated Draft Response Tool, Message Turnaround Time, and After-Hours Replies Among Health Care Professionals.
abstract: Importance Patient portal message volumes have increased, creating substantial administrative burden for clinicians and contributing to after-hours electronic health record work. The Epic In Basket Augmented Response Technology tool generates artificial intelligence-drafted replies to patient messages and has been widely deployed to reduce this burden, yet assessment of efficiency remains limited. Objective To examine the associations of response tool adoption, use, and habituation with message turnaround time and after-hours response. Design, setting, and participants This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinician-level panel regression with individual fixed effects. All first responses to patient portal messages sent at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC) between March 1, 2023, and May 15, 2025, were analyzed. Exposure Enterprise-level response tool deployment December 2024. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcomes were log-transformed message turnaround time, defined as the elapsed time between patient message submission and first response sent by a clinician, and whether the response was sent outside working hours. Results The analysis included 983 154 responses from 1542 clinicians (770 [49.9%] female) and 272 091 patients (mean [SD] age, 48.1 [21.6] years; 121 370 [44.6%] female) at CUIMC. Response tool adoption was associated with an 8.6% (95% CI, 4.6%-12.9%; P Conclusions and relevance In this cohort study, response tool adoption was associated with increased turnaround time. Response tool use was associated with reduced turnaround time and with fewer after-hours responses for test results-related queries received during working hours, but more after-hours responses for messages received outside working hours. These findings suggest that the tool may reduce the barrier to responding to certain messages while not uniformly reducing burden.

title: Evaluation of the <i>Strongyloides stercoralis</i> VirClia IgG monotest for the diagnosis of strongyloidiasis in a diverse clinical cohort.
Clinical accuracy and operational evaluation of a novel nanopore-based 16S sequencing workflow for diagnostic pathogen detection.
Precision Oncology: Cancer Specialists' Perspectives on Molecular Profiling, Targeted Therapy, and Barriers to Access.
abstract: Background Precision oncology has transformed cancer care through molecular profiling and biomarker-guided therapies. However, access remains uneven in resource-constrained settings. In Bangladesh, quantitative evidence characterizing barriers to molecular profiling and targeted therapy remains limited, particularly regarding barriers beyond financial constraints. This study aims to describe oncologists' perspective regarding current molecular profiling practices and receipt of targeted therapy among eligible patients, and to identify major financial and non-financial barriers and potential strategies for improving access to precision oncology as perceived by the physicians. Methods A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted from June to July 2026 among cancer specialists actively involved in cancer care in Bangladesh. A structured questionnaire assessed molecular profiling and targeted therapy practices, perceived barriers, and potential strategies for improving access. Data from 52 respondents were analyzed descriptively using frequencies and percentages. Results Molecular profiling was recommended often or always by 27 (51.9%) respondents. estrogen receptor/progesterone receptor/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (ER/PR/HER2) (90.4%), microsatellite instability/mismatch repair (MSI/MMR) (82.7%), and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) (80.8%) were the most requested molecular tests. However, 45 (86.5%) respondents reported that no more than 25% of eligible patients ultimately received targeted therapy. High cost of targeted therapy was rated as a major or very major barrier by 46 (88.5%) respondents, followed by high cost of molecular testing (45, 86.5%). Among non-financial barriers, limited testing facilities (29, 55.8%), limited patient understanding or acceptance of molecular testing (28, 53.8%), and long turnaround time for molecular testing results (25, 48.1%) were most frequently rated as major or very major barriers. Most respondents (42, 80.8%) agreed or strongly agreed that targeted therapy should become standard practice in Bangladesh where indicated. Reduced testing costs (43, 82.7%) and government-subsidized insurance coverage (33, 63.5%) were the most frequently selected strategies for improving access. Conclusion Cancer specialists in Bangladesh reported substantial use of molecular profiling but limited receipt of targeted therapy among eligible patients. Although financial constraints emerged as the most prominent barriers, important non-financial challenges related to testing infrastructure, patient understanding and acceptance, and turnaround time were also identified. In the context of limited existing quantitative evidence from Bangladesh, these findings provide initial insight into the relative prominence of financial and non-financial barriers and may inform strategies to improve access to precision oncology.

title: Rapid molecular screening of adult AML: Experience from the Spanish CETLAM cooperative group.

Survey-based perspectives and reported barriers to <i>DPYD</i> testing among U.S. oncologists.
abstract: Background Patients with cancer with deleterious DPYD variants are at significantly increased risk for severe toxicity with standard fluoropyrimidine doses. Prior to recent guidelines recommending it, the uptake of pre-treatment DPYD testing in the United States has been low. We aimed to explore oncologists' perceptions and barriers to DPYD testing adoption on a national level. Materials and methods Survey invitations were sent to U.S. oncologists listed in the American Medical Association (AMA) Masterfile in April and May 2025. The surveys assessed physician knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of DPYD testing in clinics caring for patients with cancer in the United States. Descriptive statistics were used to evaluate survey responses. Results Of 5,525 physicians invited to participate, 47 oncologists completed the survey (response rate: 0.85%). The majority (85%) indicated that DPYD testing could help them manage patients; however, only 34% reported routinely performing DPYD testing. Most physicians (77%) agreed that adequate resources were available to order DPYD testing. When directly asked, 36% indicated that limited laboratory access was a barrier. In open-ended responses, respondents identified insurance reimbursement concerns (21%) and prolonged turnaround time (19%) as additional barriers. Forty-three percent reported needing assistance interpreting results and applying them to drug selection and dosing. Webinars (25.5%) and self-paced online modules (21%) were the most preferred educational modalities. Conclusion Most respondents indicated that DPYD testing could help manage patients, yet concerns persist. While regulatory guidance is evolving, these preliminary findings from a small sample highlight the need for future research to characterize implementation barriers and inform policy development. Implications for practice Our findings highlight gaps in implementation that can inform targeted strategies to improve the integration of DPYD testing into oncology practice, with the potential to enhance patient safety and reduce fluoropyrimidine-related toxicity.

Clinical validation of a novel multiplex real-time PCR for diagnosing community-acquired pneumonia in the emergency department: a promising diagnostic tool for <i>Mycoplasma pneumoniae</i>.
abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a global public health burden with high morbidity, but timely diagnosis is hindered by limitations of conventional methods. We validated a novel multiplex real-time PCR (mRT-PCR) for CAP diagnosis in the emergency department, focusing on Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ). A retrospective cohort of 371 CAP patients (2019-2021) from the Chinese PLA General Hospital was enrolled. The panel targeted 85 pathogens (40 bacteria, 18 viruses, 17 fungi, 10 other) plus 8 resistance genes, with a turnaround time (TAT) under 4 h and a cost of approximately US$100 per test. mRT-PCR showed performance comparable to mNGS for common pathogens (concordance >69% for bacteria/fungi) and high concordance with the final clinical diagnosis. Notably, it detected M. pneumoniae in 36.7% (136/371) of cases, outperforming conventional methods by identifying 204 exclusive positives (55.0% of cohort), with M. pneumoniae (40%) and viruses (30%) predominating. Polymicrobial infections occurred in 36.1% of cases; M. pneumoniae co-infections (38 cases) showed elevated neutrophils and reduced lymphocytes vs. single infections. An independent reference standard analysis excluding both index tests showed that 24.1% (210/873) of calls were independently corroborated - high for influenza, SARS-CoV-2 and M. pneumoniae , lower for S. pneumoniae , consistent with the limited sensitivity of sputum culture. Unlike conventional syndromic panels such as FilmArray, which profile fewer targets without concurrent resistance-gene detection, this mRT-PCR combines broad coverage with rapid TAT and low cost, making it promising for timely CAP diagnosis, particularly in resource-limited settings and for targeted therapy.

title: Microfluidic integrated nucleic acid test (MINT) enabled by coupling FEN1-aided RPA with wax-purification and bead-carrier.
Patient-derived gastric cancer organoids for functional precision oncology: disease-specific bottlenecks and clinical readiness.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) poses a distinct modeling challenge. The disease varies by region, histology, metastatic site, and treatment history. It also develops within a gastric niche shaped by acid, mucus, polarity, microbes, and stroma. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) can preserve tumor-linked epithelial states and support living biobanks. They also enable genotype-phenotype studies and functional testing of therapeutic vulnerabilities. Their clinical value depends on representation, not model complexity alone. The assay must also return clear results within a useful clinical window. This review evaluates GC PDOs as functional companion models for precision oncology rather than stand-alone treatment decision tools. We discuss four barriers that limit clinical readiness. Establishment bias reduces representation of diffuse-type, scirrhous, and signet-ring cell carcinomas. Standard organoid lumens do not reproduce gastric acidity, stratified mucus, or Helicobacter pylori-driven polarity loss. Long-term expansion can select culture-adapted clones and weaken clinical representativeness. PDO drug screening also remains difficult to align with urgent treatment timelines. Fresh-sample assays may shorten turnaround time but reduce scale and depth. We further highlight biological insights gained from GC organoids. These include niche independence, epigenetic dependencies, ARID1A-linked vulnerabilities, and chemotherapy resistance. We propose a readiness framework based on six criteria: tumor authenticity, subtype coverage, niche fidelity, turnaround time, assay standards, and outcome validation. This framework may help define where GC PDOs can support clinical reasoning.

title: Evaluation of the Bruker IR Biotyper for <i>Streptococcus pyogenes emm</i> typing.
Clinical and metagenomic characterization of HHV-6 versus HHV-7 encephalitis in immunocompetent children.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Background Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) and human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) are betaherpesviruses that can cause encephalitis/encephalopathy in immunocompetent children. However, early clinical manifestations, routine laboratory tests, and neuroimaging findings often lack specificity, making etiological characterization challenging. This study aimed to characterize the clinical features and metagenomic findings of HHV-6 and HHV-7 encephalitis in immunocompetent children. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included children ( Results A total of 20 children with CSF HHV-6 or HHV-7 sequence detection were included (HHV-6, n=5; HHV-7, n=15). HHV-6 cases mainly occurred in infants and young children, whereas HHV-7 cases were predominantly observed in older children. Fever and seizure-related symptoms were the most common clinical manifestations. Peripheral inflammatory markers, CSF parameters, and neuroimaging findings showed heterogeneous patterns among patients. CSF mNGS detected HHV-6 or HHV-7 sequences in all included cases, with variable sequencing read counts (HHV-6: median 257 reads, range 55-52, 686; HHV-7: median 2, 635 reads, range 457-26, 355). The median turnaround time of mNGS reporting was 1 day (range, 1-2 days). All patients received antiviral therapy, with some receiving adjunctive corticosteroids and/or intravenous immunoglobulin. Short-term outcomes at discharge were generally favorable, and only one patient developed secondary autoimmune encephalitis. Conclusions HHV-6 and HHV-7 encephalitis in immunocompetent children share overlapping clinical characteristics and lack specific early laboratory or imaging features. CSF mNGS enabled rapid and unbiased detection of HHV-6 and HHV-7 sequences and provided complementary etiological information when interpreted together with clinical and ancillary findings.

title: Pathogen-targeted quick multiplex PCR identification of <i>Chlamydia psittaci</i> and <i>Haemophilus influenzae</i> coinfection in pneumonia: a case report.
abstract: This study describes a rare case of pneumonia induced by coinfection with Chlamydia psittaci ( C. psittaci ) and Haemophilus influenzae (H. influenzae) . The patient had a history of chronic nephritis and long-term pigeon breeding. The initial manifestation was slurred speech, followed by rapid progression to high fever and respiratory failure. Chest computed tomography revealed bilateral interstitial pneumonia, predominantly in the right lung. Pathogen-targeted quick multiplex polymerase chain reaction (pt-qPCR) confirmed the pathogens as C. psittaci and H. influenzae , and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) further verified consistent results. After 7-days of combination therapy with doxycycline and azithromycin, the treatment was switched to doxycycline combined with moxifloxacin for an additional 8-days. The patient achieved complete recovery and was discharged from the hospital. This case suggests that pt-qPCR may facilitate early identification of mixed infections in patients with severe pneumonia and a history of avian exposure, thereby providing valuable information to guide clinical decision-making.

title: Building process improvement capacity in epidemiologic research operations: the Nurses' Health Studies experience.
Implementation of Rapid CYP2C19 Genotyping to Guide Antiplatelet Therapy for Secondary Prevention of Ischemic Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack.
Multicenter evaluation of the multiplex polymerase chain reaction QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis Panel for the detection of central nervous system pathogens directly in the cerebrospinal fluid.
abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of pathogens causing meningitis/encephalitis (MEN/EN) is critical to improving clinical outcomes. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) enables simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), offering advantages over traditional methods. This multicenter study evaluated the performance of the QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis (ME) Panel versus conventional methods, including the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel. The CSF samples from patients with suspected MEN/EN along with contrived samples were tested across 13 sites in Europe/USA. Positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel and comparator methods were determined. A total of 1,667 clinical samples (1,527 prospective, 140 archived) were tested. Pathogens were detected by the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel in 115 (7.5%) prospective samples, including Streptococcus pneumoniae (1.1%), Haemophilus influenzae (0.5%), Listeria monocytogenes (0.3%), S. agalactiae (0.2%), Escherichia coli K1 (0.1%), Neisseria meningitidis (0.1%), S. pyogenes (0.1%), enterovirus (1.5%), human herpesvirus-6 (1.0%), herpes simplex virus-2 (0.9%) and -1 (0.3%), varicella zoster virus (0.7%), cytomegalovirus (0.3%), human parechovirus (0.3%), and Cryptococcus gattii/neoformans (0.4%). Overall PPA versus BFME ( n = 1,664) was 85.4%, increasing to 95.3% after discordance resolution. PPA was 100% for N. meningitidis , S. pneumoniae , and S. agalactiae . Overall NPA was 99.9%. Among 1,154 contrived positive samples, only 27 (2.3%) incorrect results were observed. The QIAstat-Dx ME Panel demonstrated high concordance with BFME, supporting its use as a reliable, fully automated multiplex PCR platform for rapid diagnosis of community-acquired MEN/EN.IMPORTANCEThis multicenter study demonstrated that the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel delivers clinical performance comparable to that of the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel, supporting its validity as a reliable syndromic molecular diagnostic tool for MEN/EN. With its broad pathogen coverage, rapid turnaround time (TAT), and the ability to provide amplification curves and Ct values, the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel offers a valuable option for broad and timely detection of bacterial, viral, and fungal CNS pathogens. When used alongside the SoC diagnostic methods, this panel has the potential to improve early diagnosis, guide targeted therapy, and support effective clinical management of patients with suspected MEN/EN.

title: Patient-specific genomic measurable residual disease markers for monitoring acute myeloid leukaemia and myeloid malignancy.
Diagnostic evaluation of long-read nanopore sequencing for pediatric CNS tumors.
abstract: Long-read nanopore sequencing enables methylation-based CNS tumor classification while providing additional genomic information within a single assay. However, its performance across molecular features relevant to pediatric CNS tumor diagnostics and across available methylation classifiers remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated nanopore sequencing for integrated molecular characterization of pediatric CNS tumors and compared with data from DNA methylation arrays and Illumina short-read sequencing used in the clinical diagnostic work-up. Twenty tumor samples representing three major pediatric CNS tumor groups (gliomas, ependymomas and medulloblastomas) were subjected to long-read nanopore sequencing, which generated robust long-read data across all tumor groups, with a mean genome coverage of approximately 40x. Nanopore-derived copy-number profiles showed good concordance with methylation array-derived profiles (median Pearson r = 0.816). Nanopore evidence was identified for 74/78 (95%) clinically relevant small variants detected by Illumina sequencing, although 53/78 (68%) were recovered as exact high-confidence nanopore calls. Structural variant profiles showed limited breakpoint overlap and differed in the number, type, and size distribution of detected events between Illumina and Nanopore sequencing. Nanopore-derived methylation classifications were largely concordant with integrated WHO CNS5 diagnoses. Ependymomas, medulloblastomas, and pilocytic astrocytomas, were concordantly classified across all evaluated classifiers, although not all classifications reached the respective classifier-specific confidence thresholds. In contrast, diffuse gliomas showed greater variability in classification across classifiers. Downsampling indicated that concordance with integrated WHO CNS5 diagnoses remained high at substantially reduced sequencing depths, whereas the proportion of classifications reaching classifier-specific confidence thresholds was more classifier dependent. Long-read nanopore sequencing enables integrated molecular characterization of pediatric CNS tumors within a single assay, although concordance with established methods varied by genomic feature and tumor type. The preservation of methylation classification performance at reduced sequencing depth supports the feasibility of shorter sequencing workflows. Prospective studies are required to establish performance and turnaround time in routine clinical diagnostics.

title: Validation of an AI-Driven Sputum Analysis Platform for Accurate and Reliable Tuberculosis Detection in South-Western Uganda.
abstract: Background Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) sputum smear microscopy remains an accessible method for detecting acid-fast bacilli (AFB), but its interpretation is dependent on specimen quality and trained microscopy personnel. Artificial intelligence (AI) may provide a microscopy reading aid that supports consistent identification of AFB-positive and AFB-negative smear images. Objective To evaluate transfer-learning deep learning models for classification of AFB-positive and AFB-negative digitized ZN-stained sputum smear images generated in a Ugandan regional referral laboratory. Methods A retrospective laboratory-based cross-sectional study used 512 archived digitized ZN-stained sputum smear images from Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital. The dataset contained 256 AFB-positive and 256 AFB-negative images and was partitioned by stratified sampling into training (n=358), validation (n=77), and an internal hold-out test set (n=77). ResNet-50 V2, DenseNet-121, and Swin Transformer-Tiny models were trained using ImageNet-pretrained weights in PyTorch. Performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Results On the internal test set, Swin Transformer-Tiny achieved 97.40% accuracy, 97.37% sensitivity, 97.44% specificity, 97.37% PPV, 97.44% NPV, 97.37% F1-score, and ROC-AUC 0.9939. DenseNet-121 achieved 88.31% accuracy, 84.21% sensitivity, 92.31% specificity, and ROC-AUC 0.9730. ResNet-50 V2 achieved 85.71% accuracy, 81.58% sensitivity, 89.74% specificity, and ROC-AUC 0.9555. Wilson 95% confidence intervals were calculated for the threshold-based metrics. Conclusion The models demonstrated promising internal performance for classification of microscopy-defined AFB status. Swin Transformer-Tiny had the highest observed performance, but the small, balanced, single-centre internal test set and use of routine microscopy labels rather than an independent microbiological reference standard limit clinical interpretation. The platform should therefore be considered an AI-assisted microscopy reading aid rather than an autonomous tuberculosis diagnostic system. Prospective, multicentre evaluation using patient/specimen-level separation, independent microbiological reference standards, and multiple blinded readers is required before clinical deployment.

title: Individualized perioperative decision-making for intraoperative cell salvage in an Rh(D)-negative patient with placenta percreta: a case report
From Algorithm Performance to Laboratory Deployment: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Chemistry.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in clinical laboratories to support laboratory processes and interpretation of test results. Recent developments in machine learning, deep learning, and large language models have expanded the potential applications of AI across different stages of laboratory testing. However, the use of AI in clinical laboratories also raises important questions regarding validation, analytical performance, and transferability between laboratories. This narrative review examines recent applications of AI across the total testing process in clinical chemistry. Recent English-language scientific literature published from 2023 to 18 August 2026 was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. It describes AI-assisted test utilization; specimen handling and quality assessment; detection of laboratory errors; patient-based quality control; interpretation of complex analytical outputs, including signals from emerging AI-integrated biosensors and nanomaterial-based analytical platforms; result verification; and laboratory-report interpretation. The review also discusses major implementation challenges, including analytical variability, data quality, sensor and platform reproducibility, model generalizability, interoperability, and limitations of large language models. Particular attention is given to external validation, transportability, and real-world implementation. Among the studies considered in this review, many applications remain supported mainly by retrospective or internally validated studies, while prospective and operational evaluations are less common. Finally, practical considerations for validation, local verification, quality assurance, and performance monitoring are discussed. AI has considerable potential to support clinical chemistry laboratories, but safe use requires appropriate evaluation and continued involvement of laboratory professionals.

title: Management of bleeding and nonelective invasive procedures in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs): a 5-year single-center observational study.
journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
abstract: Background Guidelines exist for managing bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures in patients on direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), but their clinical impact remains unclear. Objectives To describe the management of patients who had DOAC concentrations measured for bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures and to assess associations between guideline compliance, outcomes, and DOAC concentrations. Methods This retrospective, single-center study (2014-2018) included adult patients receiving dabigatran etexilate, rivaroxaban, or apixaban who required hospital care for bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures and had DOAC concentrations measured at the time of the event. Compliance with French and European guidelines was assessed. Adverse outcomes-a composite of all-cause mortality, worsening or new bleeding, and thrombotic events-were recorded until discharge. Results A total of 584 events (432 procedures and 152 bleeding episodes) in 547 patients were analyzed. Guideline compliance was 79% and showed no association with outcomes. Among 95 events treated with prothrombin complex concentrates, one thrombotic event occurred. DOAC concentrations were higher in the bleeding group than in the procedural group (122 [IQR, 57-219] vs 55 [IQR, 25-127] ng/mL), but bleeding severity was not associated with drug levels. In bleeding patients, rivaroxaban concentrations were higher in those with adverse outcomes compared with those without (243 [IQR, 74-367] vs 88 [IQR, 35-199] ng/mL). Conclusion In a large cohort of patients who had DOAC concentrations measured at the time of a bleeding or a nonelective invasive procedure, compliance with guidelines was high and not associated with outcomes. In bleeding patients, rivaroxaban concentrations were higher in those with vs without adverse events.

title: Molecular Reclassification of Diffuse Gliomas: A Feasibility Study of Clinical Features and Survival Outcomes in Colombia.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The 2021 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (WHO CNS5) integrates histological and molecular criteria for adult diffuse gliomas, but comprehensive molecular testing may be difficult to implement in resource-limited settings. This study assessed the feasibility of a sequential, marker-based approach for diagnostic reassessment and described its association with clinical characteristics and overall survival (OS) in adults from Colombia. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 68 adults with diffuse gliomas treated at two referral hospitals in Bogotá, Colombia, between 2015 and 2023. Molecular assessment used IHC, FISH, PCR, and Sanger sequencing according to the available tissue and diagnostic workflow. The study did not include comprehensive NGS or systematic assessment of combined whole-chromosome 7 gain/chromosome 10 loss (+7/-10). Results: The diagnosis changed after molecular reassessment in 51.5% of cases. The proportion classified as glioblastoma increased from 48.5% under the historical histologic classification to 66.2% under the WHO CNS5-based algorithm, whereas FISH-defined oligodendrogliomas decreased from 17.6% to 11.8%. OS differed among historical histologic groups ( p = 0.03), but not among the WHO CNS5-based groups ( p = 0.13). Female sex was associated with longer OS in unadjusted analysis ( p = 0.02), while age was the only independent predictor in the multivariable analysis. Conclusions: Sequential molecular reassessment materially changed diagnostic categorization in this cohort and was feasible using locally available marker-based methods. However, the results are exploratory, limited by small molecular subgroups, incomplete molecular coverage, and the retrospective treatment context; they should not be interpreted as demonstrating improved treatment selection or survival after reclassification.

title: Reproductive congenital anomalies: identifying paths to care within student-run free clinics.
abstract: Reproductive system congenital anomalies can have debilitating impacts on patient sexual function and reproductive capacity. We present the experience of a 26 year-old phenotypic female patient who identified as female with primary amenorrhea in the student-run free clinic (SRFC) setting. Following clinical evaluation, bloodwork noted an elevated testosterone level. Pelvic ultrasound demonstrated intact bilateral upper genitourinary tracts, bilateral adnexal masses without follicles, with absence of uterus, cervix and upper vagina. Subsequent pelvic magnetic resonance imaging confirmed these findings. Karyotype testing resulted 46XY, confirming androgen insensitivity syndrome. Urologic consultation was obtained, with plans for subsequent referral to a regional SRFC associated with a multi-disciplinary team specializing in reproductive tract anomalies. Unfortunately, despite approvals for charity care and extensive care coordination between the patient and our SRFC, the patient ultimately was lost to follow-up. Despite this suboptimal outcome, this experience provided valuable exposure to rethink how both our SRFCs and others can evolve operations into effective care systems for similar patients in the future. Lessons accrued here provided opportunities to reflect on how to develop a standardized referral and operational framework generalizable to other SRFCs who may care for similar patients.

title: Understanding diagnostic challenges and identifying priorities to tackle antimicrobial resistance in conflict zones.
abstract: Armed conflict is a key driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Diagnostics are critical tools for limiting the impact of AMR where resources are limited. We analyse how conflict shifts the needs and deliverability of AMR diagnostics and identify opportunities to strengthen scope and capacity in these settings with persistent state-delivered health governance and policy. Key priorities include optimisation of robust diagnostic processing, workload and data sharing tools, and procurement policies suitable for resource-limited settings, including linked electronic workload and data-sharing tools with offline options, to support delivery of individual patient care, infection prevention and control, and surveillance.

title: Evaluation of real-time LAMP assay for detection of <i>Entamoeba</i> species in clinical stool samples from a tertiary care center in North India.
abstract: Background Enteric protozoa infections contribute to diarrheal diseases in low and middle income countries, affecting those with limited access to clean water and sanitation. Entamoeba histolytica is an invasive water and food-borne parasite, associated with mucosal inflammation causing symptoms of amoebic colitis that can overlap with ulcerative colitis (UC). As conventional diagnostic methods such as microscopy cannot differentiate morphologically similar species, diagnostic challenges frequently arise. The present prospective study evaluated the clinical diagnostic performance of Real-Time Loop Mediated Isothermal Amplification Assay (LAMP) for detecting and differentiating Entamoeba species in clinical endemic settings, with a focus on patients with UC. Methods The study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in North India from January 2021 to January 2023. Stool samples (n=494) were collected across four groups: patients with UC (n=117), non-inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) diarrhea patients (n=177), community participants (n=100), and diseased controls (n=100). All samples were analyzed using microscopy, conventional PCR, real-time PCR, and real-time LAMP, followed by phylogenetic analysis for species confirmation. For real-time LAMP, the SREHP gene and LSU rRNA gene reactions were performed separately in single run to ensure accurate identification. Statistical evaluation was performed using Bayesian latent class analysis. Results The sensitivity of microscopy, conventional PCR, real-time PCR, and real-time LAMP was calculated to be 39.4% 84.3%, 99.3%, and 99.3%, respectively, with 99.4-100% specificity for real-time LAMP. Five samples missed by conventional PCR were successfully detected by both real-time PCR and real-time LAMP. The overall infection rate across was 6.7% (33/494), with differential detection of Entamoeba species. Samples positive for E. histolytica showed amplification of both SREHP and LSU rRNA genes, whereas E. dispar and E.moshkovskii showed amplification of the LSU rRNA gene only. Among patients with UC, those with active disease had a higher incidence of E. histolytica infection (13/88) than those in remission (4/29). Interpretation Real-time LAMP demonstrated specificity and sensitivity of 99.3% (92.5-100) equivalent to that of real-time PCR with an added advantage of shorter turnaround time than conventional PCR and real-time PCR (60 minutes vs. 200 minutes vs 120 minutes), facilitating prompt differential diagnosis of Entamoeba species in patients with UC. These finding support considering molecular tests in microscopy-negative cases to improve detection and differentiation of Entamoeba species in high-incidence areas and among high-risk patients. However, cost effectiveness and downstream impact on clinical outcomes warrant further study.

title: A modified Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein for mortality prediction in septic shock.
abstract: Objective The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic performance of the Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein for predicting 30-day mortality in patients with septic shock and to compare its performance with the Rapid Emergency Medicine Score, National Early Warning Score, Modified Early Warning Score, quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment. Methods This retrospective observational study included 124 adult patients diagnosed with septic shock in a tertiary emergency department. Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein was calculated as Rapid Emergency Medicine Score +(C-reactive protein /50), using an a priori clinically determined C-reactive protein scaling factor. Results The median age was 63 years, 52.4% of patients were female, and 76 patients (61.3%) died within 30 days. Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein had the highest numerical AUC (0.770), corresponding to moderate discrimination, followed by National Early Warning Score (0.755), Modified Early Warning Score (0.746), quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (0.688), Rapid Emergency Medicine Score (0.638), and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (0.593). Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein had significantly higher AUCs than Rapid Emergency Medicine Score (ΔAUC=0.132, p Conclusion Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein showed moderate discrimination for 30-day mortality in this exploratory development cohort but did not demonstrate superior discrimination compared with National Early Warning Score, Modified Early Warning Score, or quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment. Because Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein was developed and evaluated in the same cohort, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Independent external validation is required before its clinical utility can be established.

title: Diffuse Alveolar Haemorrhage Masquerading as Worsening ARDS in a Young Polytrauma Patient: Diagnostic Reasoning and a Conservative Management Bundle - A Case Report.
abstract: Background Diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (DAH) is a rare, under-recognised complication of blunt polytrauma. In patients with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), new airway bleeding may be mistaken for pulmonary contusion, ventilator-associated pneumonia or transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI), delaying appropriate treatment. The timing of definitive fracture fixation also remains uncertain. Case presentation A previously healthy man in his mid-20s sustained blunt polytrauma (Injury Severity Score 29; Glasgow Coma Scale 8), including multiple open comminuted fractures, a T11 compression fracture and bilateral pulmonary contusions. After emergency external fixation, he was transferred in haemorrhagic shock and respiratory failure, with severe ARDS (PaO 2 /FiO 2 78 mmHg), lactate 7.0 mmol/L and creatine kinase 4443 U/L. On day 4, he developed bloody endotracheal secretions, recurrent hypoxaemia, and abrupt decreases in haemoglobin (114 to 76 g/L) and platelets (139 to 65 × 10 9 /L). Bronchoscopy showed diffuse, non-focal mucosal oozing. Vasculitis and cytokine panels were negative. Targeted next-generation sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid detected high burdens of Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae , low-abundance Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and multiple carbapenemase and extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes. Presumed non-immune post-traumatic DAH with possible TRALI contribution was diagnosed. Treatment included withholding further transfusion, methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg/day, lung-protective ventilation, four prolonged prone-positioning sessions, antimicrobial therapy and damage-control orthopaedics, with definitive fixation on day 17. Tracheostomy was decannulated on day 28, and he was discharged to rehabilitation. At follow-up, he walked independently without recurrent DAH or ARDS. Conclusions In polytrauma patients, new diffuse airway bleeding, disproportionate anaemia and worsening hypoxaemia should prompt consideration of non-immune DAH, particularly after transfusion. In this single case, recovery followed a combined strategy of bronchoscopic assessment, restrictive transfusion, corticosteroids, prone ventilation and physiology-guided orthopaedic management. However, concurrent interventions and the absence of histological confirmation preclude causal attribution; the findings are hypothesis-generating.

title: Biomarker-Enriched Host-Directed Trials in Sepsis: Integrating Immune, Endothelial, Coagulation, Redox, and Metabolic Domains.
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening, biologically heterogeneous syndrome in which immune dysregulation, endothelial injury, coagulation activation, redox imbalance, and metabolic reprogramming contribute to microvascular and organ dysfunction. This structured narrative review integrates these five domains to inform biomarker-enriched trials of host-directed interventions, emphasizing the endothelium as an interface between inflammation, immunothrombosis, and impaired cellular bioenergetics. Candidate biomarkers of immune competence, endothelial injury, coagulation, and metabolism are examined alongside investigational immunomodulatory and restorative strategies. The proposed framework distinguishes three functional tiers: screening and biological enrichment; pharmacodynamic target engagement and safety assessment; and patient-centered outcomes. Candidate host-response profiles are hypothesis-generating, may overlap, and require prospective validation, with explicit provisions for mixed and indeterminate classifications. A complementary implementation model separates routine assessments from trial-specific assays and advanced mechanistic substudies, addressing sampling, reporting, missing measurements, and assay harmonization. Evidence remains heterogeneous and largely preclinical, observational, or early-phase; predictive thresholds, therapeutic windows, and patient-centered benefits remain unestablished for most candidate strategies. This framework supports prospective trial design rather than routine bedside treatment selection. Biomarker improvement must be evaluated alongside pathogen control, organ recovery, adverse events, and longer-term outcomes and should not be assumed to indicate clinical benefit.

title: Beyond overall accuracy: subgroup performance and threshold calibration of AI-assisted chest radiography for equity-oriented pulmonary tuberculosis screening.
abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted computer-aided detection (CAD) can expand access to chest radiography interpretation for pulmonary tuberculosis screening and triage, but high overall discrimination does not ensure safety at a deployed threshold. This focused narrative Mini Review synthesizes evidence on subgroup performance, threshold calibration, external validity, and implementation of CAD for adult pulmonary tuberculosis. Smear-negative, asymptomatic, and some HIV-associated disease may be less radiographically visible, increasing false-negative risk. Conversely, previous tuberculosis and competing chronic abnormalities reduce specificity and concentrate unnecessary confirmatory testing. Sex, age, geography, clinical setting, verification design, and software version can further alter operating performance. A numerical threshold is therefore not a portable algorithm property but a context-specific clinical resource-allocation policy. We propose a lifecycle in which programs define the intended use, lock the product and version, conduct representative local validation, select an operating point under explicit sensitivity and capacity constraints, audit clinically relevant subgroups, and monitor the complete care pathway. Stratified thresholds and multivariable models may improve selected settings, but current evidence does not justify replacing robust local calibration and governance. Prospective evaluations should compare threshold strategies under common verification standards and report missed cases, referral burden, treatment initiation, and patient-important outcomes.

title: Development and evaluation of a practical teaching model for medical laboratory interns based on the "quality-safety-patient-centered" triple helix framework.
abstract: Background Balancing competency-based education, quality improvement, and patient-centered care remains a challenge in laboratory medicine internships. This study developed a "quality-safety-patient-centered" triple helix framework and evaluated its association with educational outcomes in an exploratory quasi-experimental setting. Methods This study employed a two-phase, quasi-experimental, non-randomized design with a historical control group. The control group ( n = 30, grade 2022) received conventional teaching, while the experimental group ( n = 32, grade 2023) underwent the Triple Helix-based model. Both completed a 48-week internship. Outcomes included the Triple Helix Integrated Literacy Scale, Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX), theoretical and practical examinations, process quality and safety indicators, and satisfaction ratings. Results The experimental group showed higher scores than the control group on the Triple Helix Integrated Literacy Scale total score (106.25 ± 7.96 vs. 88.70 ± 8.25; mean difference 17.55, 95% CI: 13.42-21.66; P P P P P = 0.014), critical value notification timeliness (100% vs. 80.0%; risk difference 20.00%, 95% CI: 5.69-34.31; P = 0.010), and patient identification compliance rate (93.8% vs. 73.3%; risk difference 20.42%, 95% CI: 2.51-38.33; P = 0.040). Satisfaction ratings from clinicians, patients, and preceptors were all higher in the experimental group (all P Conclusion In this exploratory study, the triple helix teaching model was associated with better performance across quality, safety, and patient-centered competencies. Causal inference is limited by the historical control design, yet the framework may offer a promising direction for guiding teaching reform in laboratory medicine.

title: Clinical laboratory diagnostic stewardship as boundary infrastructure: a multi-stakeholder qualitative study of digital public health governance in two Chinese regional referral hospitals
Diagnostic utility of whole exome sequencing in children with suspected genodermatoses: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Introduction Genodermatoses are a group of monogenic inherited skin disorders characterized by marked genetic heterogeneity. Although the phenotype of many genodermatoses is readily recognizable on clinical examination, it is often insufficient to establish the precise molecular genetic etiology. Currently, the use of whole exome sequencing in pediatric dermatology is considered preferable because of its accessibility and higher diagnostic accuracy compared with targeted sequencing approaches. Methods Singleton whole exome sequencing was performed in 18 children (10 boys and 8 girls) aged 1-15 years with suspected genodermatoses. Before whole exome sequencing, all patients underwent dermatological evaluation, including a comprehensive phenotypic assessment, to determine indications for whole exome sequencing. Results Previously described and novel pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and copy number variation in 10 genes associated with genodermatoses were identified in 9 of the 18 patients (50%). In an additional 2 of the 18 patients, genetic variants were identified in 2 genes associated with other inherited disorders. These were Noonan syndrome, type 4, and pseudohypoaldosteronism, type IB2. The referral diagnosis was concordant with the whole exome sequencing findings in 6 of the 11 cases with pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (54.54%). Variants of uncertain significance were identified in 4 patients. Two previously unreported likely pathogenic variants were detected in the JUP and SCNN1B genes. Previously reported variants were identified in SOS1, FLG, JUP, KRT10, SPINK5, LEMD3 , and NIPAL4 . Overall, 17 sequence variants were detected, including 6 pathogenic, 7 likely pathogenic, and 4 of uncertain clinical significance. In addition, one pathogenic deletion involving the STS gene was identified. In one patient with Netherton syndrome, the molecular diagnosis enabled the initiation of targeted pathogenic therapy. No disease-causing genetic variants were identified in 3 patients. Conclusion Comprehensive phenotypic assessment combined with whole exome sequencing represents a useful diagnostic tool in pediatric dermatology, enabling rapid diagnosis in clinically challenging and undifferentiated cases. Furthermore, this approach facilitates the identification of pathogenic variants not only in genes associated with inherited skin disorders but also in other clinically relevant genes consistent with the suspected diagnosis.

title: Viscoelastic Hemostatic Testing as a Diagnostic Tool for Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy with a Focus on Arabian Gulf Countries: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) at admission to the emergency department is associated with severe bleeding, massive transfusion, increased morbidity, and mortality. There are significant regional variations in the accessibility and acceptance of point-of-care technology, such as viscoelastic hemostatic testing (VET), for coagulation monitoring and bleeding management in the Arabian Gulf council countries (GCC). Notable regional differences among these countries are mainly due to variation in the awareness of the benefits of VET-guided bleeding management using rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) or thromboelastography (TEG), compared with a transfusion ratio-based approach using shock packs, rather than for economic reasons. This review highlights the superiority of VET-guided bleeding management in severe trauma over conventional coagulation tests (CCTs) for early TIC detection and the importance of monitoring hemostatic disorders, whether hypocoagulability or hypercoagulability. VET consistently outperforms traditional coagulation tests in detecting early coagulation abnormalities and predicting massive transfusion and mortality in major trauma. Besides hyperfibrinolysis, fibrinogen deficiency often represents the first issue in TIC. Recent meta-analyses consistently demonstrated a reduction in mortality by implementing VET-guided bleeding management algorithms in severe trauma. Several studies demonstrated that VETs are valuable tools for massive transfusion and mortality prediction in bleeding patients with severe trauma. There is a notable variation in VET adoption and practice across trauma settings in the Arab Gulf. GCC-specific primary evidence is limited, with the Qatar cohort representing the largest directly identified regional study.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of VE1 Immunohistochemistry for BRAF p.V600E in Colorectal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and Objectives : BRAF p.V600E status has diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance in colorectal carcinoma. Molecular assays remain the reference methods, whereas mutation-specific BRAF (VE1 clone) immunohistochemistry offers a rapid tissue-based alternative. We evaluated VE1-molecular concordance and factors affecting diagnostic performance. Materials and Methods : PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in August 2025 and updated on 27 July 2026 for English-language original studies published from 2014 through the update date. Eligible reports applied VE1 and a recognized molecular reference method to the same colorectal carcinoma specimens or a defined overlapping cohort. Study selection and data extraction were performed by one reviewer and independently verified by a second reviewer. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed at the estimate level with QUADAS-3. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, no meta-analysis was performed, and the findings were synthesized descriptively. Results : Of 704 database records, 358 unique records were screened; 38 full-text reports were assessed and 28 were included. Twenty-three reports or defined subcohorts provided complete or clearly reconstructible 2 × 2 comparisons. Sensitivity ranged from 74.6% to 100% and specificity from 66.7% to 100%. Most optimized protocols exceeded 90% for both measures, whereas selected sampling, weak or focal staining, post hoc thresholds, protocol effects, and selective molecular verification reduced reliability. Conclusions : VE1 immunohistochemistry may provide a rapid, locally validated triage method for detecting BRAF p.V600E in colorectal carcinoma. However, substantial heterogeneity and recurrent risk-of-bias concerns limit the generalizability of the available estimates and do not support universal substitution for molecular testing. Equivocal, technically inadequate, or clinically discordant results require molecular clarification.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Complete Blood Count Derived Indices for Acute Coronary Syndrome in Emergency Department Patients With Acute Chest Pain: A Single‐Center Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study

Antimicrobial Resistance-Stratified Efficacy of Vonoprazan, Clarithromycin, and Metronidazole Therapy for <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> Eradication in Penicillin-Allergic Patients: A Single-Arm Prospective Interventional Study.
journal: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
abstract: Background Choosing an effective Helicobacter pylori eradication regimen for patients with penicillin allergy remains a clinical challenge. Although vonoprazan-based regimens yield excellent outcomes in standard populations, we still lack sufficient evidence regarding penicillin-allergic patients. To address this gap, we investigated how a 1-week triple therapy (vonoprazan, clarithromycin [CAM], and metronidazole [MNZ]) performs in this specific cohort, particularly considering the influence of antimicrobial resistance. Methods This exploratory, single-arm, open-label interventional study was conducted at Yokohama City University Hospital (jRCTs031200171). Patients with H. pylori infection and confirmed penicillin allergy were enrolled. The treatment regimen consisted of vonoprazan (20 mg), CAM (200 mg), and MNZ (250 mg), each administered twice daily for 7 days. The primary endpoint was the eradication success rate. Secondary endpoints included safety and the association between eradication success and antimicrobial susceptibility. Results Thirty patients completed the intervention. The overall eradication rate was 90.0% (27/30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 73.5%-97.9%) in per-protocol and intention-to-treat analyses. Adherence was high (99.7%). According to resistance profiles, eradication rates were 100% (15/15; 95% CI, 78.2%-100%) in CAM-susceptible strains, 78.6% (11/14; 95% CI, 49.2%-95.3%) in CAM-resistant strains, 92.0% (23/25; 95% CI, 74.0%-99.0%) in MNZ-susceptible strains, 75.0% (3/4; 95% CI, 19.4%-99.4%) in MNZ-resistant strains, and 50.0% (1/2) in dual-resistant strains. No serious adverse events were documented. Conclusions A 1-week triple therapy with vonoprazan, CAM, and MNZ is an effective and safe treatment option for H. pylori eradication in patients with penicillin allergy. While the regimen achieved excellent results in CAM-susceptible strains, further optimization may be required for cases involving dual antibiotic resistance.

title: N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (NT-proBNP) Versus Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiography for the Diagnosis of Acute Heart Failure in Emergency Departments: A Systematic Review
Clinical and Therapeutic Profile of Dravet Syndrome in Patients Followed at a Brazilian Pediatric Referral Center: Real-World Data from a Tertiary Service.
abstract: Background: Dravet syndrome (DS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, and data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce. We characterized the clinical, genetic, and therapeutic profiles of patients with DS at a Brazilian tertiary referral center. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 27 patients with clinically and genetically confirmed DS (pathogenic/likely pathogenic SCN1A variants). Outcomes were ≥6-month and ≥12-month seizure freedom and seizure control in the previous month, described by treatment exposure without inferential testing. Results: The median age at seizure onset was 4 months and at diagnosis 42 months; the median individual onset-to-diagnosis interval was 29 months (range, 4-283; n = 14). All patients received polytherapy; 51.9% used cannabidiol, 40.7% vagus nerve stimulation, and 7.4% fenfluramine. Only 2/20 patients (10.0%) achieved ≥6-month and 1/20 (5.0%) ≥ 12-month seizure freedom. All six patients seizure-free in the previous month were receiving valproate, a descriptive finding likely reflecting confounding by indication. Recorded comorbidities, mainly autism spectrum disorder (29.6%), were likely underestimated in the absence of systematic neurodevelopmental assessment. Conclusions: This Brazilian DS cohort showed marked diagnostic delay, high seizure burden, and limited access to DS-specific therapies. These findings support earlier genetic testing and broader access to recommended treatments and generate hypotheses for larger prospective studies.

title: Isolating viable bacteria from positive blood cultures: impedance cytometry analysis.
abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) lead to sepsis, an acute inflammatory response associated with high mortality. Current clinical treatment pathways rely on culture-based diagnostics to identify the infectious agent and determine its susceptibility to antibiotics, delaying targeted therapy. Recent approaches to accelerate this focus on the isolation of bacteria directly from blood cultures for rapid downstream analysis using haemolytic agents to replace the gold-standard purity plate subculture. However, many of these methods impact bacterial viability during the early stages of growth. Rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing requires a pure inoculum of actively dividing bacteria to deliver early results (within 3 h), but most isolation chemistries are developed for mass spectrometry identification which does not require viable bacteria. This is particularly relevant for Gram-positive pathogens, as these are more susceptible to detergent agents used for haemolysis. This study investigated five different blood lysis protocols for the isolation of two different bacteria; Escherichia coli (Gram-negative) and Staphylococcus aureus (Gram-positive) from positive blood bottles. Bacterial viability was determined with microfluidic impedance cytometry and standard colony counting, which was also used to determine the extraction efficiency. For all five protocols, the numbers of extracted bacteria were generally high for the two organisms when determined with colony counting (following overnight incubation). However, when determined immediately after extraction with impedance cytometry, the counts were lower for S. aureus. The bacterial viability was also investigated with optical flow cytometry immediately after extraction showing inhibition of S. aureus growth with Sepsityper ® but not with the milder detergent saponin.

title: Automating the triage of rheumatology outpatient referrals: a comparative evaluation of 23 large language models under simple and advanced prompting.
abstract: Triage of rheumatology outpatient referrals is a high-volume administrative task that consumes senior specialist time without advancing patient care. The human triage system is only moderately accurate and reproducible. We assessed whether contemporary large language models (LLMs) are able to perform well enough to support automating this task in practice. In addition, the effects of different prompting techniques on triage accuracy and cost was assessed to help identify the optimal approach. Twenty referral scenarios spanning the urgency spectrum were created by a certified Australian rheumatologist. Four rheumatologists triaged all cases independently and blinded to produce a consensus reference standard; inter-rater reliability was quantified. Twenty-three LLMs each triaged every referral into one of five urgency categories, three times (1380 outputs per referral). The experiment was run with a simple prompt and repeated with an advanced prompt supplying explicit triage expectations and worked examples. In line with published literature, agreement among the four rheumatologists was moderate (Fleiss kappa 0.60; mean pairwise linear-weighted kappa 0.79), with all four assigning categories within one level of each other in 90% of cases. All 2760 model calls returned an interpretable result. Under the simple prompt, performance separated into distinct tiers, larger models were more accurate (Spearman rho = 0.42; P=.047) and accuracy tracked cost. Advanced prompting reduced between-model variance in accuracy 5.3-fold (0.014 to 0.003; Levene P=.01), abolished the size-accuracy association (rho=-0.05; P=.83) and removed the accuracy-cost relationship. The best models matched expert consensus on 18 of 20 cases, comparable to the reproducibility observed among the rheumatologists themselves. Under-triage errors persisted with some LLMs. Contemporary LLMs categorised rheumatology referral urgency with an accuracy and reproducibility comparable to that reported for human triage systems, although human triage was not tested in this study. Advanced prompting appeared to substitute for the reasoning capability of larger models, suggesting that adequate performance on this task may not require the most expensive models. These findings indicate that automation of this administrative task is technically feasible. Candidate models that warrant prospective evaluation are identified.

title: Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy.
abstract: Background The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece. Methods The framework integrates object detection with image-level classification, termed detection-based image classification, to identify diagnostically relevant microscopic structures without requiring exhaustive enumeration of all objects. Five diagnostic categories included vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC), bacterial vaginosis (BV), trichomoniasis (TV), gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis (GU), and healthy vaginal condition (HL). YOLOv26, RT-DETR and EfficientDet0 were independently trained and evaluated using 1,966 microscopic images comprising 11,069 annotated diagnostic objects. Model explainability and computational benchmarking were assessed. The localization quality was independently evaluated by eight clinicians and microbiologists. Results Class-specific analysis demonstrated that TV and GU consistently achieved the highest detection performance across all models (mAP50 = 0.622-0.752), whereas RT-DETR demonstrated superior performance for VVC, BV, and HL. Expert evaluation showed favorable localization, with Good/Excellent ratings in 84.8 and 85.1% of valid evaluations for YOLOv26 and RT-DETR, respectively, with no significant difference between models (OR = 0.97; 95% CI, 0.58-1.61; p = 0.895). Conclusion This study presents an accurate and clinically interpretable framework that integrates microbiota-associated conditions and sexually transmitted infections for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using conventional light microscopy. By linking image-level predictions to localized diagnostic morphology, the framework provides human-verifiable AI evidence as a proof-of-concept prototype. While promising for low-cost implementation, rigorous prospective multi-center validation is required before broad clinical deployment or autonomous diagnosis.
