The findings may also inform future research on standardised education, advanced simulation and aviation safety training. Further research is needed to determine whether these educational approaches improve clinical decision-making, patient safety and operational effectiveness in aeromedical transport. Impact The findings highlight the lack of a clearly defined and standardised competency framework and training pathway for HEMS nursing professionals in Spain. Participants perceived effective HEMS practice as requiring extensive prior critical-care experience, advanced technical competencies, supervised practical training and specific personal attributes, including emotional resilience and physical preparedness. These findings are relevant to HEMS nurses, educators, policymakers and healthcare managers involved in aeromedical services in Spain and may also contribute to international discussions on advanced nursing practice in air medical transport. Reporting method This study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Patient or public contribution No Patient or Public Contribution.

title: Incidence and mortality of severe trauma in South Korea: A nationwide registry-based cohort study, 2016 to 2024.
abstract: Severe trauma is a leading cause of mortality worldwide; however, contemporary data on mechanism-specific incidence trends and factors associated with in-hospital mortality remain limited. We conducted a nationwide cohort study using a South Korean severe trauma registry spanning 2016 to 2024. Severe trauma was defined as an Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥ 16. Annual incidence trends were assessed using negative binomial regression with incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Factors associated with in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression, performed separately for patients with and without prehospital cardiac arrest. A total of 73,232 patients were included, of whom 44.9% had prehospital cardiac arrest. Overall in-hospital mortality was 58.2% (26.0% vs 97.7% for patients without versus with prehospital cardiac arrest, respectively). Transport-related injuries were the most common (53.5%), followed by falls/slips (38.2%). Transport-related severe trauma declined by 3.6% annually (IRR, 0.964; 95% CI, 0.955-0.974; P < .001), whereas falls/slips increased by 3.7% annually (IRR, 1.037; 95% CI, 1.024-1.050; P < .001). Among patients without prehospital cardiac arrest, higher ISS (ISS 25-40: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.45; 95% CI, 3.26-3.64; ISS 41-75: aOR, 6.12; 95% CI, 5.40-6.93) and older age (≥65 years: aOR, 2.87; 95% CI, 2.16-3.84) were the strongest independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. Male sex, unintentional injury, lower-level receiving emergency departments, and falls/slips as the injury mechanism (aOR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.13-1.26) were also independently associated with increased mortality. Among patients with prehospital cardiac arrest, conventional trauma system factors lost prognostic significance; self-harm was the strongest independent predictor (aOR, 2.14; 95% CI, 1.53-3.08). Female sex and injury in nonmetropolitan areas were also independently associated with increased mortality. The epidemiology of severe trauma in South Korea is evolving, with transport-related injuries declining and falls/slips increasing. Preventive strategies for falls/slips should become a public health priority. Given the near-universal mortality among patients with prehospital cardiac arrest, in whom conventional trauma system factors lose prognostic significance, primary prevention strategies, including suicide prevention and injury awareness programs, may yield greater reductions in severe trauma mortality than trauma system development alone.

title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.
abstract: Background AI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking. Objective We synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non-AI-based systems in primary care settings. Methods We conducted a systematic review following the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and reported the results according to PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. We included experimental and quasi-experimental studies evaluating AI-CDSSs used by health care professionals in primary care settings, compared with usual care or non-AI-based decision support systems, and that reported clinician-, patient-, or system-level outcomes, or safety. An information specialist designed the search strategies and systematically reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from inception to June 27, 2025. Reviewers independently performed the selection and extraction processes. Data extraction was informed by the DECIDE-AI and CONSORT-AI (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-AI) reporting guidelines and the APPRAISE-AI tool. We independently assessed the risk of bias using Risk of Bias-2 or Risk of Bias in Non-Randomized Studies of Interventions. Owing to substantial heterogeneity, we conducted a synthesis without meta-analysis and explored heterogeneity using an adapted Non-Adoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread, and Sustainability-informed implementation-context classification. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251119225). Results We identified 4074 records through database searches and 12 additional records through citation searching and trial registration checking. We included 14 records on 11 distinct studies, including 4 experimental and 7 quasi-experimental studies. The risk of bias was high in all experimental studies and serious to critical in quasi-experimental studies. AI-CDSSs showed more consistent positive effects on workflow-related outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, particularly for screening, referral, and alert optimization tasks. Patient-level effects were limited and inconsistent, particularly in more complex contexts involving heterogeneous conditions or preference-sensitive decisions. System-level outcomes were heterogeneous, with isolated improvements in service delivery and utilization outcomes. Safety evaluation was rare and poorly specified. Only 2 studies prespecified safety outcomes, and the reported safety information mainly involved technical malfunctions or self-reported side effects. No study reported clinician interaction measures such as agreement with, override of, or reliance on AI outputs. Interpretation of the findings is limited by substantial heterogeneity, short follow-up periods, predominantly high or critical risk of bias, and evidence derived exclusively from high-income countries. Conclusions AI-CDSSs in primary care may provide more consistent benefits for workflow-related and process-level outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, while evidence on safety remains insufficient to support confident routine implementation. This systematic review reveals an important gap between the rapid development of AI-CDSSs and the lack of robust, comparable evidence to support their reliable use in primary care.

title: Fluoroquinolone Prescribing in Primary Care: Patient Safety, Antimicrobial Stewardship and Forensic Implications Under the Italian Framework-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Fluoroquinolones remain widely prescribed in primary care although regulators have restricted their use because of rare but serious, potentially disabling and irreversible adverse reactions. This narrative review, based on a PubMed search (2008-2026) and regulatory and Italian legal sources, examines fluoroquinolone safety, prescribing patterns and forensic implications from a general-practice and legal-medicine perspective. The evidence behind regulatory warnings is uneven: tendon and aortic events have the strongest observational support, other associations remain uncertain, and absolute risks are low. The US Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency advise against fluoroquinolones for mild or self-limiting infections when alternatives exist, yet US, European and Italian data show persistent use, particularly for uncomplicated cystitis. The forensic analysis is limited to the Italian framework (Laws no. 24/2017 and no. 219/2017) and cannot be generalised to other jurisdictions: prescribing that departs from the product information or from guidelines is not in itself negligent, and liability depends on the individual case, clinical reasoning, information given and documentation. General practitioners and pharmacist-led stewardship, prescription review and patient counselling can support appropriate use. Fluoroquinolones should be reserved for, not withheld from, patients in whom they are clinically indicated. A proposed, non-validated checklist for prescribing and documentation is provided.

title: Relationship extraction for adverse drug events in clinical notes using large language models: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes. Methods We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models. Findings Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings. Interpretation This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety. Funding None.

title: Adverse events in paediatric spinal deformity surgery - 12-year review of specialist spinal deformity practice.
abstract: Aims Adverse events following paediatric spinal deformity surgery in the UK suffers from significant reporting gaps, as current data relies predominantly on voluntary incident submissions. This retrospective study aims to comprehensively assess the incidence of all surgical adverse events at a specialized paediatric spinal orthopaedic centre. Methods A retrospective review of prospectively collected data from January 2010 to December 2022 systematically evaluated perioperative and postoperative adverse events. Patients were analyzed by scoliosis aetiology and adverse events were stratified according to the Clavien-Dindo classification system. Adverse events were further grouped by common themes including implant-related, infection-related, and neurological events. Results A total of 871 paediatric spinal deformity patients undergoing 1,020 operations with at least two years follow-up were identified. Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis was the most common primary pathology with 545 patients (62.6%). Overall, 324 patients (37.2%) experienced an adverse event. Adverse events were categorized by severity: 14.8% grade 1, 5.3% grade 2, 1.1% grade 3A, 14.6% grade 3B, 1.1% grade 4, and 0.1% grade 5. Implant-related issues were most frequent (n = 113, 13.0%), followed by curve progression (n = 33, 3.8%) and persistent pain (n = 33, 3.8%). Neurological events included four complete cord injuries (0.5%) and four incomplete cord injuries which fully recovered (0.5%). One perioperative death occurred. Conclusion In this cohort of paediatric spinal deformity surgeries, over one-third of patients experienced adverse events, predominantly of low severity requiring minimal or no further intervention. Implant-related adverse events were most frequent, while the incidence of both complete and incomplete spinal cord injury, as well as mortality, remained reassuringly low across all procedures.

title: Beyond complication rates: Nationwide neurosurgical compensation claims in a No-fault system.
abstract: Background and objectives Medico-legal claims are often used as proxies for malpractice burden and health care quality. However, they reflect not only underlying clinical events but also the structure of the compensation system through which they are adjudicated. This is particularly relevant in neurosurgery, where high baseline risk and uncertainty in outcome attribution may influence both the propensity to file claims and their subsequent resolution. The objective of this study was to characterize compensation outcomes, clinical domains, decision grounds, and failure-process patterns in a nationwide no-fault neurosurgical dataset. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 620 neurosurgery-related compensation decisions issued in Norway between 2015 and 2024, examining clinical domains, decision grounds, and failure-process patterns. Results Compensation was granted in 93 of 620 decisions (15.0%). Nontraumatic spinal disorders represented the largest domain (225/620, 36.3%) but had a low grant rate (23/225, 10.2%), whereas grant rates were higher in cerebrospinal fluid and shunt disorders (17/43, 39.5%) and trauma (9/29, 31.0%). Within nontraumatic spinal disorders, cervical degenerative disease showed particularly low compensability (8/149, 5.4%). Among granted decisions, the leading failure-process domains were preoperative or diagnostic (35/93, 37.6%), intraoperative or procedural (22/93, 23.7%), and perioperative or postoperative management (13/93, 14.0%). Conclusion In this nationwide neurosurgical series from a no-fault compensation system, compensation was granted in 15.0% of decisions and primarily reflected avoidable failures along the care pathway rather than adverse outcomes alone. Compensation decision data should therefore not be interpreted as complication rates, but as system-filtered signals of compensable and avoidable harm shaped by adjudicatory framework and system design.

title: Crisis Resource Management and Non-Technical Skills Training in Anesthesia: A Narrative Review.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
abstract: Adverse medical events remain a serious concern worldwide; deficiencies in human factors contribute to a large proportion of medical incidents and preventable patient harm. In anesthesiology, where high-risk and complex clinical events are routine, non-technical skills (NTS)-including communication, teamwork, situational awareness, and decision-making-play a critical role in preventing errors during high-acuity emergencies. Furthermore, Crisis Resource Management (CRM) provides a structured framework for enhancing team performance and coordination during medical crises by emphasizing effective leadership, task management, and the optimal allocation of resources within a multidisciplinary team. Simulation-based training is central to teaching and assessing NTS; validated tools such as the Anesthetists' Non-Technical Skills (ANTS) system allow objective evaluation of team performance and behaviors across various clinical scenarios. This modality is particularly effective because it incorporates structured debriefing, enabling practitioners to reflect on their clinical performance in a safe, risk-free environment. Evidence shows that CRM- and NTS-focused simulation training improves crisis response, adherence to protocols, and clinical outcomes. Despite widespread international adoption, CRM and NTS training in Poland remains limited because of institutional and systemic barriers. Implementation of structured CRM and NTS curricula in Poland could enhance patient safety, foster effective teamwork, and reduce medical errors, particularly in high-risk clinical settings, thus aligning Polish medical education with international standards. This narrative review synthesizes global evidence regarding the effectiveness of CRM and NTS training, highlights the benefits of simulation-based training and its impact on long-term skill decay, and identifies gaps in Polish residency programs.

title: Narrative review of non-pharmacological interventions for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: exercise, physical therapy, cryotherapy and acupuncture.
abstract: Purpose Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a heterogeneous, treatment-limiting adverse event of cytotoxic chemotherapy that impairs sensory, motor, autonomic and balance function, and substantially reduces cancer patients' quality of life. Current pharmacotherapy options are limited: duloxetine is the only guideline-recommended agent for established painful CIPN, while no drugs are approved for primary prevention. Non-pharmacological interventions have emerged as promising adjunctive strategies, yet evidence strength varies widely across modalities and patient subgroups. This narrative review aimed to synthesize contemporary clinical evidence of non-pharmacological interventions for CIPN prevention, symptom treatment and functional rehabilitation, to deliver stratified, chemotherapy-specific clinical guidance and identify gaps for future research. Method A narrative review design was adopted, without pre-registration or standardized systematic review screening protocols. Targeted manual literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI and Wanfang Data for peer-reviewed human clinical studies published between January 2018 and March 2025. We focused on four core non-pharmacological modalities for CIPN: multimodal exercise therapy, physical therapy incorporating cryotherapy, acupuncture-based complementary therapies, and behavioral self-management interventions. High-certainty evidence was defined as consistent results from large multicenter randomized controlled trials and network meta-analyses; moderate/low-certainty evidence was derived from small single-center trials and observational studies. Results Cumulative stratified evidence demonstrates clear heterogeneity in intervention efficacy and clinical applicability. Multimodal supervised exercise and physical rehabilitation carry the most consistent high-certainty evidence for both primary CIPN prevention and functional recovery, with significant improvements in numbness, neuropathic pain, balance and muscle strength. Cryotherapy shows robust preventive efficacy exclusively in patients receiving taxane chemotherapy, with insufficient supportive data for platinum or vinca alkaloid regimens. Acupuncture, including warm needle acupuncture, TEAS and electroacupuncture, provides moderate-to-low certainty adjunctive relief for refractory established CIPN symptoms but is not recommended as first-line therapy. Behavioral interventions exert limited direct therapeutic effects on nerve injury, yet effectively improve symptom coping, treatment adherence and long-term self-management. All interventions exhibit favorable safety profiles with minimal severe adverse events when individualized to patient fitness, comorbidities and chemotherapy regimens. Conclusion Non-pharmacological interventions cannot be considered uniformly effective for all CIPN populations; evidence strength and clinical indications differ markedly by modality. Supervised multimodal exercise and physical rehabilitation represent first-line adjunctive strategies for broad CIPN prevention and functional recovery. Cryotherapy is a targeted preventive option limited to taxane-treated patients. Acupuncture serves as secondary adjunctive care for persistent symptoms, while behavioral interventions function as supportive self-management tools. Clinical implementation requires agent-specific patient stratification, individualized intervention prescription, standardized validated CIPN assessment tools, and integrated multidisciplinary oncology rehabilitation pathways. Further large, stratified randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up are required to standardize intervention protocols and validate sustained clinical benefits.

title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke.

Effects of a Standardized Music Intervention on Propofol Requirements and Serum Interleukin-6 and Prolactin in Deeply Sedated Mechanically Ventilated Adults: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Prolonged exposure to sedative agents in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Music interventions have emerged as a promising non-pharmacological strategy to improve patient comfort and potentially reduce sedative requirements. This prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial originally powered to detect differences in cortisol concentrations evaluated the effects of a standardized music intervention on sedative requirements and selected inflammatory and neuroendocrine biomarkers in deeply sedated mechanically ventilated adults. Methods : An open-label randomized controlled trial involving 110 critically ill adults receiving IMV under deep sedation was conducted. Participants were randomly assigned to a 60-min standardized music intervention delivered through active noise-cancelling headphones or to standard care. Changes in sedative requirements, serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and prolactin (PRL) concentrations, physiological parameters, and safety outcomes were assessed. Results : Among participants receiving propofol at the time of the intervention (n = 84), the music intervention group showed a significantly greater reduction in propofol requirements than those receiving standard care (between-group difference 0.079 mg/kg/h, 95% CI 0.008-0.149; p = 0.029). Any reduction in propofol requirements was observed in 46.7% of intervention participants compared with 7.7% of controls. BIS values remained within the target range for deep sedation throughout the intervention period, and no clinically relevant changes were observed in physiological or ventilatory parameters. No significant between-group differences were observed in IL-6 or PRL concentrations after adjustment for baseline values (IL-6: p = 0.606; PRL: p = 0.093). No intervention-related adverse events were reported. Conclusions : A standardized music intervention was associated with reduced propofol requirements without evidence of a between-group difference in BIS trajectory during the intervention period and without clinically relevant physiological instability in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients. No significant between-group effects were observed on IL-6 or PRL concentrations during the study period. As a prespecified secondary analysis of a trial originally powered for a different primary outcome, these findings should be interpreted in that context and warrant confirmation in future randomized trials specifically designed to evaluate music-related effects on sedative requirements. Future randomized trials incorporating appropriate attention-control conditions are warranted to further clarify the specific effects attributable to the musical stimulus.

title: Virological Events During Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: A Multi-Source Evaluation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Virological findings during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy may represent viral loss of control, pre-existing infection, tumour biomarkers, or infection after immune-related adverse event (irAE)-directed immunosuppression. Distinguishing these possibilities is important for treatment and diagnostic decisions. We evaluated virus-specific patterns across complementary data sources. Methods: We evaluated HBV, HCV, HIV, EBV, CMV, HSV, and VZV using FAERS disproportionality analysis (2011Q1-2026Q1), PubMed evidence mapping and appraisal, EBV endpoint verification, and review of ClinicalTrials.gov protocols by start era. Findings were interpreted in relation to prevention, monitoring, endpoint interpretation, and infectious mimic evaluation. Results: Among 200,699 primary suspect ICI reports, only HBV reactivation met the prespecified reporting criterion (226 reports; reporting odds ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.06-1.37); this estimate did not persist with an oncology-restricted comparator (0.81, 0.71-0.94). Same report overlap of HBV with hepatic events and CMV with enterocolitis or pneumonitis identified diagnostically ambiguous settings without establishing event sequence. EBV DNA reflected viral inflammatory activity in some conditions but tumour burden in EBV-associated cancers. The evidence map included 198 publications, with design-specific appraisal of 84. Among 164 trials, conditional viral eligibility appeared in 49.0-57.1% across start eras, whereas longitudinal monitoring appeared in 8.2-19.6%. Conclusions: Reporting patterns were virus-specific and comparator-sensitive. The findings support HBV prevention, confirmation of HCV and HIV control, disease-specific interpretation of EBV markers, and CMV evaluation when inflammation or irAE-directed immunosuppression raises concern for infection. Context-specific assessment may help avoid unnecessary ICI interruption while identifying viral loss of control and infectious mimics.

title: Culture in Multidisciplinary Tumor Conferences: An Exploratory Study of Clinical Decision Making in Two Breast Cancer Centers.
abstract: Background Despite a growing body of research into Multidisciplinary Tumor Conferences (MTCs), the specific relationship with organizational and team culture, especially in the context of Breast Cancer Centers (BCCs), is not well understood. Investigating this connection is critical to understanding how cultural norms, attitudes, beliefs, knowledge, and behaviors shape clinical decision-making and multidisciplinary collaboration. Methods This qualitative study explores the role of organizational and team culture within multidisciplinary tumor conferences in BCCs in Germany via the Grounded Theory Methodology. Analyzing secondary video and interview data from the Patient Participation in Multidisciplinary Tumor Conferences (PINTU) project, we compared two BCCs, each characterized by its own unique pattern of culture. Results Nine interrelated cultural dimensions were identified: physical environment, hierarchy, efficiency, conflict and critique, communication patterns, documentation practices, team cohesion, overt patient empathy, and parallelities. Differences between the centers highlighted these dimensions. BCC1 was characterized by steep hierarchy, efficiency, a reserved emotional expression, formal communication, and outsourced documentation. In contrast, BCC2 featured flatter hierarchies, overt empathy, collective documentation, and greater space for informal dialogue. Conclusion The marked differences between the two German BCCs highlight culture as a pivotal factor in shaping MTC collaboration. Future research into MTCs would benefit from adopting a cultural lens to enhance understanding of these multidisciplinary settings.

title: Chronically pressed for time: a grounded theory of time-pressure experiences among perioperative nurses working in operating rooms and post-anesthesia care units in South Korea.
abstract: Background Time pressure is an important source of occupational stress in clinical nursing and has implications for patient safety. Despite its potential consequences, how perioperative nurses experience and manage time pressure remains underexplored. This study aimed to develop a substantive theory explaining how operating room and post-anesthesia care unit nurses experience and manage chronic time pressure. Methods A grounded theory study was conducted in tertiary general hospitals in South Korea. Twenty nurses working in an operating room or post-anesthesia care unit, with at least 1 year of experience and a perceived time pressure score of ≥ 4 on a validated 7-point scale, participated. Individual in-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted from December 2022 to April 2023. Data were collected and analyzed concurrently using the constant comparative method, and theoretical saturation determined the sample size. Results The core phenomenon was chronically feeling time pressure. Four contributing conditions-professional responsibility and personal traits, the demands of perioperative nursing work, a hierarchical and blame-oriented perioperative work culture, and revenue-driven organizational policies-were identified, and time pressure intensified in situations involving unfamiliar tasks, unpredictable perioperative events, and interpersonal dynamics with colleagues. Participants coped in three ways-proactive self-directed coping, colleague-reliant coping, and resigned acceptance of an unchanging reality. Participants described consequences spanning psychological burden, work-related breakdown, reduced nursing care quality, and threats to patient safety. Over time, participants described relief after task completion, becoming an unwanted version of oneself, and consideration of leaving the profession. These categories were integrated by the core category, "fulfilling tasks while chronically enduring time pressure," which captures how nurses continued to complete required work while the underlying pressure remained unresolved and was reinforced or eased through interactions with others. Conclusions This study explains how perioperative nurses continue to fulfill work demands while chronically enduring time pressure, and how their responses and interactions ease or reinforce pressure within this ongoing process. These findings suggest that understanding and addressing time pressure in perioperative nursing requires attention to individual coping alongside the organizational and interpersonal conditions surrounding the work.

title: When emergency medicine isn't there: a scoping review of global acute care substitutes and complements for disaster response and surge capacity.
abstract: Background Disasters and everyday gaps in emergency care force acute illness and injury to be managed outside of formal emergency medicine (EM) and emergency medical services (EMS) systems. Because EM capacity varies substantially worldwide, this scoping review applies a substitutes-and-complements framework to the mechanisms that deliver acute care in and around formal EM or EMS, classifying their roles as substitutes, complements, or both across levels of EM system maturity and disaster conditions. The resulting typology serves as an inventory of latent disaster surge capacity. Main text Following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL) were searched, yielding 11,161 records. After title and abstract screening, 758 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility and 115 studies were included. We charted study type, country, and EM system maturity, using a codebook derived from American College of Emergency Physicians' (ACEP) International Ambassador country reports, the primary acute-care mechanism, care-delivery context, and COVID-19 relevance. Mechanisms were then classified by whether they substituted for or complemented formal EM. Publications were concentrated in the COVID-19 era (82/115, 71% from 2020 or later) and in high-income, mature-EM settings (United States 30%; 64/115 mature-EM). The most common mechanisms were lay and community first-responder programs (n = 18), hospital-at-home and remote monitoring (n = 15), and telehealth-based emergency and behavioral-health services. Overall, substitutes predominated (75/115), whereas complements (18/115) clustered in mature-EM systems. Conclusions Our inventory of latent surge capacity reframes each mechanism as a potential candidate for transfer across the EM-maturity spectrum: routine substitutes used in low-maturity systems may offer pre-planned crisis capacity for mature systems, while lower-infrastructure telehealth models may provide decision support or partial substitution where formal EM is limited. The substitute-complement balance tracks maturity, but the opportunity lies in translating mechanisms to the settings where they are not currently used as such.

title: Culturally inclusive education for international nursing students in Australia - barriers, educator preparedness and inclusive teaching strategies :An integrative review.
journal: International journal of nursing studies advances
abstract: Aim This review explored and described the state of cultural inclusivity in teaching practices within Australian nursing programs, with particular attention to how those practices shaped the educational experiences of international and other culturally and linguistically diverse nursing students. Background Nursing programs in Australia serve increasingly culturally diverse student cohorts. Cultural inclusion has been a long-standing concern in Australian nursing education, with growing numbers of international and other culturally and linguistically diverse students over the past two decades. Australian qualitative evidence indicates that teaching and learning environments can privilege Western educational and communication norms. Inclusivity is central to student engagement, readiness for practice, and patient safety. Design An integrative review design was adopted to synthesise qualitative evidence related to cultural inclusivity in Australian nursing education. Methods Eligibility permitted qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods empirical studies; all studies meeting the criteria were qualitative. No date limit was applied, which traced how cultural inclusion for international nursing students in Australia evolved over time. Four databases were searched. Eight qualitative studies were included, appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme Qualitative Studies Checklist, and analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Results Analysis of the eight qualitative studies produced five interconnected themes: language and communication barriers; social inclusion challenges and discrimination; educator unpreparedness; curriculum and support limitations; and inclusive teaching strategies. Two themes contained a distinct sub-theme, gendered cultural stigma within Theme 2 and pre-placement readiness within Theme 4. Across the included studies, attention to cultural inclusivity was uneven across academic and clinical learning contexts. Conclusions Available qualitative evidence suggests that culturally inclusive nursing education requires coordinated educator development, explicit curriculum design, structured student support, and inclusive clinical-learning partnerships. The findings support a shift from reliance on individual educator initiative towards consistent institutional expectations, with local evaluation of any strategies adopted.

title: Traumatic Dental Injuries at a Tertiary Dental Trauma Center in Eastern Bavaria: Findings from the Regensburg Dental Trauma Registry.
abstract: Background: Traumatic dental injuries (TDIs) are highly prevalent worldwide; however, structured and standardized datasets remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the demographics, injury characteristics, diagnostic findings, and initial management of TDIs in Eastern Bavaria using data from the Regensburg Dental Trauma Registry (RDTR). Methods : This single-center, retrospective study included 1000 cases with TDIs presented within three days after trauma and treated at the Center for Dental Traumatology, University Hospital of Regensburg, between June 2016 and December 2020, representing the initial cohort of the ongoing RDTR. Data were recorded in a standardized way using a REDCap-based electronic case report form. Descriptive analyses were performed at both the case and tooth levels. Results: The cohort comprised 1000 cases (61.6% male, 38.4% female; median age 13 years [IQR: 7-26]), with a total of 1904 permanent and 528 primary teeth affected. A total of 84.1% presented within 24 h of injury. The age distribution of presenting cases peaked at 2-4 and 7-9 years, irrespective of sex. The relative distributions were similar among children aged ≤3 years. Age groups between 4 and 27 years accounted for larger proportions of male than female registry cases, whereas age groups ≥28 years accounted for larger proportions of female than male registry cases. Falls were the leading cause of injury (67.8%), with cycling being the most common activity at the time of trauma (18.6%). Maxillary central incisors were the most frequently affected teeth in both dentitions (58.7% primary; 54.9% permanent). Luxation injuries predominated in primary teeth (92.8%) compared with permanent teeth (69.8%), whereas fractures were more common in permanent teeth (57% vs. 14.2%). Avulsion injuries affected 202 teeth (139 permanent, 63 primary). Among cases involving at least one avulsed permanent tooth, dry storage was documented in 40.9% of cases. The most frequent initial treatments were splinting (36.5%), restoration or coverage of fractured surfaces (27.0%), and repositioning (11.3%). Conclusions : Standardized registry-based documentation can provide a comprehensive basis for understanding the clinical presentation and management of traumatic dental injuries and for identifying opportunities to improve trauma care. The RDTR establishes a framework for systematic data collection that can support quality improvement, comparative research, and longitudinal evaluation of treatment outcomes. Its continued development and expansion across centers may contribute to a more robust evidence base for the management of TDIs.

title: HepDecide: A Standards-Oriented, Explainable Clinical Decision Support Prototype for the Chronic Liver-Disease Spectrum-Design, Guideline-Grounded Reporting, and a Leakage-Controlled Retrospective Evaluation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Specialist hepatology capacity is small relative to the population needing assessment, so most decisions about whom to investigate for chronic liver disease fall to non-specialists guided by static laboratory indices reported in isolation. This study presents HepDecide, a standards-oriented decision support prototype consolidating stage-specific risk estimation, explainability and guideline-traceable reporting into one physician-facing service, and reports a leakage-controlled retrospective evaluation of its predictive layer. Methods: HepDecide combines stage-specific tabular classifiers, an explainability layer based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) anchored to EASL and AASLD guidelines; outputs are expressed as HL7 FHIR R4 resources, with inputs mapped to LOINC and diseases to ICD-10. Three endpoints were modelled on two publicly available, de-identified cohorts: steatohepatitis versus simple steatosis and histological cirrhosis (F4) in a biopsy-characterised MASLD cohort ( n = 605), and one-year survival among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n = 165). Because patient-level predictions from the original development runs were not retained, the primary evaluation is a separate re-analysis with a locked patient-wise test partition, imputation, scaling and resampling fitted within training folds only, 25 classifier-imbalance configurations per endpoint, training-only calibration, and calibration, precision-recall, decision-curve and SHAP analyses. Results: On the locked test partitions, ROC-AUC was 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.84) for steatohepatitis ( n = 121), 0.81 (0.52-1.00) for cirrhosis ( n = 121; five events) and 0.76 (0.56-0.92) for one-year HCC survival ( n = 33), with Brier scores of 0.096, 0.028 and 0.199. On the same cirrhosis test partition FIB-4 reached an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (0.82-0.99). The five highest-ranked SHAP features accounted for 58-73% of total attribution. Development-phase estimates of 0.90, 0.98 and 0.92 are reported separately as archived values; the cirrhosis estimate is documented in a retained training output, although its original input tables and individual test probabilities are unavailable. No quantitative evaluation of the language-generation layer is claimed, because the corresponding records were not retained. Conclusions: Under leakage-controlled retrospective conditions the predictive layer showed moderate discrimination with wide confidence intervals and did not outperform FIB-4 for cirrhosis. The value of the prototype lies in its standards-oriented, explainable and guideline-grounded design and in a fully documented, reproducible evaluation pipeline; transportability, the text-generation layer and clinical usefulness remain to be established prospectively. HepDecide is intended as a clinician-supervised triage and reporting prototype, not a clinically ready system.

title: Factors Contributing to Discriminatory Nursing Care: A Qualitative Study From Nurses' Experiences.
abstract: Background Justice and non-discrimination are core principles of professional nursing ethics. Yet, growing evidence shows that discriminatory behaviours still occur in clinical environments. This study seeks to explore clinical nurses' experiences and perceptions regarding the factors that lead to discrimination in nursing care. Methods This qualitative secondary analysis employed a conventional content analysis. The dataset comprised 13 in-depth, semi-structured interviews with clinical nurses working in public and private hospitals in Tehran, Iran. These data were originally collected between June 2023 and May 2024 for two primary studies by the same research team. Purposive sampling with maximum variation was used. The data analysis was conducted manually following the method outlined by Graneheim and Lundman. Trustworthiness was maintained by applying Lincoln and Guba's criteria, including member checking, peer debriefing, and external audit. Results Three main categories of factors contributing to discrimination in nursing care were identified: (1) patient-related factors (including social and economic status, demographic characteristics, clinical condition, and interaction and behavioural characteristics); (2) organizational factors (including hospital policies and guidelines, resource constraints, workload pressures, external influence or interference, and lack of formal education on discrimination and justice); and (3) nurse-related factors (including receipt of informal benefits and nurses' prior experiences and emotions). Conclusion Discrimination in nursing care is a complex, systemic issue that results from the interactions between patient traits, organizational needs, and individual nurse factors. Addressing this effectively involves shifting from a solely individual approach to implementing organizational changes, alleviating systemic pressures, and offering focused education on justice and non-discrimination within nursing practice. Implications for the profession and/or patient care The findings provide a multi-level causal framework to guide interventions at the point of care, the unit level, and the educational level. Addressing organizational pressures, informal referrals, and educational gaps can reduce discriminatory practices and promote equitable, dignity-conserving care. Impact This study addresses the question of why discriminatory nursing care occurs, moving beyond descriptive accounts to identify actionable contributing factors. The findings benefit nurses, nursing managers, educators, and policymakers by providing an evidence base for targeted interventions. Reporting method The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) checklist. Patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution.

title: Efficacy and Safety of 5% Topical Caffeine Added to 0.025% Fluocinolone Acetonide Cream for Plaque Psoriasis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether adding topical 5% caffeine to fluocinolone acetonide 0.025% cream (FAC) improves short-term clinical outcomes compared with FAC alone in patients with chronic plaque psoriasis. Patients and methods This randomized, parallel-group, masked, active-controlled clinical trial included 40 patients with chronic plaque psoriasis treated at the dermatology outpatient clinic of Sina Hospital, Tabriz, Iran. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either topical 5% caffeine plus fluocinolone acetonide 0.025% (intervention group, n=20) or topical fluocinolone acetonide 0.025% alone (control group, n=20). Psoriasis severity was assessed using the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) at baseline and weekly for four weeks. Treatment response and adverse events were also recorded. Results Baseline PASI scores were comparable between the intervention and control groups (3.41 ± 1.86 vs 3.79 ± 1.51, respectively; P=0.484). PASI scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at each post-treatment assessment. At week 4, mean PASI was 0.39 ± 0.17 in the intervention group and 2.29 ± 1.31 in the control group (P=0.001). The mean reduction from baseline to week 4 was 3.01 ± 1.48 with 5% caffeine plus FAC and 1.49 ± 1.01 with FAC alone (P Conclusion Adding topical 5% caffeine to FAC produced a greater short-term reduction in psoriasis severity than FAC alone. No adverse events were reported during the 4-week treatment period. Larger randomized trials with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm efficacy and characterize longer-term tolerability. Trial registration Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), IRCT20091012002581N10, registered on October 28, 2023; https://irct.ir/trial/73367.

title: Zolpidem Intoxication Associated with Probable Reverse Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy and QT Prolongation: A Case Report.
abstract: Zolpidem is a widely prescribed non-benzodiazepine hypnotic. A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with altered mental status after intentional ingestion of approximately 300 mg of zolpidem; the blood zolpidem concentration was 674 µg/L approximately 8 h after ingestion. The initial ECG already showed QTc prolongation (499 ms). She developed chest discomfort and modest high-sensitivity troponin T elevation, and echocardiography showed transient left ventricular dysfunction (ejection fraction 42%) with basal-to-mid regional wall motion abnormalities and relative apical sparing, suggestive of probable reverse stress-induced cardiomyopathy. Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no coronary plaque or significant stenosis. On hospital day 2, telemetry captured a brief monomorphic ventricular run and QTc later peaked at 681 ms. Follow-up echocardiography on hospital day 5 showed recovery of left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 60%) and resolution of the regional wall motion abnormalities. These findings cannot be attributed solely to zolpidem. Stress may have contributed to the cardiomyopathy. Mild hypokalemia and left ventricular dysfunction may have reduced repolarization reserve. The peak QTc occurred after blood zolpidem concentrations had substantially decreased and may have reflected evolving stress-induced cardiomyopathy or concurrent exposure to cardiovascular medications. Cardiac evaluation and continuous monitoring should be considered when zolpidem intoxication is accompanied by cardiac symptoms, biomarker elevation, or ECG abnormalities.

title: Real-world comparative effectiveness of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, and CapOx as second-line chemotherapy for advanced biliary tract cancer.
abstract: Background Advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) has a poor prognosis following progression on first-line gemcitabine plus cisplatin. However, evidence comparing second-line chemotherapy regimens remains limited. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of fluorouracil, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX); fluorouracil, leucovorin, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI); and capecitabine plus oxaliplatin (CapOx). Patients and methods Adults with advanced BTC who received first-line gemcitabine plus cisplatin followed by second-line FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, or CapOx between January 2010 and July 2025 were identified from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients who subsequently received molecularly targeted therapies were excluded. The study included 825 patients receiving FOLFOX, 184 receiving FOLFIRI, and 149 receiving CapOx; after 1:1 propensity score matching, the respective comparisons included 182 and 149 patients per group. Overall survival (OS) and treatment-related adverse events were compared between the matched cohorts. Results The median OS was comparable between FOLFOX and FOLFIRI (5.7 months vs 5.8 months, P = .958) and between FOLFOX and CapOx (5.7 months vs 5.8 months, P = .803). The overall adverse event profiles were also comparable. However, FOLFOX was associated with lower rates of neutropenia but higher rates of thrombocytopenia than FOLFIRI. In contrast, FOLFOX and CapOx demonstrated similar toxicity despite modest differences in anemia and thrombocytopenia. Conclusion This real-world study demonstrates comparable survival outcomes among FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, and CapOx as second-line chemotherapies for advanced BTC. These findings support individualized regimen selection based on patient characteristics and toxicity profiles.

title: Comparable efficacy of extraoral and intraoral photobiomodulation in preventing oral mucositis during high-dose methotrexate therapy in pediatric oncology: A single-blind randomized controlled trial.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Purpose This prospective randomized controlled clinical study compared intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation (PBM) for the prevention of chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric oncology patients. Methods A total of 155 patients (1-18 years), receiving high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) for leukemia, lymphoma, or osteosarcoma, were randomized to PBM-IO (n = 73) or PBM-EO (n = 82). Preventive PBM was administered daily from hospital admission through discharge. Both protocols used red light with equivalent dosimetry (660 nm, 100 mW, 1 J per point). PBM-EO required 30 s/session, whereas PBM-IO required approximately 6 min, excluding patient handling time. OM occurrence, severity (WHO scale), plaque index, and pain (numeric rating scale) were assessed on days 0, 3, 5, and 10 after HDMTX infusion. Results The overall OM occurrence was 35.5%, with no significant difference between PBM-IO (41.1%) and PBM-EO (30.5%) groups (p = 0.168). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups for OM severity, pain, salivary pH, or plaque index at any time point (p > 0.05). Multivariable ordinal logistic regression demonstrated that PBM modality was not independently associated with OM severity. As expected, increasing age (OR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.04-1.25; p = 0.004) and higher HDMTX dose (OR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.03-1.49; p = 0.021) were significantly associated with greater OM severity. Median pain scores remained 0 at all assessment points in both groups. Conclusion Extraoral PBM demonstrated comparable effectiveness to intraoral for OM prevention in pediatric patients undergoing HDMTX chemotherapy, while reducing application time.

title: Obstetric Fistula in Somalia: A Narrative Review of Burden, Lived Experience, Health-System Gaps, and Pathways to Elimination.
abstract: Obstetric fistula is a preventable childbirth injury and an important marker of failure to provide timely, accessible, and high-quality emergency obstetric care. In Somalia, direct epidemiological evidence remains limited, but the available literature documents fistula related to prolonged obstructed labor, delayed access to repair, iatrogenic injury, low awareness, and profound social consequences. This narrative review synthesizes indexed evidence on obstetric fistula in Somalia and relevant regional literature, with emphasis on burden, pathways to injury, healthcare delays, women's decision-making autonomy, treatment barriers, surgical outcomes, rehabilitation, and prevention. A focused search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was updated through August 8, 2026. Only peer-reviewed journal articles indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE or Scopus were included. Somalia-specific studies were prioritized, while high-quality regional and global evidence was used where local data were insufficient. The literature indicates that fistula in Somalia should be understood as the end result of interacting clinical and health-system failures rather than as an isolated surgical condition. Prolonged obstructed labor remains the central pathway, while limited antenatal care, referral barriers, delayed emergency cesarean delivery, financial and geographic constraints, restricted healthcare decision-making for some women, and inadequate access to specialist repair can extend preventable morbidity. A sustainable response requires prevention of new cases, early detection, rapid referral, respect for women's informed consent, year-round repair capacity, functional continence assessment, psychosocial and reproductive rehabilitation, and national outcome surveillance. Somalia-specific research should now move beyond treatment-seeking samples toward population-based burden estimates, prospective studies of emergency obstetric delays, standardized surgical outcome reporting, and long-term follow-up after repair.

title: Association Between <i>DPYD</i> Gene Variants and Severe Fluoropyrimidine-Related Toxicity in Asian and African Populations: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Introduction Fluoropyrimidines are widely used against solid tumors, and severe treatment-related toxicity remains a major clinical problem. DPYD variants prioritized in predominantly European guidelines may not capture those most relevant elsewhere, and their predictive value in Asian and African study populations is unclear. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies reported DPYD variants with toxicity outcomes in Asian or African study populations receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. The risk of bias was assessed using the design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and findings were synthesized narratively by variant, following the PRISMA 2020. Results Twenty-three studies published between 2007 and 2025, spanning 14 countries, were included, six at low risk of bias, nine at moderate, and eight at high. Recurrent variants were c.1627A>G ( DPYD *5), c.85T>C ( DPYD *9A), c.1905+1G>A ( DPYD *2A), c.496A>G, c.1896T>C, and c.2194G>A ( DPYD* 6). Associations were most consistent for c.85T>C, with unadjusted odds ratios of 2.3 for hand-foot syndrome and 2.7 for diarrhea in South India, and an adjusted odds ratio of 4.35 for mucositis in Tunisia, all for any-grade toxicity. For c.1905+1G>A, adjusted odds ratios were 6.47 for grade 3-4 neutropenia and 5.76 for diarrhea in Bangladesh. Findings for c.1627A>G were inconsistent in direction. Only one study corrected for multiple testing, and the designs, regimens, grading systems, and genotyping platforms were highly heterogeneous. Conclusion Evidence for population-specific DPYD variation is strongest in Asian populations. Data from the African populations represented in the available studies, confined to Tunisia, Algeria, Sudan, and Zimbabwe, are too sparse for strong conclusions. No carrier of the four guideline variants was found among 150 genotyped Zimbabwean patients, yet 36% of the 50 who received fluoropyrimidine had severe adverse events. Harmonized prospective studies reporting genotype-specific numerators and denominators are needed before population-specific variants can be considered clinically actionable.

title: Effect of a potassium-competitive acid blocker on the gut microbiota in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomized pilot study.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Background and aim Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are routinely used in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding associated with dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, long-term PPI use has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. Tegoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), may exert distinct effects on the gut microbiome. This study compared the longitudinal effects of tegoprazan and pantoprazole on gut microbiota composition in patients with angina undergoing PCI. Methods This prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study randomized 38 patients 1:1:1 to tegoprazan 50 mg once daily, pantoprazole 40 mg once daily, or no acid-suppressive therapy for 24 weeks. Five participants did not provide baseline fecal samples, and nine discontinued participation before week 24. Thus, 24 participants with paired baseline and week-24 fecal samples were included in the final analysis. Fecal samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Results No drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in any group. Observed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness was significantly higher at week 24 than at baseline in the overall cohort (p = 0.003) and P-CAB group (p = 0.016), whereas the Shannon index showed no significant changes. Paired PERMANOVA with permutations restricted by patient ID revealed significant differences in Bray-Curtis beta diversity between baseline and week 24 in the P-CAB group (R² = 0.070, p = 0.031) and PPI group (R² = 0.059, p = 0.008), but not in the no acid-suppressive therapy group (R² = 0.021, p = 0.691). In the formal cross-arm analysis, the treatment group-by-visit interaction was not significant for Bray-Curtis beta diversity (R² = 0.021, pseudo-F = 0.505, p = 0.270). Although nominal within-arm taxonomic changes were observed, no treatment group-by-visit interaction survived Benjamini-Hochberg correction in ANCOM-BC2. Conclusion Tegoprazan was well tolerated, with no drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding during the 24-week follow-up. Both acid-suppressive treatment groups showed modest longitudinal microbiome changes. The taxon-level findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of treatment-specific differential effects. Larger, adequately powered studies are required to confirm these observations.

title: Digital health-enabled life-course management of endometriosis: from early recognition and assisted diagnosis to symptom monitoring and self-management.
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease that often requires longitudinal care across recognition, diagnostic assessment, symptom control, fertility planning, treatment transitions, and recurrence reassessment. The information required for these decisions is frequently fragmented across patient experience, clinical encounters, imaging, treatment history, and health-system records. This narrative Review synthesizes digital-health applications in endometriosis according to clinical function, data source, and translational maturity. Literature was identified through structured searches of major biomedical databases and targeted reference screening, with emphasis on clinically relevant validation, prospective evaluation, and implementation evidence. The most mature applications include structured electronic symptom capture, electronic patient-reported outcomes, selected app- or telehealth-based support, and digital pain interventions. AI/ML approaches for imaging, risk estimation, molecular classification, fertility outcomes, and recurrence prediction are technically active but are commonly limited by internal validation, uncertain calibration and action thresholds, and sparse prospective clinical-utility evidence. We propose a clinician-supervised life-course framework in which patient-expressed data, clinical and imaging information, treatment history, fertility goals, and follow-up data are integrated to support early recognition, assisted diagnosis, monitoring, shared decisions, and reassessment. The target state is clinical coherence rather than maximal data capture, supported by explicit institutional responsibility for review, escalation, feedback, privacy, equity, and human oversight. Progress toward routine use will depend on external validation, interoperable data architecture, low-burden measurement, prospective pathway evaluation, and accountable implementation.

title: Is intra-articular injection of high-concentration ozone (O2-O3) more effective in treating knee osteoarthritis?: A multicenter cohort study.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a prevalent joint disorder globally, resulting in pain and disability, with various treatment options available. Intra-articular ozone (O2-O3) administrations are an efficient therapeutic approach commonly employed in this condition. With this study, we aimed to compare the effect of varying ozone concentrations on treatment outcomes. This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at 2 distinct university hospitals between May 2023 and September 2024. Medical records of patients who underwent intra-articular knee ozone injections were retrospectively reviewed and divided into 2 groups as 15 μg/mL (group A) and 25 μg/mL ozone (group B). Participants' pain scores were measured by Numeric Rating Scale, functional status by Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and quality of life by 12-item Short Form Health Survey before and at 1 and 3 months following ozone therapy. A total of 190 patients were screened; 159 patients (105 females, 54 males) were included in the study, with 77 patients in group A and 82 patients in group B. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in all outcomes during follow-up. After adjustment for multiple comparisons, between-group differences in Numeric Rating Scale scores were not statistically significant at either 1 or 3 months. Group B had significantly better Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, 12-item Short Form Health Survey physical component summary, and 12-item Short Form Health Survey mental component summary scores at both follow-up assessments (all Holm-adjusted P < .001). The 25 μg/mL concentration was associated with more favorable short-term functional and quality-of-life outcomes and a trend toward greater pain improvement. These findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

title: Sustaining agency after a fall: navigating healthcare and adjusting everyday life - a qualitative interview study.
abstract: Background Falls among older adults are a major public health concern and are associated with recurrent falls, functional decline, fear of falling, and reduced quality of life. Older adults presenting to emergency departments (EDs) following a fall are often discharged directly home despite ongoing rehabilitation and support needs. Although person-centred approaches are recommended in international guidelines, less is known about older adults' and relatives' experiences following an ED visit for a fall. This study aimed to describe older adults' and their relatives' experiences of a fall, including the ED visit and the transition back home. Method A qualitative study design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with older adults aged 75 years and older and their relatives. Participants had attended the ED following a fall but were discharged without hospital admission. Seventeen participants (11 older adults and 6 relatives) were recruited. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis according to Graneheim and Lundman. Results The analysis generated one overarching theme, Sustaining agency through recovery across care and everyday life, which reflected how older adults and their relatives sought to manage daily life following a fall. Both groups described addressing immediate care needs while simultaneously adapting to longer-term changes in everyday life. Participants described difficulties navigating healthcare services to access follow-up care and rehabilitation, contributing to feelings of insecurity, financial strain, and increased responsibility. A persistent fear of falling affected daily activities and required adaptations and new roles for both older adults and their relatives. Despite these challenges, many participants demonstrated resilience and an ability to manage daily life following injury. Individual coping strategies and support from relatives were described as central to managing everyday life and healthcare contacts. Conclusions Older adults discharged home after a fall may benefit from coordinated, person-centred follow- up that supports rehabilitation, recovery, and fall prevention. Despite variation in support needs, participants described a common need for clearer guidance and improved support structures, while also demonstrating considerable resilience and capacity for self-management. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled deep clinical phenotyping in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: from patient subtypes to precision care.
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a clinical syndrome defined by shared manifestations but produced by diverse combinations of cardiometabolic, vascular, inflammatory, renal, pulmonary, atrial, skeletal-muscle, and aging-related mechanisms. This heterogeneity limits the value of classifications based only on left ventricular ejection fraction and helps explain why many mechanistically plausible interventions have produced neutral average results. Deep phenotyping can move the field from descriptive heterogeneity toward biologically coherent and clinically actionable subtypes by integrating clinical trajectories, advanced imaging, exercise and invasive hemodynamics, circulating biomarkers, multiomics, and digital physiology. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers methods to combine these high-dimensional data, but statistical clusters should not be equated with disease endotypes. A useful subtype must be reproducible across cohorts, anchored to plausible biology, associated with a distinct clinical course, and able to improve diagnosis, therapeutic selection, or clinical-trial design. This Review examines the translational continuum from experimental HFpEF models to human patient subtypes, summarizes the main deep-phenotyping domains and AI approaches, and proposes seven clinically interpretable subtype families: cardiometabolic-inflammatory, hypertensive-vascular aging, atrial myopathy, pulmonary vascular-right ventricular, cardiorenal-congestive, peripheral-frailty, and specific etiologic phenocopies. Current evidence supports a layered treatment strategy in which broadly effective therapies, particularly sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, are combined with phenotype-directed management of obesity, diabetes, mineralocorticoid receptor activation, atrial fibrillation, congestion, pulmonary vascular disease, and physical deconditioning. The central next step is prospective validation of dynamic subtype assignments in external populations and phenotype-enriched trials. Phenogroup labels should therefore be regarded as pragmatic, transitional proxies for dominant mechanisms when those mechanisms cannot yet be measured directly at the individual-patient level; their value lies in improving decisions while the field moves toward fully individualized mechanism-based treatment. Deep phenotyping will be clinically valuable only when it changes a decision and improves an outcome, rather than merely increasing descriptive complexity.

title: Sustained three-year impact of a physical therapy quality improvement project in the medical intensive care unit.
abstract: Importance Early rehabilitation and mobility are components of care bundles and clinical practice guidelines for patients who are critically ill. Improved delivery of physical therapy is associated with decreased intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS). Barriers exist to optimizing the delivery of physical therapy. Analyses of quality improvement (QI) are often narrow in scope. Care improvements may not persist. Opportunities remain to improve physical therapy delivery to patients in the medical ICU (MICU) while analyzing care delivery and ICU LOS. Objective The objective was to determine whether a QI initiative sustained improvement in physical therapy delivery and associations with ICU LOS in the MICU. Design This was a before-during-after comparative design. Setting The study took place in the MICU at a quaternary, academic medical center. Participants The study included 13,058 MICU admissions. Intervention(s) The intervention was a multifaceted physical therapy program including multidisciplinary education, physical therapists integrated into multidisciplinary rounds, automatic physical therapist consult orders, electronic health record hard stop for bedrest orders, and increased physical therapy staffing including a program coordinator physical therapist. Main outcome(s) Our primary outcomes were delivery, timing, and frequency of physical therapy, as well as ICU LOS. Measure(s) Main outcomes were assessed by (1) odds of receiving physical therapy while in the MICU and (2) time from MICU admission to first physical therapist session and (3) ICU LOS. Results During the intervention, an increased proportion of admits received physical therapy with a nearly 4-fold increase in the odds of receiving physical therapy. Time to first physical therapist session was decreased while the proportion of days with physical therapy in the ICU was increased. In adjusted analysis, ICU LOS decreased modestly. Findings were similar for 3 years post-QI. Conclusions Despite variable resources and increased illness severity in the post-intervention period, durable improvements in the percentage of patients receiving physical therapy, odds of receiving physical therapy, time to physical therapy, and proportion of days with physical therapy occurred for 3 years post-QI. Secondarily, the during and post periods were associated with modest reductions in ICU LOS. Relevance This work is applicable to the fields of: critical care rehabilitation, quality improvement, ICU mobility, and health care delivery.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of emergency nurses regarding sepsis nutritional management: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Nutritional management is an important component of supportive care for patients with sepsis, but its implementation in emergency settings may be challenging alongside other time-critical priorities. This study assessed emergency department (ED) nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding nutritional management in patients with sepsis. Methods This multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among ED nurses from hospitals in Jiangsu Province, China, between January and May 2026. A structured Chinese questionnaire with satisfactory internal consistency was used to assess KAP, with KAP levels descriptively classified using modified Bloom's cut-off criteria. Multivariable linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with KAP scores, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to further evaluate the direct and indirect relationships among KAP domains. Results A total of 630 valid questionnaires were analyzed, including 558 female nurses (88.6%). The median knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 9.00 (9.00, 15.00), 40.50 (36.00, 45.00), and 29.00 (22.25, 36.00), respectively, out of possible ranges of 0-18, 9-45, and 9-45. In multivariable analyses, nurses without recent training had significantly lower knowledge scores (β = -4.676, 95% CI: -5.386 to -3.965, p p p p p p p p Conclusion ED nurses showed insufficient knowledge, positive attitudes and moderate practice toward nutritional management in patients with sepsis. The observed associations of knowledge with both attitude and practice support the potential value of targeted, practice-oriented training, together with standardized documentation and workflow-based support.

title: Nationwide Q Fever Hospitalizations in Italy, 2014-2023: Evidence of Underrecognition and a Sardinian Hotspot.
abstract: Background Q fever is a zoonotic disease caused by Coxiella burnetii. In Italy, serologic evidence shows exposure in humans and livestock, but surveillance data are sparse, and underreporting is likely. We aimed to characterize Q fever-related hospitalizations in Italy during 2014-2023 and examine environmental risk correlates. Method We conducted a nationwide retrospective study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Hospitalizations with ICD-9-CM code 083.0 as primary or secondary diagnosis were included. We calculated hospitalization rates by age, sex, and region and described clinical characteristics. We linked hospitalizations with climatic, livestock, and land-use data; for Sardinia, we fitted Bayesian spatial regression models including bovine, ovine, and caprine density, temperature, precipitation, and land use. Results We identified 428 hospitalizations (67% male), corresponding to a rate of 0.07 per 100 000 person-years. Rates were highest in children and older adults. The overall case fatality ratio was 2.4%. The most frequent Q fever-related concomitant diagnosis was pneumonia. Sardinia had the highest case count and adjusted hospitalization rate, 7-fold the national rate (0.55 vs 0.07). Spatial models for Sardinia showed hotspots in the north of the island and a 12% increase in spatial hospitalization risk per 10 bovine heads/km 2 (adjusted relative risk 1.12, 95% credible interval 1.03-1.24). Conclusions Q fever causes an underrecognized burden of hospitalizations in Italy, with marked regional heterogeneity and a Sardinian hotspot associated with high cattle density areas. Clinical awareness, surveillance, and One Health interventions are warranted in high-risk areas.

title: P2Y<sub>12</sub> inhibition, adenosine signaling, and bone remodeling: differential skeletal pharmacology of antiplatelet agents.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, and fragility fractures frequently coexist in older adults, creating an important overlap between antiplatelet therapy and orthopedic care. This narrative review examines mechanistic, preclinical, observational, and perioperative evidence concerning the skeletal effects of aspirin, P2Y 12 inhibitors, and other clinically relevant antiplatelet agents. Purinergic signaling provides biological plausibility for interactions between platelet inhibition and bone remodeling because P2Y 12 , P2Y 1 , P2X 7 , adenosine receptors, and equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 (ENT1) regulate osteoblast differentiation, osteoclast activity, inflammatory responses, and tissue repair. Aspirin shows dose- and context-dependent skeletal effects, whereas clopidogrel has been associated with impaired osteoblast mineralization in preclinical studies and conflicting fracture-risk estimates in observational cohorts. Direct skeletal evidence for prasugrel and other agents remains limited. Selected preclinical studies suggest that ticagrelor-associated ENT1 inhibition can enhance adenosine-dependent osteogenic signaling; however, clinical evidence is limited to one retrospective cohort in which ticagrelor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was associated with lower fracture risk than clopidogrel-based DAPT, while prospective skeletal outcome data are lacking. Perioperative antiplatelet management in orthopedic surgery should remain guided by cardiovascular indications, thrombotic risk, and bleeding risk. A conceptual framework may help define priorities for evaluating skeletal outcomes during antiplatelet therapy. However, current evidence is insufficient to support antiplatelet selection or switching on the basis of presumed skeletal effects.

title: National Guidelines for Public Health Emergency Surveillance within the Brazilian Unified Health System.
journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
abstract: Objective To describe the national guidelines for public health emergency surveillance within the Brazilian Unified Health System ( Sistema Único de Saúde , SUS). Guidelines The increasing frequency of health, environmental, and technological events has led to more public health emergencies, requiring systems capable of early threat detection, risk assessment, and timely response. Public health emergency surveillance is an integral component of health surveillance and encompasses strategies such as indicator-based, event-based, hospital-based epidemiological, mass gathering, wastewater, community-based, and participatory surveillance. These strategies are complementary and should be supported by continuous monitoring and systematic risk assessment, while incorporating multisectoral approaches, risk communication, and One Health. Strengthening public health emergency surveillance involves integrating information systems, building workforce capacity, institutionalizing contingency plans and standard operating procedures, activating situation rooms and emergency operations centers, conducting timely outbreak investigations, communicating risks, and conducting intra-action and after-action reviews. Factors such as territorial inequalities, social vulnerabilities, and population-specific characteristics influence risk exposure, detection capacity, and the impacts of emergencies, underscoring the need to incorporate equity into surveillance explicitly. Conclusion The guidelines help consolidate public health emergency surveillance as a core component of preparedness and response within the Unified Health System, reinforcing participatory, integrated, and equity-oriented approaches to protect health and reduce harm.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases.
