abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: Circadian-melatonin signaling in general anesthesia: molecular mechanisms and perioperative implications.
abstract: Anesthesia and surgery are delivered to a temporally organized organism whose physiology is governed by the suprachiasmatic nucleus, peripheral molecular clocks, and pineal melatonin signaling. This review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence on how anesthetic agents, surgical stress, and the perioperative environment interact with circadian and melatonergic signaling, and on whether that interaction can be targeted therapeutically. In rodent and cellular studies, volatile and intravenous anesthetics alter clock function in an agent- and phase-dependent manner; proposed mechanisms include GABAergic and glutamatergic modulation of entrainment, transcriptional and chromatin-level repression of CLOCK-BMAL1/PER-CRY signaling, and metabolic coupling through CaMK-CREB, AMPK, SIRT1, and GSK-3β. These mechanisms have not been confirmed in humans. In patients, these effects are inseparable from surgical injury, opioids, fasting, inflammation, and disrupted light-dark exposure, all of which suppress melatonin amplitude, delay its onset, and promote internal desynchrony. Melatonin signals through MT 1 and MT 2 receptors to produce chronobiotic, anxiolytic, and antinociceptive effects, whereas the mitochondrial, redox, and anti-inflammatory actions, described almost exclusively in animal and cellular models, require substantially higher exposures and have not been demonstrated in surgical patients; the two arms are pharmacologically distinct and should not be pooled. Clinically, preoperative anxiolysis with melatonin in adults is the most consistently supported indication, whereas evidence for postoperative sleep, analgesia, delirium prevention, and organ protection remains heterogeneous and of low certainty. Most trials have used fixed clock-time dosing without measuring internal circadian phase or achieved plasma exposure, so null results cannot distinguish an ineffective mechanism from an inadequate intervention. The circadian-melatonin axis remains a plausible perioperative target, but clinical translation requires phase-aware, exposure-informed, and adequately powered trials.

title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Aim To characterize the global development, collaboration structure, publication landscape, citation influence and thematic evolution of research on selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and GLP-1-based multi-receptor agonists in T2DM. Methods A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 3736 original articles published between 2004 and 2025 and retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Publication trends, research contributions, collaboration networks, citation impact and thematic evolution were evaluated using complementary bibliometric indicators and network analysis. Results Annual publication output increased substantially. Selective-only studies remained the cumulative core of the evidence base, while mixed/comparative and multi-receptor-only studies expanded rapidly in recent years. The United States led in research output and international connectivity, and Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly were the most prominent institutional contributors based on author affiliation analysis. Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism was the leading source journal. Research output was highly concentrated across countries but more widely distributed across institutions and authors. Thematic emphasis shifted from incretin biology and glycemic efficacy toward cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, obesity, integrated treatment strategies and real-world evidence. Major trials, particularly LEADER and REWIND, and ADA/EASD consensus statements exerted strong citation influence. Sensitivity analysis supported the overall robustness of the principal findings. Conclusions Research on GLP-1-based agonists in T2DM has expanded rapidly and shifted toward an integrated cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework. Studies of selective GLP-1RAs remain central to the literature, while studies of newer GLP-1-based multi-receptor agonists are contributing to its diversification. Evidence remains comparatively less developed for longer-term outcomes of emerging agents, treatment sustainability in routine care, patient experience and diverse populations and settings.

title: Is the surgeon or hospital a larger cost driver for lumbar fusion? A hierarchical Bayesian approach using time-driven activity-based costing.
Daily Peer Review Reduces Replanning and Activity-Based Costs in a Network of Community Radiation Oncology Centers.
Calculating the Unit Cost for a Patient Treated at the Outpatient Department of National Hospital Galle, Sri Lanka
abstract: Abstract Background The outpatient department (OPD) functions as the main ambulatory gateway to hospital care and often absorbs a very high patient volume in publicly financed health systems. Reliable unit-cost estimates are therefore essential for rational budgeting, priority setting, and efficiency improvement. In Sri Lanka, where public services are provided free at the point of use, empirical costing evidence from hospital OPDs remains limited. This study was undertaken to generate a context-specific estimate for a major tertiary hospital in Southern Sri Lanka. Objectives To calculate the provider-side unit cost of a patient visit to the OPD of National Hospital Galle (NHG) and to determine the proportions of expenditure attributable to consultation-related staffing, medicines, and diagnostic investigations. Methods A retrospective descriptive costing study was conducted at NHG for the period 1–31 October 2024 using a step-down costing approach. Overhead, intermediate, and final cost centres were identified, and recurrent and capital costs were estimated using secondary institutional data. Joint costs were apportioned using appropriate allocation statistics, including floor area and service volume. Building costs were excluded because the OPD buildings were more than 20 years old and their present replacement values could not be estimated reliably within the study framework. Results During the study month, 31,406 patients were treated at the NHG OPD. The total monthly provider cost was LKR 12,466,029.32, producing a unit cost of LKR 396.93 per patient visit. Salaries represented the largest expenditure category at 59.62% of total cost, followed by drugs at 23.01%, investigations at 4.69%, and other recurrent and capital inputs at 12.68%. Among overheads, electricity and water accounted for notable shares of operating expenditure. Conclusions The estimated OPD unit cost at NHG is low relative to several published international estimates, while the internal cost structure shows a clear predominance of personnel expenditure. These findings provide a practical evidence base for local planning, budgeting, and future comparative efficiency studies. Extending similar costing work to other hospital departments and across different levels of care would strengthen allocative decision-making in Sri Lanka.

title: Cost-effectiveness of a blended learning approach for maternal and child health professional development training in Ethiopia: a quasi-experimental economic evaluation.
abstract: Introduction Ethiopia has integrated blended learning into the national continuous professional development system to address persistent gaps in in-service training access, cost and quality and strengthen primary healthcare providers' capacity to deliver reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health (RMNCH) services. However, evidence on its effectiveness and cost-effectiveness remains limited, particularly regarding provider adherence, client experience and quality of care. Guided by implementation science principles, the Kirkpatrick framework and activity-based costing, we assessed the cost-effectiveness of blended learning for improving RMNCH service delivery. Methods We conducted a quasi-experimental, post-test economic evaluation with a separate control group. Data were collected in October 2025 through facility audits, direct observations and exit interviews with providers trained through blended learning and untrained providers in control sites. The primary effectiveness outcomes were composite quality indices integrating adherence to evidence-based antenatal care (ANC) and family planning practices and client experience of care. Costs were estimated using activity-based costing from a health-system perspective. We assessed cost per trainee, incremental costs and savings and cost-effectiveness. Results Blended learning improved ANC provision scores by 10.4 percentage points and family planning scores by 25.9 percentage points compared with controls (Cohen's d=0.72 and 1.30 respectively; p Conclusion Blended learning improved RMNCH service quality while reducing training costs. Sustaining and scaling this approach will require investment in digital infrastructure, supportive implementation systems and health-worker capacity, alongside longer term monitoring to determine whether improvements in provider performance translate into population-level RMNCH outcomes.

title: Cost Analysis of Maxillofacial Trauma Treatment in Three Major Ministry of Health Malaysia Hospitals.
Hospital cost structure and resource utilization in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty and hip resurfacing arthroplasty: a single-center comparative cost analysis.
abstract: Introduction Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) and hip resurfacing arthroplasty (HRA) are joint-preserving procedures used in different anatomical and clinical settings. Although they are not competing treatment options, both require substantial hospital resources. This study compared institutional cost structure and resource utilization associated with UKA and HRA from the hospital-provider perspective. Methods This retrospective, single-center study included 68 unique patients undergoing UKA ( n = 36) or HRA ( n = 32) between January 2023 and July 2024. Each patient contributed one index hospitalization, one surgical procedure, and one independent analytical observation. The primary outcome was total index-hospitalization cost. Secondary outcomes included operating-room personnel costs, costs incurred outside the operating room, medical costs, and non-medical costs. Individual cost components and correlations with length of stay were exploratory. The association between procedure type and total index-hospitalization cost was assessed using a gamma-log generalized linear model adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4. Secondary and exploratory comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure. Results Mean total index-hospitalization cost was €5,561.53 for UKA and €6,631.18 for HRA, an unadjusted difference of €1,069.65 ( p p = 0.008). Medical costs were higher for HRA (€2,918.90 vs. €1,985.23; q q = 0.0035). Costs incurred outside the operating room and non-medical costs did not differ significantly. Implant costs were higher for HRA (€2,544.55 vs. €1,554.55; q Conclusion UKA and HRA showed distinct patterns of index-hospitalization costs and resource utilization. Higher implant expenditure was an important component of the observed cost difference. These findings represent a hospital-level comparison of two distinct arthroplasty pathways and should not be interpreted as evidence favoring either procedure. Detailed evaluation of procedure-specific cost structures may support hospital budgeting, resource allocation, implant procurement, and operational planning.

title: Bedside screening of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae using selective agar plates: A low-cost, laboratory-independent approach for rural healthcare facilities.
abstract: The global surge of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) poses a critical threat to patient safety in intensive care units (ICUs). In low- and middle-income countries, routine CRE surveillance is often limited by the lack of microbiology laboratory infrastructure and trained personnel in peripheral healthcare facilities, resulting in reliance on empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy and limited capacity to detect silent transmission. This study evaluated the operational feasibility, safety, and phenotypic agreement of a decentralized, laboratory-independent bedside CRE screening protocol using pre-formulated selective chromogenic agar and a low-cost portable incubator. Dual rectal swabs were collected from 220 ICU patients at Viet Tiep Hospital, Vietnam. One sample was processed using standard centralized laboratory procedures as the reference method, while the parallel sample was processed at the bedside by frontline nursing staff, including direct plate inoculation and point-of-care incubation. Diagnostic agreement, inter-reader reliability, procedural contamination, and operational feasibility were assessed. Gastrointestinal CRE carriage was identified in 26 of 220 patients (11.8%), with the KESC group accounting for 76.9% of positive cases. The bedside protocol demonstrated 100% phenotypic concordance with standard laboratory cultures, with 100% sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. Blinded assessment showed complete inter-reader agreement (κ = 1.0). No environmental cross-contamination was detected on CRE-negative plates (0.0%; 95% CI: 0-4.1%). The decentralized bedside screening model, costing less than US$1 per test, demonstrated high diagnostic agreement and operational feasibility when performed by frontline nursing staff in a non-sterile ICU environment. This approach may provide an affordable alternative for CRE surveillance in resource-limited healthcare facilities where centralized microbiology laboratory infrastructure is unavailable.

title: Costs of TB preventive treatment: insights from five sub-Saharan African countries.
journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease

title: Physical Performance Outcomes and Programme Delivery Costs of ELDERPLAY, a Community-Based Multicomponent Exercise and Recreational Intervention for Older Adults: A Non-Randomized Controlled Evaluation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined the association between participation in a community-based multicomponent physical and recreational programme (ELDERPLAY) and changes in physical performance and frailty-related outcomes in adults aged 65 years and older, and estimated programme delivery costs. The study was designed as a quasi-experimental, non-randomized controlled evaluation conducted in a community setting. Methods: Community-dwelling older adults (n = 184) were allocated to an intervention group (n = 103) or a control group (n = 81) through voluntary enrolment and geographic matching. Participant enrolment and data collection were carried out between July 2022 and December 2023, after ethics approval had been obtained. The intervention consisted of 20 supervised sessions (two per week) combining Vivifrail-based multicomponent exercises with simple recreational activities. Primary outcomes were physical performance and frailty-related function, assessed using the Short Physical Performance Battery and the Timed Up and Go test. Secondary exploratory outcomes included actigraphy-derived daily step count, heart rate, and sleep parameters, recorded over seven consecutive days at a single intermediate assessment point. Analyses were conducted using analysis of covariance and generalized estimating equations adjusted for cholesterol, COVID-19 vaccination and Barthel Index score. Programme costs were estimated using an activity-based costing approach. Results: Compared with the control group, participants in the intervention group showed greater improvement over time in balance, gait performance, chair-stand performance and overall physical performance (time × group interaction: gait performance p p p p Conclusions: Participation in a community-based multicomponent exercise programme incorporating recreational activities was associated with improvements in clinically relevant physical performance outcomes in community-dwelling older adults. The programme was delivered in full at a mean delivery cost of €92.3 per participant in a real-world community setting. Because allocation was not randomized, the groups differed at baseline, and outcome assessment was carried out by a single unblinded assessor who designed and coordinated the programme but did not deliver the sessions, these findings are associative and require confirmation in a randomized trial. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07864831 (retrospectively registered).

title: Paying for clinical AI: The bill is not the cost.
abstract: Clinical AI is increasingly integrated into electronic health record workflows, but its cost is difficult to define. Health systems may pay through usage-based services, subscription or enterprise licenses, local hosting, or combinations of these approaches. Usage-based pricing introduces a distinct problem because billing units such as tokens or billable sessions are vendor-defined and may vary across data types, languages, and over time. Fixed licensing agreements can make vendor charges more predictable, while locally hosted AI models shift spending toward infrastructure and personnel. Regardless of the payment structure, the full resources required to use and maintain AI, including engineering, validation, oversight, and rights to clinical data, are difficult to capture. As the complexity of multimodal and agentic systems increases, so will that of the payment structures. Health systems will need to proactively develop ways to accurately measure the cost of AI use, evaluate its clinical value, and negotiate agreements with AI vendors that allow for regular reassessment of prices and terms. Doing so will help ensure that AI does not become yet another driver of healthcare spending detached from value delivered.

title: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis in trauma: rethinking mechanism-based triage criteria in low- and middle-income countries.
abstract: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis (CT-CAP) is routinely ordered in trauma centers across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) after road traffic accidents, with mechanism of injury listed as a standalone indication alongside physiological and clinical criteria, a framework derived from Advanced Trauma Life Support guidelines developed in North American resource-abundant settings. Even in well-resourced environments, the evidence base for mechanism-only imaging is weaker than commonly assumed: of established mechanism criteria, only death of another occupant, fall distance, and prolonged extrication time demonstrate meaningful predictive value for serious injury requiring trauma center resources. The landmark REACT-2 randomized controlled trial found no mortality benefit of whole-body CT over selective imaging in 1083 severely injured patients. In resource-constrained LMICs, where CT availability is critically limited and imaging costs fall directly on patients, the case against indiscriminate mechanism-based CT-CAP is even stronger. For isolated extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma-positive findings in hemodynamically stable patients, targeted regional CT is evidence-supported, with escalation to full CT-CAP reserved for high-grade injury or hemodynamic deterioration. LMICs should move beyond uncritical adoption of high-income country protocols and develop prospective, data-driven local criteria for CT-CAP use calibrated to their patient populations, injury patterns, and resource realities.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Adjunctive Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: Secondary Analysis of EMBOLISE.
Quantifying Pharmaceutical Waste Burden and Management Costs: Implications for Healthcare Risk Management and Governance.
abstract: Background Pharmaceutical waste represents an emerging operational, financial, and governance challenge within healthcare systems, particularly in resource-limited settings where routine waste monitoring remains limited. Evidence regarding pharmaceutical waste burden and its associated management costs is still scarce, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Methods This study assessed pharmaceutical waste burden and management costs using routinely collected hazardous medical waste data from a regional referral hospital in Indonesia between 2023 and 2024. Because pharmaceutical waste was not routinely segregated or directly quantified, pharmaceutical waste quantities were estimated using a model-based proportional approach rather than direct measurement, assuming a base-case proportion of 5% of total hazardous medical waste. Management costs were estimated using an outsourced treatment tariff of USD 0.44/kg. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using alternative assumptions ranging from 3% to 6%. Results During the 24-month observation period, total hazardous medical waste generation reached 182,428.32 kg, with a mean monthly generation of 7601.18 kg. Under the base-case scenario, estimated pharmaceutical waste generation was 380.06 kg/month, equivalent to approximately 53 g/bed/day. The estimated pharmaceutical waste management cost was USD 166.28/month (USD 1995.36 annually). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated monthly costs ranging from USD 99.77 to USD 199.54 across alternative scenarios. Conclusion Pharmaceutical waste contributes a measurable and recurrent operational and financial burden within hospital waste management systems and may serve as an indicator of healthcare operational efficiency and governance performance. Routine waste segregation, direct quantification, and systematic monitoring may support risk-informed decision-making, resource optimization, and sustainable healthcare waste management.

title: Economic Evaluation of Prolonged Hypothermic Oxygenated Machine Perfusion Enabling Daytime Liver Transplantation.
Institutional volume and postoperative efficiency as determinants of in-hospital mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting: a multilevel analysis in São Paulo, Brazil.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between hospital procedural volume, postoperative efficiency, and in-hospital mortality and costs among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting in the public health system of the State of São Paulo, Brazil. Methods This retrospective ecological study analyzed isolated coronary artery bypass grafting procedures recorded in the Brazilian Hospital Information System in São Paulo between 2008 and 2024. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, postoperative length of stay, and inflation-adjusted hospitalization costs. We assessed mortality using Poisson regression models, while we analyzed costs and length of stay using linear mixed-effects models with hospital-level random intercepts. We performed sensitivity analyses using alternative inclusion criteria. Results We included 82,398 procedures from 45 hospitals. Median annual hospital volume was 71 procedures. Overall in-hospital mortality was 6.75%, and mean length of stay was 12.2 days. High-performing centers showed substantially lower mortality (4.82% versus 9.94%), shorter length of stay (12.3 versus 16.5 days), and lower adjusted costs (R$24,246 versus R$28,633) compared with low-performing institutions. At the institutional level, longer mean postoperative stay was positively associated with higher hospital-level mortality rates (incidence rate ratios: 1.015 per day; 95%CI 1.006 - 1.024), though reverse causation cannot be excluded given the ecological study design. Higher annual procedural volume was independently associated with lower costs, whereas prolonged hospitalization significantly increased expenditures. Between 2008 and 2024, total surgical volume declined, while mortality decreased, suggesting progressive improvements in care quality. Conclusion Higher institutional volume and greater postoperative efficiency are associated with lower mortality and reduced costs after coronary artery bypass grafting in the public health system of the State of São Paulo, Brazil. Postoperative length of stay emerged as a key marker of institutional performance and clinical course.

title: Assessment of the duration of continuous EEG monitoring in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
abstract: Background Electroencephalography (EEG) can detect seizures and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Because a standard duration of continuous EEG monitoring to capture these complications has not been established in aSAH, we compared a standard 6- or 7-day cEEG monitoring protocol versus longer periods of monitoring. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of aSAH patients ≥18 years old grouped by standard monitoring protocol (6-7 days, group 1) and those with longer monitoring (>7 days, group 2). Clinical characteristics, EEG features, length of stay (LOS) and functional outcome were compared using univariate analyses. Multivariable analyses tested the association between the groups and vasospasm, DCI, LOS, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Results 19 patients met criteria for group 1 and 16 patients for group 2. We found no difference in EEG's detection of worsening abnormal EEG activity, vasospasm and DCI. ICU and hospital LOS in group 2 were nearly double that of group 1 (ICU: 25.5 (19.5-35) vs. 14 (11-21) days, p = 0.0003; hospital: 32.5 (29.5-48) vs. 18 (13-29) days, p = 0.003). Good outcome (mRS ≤2) at discharge and at 6 months was similar in both groups (21.1% vs. 0% and 56.3% vs. 46.2%). In multivariable analysis, EEG duration was independently associated with ICU and hospital LOS but not with vasospasm, DCI, and mRS at 6 months. Conclusions Longer EEG monitoring correlated with significantly longer ICU and hospital LOS but not with vasospasm, DCI, and functional outcome at 6 months. Larger studies to confirm our findings are warranted.

title: Cost-effectiveness of newborn screening for phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism in Hubei, China.
abstract: Background: Newborn screening programs have long been recognized as a cornerstone of public health policy, enabling early detection and mitigation of severe neonatal conditions. However, evolving socioeconomic conditions and shifts in birth prevalence necessitate comprehensive evaluations of their long-term cost-effectiveness and health impacts. This study aimed to assess the societal costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) associated with screening for phenylketonuria (PKU) and congenital hypothyroidism (CH) in Hubei Province, China, by comparing three scenarios: no screening, single-condition screening (PKU or CH), and dual-condition screening (PKU+CH). Methods: To evaluate the long-term costs and health effects of dual-condition screening in Hubei, focusing on screening both phenylketonuria (PKU) and congenital hypothyroidism (CH) compared to no screening or screening for only one condition.A decision-analytic model was developed to project outcomes over a 78-year horizon (aligned with Hubei’s 2023 average life expectancy). The analysis incorporated data from 942,627 newborns screened between 2011 and 2023, utilizing medical records from the Hubei Maternal and Child Health Hospital and published literature. Costs were evaluated from a societal perspective, encompassing healthcare expenditures, municipal care services, and productivity losses due to morbidity. A 5% annual discount rate was applied to both costs and effectiveness. Findings: We revealed that dual screening for PKU and CH generated 36,663.3 total QALYs (55.05 per screened individual), significantly surpassing single-condition screening (6,220.65 QALYs for PKU; 30,442.65 for CH). Cost savings were substantial: ¥161.6 million with PKU screening alone and ¥1.33 billion with CH screening, primarily driven by reduced productivity losses and municipal care burdens. The dual new screening strategy demonstrated synergistic benefits, underscoring its superior cost-effectiveness. Interpretation: This study highlights dual newborn screening as a fiscally responsible intervention that enhances population health outcomes. It also underscores the substantial benefits of China's newborn screening program, 40 years after its initial implementation in the country. On this basis, we advocate for sustained public investment in early diagnosis and treatment to alleviate long-term societal burdens.

title: Remote patient monitoring and caregiver education for children with failure to thrive: a quasi-experimental study.
abstract: Background Failure to Thrive (FTT), also known as growth or weight faltering, is characterized by inadequate weight gain, poor growth, and potential developmental delays. Affecting up to 10% of outpatient pediatric populations and 5% of hospitalized children, FTT is particularly common among children with medical complexity. Traditional management depends on frequent in-person visits, which create barriers and delay interventions. To address these barriers, this study evaluated Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) combined with caregiver education as a proactive, cost-conscious approach to FTT management. Methods A quasi-experimental cohort study was conducted with children (ages 1-10 years) with FTT and requiring feeding tube support. Families transmitted weekly weight and feeding data using Bluetooth-enabled scales, supplemented by structured caregiver education. Outcomes included weight, hospital and emergency department (ED) utilization, and cost of care. Results All 15 participants completed the six-month RPM program. Forty-two percent of participants ( n = 6) achieved upward weight trends, 50% ( n = 8) maintained stable weights, and 8% ( n = 1) experienced a weight decline. Hospitalizations averaged 0.33 per patient pre-intervention, 0.60 during the intervention, and 0.33 post-intervention. Median hospitalizations were 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 0) pre-intervention, 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) during the intervention, and 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 0.5) post-intervention. Emergency department visits averaged 1.07 pre-intervention, 0.60 during the intervention, and 0.87 post-intervention. Median ED visits were 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) pre-intervention, 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) during the intervention, and 1 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 2) post-intervention. Median costs increased during the intervention phase before declining in the post-intervention period, despite mean costs being skewed upward by high utilizers. Conclusion An RPM program integrated with caregiver education demonstrated feasibility in supporting proactive management of pediatric FTT. The intervention supported weight monitoring in this medically complex pediatric population, although healthcare utilization and costs varied across study periods. These preliminary findings support RPM may be a useful approach for managing pediatric FTT.

title: Cost-effectiveness of pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy versus placebo plus chemoradiotherapy for high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer in Saudi Arabia: A model-based economic evaluation.
abstract: Background Adding pembrolizumab to standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) has shown substantial survival benefits in newly diagnosed, high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), but its economic value in Saudi Arabia has not been established. This study assessed the cost-effectiveness of pembrolizumab plus CCRT versus placebo plus CCRT as first-line treatment for high-risk LACC from the perspective of the Saudi Arabian healthcare payer. Methods A partitioned survival analysis model was developed to project lifetime costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) for a hypothetical cohort of women with high-risk LACC in the Saudi public healthcare sector, using resource use patterns consistent with major tertiary care and specialized cancer centers. Clinical efficacy data were obtained from the KEYNOTE-A18 trial. Costs were sourced from official Saudi price lists, local hospital data, and a formal Structured Expert Elicitation process, and were reported in 2025 United States dollars. Health state utilities were derived from the literature. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. Future costs and QALYs were discounted at an annual rate of 3%. Comprehensive deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess uncertainty. Results Adding pembrolizumab to CCRT resulted in an incremental gain of 3.51 life-years and 2.93 QALYs at an additional cost of $242,043 compared with placebo plus CCRT. At its current list price, the regimen yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of $82,626 per QALY. At a willingness-to-pay threshold of $90,000 per QALY, the probability of the pembrolizumab regimen being cost-effective was 67%. Conclusion Pembrolizumab in combination with CCRT provides substantial clinical benefits in patients with high-risk LACC in Saudi Arabia. At the current price, this regimen is likely to be considered cost-effective. The analysis provides a strong, evidence-based rationale for significant price negotiations to ensure that the regimen delivers value to the Saudi healthcare system.

title: Smart Paper Technology for maternal and newborn health data in The Gambia: A qualitative study of early implementation.
abstract: Many low- and middle-income countries rely on paper-based maternal and child health records that are often incomplete, fragmented, and difficult to use for continuity of care and decision-making. Smart Paper Technology (SPT), a hybrid paper-digital documentation system, has been proposed as a practical alternative to fully electronic medical records in resource-constrained settings. This study explored the early implementation of SPT in maternal and infant health services in The Gambia, focusing on feasibility and acceptability. We conducted a qualitative descriptive implementation evaluation guided by Rapid Assessment Procedures (RAP) in two pilot facilities in the Western Region of The Gambia between September and December 2024. Data were collected through 30 semi-structured interviews; four focus group discussions with 30 participants spanning facility-level clinical, management, and administrative staff, Ministry of Health staff, and technical and implementing partners; and non-participant observations across key service delivery areas. Data were analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Participants described SPT as feasible and broadly acceptable because it built on familiar paper-based workflows, was introduced through a participatory process, and offered advantages in reporting, information retrieval, and maternal-infant record linkage. However, these benefits were contingent on the implementation context. Key challenges included uneven training coverage, dual documentation, limited internet connectivity, scanning and data capture errors, storage constraints, and concerns about data governance. Staff adapted through peer mentoring, remote troubleshooting, and local workarounds. Participants emphasised that successful scale-up would require sustained training, clear governance arrangements, adequate human and technical resources, and a phased transition to government ownership. SPT offers a practical pathway towards digitisation in maternal and infant health services in LMICs, but its success depends on strong organisational systems, workforce support, and implementation processes that are responsive to routine service realities.

title: Beyond therapeutic feeding: a call for integrated strategies to end child malnutrition in Somalia.
abstract: Somalia records one of the highest global burdens of child wasting and stunting, with approximately 1.7-1.85 million children under five estimated to be affected by acute malnutrition annually during 2022-2025, including approximately 421,000-513,550 children with severe acute malnutrition. For over two decades, the dominant policy response has been community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), a curative intervention that treats clinical endpoints rather than underlying drivers. Despite meeting international cure-rate standards, CMAM alone cannot address the food insecurity, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), microbial and parasitic infectious diseases, health-system, and climatic drivers that perpetuate malnutrition. This paper integrates recent Somali survey, programme-evaluation, and administrative data to show that the national burden of acute malnutrition has remained high despite continued treatment scale-up, with stunting falling only 9.7 percentage points over 24 years, relapse after discharge remaining a documented challenge, and nationally representative Somalia-specific estimates of CMAM treatment coverage remaining unavailable. Diagnostic discordance between screening tools leaves an unknown share of wasted children undetected, and persistent sex- and region-based disparities highlight structural gaps. Ending child malnutrition in Somalia requires rebalancing investment from an emergency, treatment-centred paradigm toward integrated, multisectoral strategies combining therapeutic feeding with WASH investment, maternal and infant feeding support, primary health-care strengthening, climate-resilient livelihoods, and shock-responsive social protection. We propose four policy shifts: sustaining CMAM while addressing diagnostic gaps, mandating nutrition-sensitive financing, institutionalizing relapse prevention, and expanding anticipatory financing. These shifts require governance reforms and multi-year donor commitment to address the determinants of child nutrition in Somalia comprehensively.

title: Awareness, Attitudes, and Expectations of Indian Cancer Patients and Their Caregivers on Hereditary Cancers and Genetic Testing at a Tertiary Cancer Centre in India.
From Thoracotomy to Robotic Platforms in Thoracic Surgery: Technical Evolution, Simulation-Based Training, and Surgical Outcomes.
abstract: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.

title: Pediatric Disaster Preparedness at Rural and Critical Access Hospitals: A Mixed-Methods Study.
abstract: Objectives Over 80% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits in the United States occur outside of children's hospitals. Although previous studies have described gaps in pediatric readiness, few studies have focused on pediatric disaster preparedness at rural and critical access hospitals (CAHs). During periods of pediatric surge, CAHs may be forced to manage pediatric patients with delayed transfer times. This mixed-methods study, conducted by the Region V for Kids (RV4K) Pediatric Disaster Center of Excellence, elicited strengths and barriers to pediatric disaster preparedness in rural and CAHs. Methods We conducted a qualitative study of clinicians from CAHs in the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Region 5. After completing a demographic survey, respondents were invited to participate in focus groups about pediatric disaster preparedness, followed by an open-response questionnaire about how RV4K can support rural and CAHs. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Focus group transcripts and questionnaire responses were analyzed using a constant comparative approach to identify themes. Results Of the 41 survey respondents, 19 participated in focus groups. Most study participants worked at EDs seeing Conclusions Our study engaged directly with staff at rural and CAHs to gain insights about pediatric preparedness that will be used to develop resources specifically tailored to CAHs' unique clinical needs.

title: "The past is never dead; it's not even past"<sup>☆</sup>. From EuCARE experience to future pandemics: Evidence-based lessons for a prepared Europe.
journal: Journal of infection and public health
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has left a deep mark on healthcare systems and society worldwide. In this context, the project "European Cohorts of Patients and Schools to Advance Response to Epidemics" (EuCARE), responding to an emergency request from the European Union under the Horizon Europe programme, addressed the pandemic from different perspectives. It investigated the clinical impact of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, the performance of vaccines and diagnostics, post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), schooling and vaccine hesitancy. This short report combines a review of project outputs with a consultation of the ten project principal investigators and work package leaders, all of whom responded; no formal qualitative analysis was applied. The primary objective was to identify the operational and methodological challenges encountered during EuCARE and to explore their implications for the design and implementation of future pandemic research. Investigators reported four challenges requiring coordinated action at national and European level: fragmented ethics and regulatory procedures; difficulty in rapidly mobilising specialised personnel; vaccine hesitancy and other aspects of behavioural preparedness; and vulnerable diagnostic supply chains. From these experiences we derived six "pills of preparedness": evidence-based science, workforce surge capacity, data collection and management, specialised professional roles, collaborative networks, and evidence-based communication. These lessons derive from a single consortium and from the self-reported experience of a limited number of investigators, and should be interpreted accordingly.

title: The Impermanence of Public Health Gains-Lessons Learned from Measles Resurgence, Bangladesh, 2026.
abstract: The global resurgence of measles is a major public health concern. After the success of its Expanded Programme on Immunization, Bangladesh experienced a measles resurgence in 2026. The country faced major setbacks after measles vaccination coverage declined because of political instability, discontent among field-level staff, change in procurement policy, COVID-19-related service disruptions, and delayed supplementary immunization campaigns. During March 15-September 13, 2026, Bangladesh reported 170,638 suspected and 20,006 confirmed measles cases, including 919 deaths among suspected and 100 deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases. The outbreak disproportionately affected unvaccinated and underimmunized children. Political turmoil during 2024-2025 disrupted vaccine procurement, delayed mass vaccination campaigns, weakened the health workforce, and compromised financial and logistic continuity. Simultaneously, disruptions in vitamin A supplementation and worsening child malnutrition amplified disease severity. To prevent future resurgence, immunization programs must be depoliticized, supported by buffer vaccine stocks, strengthened through microlevel surveillance, and integrated with nutrition and primary healthcare services.

title: Epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of a large-scale upsurge of dengue in the rohingya refugee camps and host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, 2021 to 2024: A retrospective study.
abstract: Background Dengue emerged as a new public health threat in the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, in 2021 and expanded into large-scale upsurges in subsequent years. Evidence on dengue epidemiology and clinical presentation in protracted refugee settings remains limited, despite the need for stronger outbreak preparedness and case management in these contexts. Objectives To describe the epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of the dengue upsurge among Rohingya refugees and surrounding host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, and to identify predictors of inpatient admission and diagnostic positivity patterns. Methods This retrospective observational study used anonymized surveillance data from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) dengue patient database. Rapid diagnostic test (RDT)-confirmed dengue cases identified across 36 IOM-supported health facilities in Ukhiya and Teknaf between 1 October 2021 and 31 December 2024 were included. Demographic, epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory variables were summarized using descriptive statistics. Weekly case counts were aggregated by epidemiological week and calendar year, and epidemic growth and decay phases were modelled using phase-specific Poisson regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with inpatient admission, while separate models examined associations between delay in presentation and RDT positivity patterns, adjusting for age and sex. Results A total of 35,581 RDT-confirmed dengue cases were reported, of which 90.2% occurred among Rohingya refugees. The median age was 17 years (IQR 7-30), and 46.0% of cases were among children aged 0-14 years. Annual caseload increased from 1,011 in 2021-11,752 in 2022, 10,669 in 2023 and 12,149 in 2024, with seasonal peaks during the monsoon period and progressively later peaks and longer epidemic tails over time. Poisson models showed decreasing growth rates across years (r = 0.449 in 2021 to r = 0.091 in 2024) with increasing doubling times, while decay rates remained broadly comparable (halving time ~4.4-6.0 weeks). Overall, 8.0% of cases required inpatient admission, 1.3% were referred, and four deaths were reported (case fatality Conclusion Sustained dengue preparedness is required in Cox's Bazar, including strengthened surveillance, community-based early referral, targeted monitoring of high-risk groups, environmental vector control, and phase-appropriate use of NS1 and IgM/IgG diagnostics to reduce missed diagnoses and prevent progression to severe disease. These findings highlight the need for a policy shift from episodic outbreak response toward sustained dengue preparedness in humanitarian settings, including strengthened surveillance systems, integrated diagnostic strategies, community-based early referral, and coordinated vector control interventions.

title: Episode of epidemic thunderstorm asthma in Shanxi China September 2025: epidemiological characteristics, mechanisms, and emergency management strategies.
abstract: Background In September 2025, our emergency department (ED) experienced a sudden influx of 39 asthmatic patients following a thunderstorm. Based on our data, we summarized demographic features of the 39 patients, reviewed literature to describe thunderstorm asthma pathogenesis, and compiled patients' emergency management processes. Method This was a retrospective observational study. Clinical data were collected from electronic medical records and subsequent follow-up. Data were summarized and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results Following standardized management, all patients were successfully managed, ensuring their safety. In this study, male patients accounted for a slightly higher proportion than females. The mean age of the 39 patients was 31.62 ± 12.86 years. The vast majority of patients had a history of allergic rhinitis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated peripheral blood eosinophil counts in some patients. The primary medications administered for thunderstorm asthma included inhaled corticosteroid, short-acting muscarinic antagonists, and short-acting β 2 -adrenergic agonist. Discussion This study indicates that thunderstorm-related asthma in northern China predominantly occurs in early autumn, with Artemisia pollen as the major allergen. In terms of pathogenesis, thunderstorms induce rupture of Artemisia pollen and release tiny allergenic particles that are inhaled into the airway. Antigens are presented by dendritic cells to activate CD4⁺, Th2 cells, which secrete cytokines such as IL-4 and initiate IgE-mediated allergic inflammation, thereby triggering acute asthma attacks. Meteorological early warning and preventive strategies, as well as hospital-based specialized emergency systems are required.

title: Signal detection of substance-related emergency department visits during UEFA EURO 2024 in Germany: enhancing public health surveillance for future mass gatherings.
abstract: Introduction Germany hosted the men's UEFA European Championship (EURO 2024) in summer 2024, attracting millions of visitors across multiple cities. Mass gathering events (MGEs) can rapidly alter social environments which impact substance use behaviors, potentially increasing demand on local healthcare systems. In response, the German national public health institute (Robert Koch Institute, RKI) piloted substance-related indicators using routine emergency department (ED) data from the Emergency Department Data Registry throughout the tournament to explore their applicability for real-time emergency department surveillance. Methods We aimed to monitor substance use patterns in ED visits during EURO 2024 by developing an umbrella syndrome definition for psychotropic substance intoxication (SATX) and two more specific syndrome definitions for acute alcohol intoxication (ATX) and substance intoxication other than alcohol (STX), based on diagnoses, chief complaints, and age criteria. Descriptive analyses compared identified cases during the tournament period (14 June-14 July 2024) with a reference period. Analyses were stratified by sex, age group, and triage level. A quasi-Poisson regression model was used to estimate expected values and 95% prediction intervals (95% PI) for each indicator during the tournament period. Signals were detected when observed case counts exceeded the upper threshold of the 95% PI. Results Between 1 January 2018 and 9 September 2024, 5,602,933 visits from 39 EDs were included. Across both the tournament and reference periods, SATX, ATX, and STX cases were more common among males, particularly for ATX. Most SATX and ATX cases occurred among individuals aged 30-59 years, whereas STX cases were most frequent among those aged 20-39 years. Relative increases in triage level 4 cases were observed during the tournament period. During EURO 2024, signals exceeding the upper threshold of the 95% PI were detected for all indicators, including 16 SATX, three ATX, and 13 STX signals. The largest deviation was observed for SATX on 29 June 2024, with 127 observed cases compared to 74 expected cases. Conclusion This study demonstrated that rapid changes in substance-related ED utilization during MGEs can be effectively monitored using the syndrome definitions and signal detection methods, whose application can support public health surveillance during future events.

title: Modeling framework and reference model for data-driven simulation of patient flows in emergency departments.
Reclaiming human clinical reasoning in generative AI-enabled healthcare: a perspective on cognitive agency, skill evolution, and accountability.
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) are transforming clinical decision support systems (CDSS) from traditional discrete predictions into fluent, context-aware clinical narrative generation. Although these capabilities substantially improve the efficiency of clinical workflows, they also introduce distinctive cognitive challenges: highly fluent and seemingly plausible medical narratives may reshape the way physicians construct clinical meaning and make analytic judgments. This perspective paper introduces the concept of Narrative Cognitive Substitution (NCS), proposed as a testable mid-level theoretical construct, which describes the hypothesized shift in human cognition from active hypothesis generation to passive retrospective validation when GenAI outputs pre-organize diagnostic reasoning and therapeutic pathways. We further propose a Skill Evolution Framework that characterizes the potential effects of GenAI on physician competence across five trajectories: Augmentation, Restructuring, Deskilling, Never-skilling, and Mis-skilling. In addition, we analyze the resulting Accountability Gap: although algorithmic outputs are increasingly embedded in clinical decision-making, decision influence is distributed across clinicians, institutions, developers, and deployers, yet professional accountability and final decision authority remain formally concentrated on the individual physician. To address these systemic challenges, we propose a human-centered governance framework -presented as design hypotheses requiring prospective evaluation- encompassing user interface design (embedding risk-adaptive cognitive friction), medical education (establishing targeted, protected AI-free reasoning exercises ("Reasoning Cleanrooms")), and institutional policies (implementing substantive human oversight and algorithmovigilance). We argue that the goal of digital health governance should not be to maximize automation, but rather to safeguard human cognitive agency, diagnostic vigilance, and layered, distributed accountability within AI-enabled healthcare systems.

title: Establishing a regional prehospital whole blood program in a border community: the Trauma Regional Advisory Council-V initiative in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas.
abstract: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable death after traumatic injury, and the prehospital interval is the most critical, underused window for hemostatic intervention. Low Titer O-Positive Whole Blood (WB) improves survival in military and civilian settings, yet its implementation in rural, border-region communities with limited healthcare infrastructure remains largely undescribed. The Rio Grande Valley (RGV) of Texas-a predominantly Hispanic, medically underserved region along the USA-Mexico border-presents logistical, demographic, and infrastructural challenges that make prehospital hemorrhage control both harder and more consequential. We describe how the Trauma Regional Advisory Council-V (TRAC-V, Cameron, Hidalgo, Starr, and Willacy counties, South Texas) conceptualized, operationalized, and expanded a regional prehospital WB program across four RGV counties, encompassing emergency medical service (EMS) agencies and trauma-receiving hospitals. The region is defined by extended transport intervals, a predominantly rural, medically underserved population, limited trauma infrastructure relative to population burden, and high injury rates. A phased, stakeholder-driven implementation methodology spanned eight domains: (1) stakeholder engagement and governance development; (2) memorandum of understanding between TRAC-V, the South Texas Blood and Tissue Center, EMS agencies, and hospitals; (3) evidence-based clinical protocols and transfusion criteria; (4) a structured blood product rotation system to minimize waste; (5) standardized provider training and credentialing; (6) regional data collection and quality improvement; (7) grant funding and equitable equipment distribution to rural EMS agencies; and (8) community blood drive engagement. The TRAC-V regional WB program demonstrates that a structured, collaboration-driven methodology can establish prehospital whole-blood capability in resource-limited, geographically challenging environments. This stepwise model offers a replicable framework for regional advisory councils and EMS systems in underserved communities. Prospective outcome data will inform programmatic refinements and contribute to the national evidence base for prehospital WB programs.

title: Nutritional Care After Hospital Discharge (NutriCAD): protocol for a stepped-wedge, multicentre, randomised controlled trial in paediatrics.
Advancing Ultrasound Beamforming With Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Datasets, Benchmarks, and Computational Challenges.
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is a widely used diagnostic tool, and beamforming techniques are integral to its performance. Traditional methods such as delay-and-sum (DAS) and delay-multiply-and sum (DMAS) have limitations in terms of image quality and computational efficiency. Recently, deep learning approaches have shown significant promise in improving ultrasound beamforming, offering enhanced image resolution and quality, alongside potential for real-time processing. This review is aimed at providing a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in deep learning-based ultrasound beamforming. It focuses on analyzing various deep learning models, their applications, challenges, and the integration of hardware optimization strategies to enhance performance and efficiency. The review examines a range of deep learning models applied to ultrasound beamforming, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), transformer-based models, and hybrid approaches. It also discusses the challenges associated with dataset limitations, model interpretability, and the risk of overfitting. Furthermore, the review explores hardware acceleration using field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), along with cloud-edge frameworks for real-time inference. The findings highlight the potential of deep learning models to outperform traditional methods in terms of image quality and resolution. However, challenges such as the need for large and diverse datasets, the black box nature of deep learning models, and the risk of overfitting remain. Hardware optimization through FPGAs has proven effective in enabling real-time processing, but the integration of edge computing with cloud-based solutions offers promising avenues for balancing performance, latency, and energy efficiency. Deep learning-based ultrasound beamforming has great potential to advance medical imaging. Future efforts should enhance model generalizability with diverse and synthetic data, optimize hardware for real-time use, and establish standardized validation protocols to support clinical adoption.

title: Longitudinal relationships between anxiety and fear of progression in post-CABG patients: a cross-sectional and cross-lagged panel network analysis.
abstract: Background Patients following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) frequently experience elevated anxiety and fear of progression (FoP), which has a high comorbidity and significantly increases adverse postoperative event risks. This prospective study explored the dynamic longitudinal associations between anxiety and FoP in post-CABG patients using network analysis methods. Methods A prospective longitudinal design enrolled first-time CABG patients from three tertiary hospitals in Urumqi, China. Anxiety and FoP were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF) at three time points: hospital discharge (T1), 1 month (T2), and 3 months (T3) post-discharge. Cross-sectional Gaussian Graphical Models were constructed at each time point, and cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis was performed to examine longitudinal symptom associations. Six a priori selected covariates (age, gender, educational level, duration of CHD, chronic comorbidities, and NYHA functional classification) were residualized prior to network estimation. Results A total of 343 patients were included in the network analysis. From T1 to T3, total GAD-7 scores demonstrated a notable downward trend, whereas FoP-Q-SF scores exhibited a continuous upward trend. The core node at both T1 and T2 was FoP11 "Worrying about what will become of the family if something should happen to the patient, " which shifted to FoP2 "Being nervous prior to doctors' appointments or periodic examinations" at T3. In the T1-T2 CLPN, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD7 "Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen" to FoP2 "Being nervous prior to doctors' appointments or periodic examinations". In the T2-T3 CLPN, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD2 "Not being able to stop or control worrying" to FoP6 "Being afraid of the possibility that the children could contract disease". In the T1-T3 network, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD4 "Trouble relaxing" to FoP3 "Being afraid of pain". Anxiety nodes generally exhibited higher Out-Expected Influence, while FoP nodes showed higher In-Expected Influence. Conclusion Anxiety levels gradually decreased during early rehabilitation, whereas fear of progression increased over time. Early anxiety symptoms showed positive cross-lagged associations with later fear of progression. These findings suggest that clinical nurses should consider phased, precision-based psychological interventions targeting stage-specific symptoms during different rehabilitation stages.

title: TrajGNN-RL: Adaptive Mobile Sink Intelligence for Lifetime-Aware Wireless Sensor Networks.
abstract: Mobile wireless sensor networks require adaptive routing and sink mobility strategies to reduce energy imbalance, congestion, and communication delay. In this study, we propose a new method called TrajGNN-RL that combines the topology learning method based on a graph neural network with the deep reinforcement learning method to plan the trajectory of the mobile sink and route the packet in a coordinated manner. Dynamic communication graphs model the residual energy, link quality, neighborhood connectivity, and traffic conditions, and reinforcement learning optimizes the sink movement and forwarding decisions via a multi-objective approach. The graph changes during network operation to handle topology and traffic changes. The performance of the proposed routing scheme was compared with the performance of the evaluated routing schemes through experimental evaluation using varying numbers of sinks and varying sink mobility. The proposed TrajGNN-RL enhanced the normalized scores of the lifetime, energy efficiency, throughput, PkDel, routing reliability, and delay reduction by 98.34%, 97.86%, 98.12%, 98.57%, 98.83%, and 96.75%, respectively. The relative improvements in the normalized lifetime, energy efficiency, throughput, packet delivery ratio, and delay reduction, respectively, were around 1.47%, 1.55%, 0.68%, 1.19%, and 1.07%, compared to the best corresponding baseline used in the experiments.

title: Identifying components for antimicrobial stewardship in primary healthcare centres in Nigeria: findings from an open call.
abstract: Background Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) struggle with the inappropriate use of antimicrobials, contributing to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Antimicrobial Stewardship Programmes (ASPs) in these regions are often designed by experts from high-income countries, undermining their relevance to local settings. Crowdsourcing could be an effective strategy to engage local stakeholders and generate strategies that inform ASPs tailored to their specific contexts. Methods A six-week crowdsourcing open call was conducted from 15 April to 30 May 2024, following the WHO/TDR six-stage framework. Eligible submissions were evaluated based on a pre-specified judging rubric. Inductive thematic analysis was performed on high-scoring submissions, while descriptive analysis was carried out on demographic data. Results The call received 75 submissions from 19 countries, 45 of which were selected for thematic analysis. Six key themes emerged: Leadership and structure, Capacity building and communication, Digital tools and technology, Monitoring and evaluation, Collaboration and partnership, and Policies and guidelines. Conclusions Insights obtained through this open call can serve as foundational components of an ASP framework relevant to the unique contexts of PHCs in Nigeria. However, further validation is required to ensure the practical applicability of these proposed components.

Clinical Profile, Glycemic Management Practices, and Direct Medical Costs among Hospitalized Diabetic Patients in Ethiopia: A Multicenter Prospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Diabetes mellitus is a growing public health challenge that imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden on healthcare systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite its association with poor inpatient outcomes and rising healthcare costs, evidence on inpatient glycemic management and direct medical costs remains limited in Ethiopia. This study aimed to assess the clinical profile, inpatient glycemic management practices, direct medical costs, and factors associated with healthcare expenditure among hospitalized patients with diabetes. Methods A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted from July 2023 to February 2024 at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Zewditu Memorial Hospital, and St. Paul’s Hospital Millennium Medical College. Data were collected from 398 hospitalized patients with diabetes through medical chart review and patient interviews. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, inpatient diabetes management practices, treatment outcomes, and direct medical costs were assessed. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the study population, and multiple linear regression analysis was conducted to identify factors associated with direct medical costs. Result Among 398 hospitalized patients with diabetes, 82.9% had type 2 diabetes, and 48.2% had suboptimal glycemic control before admission (HbA1c > 7%). Basal insulin with correctional insulin was the most frequently used inpatient regimen (45.5%). Nearly half of the patients (47.5%) developed at least one complication, most commonly acute kidney injury (13.1%), and 7.5% died before discharge. title: From trauma capacity to neurotrauma capacity: A scoping review of existing assessment frameworks.
abstract: Introduction Neurotrauma, comprising traumatic brain injury (TBI) and traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI), remains a major global health issue, with low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) bearing a disproportionate burden. Effective neurotrauma care requires timely and coordinated access to prehospital care, imaging, surgery, neurocritical care, and rehabilitation, yet current assessment frameworks often fail to capture these interdependent requirements. Research question What instruments are currently available to evaluate trauma and neurosurgical capacity across diverse global settings, and to what extent do these tools capture indicators relevant to neurotrauma care? Material and methods We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Global Health from inception to March 2026, supplemented by grey literature. We included studies describing instruments assessing system or facility-level capacity for trauma or neurosurgical care. Data extraction and domain mapping were performed independently by two reviewers. Results Twenty-six documents were included, describing 19 distinct instruments. Instruments were categorized as surgical capacity (n = 4), trauma capacity (n = 4), neurosurgical/neurocritical care capacity (n = 4), and quality indicator sets (n = 7). Emergency and imaging readiness was the most frequently covered domain (89%), followed by quality and audit systems (68%), operative capacity (53%), and neurocritical care (47%). Prehospital referral systems and workforce/training were the least covered domains (37% each). Only two instruments covered all six predefined neurotrauma domains. Discussion and conclusion Existing tools assess important components of trauma and neurosurgical capacity but remain heterogeneous and fragmented. No identified instrument provides a comprehensive, multidisciplinary assessment of neurotrauma capacity across the full continuum of care. These findings support the development of an integrated framework combining indicators across the neurotrauma care pathway.

title: Clinical audit as a catalyst for quality improvement in healthcare systems: strategic insights from a systematic review and SWOT-TOWS analysis.
A de-identified inpatient clinical pathway dataset integrating ICD-10 diagnoses, ICD-9-CM procedures, Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBG), and length of stay for healthcare analytics
abstract: Background: Healthcare administrative databases have become indispensable resources for healthcare analytics, hospital management, clinical pathway analysis, health services research and artificial intelligence. Modern hospital information systems routinely collect standardized diagnoses, procedures, reimbursement classifications, and hospitalization outcomes in everyday clinical practice. Despite their importance, publicly accessible datasets integrating diagnosis codes, procedure codes, case-mix classifications, and hospitalization outcomes remain scarce, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The absence of comprehensive administrative datasets limits reproducible research in clinical pathway modelling, healthcare operations, reimbursement analysis, and machine learning. To address this gap, we developed and publicly released a de-identified inpatient clinical pathway dataset derived from routine hospital administrative records processed through the Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBG) reimbursement system. Methods The dataset was constructed from finalized inpatient hospitalization records collected between November 2016 and April 2026. Clinical diagnoses were represented using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10), and clinical procedures were encoded using the International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-9-CM). Each hospitalization episode included one primary diagnosis, up to 11 secondary diagnoses, one primary procedure, up to 16 secondary procedures, one INA-CBG classification code, one INA-CBG description, and one length-of-stay (LOS) variable. Data extraction, transformation, harmonization, de-identification, quality assessment, and validation were performed using a reproducible Python-based computational workflow. The final repository contained 165,391 hospitalization episodes represented by 32 standardized variables. Conclusions The dataset provides an openly available resource for healthcare analytics, clinical pathway research, process mining, hospital management, reimbursement analysis, predictive modelling, explainable artificial intelligence, and healthcare operational research. The combination of standardized ICD-10 diagnoses, ICD-9-CM procedures, INA-CBG classifications, and hospitalization outcomes enables diverse secondary analyses while maintaining interoperability with existing healthcare information systems. All datasets, metadata, source codes, and supporting documentation are publicly available through Zenodo to facilitate transparency, reproducibility, and future methodological development.

title: Neurology and headache medicine in Malawi: territory, education, and the path to strengthening primary care in sub-Saharan Africa.
abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bears a disproportionate burden of neurological and pain-related diseases while facing a severe shortage of trained specialists. In this context, expanding neurology and, particularly, headache medicine, through education and integration within primary care represents both a necessity and an opportunity. This Perspective proposes a context-sensitive framework in which three interconnected domains-territory, culture, and capacity-shape the accessibility, acceptability, and sustainability of neurological care. Drawing on the experience of the International Headache Society (IHS)-DREAM healthcare network partnership in Malawi, we examine how locally adapted education, task-shifting and task-sharing can contribute to capacity building while highlighting the limitations of approaches that focus on training alone. We argue that closing the neurological treatment gap requires a shift from specialist-centred to system-centred neurology, integrating workforce development with primary care, culturally grounded community engagement, appropriate supervision and referral pathways, supportive national health policies, and equitable access to essential medicines. Task shifting and task sharing between physicians and non-physician clinicians may constitute a sustainable component of this model when appropriately regulated, supervised, remunerated, and integrated with specialist support and referral pathways. Rather than proposing a model for direct transfer across SSA, this Perspective advocates locally led, context-dependent implementation strategies capable of adapting to diverse health systems. Such an approach reframes global neurological capacity building from the episodic transfer of expertise towards the development of resilient and sustainable systems of care.

title: Reporting Gaps in mHealth Intervention Studies for Adults With Diabetes: Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Diabetes self-management education and support requires scalable digital solutions, making mobile health (mHealth) interventions increasingly vital. Despite their proven clinical efficacy, the real-world translation and scalability of these interventions are severely hindered by fragmented and opaque reporting. To address this methodological gap, the World Health Organization developed the mHealth evidence reporting and assessment (mERA) checklist to standardize reporting transparency. Objective This study aimed to systematically evaluate the reporting completeness of published randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on mHealth interventions for adult diabetes using the mERA checklist; identify critical reporting gaps; analyze how these deficiencies undermine feasibility, scalability, and sustainability; and propose targeted strategies for future optimization. Methods A PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-compliant systematic review was conducted. Five major databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library) were systematically searched for relevant RCTs published from inception to July 2026. Data extraction and reporting completeness assessments were conducted using the 16-item mERA core checklist. Nonparametric and categorical analyses were used to evaluate factors associated with reporting completeness. Results A total of 144 RCTs conducted across 49 countries were included in the final analysis. The mean overall mERA reporting score was 6.74 out of 16 (SD 2.71). While basic characteristics such as intervention delivery (n=128, 88.9%) and technology platform (n=117, 81.3%) were well reported, critical system-level domains were largely omitted. Specifically, interoperability (n=12, 8.3%), data security (n=28, 19.4%), compliance with guidelines (n=41, 28.5%), and intervention fidelity (n=53, 36.8%) were severely underreported. Additionally, reporting completeness was significantly higher in studies published between 2016 and 2026 ( P =.01) and in multicomponent interventions compared to single-component ones ( P =.04). Conclusions Empirical research on mHealth interventions for adult diabetes exhibits systemic structural flaws in reporting, particularly concerning system integration, data security, and regulatory compliance. These omissions significantly undermine the transparency, reproducibility, and real-world scalability of digital diabetes care solutions. Future trials must rigorously adopt standardized reporting frameworks such as the mERA checklist to bridge the gap between clinical efficacy and large-scale public health policy translation.

title: Clinical Characteristics, Staging, and Treatment Outcomes of Retinoblastoma at a National Referral Center in Tanzania: A Retrospective Study (2023–2025)
Data Collection Methods, Training, and Perceived Health Information Quality Among Professionals in Three Ghanaian Hospitals: A Cross-Sectional Study.
