abstract: Background and aims Reliable health information underpins clinical care, disease surveillance, and health-system planning. However, routine data in many low- and middle-income countries, including Ghana, are often incomplete, inaccurate, or delayed. Most prior evidence concerns objectively measured data quality in single facilities. Less is known about how healthcare professionals perceive the adequacy of their data-collection methods and collected-data quality. Also, how these perceptions relate to the method used and to prior training is unknown. This cross-sectional study assessed those perceptions and their associations across three Ghanaian hospitals. Methods Of 574 professionals sampled, 564 responded (98.3%). A pretested questionnaire measured perceptions on five-point scales, dichotomized at a two-thirds cut-off. Associations were quantified with crude and adjusted binary logistic regression (odds ratios with 95% CIs). Results Methods were perceived adequate by 67.2% (379/564) and data quality by 60.1% (339/564). Training showed the strongest association with perceived method adequacy (adjusted OR: 5.54, 95% CI: 3.66-8.39). Electronic methods showed no significant advantage over manual methods in either crude or adjusted models. Conclusion In this study, training demonstrated a stronger adjusted association with favorable perceptions than the type of data-collection method used. Because the design is cross-sectional and outcomes self-reported, causation cannot be inferred. Longitudinal studies with objective data-quality verification are needed.

title: Prevalence, Socioeconomic Determinants, and Health-System Factors Associated with Laboratory-Confirmed Renal Impairment Among Adults Attending Tertiary Referral Hospitals in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Cross-Sectional Study
Massive Burns Versus Less Extensive Burns in Children: Clinical Outcomes and Independent Predictors of Mortality.
abstract: Background/objectives Massive burns are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in children. Data comparing pediatric burns of different severities and identifying mortality predictors remain limited. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics and outcomes of children with burns involving 20-49% and ≥50% total body surface area (TBSA) and to identify independent predictors of mortality. Methods This retrospective cohort study included children with burns involving ≥20% TBSA treated at a national referral pediatric burn center. Patients were categorized as 20-49% TBSA or ≥50% TBSA. Demographic characteristics, burn etiology, inhalation injury, intubation, intensive care requirements, length of hospital stay, pBaux score, and mortality were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify mortality predictors. Results Among 260 children, 206 had burns involving 20-49% TBSA and 54 had burns involving ≥50% TBSA. Scald burns predominated in the 20-49% TBSA group, whereas flame burns were more frequent in the ≥50% TBSA group. Inhalation injury and intubation were also more common in the ≥50% TBSA group. Mortality was significantly higher in patients with ≥50% TBSA burns (29.6% vs. 3.4%; p Conclusions Massive pediatric burns are associated with markedly worse outcomes. Burn extent ≥ 50% TBSA and intubation may help identify children at particularly high risk of mortality.

title: Predictors of Delayed Cleft Lip and Palate Surgery: A Case-Control Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
abstract: Background Orofacial clefts are common anomalies, and timely treatment is essential for optimal outcomes. In low- and middle-income countries, surgical delays are frequent, yet contributing factors remain understudied. This study aims to identify and quantify these factors at a tertiary medical center in Ethiopia. Methods An institution-based unmatched case-control study was conducted among 98 patients between January 2023 and December 2024. Cases included patients undergoing surgery after the recommended age (cleft lip >6 mo; cleft palate >12 mo), whereas controls received timely surgery. Data were collected from medical records and telephone interviews. Bivariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression were performed to determine predictors. Results Isolated cleft palate (adjusted odds ratio = 21.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.17-113.12; P P = 0.007) were significantly associated with delayed treatment. Lack of formal education of caregivers showed a strong borderline association (adjusted odds ratio = 8.61; 95% CI, 0.68-108.89; P = 0.096). Post-hoc power exceeded 99.9%. The final model demonstrated good performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.875 and acceptable fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ 2 = 11.037; degrees of freedom = 8; P = 0.200). Conclusions Cleft type and geographic barriers were the primary determinants of delayed surgery. Patients with isolated cleft palate and those residing farther from specialized centers had higher odds of delayed treatment. Interventions should focus on improving early detection, referral pathways, and access to cleft care.

title: Improving sleep duration in NICU graduates: a quality improvement initiative.
abstract: Background Protected sleep is a core component of developmental supportive care in neonates. However, the overstimulating neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) environment and procedures often disrupt neonatal sleep periods. With improving neonatal survival rates in low- and middle-income countries like India, focus must shift towards ensuring neurologically intact outcomes. We implemented a point of care quality improvement initiative using environmental modification to improve sleep duration in neonates admitted to the low dependency unit (LDU) of our NICU. Methods This prospective quality improvement study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India from May to August 2024. All stable neonates admitted to the LDU during the study period were enrolled. Four sequential plan-do-study-act (PDSA) cycles were implemented, targeting cyclic lighting, noise reduction through alarm management and equipment repair, staff sensitisation and caregiver involvement. The primary outcome was the proportion of neonates achieving adequate sleep duration of more than 16 hours/day. Results A total of 625 neonates were enrolled across three phases (baseline: n=115; implementation: n=312; post implementation: n=198). The proportion of neonates achieving adequate sleep increased from 15.7% at baseline to 62.2% during implementation and sustained at 58.1% post implementation. Mean sleep duration increased significantly from 12.95±3.22 to 16.38±3.12 hours/day (p Conclusion Simple, low-cost environmental modifications implemented through sequential PDSA cycles can significantly improve sleep duration in NICU neonates.

title: Advanced Age and Low Parity as Predictors of Non-Endometrioid Histopathological Subtypes in Endometrial Carcinoma: A Cross-Sectional Study in Indonesia.
abstract: Background Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is the most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries and is increasing in incidence in low- and middle-income settings, including Indonesia. Age and parity are well-recognized epidemiological risk factors; however, their differential impact on histopathological tumor subtypes-particularly in older women-remains insufficiently characterized in Southeast Asian populations. Purpose To evaluate the associations between patient age and parity with the histopathological subtype of endometrial carcinoma in women treated at a tertiary referral hospital in Indonesia. Patients and methods A cross-sectional analytic study was conducted using retrospectively collected medical records from 207 patients aged ≥50 years with histopathologically confirmed endometrial carcinoma at Prof. Dr. Margono Soekarjo Regional Public Hospital, Purwokerto, between January and December 2024. Patients with incomplete clinicopathological data were excluded. Age was categorized into 50-60 years and >60 years; parity into nulliparous/primiparous and multiparous (≥2 deliveries). Histopathological subtypes were classified as endometrioid vs non-endometrioid carcinoma. Associations were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression; statistical significance was defined as p Results Of 207 eligible patients, the majority (92.5%) were aged 50-60 years. Non-endometrioid carcinoma predominated in women aged >60 years (p Conclusion Advanced age (>60 years) and low parity are independently associated with non-endometrioid histopathological subtypes of endometrial carcinoma in an Indonesian tertiary center. These findings underscore the clinical importance of incorporating patient age and reproductive history into risk stratification and surveillance strategies for endometrial cancer.

title: Equity Meets Primary-Care-Sensitive Performance: A Longitudinal Benchmark of Cost-Related Unmet Care and Avoidable Hospitalization in Europe.
abstract: Background/objectives This study compares European health systems by considering the cost-related unmet-care inequality between income groups and primary-care-sensitive avoidable hospitalizations. Methods This was a longitudinal comparative benchmarking study. The main sample consists of 275 country-year observations from 20 European countries with at least ten years of data during 2009-2023. The first dimension is measured by the absolute difference between the lowest and highest income quintiles in the prevalence of unmet medical examination or treatment because it was too expensive. The second dimension uses age- and sex-standardized avoidable hospitalization rates for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, congestive heart failure, and diabetes. The 20-country core sample was defined before within-year rank normalization. The indicators were converted into rank scores on a scale of 0-1 within each annual comparison set, with equal weighting for both dimensions. Temporal uncertainty in country rankings was examined using a three-year synchronized moving-block bootstrap with 10,000 iterations. Results In the main comparison, the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, and Finland ranked in the top five. The Netherlands and Slovenia remained in the top five in all valid bootstrap replications; the corresponding probabilities were 99.90% for Spain, 90.67% for Sweden, and 95.66% for Finland. Top-five membership nevertheless changed under some alternative weighting, disease-omission, scaling, and balanced-period specifications. In the spending-adjusted assessment, each country was compared based on a nonlinear spending-performance relationship established from other countries, without including its own observations in the estimation equation; Slovenia, the Netherlands, and Spain took the top three positions. Conclusions The findings should be interpreted not as a definitive country ranking, but as a relative assessment of health systems that highlights the differences between health inequality, primary care-sensitive outcomes, and resource intensity.

title: An assessment of the health system's capacity for major structural birth defects care in Tanzania using anorectal malformations as a tracer condition: A multi-phase, mixed-methods study protocol.
abstract: Background Structural birth defects cause disproportionate neonatal and under-five morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, where 90-95% of births and associated deaths occur; however, health-system readiness for prevention uptake, early detection, and management remains poorly understood. Anorectal malformations account for 33-40% of the paediatric surgical workload in sub-Saharan Africa, making it a tracer condition for evaluating Tanzania's capacity across primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention levels. Although delayed detection, high postoperative morbidity, and referral dysfunction are documented, the upstream preconception, antenatal, delivery, and postnatal profile, parental lived experience, external benchmarking of paediatric surgical capacity, and feasibility of a context-specific preoperative checklist remain to be quantified within the Tanzanian clinical environment. Methods This multi-phase mixed-methods protocol comprises four phases. In Phase I, all mother-newborn dyads where the infant has an anorectal malformation presenting to Muhimbili National Hospital will be enrolled in a cross-sectional study quantifying preconception, antenatal, delivery, and postnatal prevention uptake; multivariable logistic regression will identify predictors of early detection; the sample size will be derived via Cochran's formula using finite population correction. Phase II will use descriptive phenomenology through purposive in-depth interviews with parents exploring socio-cultural access determinants, analysed via the Stevick-Colaizzi-Keen method. Phase III will conduct a facility-level survey against the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery checklist at four tertiary hospitals; domain-specific and total compliance scores will be calculated, gaps quantified against benchmarks, and centres compared using Friedman tests and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Phase IV will test feasibility of a preoperative anorectal malformation checklist at Muhimbili National Hospital, examining practicality and acceptability (non-parametric comparisons). Discussion This study will produce a system-level appraisal of Tanzania's capacity to prevent, detect, and manage major structural birth defects using anorectal malformation as a tracer condition. Findings will inform policy, guide resource allocation, and support targeted interventions.

title: Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.
abstract: Background Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Although numerous treatment approaches are recommended by international clinical guidelines, there is still limited understanding of which interventions provide the best value for money. We aimed to critically appraise and summarise the evidence on the cost-effectiveness and costs of interventions endorsed in recent guidelines to manage low back pain (LBP), compared to usual care. Methods and findings We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. The primary outcome was cost/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), which was converted to 2024 Great British Pound values, tabulated and summarised qualitatively. Secondary outcomes were direct costs (total, interventional, health service use, community services and out-of-pocket costs) and indirect costs (e.g., lost wages, lost productivity, absenteeism). We assessed methodological quality using the Consensus Health Economics Criteria (CHEC) checklist for within-trial economic evaluations or the Philips checklist for modelling studies. Our review included 20 studies (17 within-trial economic evaluations and three modelling studies), published between 2005 and 2026. Half (n = 10) focussed on chronic LBP (>3-month duration), and eight included mixed populations (i.e., acute, subacute and chronic). All studies were of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, both single-modality and multimodal interventions (e.g., exercise plus spinal manipulation; diet plus physical activity). Most interventions are cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000. Moreover, interventions aiming to reduce fear and stress or support self-management in people with chronic LBP, as well as clinician-delivered interventions including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support are potentially cost-saving from the healthcare, societal and payer's perspectives, as they are both more effective and less costly than usual care (e.g., first contact management, including advice and medication). All of the evidence is derived from high-income countries, and from a considerable heterogenous body of literature. Evidence on cost-effective treatments in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Conclusions Non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions that include education, psychological support, acupuncture and exercise seem to be cost-effective for managing LBP, compared to usual care. Improved access to and implementation of these effective treatments is urgently needed so more people can benefit from them in routine care. Registration The review was registered on PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk; CRD42024510270).

title: Sustained neurosurgical decision support through remote multidisciplinary case conferencing: A six-year LMIC-HIC collaboration.
abstract: Introduction Global disparities in neurosurgical care remain substantial in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where limited access to specialist expertise and supporting services can restrict timely treatment. Remote multidisciplinary case conferencing may provide specialist decision support using existing digital infrastructure, but longitudinal descriptions remain limited. Research question Can a low-cost, clinician-led remote case-conference model provide sustained neurosurgical decision support in a resource-constrained setting? Methods We conducted a descriptive implementation case study of a collaboration between Haukeland University Hospital, Bergen, and Teaching Hospital Jaffna, Sri Lanka, from September 2019 to December 2025. Routine meeting logs were reviewed for meeting activity, case-discussion volume, imaging review, participants, workflow, and decision-support functions. The model combined asynchronous review of imaging and clinical information with synchronous multidisciplinary videoconferencing; direct remote patient examination was not routine. Results Across 150 meetings, 1258 case-discussion episodes were recorded, involving review of more than 2700 CT and MRI studies. Some patients were discussed more than once, and the number of unique patients could not be reliably reconstructed. Discussions addressed diagnostic clarification, operative and non-operative management, surgical prioritization, additional investigation, follow-up, and referral or escalation. The model used existing digital infrastructure and professional time without dedicated project funding. Final clinical responsibility remained with the Sri Lankan treating team. Conclusion This cross-border model was maintained for more than six years and demonstrates the feasibility of longitudinal neurosurgical decision support in a resource-constrained setting. Effects on clinical outcomes, professional development, implementation sustainability, and local capacity require prospective evaluation.

title: Implementing a programme to treat severe acute malnutrition in Indonesia: What works?
journal: Asia Pacific journal of clinical nutrition

title: Process mapping of a collaborative quality improvement study to optimise the use of antibiotics in intensive care units in Argentina: a Pathfinder study.
abstract: Objective To systematically document the operational components, barriers, facilitators, and solutions of a quality improvement collaborative for antibiotic stewardship in intensive care units (ICUs) in the public sector of Argentina, using the Pathfinder methodological framework. Methods Retrospective, descriptive observational study using mixed methods. Data sources included a documentary review of protocols, standard operating procedures, monitoring reports, and host study publications; an online survey with closed and open-ended questions administered to research team members; interviews with team researchers to estimate effort and triangulation with findings from the host study's previously published process evaluation, structured according to Normalisation Process Theory. Integration was performed using the Pathfinder Tracker. Analysis combined descriptive statistics with content analysis of open-ended responses. Results Eleven stages of the research process were mapped, from question formulation to dissemination, with an estimated total effort of approximately 1,020 person-hours. The stages with the highest perceived difficulty (4/5) were ethical and institutional approvals, data collection, analysis, and dissemination, which together accounted for approximately 50% of the total estimated effort. Barriers were identified across three domains: institutional and regulatory (heterogeneity of ethical requirements, absence of stable local coordinators, publication costs); operational and technical (complex data collection forms, displacement of implementation focus due to the burden of data collection, variable connectivity); and human resources and capacity (clinical workload, staff turnover, insufficient training in implementation science). Solutions included a collaborative format with mentoring, agile communication via accessible digital tools (REDCap, WhatsApp, Zoom), and the use of theoretical frameworks for structuring (NPT, CFIR). Conclusions The Pathfinder framework enabled a systematic reconstruction of the host study's processes, revealing barriers and solutions that conventional results reports do not capture. The findings are relevant for research teams in middle-income countries designing quality improvement collaboratives in complex hospital settings.

title: From missed diagnosis to lifelong survivorship: a precision oncology roadmap for equity in pediatric and AYA cancer care.
abstract: Cancer in children, adolescents, and young adults (AYA) remains a global health challenge, with disparities in survival and quality of life between high-resource and low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). These disparities arise across the cancer continuum, including delayed recognition, inadequate diagnostic capacity, fragmented referral pathways, treatment abandonment, limited supportive care, unequal access to molecular diagnostics, and insufficient survivorship services. Precision oncology provides an opportunity to address these challenges, but its equity potential extends beyond genomic sequencing and targeted therapies. This narrative review examines an integrated precision oncology continuum encompassing early recognition, diagnostic and pathological accuracy, molecular characterization, risk stratification, precision treatment, response monitoring, supportive care, and lifelong survivorship. Evidence from LMIC settings is used to illustrate diagnostic delay, referral barriers, treatment abandonment, health-system limitations, and outcome disparities without attempting an exhaustive country comparison. The review proposes a tiered, equity-centered framework in which foundational cancer services are strengthened alongside progressively accessible molecular and digital technologies. Regional referral networks, patient navigation, tele-oncology, pathology and laboratory networks, targeted molecular testing, multidisciplinary care, survivorship planning, and longitudinal cancer registries are emphasized as practical components. For AYA patients, fertility, reproductive health, mental health, education, employment, and transition between pediatric and adult services are incorporated into precision care. Ultimately, equitable precision oncology should connect biological precision with health-system precision, ensuring that every young person can receive timely diagnosis, appropriate treatment, continuous monitoring, and lifelong survivorship support.

title: Global oncological surgery at a crossroads: Overcoming inequities and disparities through collective action and strategic vision.
journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology

title: Ocular infections and stewardship practices for Ophthalmologists: The RED EYE AMSP model.
abstract: Ocular infections, ranging from conjunctivitis and keratitis to postoperative and device-associated endophthalmitis, remain a significant cause of preventable visual morbidity worldwide. In India and other low- and middle-income countries, the irrational use of topical and systemic antimicrobials, often without microbiological confirmation, has contributed to the emergence of multidrug-resistant ocular pathogens. Fluoroquinolone-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa , methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus , and resistant Fusarium and Candida species are now major challenges in ophthalmic practice. The widespread availability of over-the-counter ophthalmic drops, empirical perioperative prophylaxis, and the use of steroid-antibiotic combinations exacerbate this problem. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) in ophthalmology, though relatively underdeveloped, is now a global priority. The Society of Antimicrobial Stewardship PractIce (SASPI) in India advocates an integrated AMS model linking diagnostic, preventive, therapeutic, and administrative strategies. For ophthalmologists, this translates into culture-guided therapy for recalcitrant or postsurgical infections, restricting the use of broad-spectrum or prolonged topical antimicrobials, enforcing asepsis during surgeries, and adopting antimicrobial auditing systems. The RED EYE AMSP model presented in this perspective provides a ten-point, ophthalmology-specific adaptation of the SASPI framework focusing on rational prescribing, evidence-based diagnostics, environmental safety, and interprofessional partnership. By embracing stewardship, ophthalmologists can preserve antimicrobial efficacy, minimize iatrogenic resistance, and contribute to the broader One Health goal of antimicrobial resistance containment.

title: Prevalence and Hematological Profile of Anemia Among Third-Trimester Pregnant Women: A Retrospective Study From Al Adan Hospital, Kuwait.
abstract: Background Anemia during pregnancy remains a significant global health problem, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where nutritional deficiencies are prevalent. Despite established antenatal screening programs, data on the prevalence and hematological characteristics of anemia among pregnant women in Kuwait are limited. Objective To determine the prevalence, severity, and hematological profile of anemia among third-trimester pregnant women attending Al Adan Hospital, Kuwait. Methods This retrospective observational study analyzed medical records of 5129 third-trimester pregnant women who received antenatal care between January 2022 and December 2023. Demographic and hematological data-including hemoglobin, hematocrit, mean corpuscular volume (MCV), and ferritin-were collected. Anemia was classified using the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria, and iron deficiency anemia was defined by ferritin Results The overall prevalence of anemia (Hb 40 yrs; p ρ = +0.42, p Conclusion Anemia affected over one-third of third-trimester pregnant women at Al Adan Hospital, with iron deficiency as the leading cause. Routine ferritin assessment and targeted iron supplementation are warranted to improve maternal hematologic health and perinatal outcomes in the region.

title: Telemedicine in Retinopathy of Prematurity: A Review of Current Evidence and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of preventable childhood visual impairment, particularly in settings where access to specialized ophthalmologic care is limited. Telemedicine offers an alternative approach to ROP screening and monitoring through remote retinal imaging and expert interpretation. This narrative review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance, clinical benefits, implementation challenges, and future perspectives of telemedicine in ROP screening and management. Methods : A narrative literature review was conducted with consideration of the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched in August and August 2026 for relevant publications from January 2000 to the search date. Two authors independently screened titles and abstracts, followed by full-text assessment according to predefined eligibility criteria. A total of 143 scientific articles and other high-quality sources were included in the final narrative synthesis. Evidence was evaluated qualitatively, without a formal risk-of-bias assessment. Findings : The reviewed literature indicates that telemedicine can expand access to ROP screening, facilitate remote specialist consultation, support longitudinal disease monitoring, and improve the triage of infants requiring urgent assessment. In selected settings, remote retinal image interpretation has demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to conventional examinations for clinically significant and vision-threatening ROP. Artificial intelligence-based assessment and smartphone-based retinal imaging represent promising approaches to improving screening accessibility and workflow efficiency, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, implementation remains constrained by equipment costs, infrastructure limitations, image quality, workforce training requirements, and ethical and legal considerations. Conclusions : Telemedicine represents a promising complementary strategy for ROP screening and management, with the potential to improve access to timely specialist assessment and help prevent ROP-related visual impairment. Its successful integration into clinical practice requires sustainable infrastructure, standardized protocols, trained personnel, and reliable referral pathways that ensure timely in-person examination and treatment when indicated. Further research is needed to establish the effectiveness, cost-efficiency, and long-term sustainability of different telemedicine-based approaches across diverse healthcare settings.

title: From validation to public health impact: implementing equitable AI-enabled diabetic retinopathy screening.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a preventable cause of vision loss as diabetes prevalence rises worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled retinal screening has progressed from retrospective validation to prospective and real-world deployment, with recent reviews showing high diagnostic performance across fundus photography, smartphone-based systems, and autonomous platforms. Yet diagnostic accuracy alone does not ensure public health benefit. Population impact can be lost when eligible people are not reached, images are ungradable, results are delayed, referrals are incomplete, treatment capacity is insufficient, or disadvantaged groups face financial, geographic, or digital barriers. Unlike reviews centered mainly on diagnostic accuracy or economic performance, this Mini Review reframes AI-enabled DR screening as a population-health intervention spanning detection through completion of effective eye care. We synthesize evidence on diagnostic validity, implementation, economics, referral completion, care cascades, patient-centered outcomes, equity, and governance. We argue that effectiveness and cost-effectiveness are properties of the complete screening-to-treatment pathway, not the algorithm alone, and propose a four-domain framework encompassing technical validity, service integration, population impact, and equity and sustainability. Future research should prioritize comparative implementation studies and outcome sets that capture screening reach, gradability, referral completion, treatment initiation, time to treatment, avoidable vision loss, vision-related quality of life, acceptability, costs, and subgroup equity. The policy question is no longer whether AI can detect DR, but whether health systems can translate automated detection into equitable completion of effective eye care at scale.

title: TORCH-Related Maternal Infections in a Tertiary Referral Center: Diagnostic Pathways and Prenatal Management in the Context of Canadian and European Recommendations.
abstract: Maternal TORCH-related infections remain a major cause of adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes despite advances in prenatal diagnosis and prevention. We conducted a retrospective observational study of 71 HIV-negative pregnant women referred to the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit of a tertiary referral center in Palermo, Italy, between June 2020 and December 2024 for suspected maternal TORCH infections. Demographic, microbiological, clinical, therapeutic, and neonatal data were retrospectively collected to characterize referral patterns, diagnostic pathways, treatment uptake, and pregnancy outcomes. Overall, 43 women (60.6%) had a confirmed maternal infection; cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Toxoplasma gondii accounted for most confirmed maternal infections. Maternal treatment was administered to 12/23 (52.2%) women with confirmed CMV infection and to all women with confirmed toxoplasmosis (17/17, 100%), corresponding to significantly greater treatment uptake for toxoplasmosis ( p = 0.0008). Maternal demographic characteristics, obstetric history, treatment, and neonatal outcomes showed no significant association with trimester at referral. Three newborns were diagnosed with congenital CMV infection. Most referrals followed uncertain serological findings rather than clinically apparent maternal disease. These findings highlight the role of specialist assessment in clarifying maternal infection status, counseling patients, and informing pathogen-specific prenatal management; prospective multicenter studies are required to assess its effects on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

title: Postnatal interventions to support newborn survival: updates for the Lives Saved Tool.
abstract: Background The period immediately after birth represents a highly vulnerable time for newborns, particularly in contexts without access to high-quality secondary care for small and/or sick newborns. Scaling up existing evidence-based interventions can avert much of the mortality and morbidity that occurs during the neonatal period. We summarise the evidence for interventions delivered postnatally and propose a set of effect estimates for inclusion in the Lives Saved Tool (LiST). Methods We first conducted a set of systematic reviews and updates on the most recent evidence from randomised controlled trials on the effectiveness of interventions for reducing neonatal mortality and associated risk factors. We then assessed the evidence using standardised set of considerations alongside an iterative consultation process with newborn care experts to determine whether and how new meta-analysed effect estimates could be incorporated into the LiST model, as well as which of these estimates should be updated and which should be retained. Results We proposed a new set of interventions that involve three packages of newborn care: a basic package (i.e. primary/community, secondary hospital care), a referral care package (i.e. tertiary care), and a package of promising innovative interventions whose evidence base is still developing. We included five new interventions within the updated LiST model's basic and referral packages: nasal continuous positive airway pressure coupled with preterm supportive care, newborn referral and transportation, animal-derived surfactant, prophylactic antifungals, and antibiotic stewardship. Three new interventions were proposed for the innovation package: magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection in asphyxiated newborns, topical emollient therapy, and probiotics/synbiotics for hospitalised preterm newborns. Conclusions We synthesised the evidence base for the impact of a package of effective postnatal interventions for neonates for an updated LiST model. The new interventions and updated effect estimates can provide more accurate projections of potential impacts on neonatal survival for different intervention coverage scale-up scenarios in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Geographic Variation in Diagnosis, Treatment, and Outcomes of Adrenocortical Carcinoma in the Americas: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Objective Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy of the adrenal cortex. Given the heterogeneity of healthcare systems across the Americas, this review examines regional differences in access to diagnosis, treatment availability, and clinical outcomes, as well as their association with structural and socioeconomic factors. Design Narrative literature review of observational studies and relevant regional evidence. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were investigated for studies published between 2010 and 2025 reporting on diagnostic resources, treatment availability, clinical outcomes, or ACC-related population-specific genetic epidemiology across the Americas and the Caribbean. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, populations, and outcome measures, results were synthesized narratively and organized by geographic region and thematic domain. Results Available evidence, particularly from the United States, indicates greater representation of high-volume referral centers, specialized multidisciplinary care, and structured diagnostic and treatment pathways. Conversely, reports from selected settings in Central and South America and the Caribbean describe limitations related to healthcare funding, fragmented care networks, and access to specialized therapies. These differences may be associated with diagnostic delays and reduced access to specialized treatment; however, the strength, depth, and comparability of the available evidence vary substantially across regions. Conclusions Available evidence indicates regional variation in ACC diagnosis, treatment access, and reported outcomes across the Americas. Structural, socioeconomic, and geographic factors may contribute to these differences. Potential priorities include strengthening referral pathways, expanding specialized care, and supporting multidisciplinary management. More representative data are needed to enable robust regional comparisons and guide context-specific strategies.

title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging.
abstract: Background Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. Methods This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants' usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. Findings Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p Interpretation Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. Funding The Brazilian National Council for Scientific and Technological Development, the Alzheimer's Association, and the National Institute on Aging.

title: Baseline Clinical Predictors and Toxicological Drivers of In-Hospital Poisoning Mortality in Resource-Constrained Emergency Care: A Firth Penalized Regression Analysis.
abstract: Background Evidence regarding clinical characteristics and determinants of mortality among patients with acute poisoning in agricultural regions of Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate baseline clinical predictors associated with in-hospital mortality among acutely poisoned patients in a low-resource tertiary emergency department. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted among consecutive acute poisoning cases presenting to Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital (October 2022-September 2024). Of 372 screened cases, 7 patients who left against medical advice were excluded, yielding a final analytical cohort of 365 patients. Sociodemographic, toxicological, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was performed to minimize small-sample bias given sparse outcome events (15 deaths). A sensitivity model additionally adjusted for sex and rural residence. Results The median age of patients was 22.0 years (IQR: 19.0-27.0); 230 (61.8%) were aged 15-24 years, 199 (53.5%) were female, and 245 (65.9%) were rural residents. Insecticides were the predominant poisoning category (157; 42.2%). Aluminum Phosphide (AlP) exposure occurred in 43 (11.6%) patients, resulting in 12 deaths (case-fatality rate: 27.9%; 95% CI 15.3%-43.7%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (15/365; 95% CI 2.3%-6.6%), with AlP accounting for 80.0% of all cohort deaths. In the primary multivariable Firth model, AlP exposure (aOR 30.48, 95% CI 7.88-117.95) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale Conclusions Impaired consciousness at admission (GCS < 15) and Aluminum Phosphide exposure serve as critical baseline indicators for rapid, low-cost risk stratification. While these exploratory parameters highlight high-risk groups, prospective multi-center validation across diverse hospital tiers is required before formal integration into clinical triage algorithms.

title: Exploring Caregivers Lived Experiences in Accessing Comprehensive Cleft Care at Jimma University Medical Center: A Phenomenological Study in Southwest Ethiopia.
abstract: Background: Orofacial clefts are one of the most common congenital anomalies worldwide. Comprehensive cleft care interventions aim to address the complex surgical, nutritional, dental, speech, audiology, and psychosocial needs of patients with clefts. While studies from other countries have identified various implementation barriers and facilitators, evidence from Ethiopia remains limited, particularly regarding caregivers' experiences accessing comprehensive cleft care. This study explored caregivers' lived experiences of accessing comprehensive cleft care at Jimma University Medical Center in southwestern Ethiopia. Methods: We conducted a phenomenological study at the Comprehensive Cleft Care Center of Jimma University Medical Center. Participants were purposively selected from caregivers of children with orofacial clefts who had received at least two components of comprehensive cleft care. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data collection continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Audio recordings were transcribed verbatim, translated into English, and managed in ATLAS.ti version 7.5.18. Data were analyzed inductively using Colaizzi's seven-step descriptive phenomenological method. Trustworthiness was enhanced through member checking, reflexive bracketing, and systematic procedures. Results: Twelve caregivers of children with orofacial clefts participated in the study. The analysis generated eight overarching themes. Participants reported limited initial awareness of cleft conditions, cultural misconceptions, stigma, emotional distress, and delayed care-seeking. Key barriers included poor referral linkages, transportation difficulties, financial constraints, and geographic inaccessibility. Participants reported that engagement with comprehensive cleft care was associated with increased knowledge, caregiving confidence and skills, and trust in healthcare providers. They also described perceived improvements in feeding, nutritional status, speech development, physical appearance, and social integration, alongside reduced stigma and increased caregiver advocacy and community awareness of cleft conditions. Conclusions: Caregivers described a transition from limited awareness of orofacial clefts, emotional distress, stigma, and challenges accessing care toward greater knowledge, confidence, trust in healthcare providers, and perceived improvements in their children's health, functional abilities, and social participation. Persistent barriers related to poverty, transportation difficulties, referral delays, and limited community awareness remained. These findings can inform policy and program planning to strengthen comprehensive cleft care and address inequities in access to care for children with orofacial clefts and their families in similar settings in Ethiopia.

title: Undertreatment of Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol-related clinical contexts: a scoping review of diagnosis, thiamine regimens, and clinical management.
abstract: Background Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is a potentially reversible neurological emergency that remains frequently missed and undertreated in patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD). Although thiamine is widely accepted as the cornerstone of prevention and treatment, diagnostic uncertainty, limited comparative evidence, and heterogeneous clinical recommendations contribute to substantial variability in real-world management. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence on the diagnosis and clinical management of WE in patients with AUD or clinically significant alcohol use, with particular attention to practice variability, undertreatment, and clinically actionable gaps in care. Methods We conducted a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidance. Electronic databases and trial registries were searched for studies addressing the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of WE in populations with AUD or clinically significant alcohol use. Eligible sources included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, clinical audits, and implementation-focused reports. Data were charted and synthesized thematically. Results A total of 26 studies were included. The evidence base was limited and heterogeneous. Only two randomized controlled trials evaluated thiamine regimens, and no consensus emerged regarding optimal dosing. Diagnostic criteria for WE varied widely across studies, with inconsistent use of formal criteria such as the Caine criteria. Across observational studies and prescribing audits, undertreatment was consistently reported, including delayed initiation of therapy and frequent use of oral thiamine in high-risk scenarios. Studies describing more protocolized and guideline-concordant care more often reported earlier treatment initiation and use of parenteral thiamine in suspected or confirmed cases. Conclusions WE remains underrecognized and undertreated in AUD and clinically significant alcohol use. The mapped evidence suggests that diagnostic uncertainty, limited trial data, and inconsistent implementation of recommendations are associated with persistent variability in care. Although the optimal thiamine regimen remains unresolved, early recognition and appropriate parenteral treatment in high-risk or suspected cases represent actionable opportunities to reduce preventable neurological morbidity.

title: Exploring patient perspectives on barriers contributing to lost to follow-up in hypertension care: A qualitative study in a tertiary-care hospital in Coastal Karnataka, India.
abstract: Background Hypertension requires lifelong treatment and regular follow-up to prevent complications; however, lost to follow-up (LTFU) remains a major challenge in long-term hypertension care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Objective This study explored patient perspectives on barriers contributing to LTFU in hypertension management. Methods A qualitative study was conducted among 32 hypertensive patients who were LTFU at a tertiary care hospital in Coastal Karnataka, India. Participants were aged 31-69years, with 21 (65.6%) men and 11 (34.4%) women. Participants were identified through hospital records and interviewed using a semi-structured interview guide. Interviews were conducted from February to April 2026 Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically following COREQ guidelines. Results Six major themes emerged.: (1) illness perception and self-management practices, (2) care-seeking and follow-up behaviour, (3) structural and socioeconomic barriers, (4) health system and continuity gaps, (5) patient-perceived strategies to improve continuity of care, and (6) health information continuity and interoperability needs. Participants described symptom-driven healthcare seeking, medication non-adherence, occupational responsibilities, and competing family priorities contributing to irregular follow-up. Financial burden, including treatment costs, transportation expenses, and wage loss, substantially affected continuity of care. Long travel distances, dependence on family members, overcrowding, rushed consultations, and inadequate follow-up mechanisms further influenced disengagement from care. Participants also reported fragmented healthcare utilisation, repeated investigations, dependence on paper-based records, and poor continuity of medical information across healthcare facilities. Several participants perceived that integrated digital health information systems, decentralised services, appointment reminders, and improved counselling could strengthen long-term hypertension follow-up. Conclusions LTFU in hypertension care is influenced by interconnected individual, socioeconomic, and health system-related barriers. A notable finding was the fragmented nature of continuity of care and poor health information continuity across healthcare facilities. Strengthening patient-centred follow-up systems, decentralised chronic disease services, financial protection mechanisms, and interoperable health information systems may improve continuity of hypertension care and reduce long-term disengagement from chronic disease management.

title: Evidence landscape for surgical site infection prevention strategies in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review of literature for intervention development as part of the IMPRESS study.
abstract: Objectives Surgical site infections (SSIs) contribute to about 20% of hospital-acquired infections, with an 8–30% incidence in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Hospitals in LMIC settings face limited resources, overcrowding, staff shortages and poor infection control. Evaluating effective, feasible and evidence-based multipronged interventions implementable in LMICs is crucial to guide sustainable SSI prevention strategies and improve outcomes. This scoping review addressed the question: “Which SSI prevention interventions have been evaluated in LMICs?” Design The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Data sources The comprehensive literature search was conducted using three databases: PubMed (National Library of Medicine), Scopus (Elsevier) and Embase (Ovid) during August–September 2024. Eligibility criteria Peer-reviewed interventional studies evaluating one or more SSI prevention interventions or intervention bundles were included. Data extraction and synthesis Title and abstract screening was performed by two independent reviewers in Rayaan according to pre-defined inclusion–exclusion criteria, followed by full-text screening from January to March 2025. Data were extracted from the included studies using a standardised Excel sheet, including absolute reductions in SSI rates. Results Of the 8368 studies identified, 5577 remained after de-duplication and underwent title and abstract screening, 245 full-text articles were assessed for full-text review and 186 studies were included in the review. Among the included studies, 101/186 (54.3%) were published between 2020 and 2024, 144/186 (77.4%) were randomised controlled trials and 88 (47.3%) were conducted in India. Overall, 64 SSI prevention interventions were identified, including 13 pre-operative (20.3%), 35 intra-operative (54.7%) and 16 post-operative (25.0%) interventions. The most frequently evaluated interventions were single-dose surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (SAP) for clean/clean-contaminated surgery (32 studies, 17.2%), post-operative restriction of SAP to <24 hours (22, 11.8%), appropriate antibiotic selection (13, 7%) and timing of SAP within 60 min of surgical incision (12, 6.5%), chlorhexidine skin preparation (11, 5.9%) and WHO Surgical Safety Checklist implementation (10, 5.4%). Across the studies, the most consistent reduction in SSI was observed with guideline-concordant perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis, alcohol-based chlorhexidine skin preparation, surgeon hand preparation, limiting operating theatre traffic, negative pressure wound therapy, early postoperative bathing, sterile wound care, patient education and SSI surveillance. Conclusions The review suggests that the evidence from LMICs supports optimisation of perioperative antimicrobial therapy alongside implementation of simple, evidence-based infection prevention practices rather than reliance on prolonged post-operative antibiotic use. Developing context-specific SAP policies and strengthening SSI surveillance and staff education are essential for sustainable improvement. There remains a critical need to design and implement multipronged interventions that are scalable and feasible in LMIC settings.

title: A qualitative assessment of learner experiences with a novel Paediatric Emergency Medicine curriculum in Kenya.
journal: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence
abstract: Introduction Paediatric emergency and critical care (PECC) services are essential in reducing childhood mortality from treatable conditions, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where the burden remains high. Despite this need, access to subspecialty training in PECC has been limited in the region. Launched in 2019 at the University of Nairobi, the PECC-Kenya fellowship is a novel subspecialty training program for regional paediatricians in both paediatric emergency medicine (PEM) and critical care. Curricular elements for PEM within the fellowship were adapted from international guidelines for local context. The objective of this study was to explore the perspectives of current fellows and recent graduates on the content of the PEM portion of their curriculum to inform improvements and future development for the program and the region. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with current and former PECC-Kenya fellows. Program faculty developed an interview guide which included questions about perceptions on PEM, anticipated future practice, and strengths and opportunities within the curriculum. Interviews were conducted and recorded via Zoom by a non-faculty interviewer. Anonymized transcriptions were uploaded into Dedoose. After establishing inter-rater reliability, three reviewers coded the data, and key themes were identified. Results Ten interviews were conducted in 2022 and 2023, revealing several themes. Fellows anticipated providing continuous care from the emergency department to the intensive care unit as the sole PECC specialist in their institution or region. They highlighted program strengths including high-quality live online lectures, in-person PEM intensive training, diverse clinical exposure, and establishment of a peer network. Fellows expressed a desire for more hands-on training and recognized the importance of point-of-care ultrasound in facilitating rapid diagnosis and assisting in procedures, with need for additional training. Discussion Given the innovative nature of this training program and its distinctive demands, these themes and findings could serve as valuable guidance for similar initiatives emerging in the region.

title: Radical trachelectomy in Brazil: a multi-institutional review on fertility preservation and oncologic outcomes.
journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society

title: Traumatic Cervical Spine Injury in Children and Adolescents Requiring Neurosurgical Intensive Care: A Seven-Year Retrospective Descriptive Cohort.
abstract: Traumatic cervical spine injury in children and adolescents is uncommon but may cause major disability and prolonged critical care. This retrospective descriptive cohort characterizes patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to the Neurosurgical Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of a tertiary trauma center in New Delhi, India, during 2008-2015. Discharge status was classified as favorable (American Spinal Injury Association [ASIA] Impairment Scale D-E) or unfavorable (ASIA A-C or in-hospital death). We used chi-square tests with Yates' continuity correction, with unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 112 patients, 83.0% were male, 85.7% were aged 9-18 years, and 77.7% had spinal canal compromise. Forty-seven patients (42.0%) had favorable and 65 (58.0%) had unfavorable discharge status, including nine in-hospital deaths (8.0%). Favorable status was associated with absence of spinal canal compromise (OR 6.67, 95% CI 2.40-18.54) and absence of the composite ICU complication indicator (OR 6.44, 95% CI 2.61-15.93), and with fracture rather than subluxation, absence of tracheostomy, and favorable admission ASIA category. No multivariable adjustment was performed; these exploratory, unadjusted associations do not establish independent or causal effects. The cohort provides descriptive data from an under-reported tertiary trauma setting and identifies variables for prospective multicenter study.

title: A Study of Staff Experiences of Delivering Prehospital Emergency Services in India in the Context of the EMS Agenda 2050 Objectives.
abstract: Background and objective Emergency care services are crucial to the delivery of modern healthcare. This study investigated prehospital staff experiences in delivering emergency care in a low- to middle-income country (LMIC) India. The study was guided by the EMS Agenda 2050 principles for people-centred and technology-enabled health systems. The study was performed with emergency medical staff from the city of Gandhinagar, India, which is designated as a future smart city. Method This research used purposive and snowball sampling with 23 participants (ambulance drivers, emergency medical technicians, paramedics and first-aiders) from government, non-governmental and private organisations. Online semistructured interviews explored current prehospital care practices, challenges and opportunities. NVivo software was used for qualitative analysis, with a reflexive thematic analysis approach used to derive themes and present findings. Results The thematic analysis identified four primary themes with subthemes: (1) job satisfaction and challenges, (2) attitudes and emotions, (3) technological factors and (4) efficiency and caring. Findings highlight opportunities for technological interventions to enhance citizen awareness and training, support relatives during emergencies, provide bystanders with medically safe guidance and facilitate digitalisation in prehospital care. Conclusions This research advances understanding of the human and operational realities of prehospital care in a future smart-city context. Healthcare professionals demonstrated expertise and empathy in managing complex emergencies while recognising the importance of their role in caring for critically ill and injured patients. Although digital technologies are increasingly integrated into practice, hands-on skills and experiential judgement remain fundamental to effective care. The findings underscore the need for stakeholder collaboration, enhanced professional training and innovative citizen awareness initiatives to strengthen resilient prehospital care systems.

title: Support Utilization, Not Availability, Is Associated With Lower Burnout and Presenteeism Among Haemodialysis Nurses: A JD-R Model Study.
abstract: Aim To investigate the distinct pathways of social support and safety attitudes on presenteeism mediated by burnout in haemodialysis nurses and to identify the most potent protective resources within the JD-R model. Design A multicentre, cross-sectional survey. Methods Data from 583 haemodialysis nurses across multiple provinces were analysed using validated scales (SSRS, SAQ, MBI-HSS and SPS-6) and mediation analyses (PROCESS macro). Results Burnout fully mediated the relationship between job stress and presenteeism. Support utilization (rather than mere availability) was associated with the largest protective indirect effect. Management perceptions had a unique direct association with presenteeism. Clinically significant presenteeism was observed in 47.2% of the nurses. Low income combined with overtime was associated with higher burnout. Conclusion In clinical practice, activating support utilization (e.g., help-seeking behaviours) appears more critical than merely providing resources. Trust in leadership may directly safeguard organizational performance. Nursing managers should implement structural interventions (overtime caps, specialty premiums) to reduce the effort-reward imbalance. Nursing implications Creating help-seeking cultures and trustworthy leadership, alongside correcting systemic inequities, can break the burnout-presenteeism cycle and improve patient safety. Nursing managers should implement structured interventions such as overtime caps and specialty premiums to reduce effort-reward imbalance and develop resource navigation systems to activate support utilization at the unit level. Impact This study suggests that support utilization may be a key protective factor against burnout and presenteeism in high-reliability nursing settings, offering a targeted, tiered intervention framework for managers and policymakers. Reporting method The STROBE guidelines for cross-sectional studies. Patient or public contribution None.

title: Latent profiles of nutrition literacy among patients receiving peritoneal dialysis and their associations with dietary adherence and nutritional and metabolic indicators: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background Nutrition literacy is important for dietary self-management among patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD), yet the heterogeneity of nutrition literacy and its associations with dietary adherence and nutritional and metabolic indicators remain poorly understood. Aims To identify latent nutrition literacy profiles among patients receiving PD, examine factors associated with profile membership, and explore differences in dietary adherence and nutritional and metabolic indicators across profiles. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among 307 patients receiving PD from three tertiary hospitals in Hainan Province, China, between May and December 2025. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, the Nutrition Literacy Scale for Patients with End-Stage Kidney Disease Undergoing Dialysis, and the Renal Adherence Attitudes Questionnaire and the Renal Adherence Behaviour Questionnaire. Nutritional and metabolic indicators were extracted from electronic medical records. Latent profile analysis was performed using Mplus 8.3, and group comparisons and multinomial logistic regression analyses were conducted using SPSS 27.0. Results The mean nutrition literacy score was 14.10 ± 5.01. Three nutrition literacy profiles representing relatively low (46.5%), moderate (30.0%), and high (23.5%) levels were identified. Compared with the low profile, female sex and higher monthly personal income were associated with the moderate profile, while female sex, younger age, higher educational attainment, higher income, and longer dialysis duration were associated with the high profile (all p p Conclusion Nutrition literacy among patients receiving PD was heterogeneous, with three profiles differing in sociodemographic and disease-related characteristics, dietary adherence scores, and several nutritional and metabolic indicators. These profiles may provide a descriptive framework for recognizing subgroups with different nutrition support needs; however, their clinical utility requires external and longitudinal validation.

title: The hidden mental health burden of corruption in healthcare: Findings from a scoping review and key informant interviews.
abstract: Corruption in healthcare is a pervasive global challenge that undermines equity, efficiency, and trust in health systems. Whilst its economic and governance impacts are well documented, the psychological consequences for patients, providers, and those involved in anti-corruption reform remain under-explored. Understanding these mental health effects is critical for designing anti-corruption strategies that safeguard wellbeing and strengthen health systems. An exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted to map an emerging evidence base. A scoping review of 25 peer-reviewed and grey literature sources was complemented by four key informant interviews, which were used to interpret and contextualise the review findings. Findings were synthesised into a conceptual framework mapping pathways between corruption and mental health outcomes. Corruption was reported to be associated with psychological distress among patients, providers, and anti-corruption actors. This included stress, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and moral injury. At a community level, corruption eroded trust and collective agency, whilst institutional effects included normalisation of unethical practices. Structural determinants were found to perpetuate corruption's harms. Anti-corruption efforts produced mixed outcomes: reform targeting high-level officials improved public mental health modestly, whereas punitive measures against frontline workers exacerbated fear and demoralisation in the workforce. Protective factors such as moral agency, and robust reporting systems were found to buffer harm but were context dependent. Policy recommendations are made for practice, research and capacity building. These include framing corruption as a public mental health issue, strengthening whistleblower protections, commissioning further research, and adapting reform to local political economy and social norms. These findings indicate that corruption is a plausible but under-recognised social determinant of mental health requiring further research. Integrating mental health considerations into anti-corruption policy and health system reforms is essential to mitigate harm and strengthen resilience.

title: End-Of-Life Care in a Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Analysis of Interventions During the Last 48 Hours.
abstract: Background Palliative care in intensive care units should be planned jointly with patients and their families and documented in medical records. Proximity to death should prompt reassessment of the therapeutic strategy. Aim To analyse the interventions performed during the last 48 h in patients who died in the cardiac intensive care unit. Study design A retrospective cohort study was conducted in the cardiac intensive care unit of a large university hospital in Southeastern Brazil between March and April 2025. The deaths that occurred in 2022, 2023 and 2024 were evaluated. Results A total of 83 deaths with more than 5 days of hospital admission were analysed. There were few records documenting patients' and families' wishes. Only 12 (14.5%) records of limitations of life-sustaining treatments and 11 (13.3%) records of do-not-resuscitate orders directed to the healthcare team were identified. Conclusion Interventions intended to modify the course of the disease exceeded those aimed at palliative care in our cohort. Relevance to clinical practice These findings may support the implementation of trigger-based protocols for palliative care assessment in cardiac ICUs, the development of training strategies focused on communication and documentation of patient preferences for ICU teams, the strengthening of the role of the multidisciplinary team, and standardized comfort-focused interventions during the last 48 h of life.

title: Patient Awareness, Willingness, and Barriers to Pharmacist-Managed Clinics in a Chinese Tertiary Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
abstract: Purpose To assess patient awareness, willingness, and barriers regarding pharmacist-managed clinics (PMCs) in a Chinese tertiary hospital, and to examine the gap between selection of free pharmaceutical care services and willingness to attend PMCs. Patients and methods This cross-sectional survey used an electronic questionnaire with on-site investigator support. Adult outpatients and inpatients were recruited from Tongde Hospital of Zhejiang Province between July and August 2026. Convenience sampling was adopted, and participants with medical or pharmaceutical backgrounds were excluded. Data were collected via QR codes on mobile devices. Descriptive statistics and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used. Results 174 valid questionnaires were analyzed (96.67% of 180 participants). Awareness was extremely low, with 95.40% having never heard of PMCs. For medication-related problems, 93.10% preferred physicians. Only 27.59% of patients might attend PMCs, while 72.41% would not. The most reported barriers were that physicians already handled medication needs (70.11%), unfamiliarity with PMC services (36.78%), and concern about consultation fees (20.69%). Although 74.71% selected medication guidance when services were free, those who did were no more willing to attend than those who did not (27.69% vs 27.27%, P=0.957). Willingness was highest at ages 40-60 years (60.00%) and lowest at ≥61 years (16.22%, P χ 2 =9.38, P=0.002). Conclusion Despite policy promotion, awareness and willingness to attend PMCs were low. Even patients who selected medication guidance when free were not more willing to attend. Low uptake may reflect a service model misaligned with patients' care-seeking pathways. Future research should evaluate physician-referral or clinically embedded models.

title: Bridging institutional expertise and democratic decentralization: a proposed hub-and-spoke framework for rehabilitation, built on Kerala's model of community-based disability care.
abstract: Community-based rehabilitation (CBR) is the World Health Organization's (WHO) endorsed strategy for extending disability services in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet documented implementation problems - workforce shortage, fragmented supervision, and weak evidence on long-term adherence - continue to limit its reach, while centralized specialist institutes remain constrained by travel-related attrition among the families they serve. Kerala, India, has built one of the more mature decentralized CBR infrastructures in an LMIC setting: Local Self-Government Institutions (LSGIs), acting jointly with Kudumbashree (a state-wide community network of women) and drawing on their statutory healthcare responsibilities toward persons with disabilities under Section 25 of India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016, fund and operate close to 330 BUDS Schools and BUDS Rehabilitation Centres (BRCs) that already provide neighbourhood-level day-care, basic special education, and vocational support. This existing infrastructure, however, currently operates with limited formal linkage to specialist clinical governance. Building on established evidence that hub-and-spoke organization design improves access and continuity in other resource-constrained health systems - including prior applications to Indian rural healthcare more broadly - we propose, as a conceptual framework rather than a system already in operation, a formal Hub-and-Spoke integration in which a Central Government institute such as the Composite Regional Centre (CRC), Kozhikode, would serve as a technical "Hub' providing task-shared protocol design, tele-rehabilitation supervision, and assistive-technology specification, while the existing LSGI network operates as the 'Spoke.' We identify the conditions under which such integration could plausibly transfer to other settings, and outline a concrete research agenda - spanning feasibility, referral continuity, equity of reach, caregiver cost, workforce competency, and governance - needed before the framework's real-world value can be established.

title: Assisted reproduction in the public sector: why secondary-level hospitals matter for equity and continuity of care.
abstract: Background Infertility is a major public health challenge, yet access to assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains unequal, particularly where public provision is limited. This Policy and Practice Review examines the role of secondary-level hospitals in integrating ART into public health systems. Methods A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS, without publication-date restrictions, including literature in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Evidence on access, service organization, referral pathways, continuity of care, workforce, health information systems, governance, and financing was synthesized thematically and interpreted through expert-informed policy analysis. Results The review identified geographic, financial, organizational, and health-system barriers to equitable ART access. Integrated models may allow specialized centers to retain high-complexity procedures while secondary-level hospitals support infertility assessment, referral coordination, follow-up, and pregnancy surveillance. Eight policy priorities were identified: integration of secondary-level hospitals; standardized referral pathways; workforce development; national ART registries; equity-oriented evaluation; patient and community participation; integrated governance and quality assurance; and sustainable financing. An implementation framework specifying responsible actors, minimum resources, implementation phases, barriers, and monitoring indicators was developed. Conclusion Integrating secondary-level hospitals into coordinated ART networks may strengthen continuity of care, geographic accessibility, and use of specialized resources. These potential benefits require prospective evaluation during implementation.

title: Knowledge Graphs for Cervical Cancer Across the Care Continuum: From Vaccination and Screening to Personalized Therapy.
abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among women worldwide, with a disproportionately high burden in low- and middle-income countries. Infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the central etiological factor. Although HPV vaccination and standardized screening can substantially reduce incidence and mortality, major bottlenecks persist in real-world settings, including inadequate coverage, loss to follow-up, data silos, and limited interpretability of algorithms. Knowledge graphs (KGs), characterized by their core "entity-relation" structure, can integrate electronic medical records, HPV genotyping, pathology/imaging, multi-omics, and public health data within a unified semantic framework, and provide traceable evidence chains and reasoning pathways to support clinical decision-making. KGs may become an important enabler. This review summarizes the potential mechanisms and application paradigms of KGs along the full continuum of cervical cancer prevention and care, including primary prevention (vaccination strategies and health education), screening and diagnosis (multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and clinical decision support systems, CDSS), as well as therapeutic decision-making and follow-up management (molecular subtyping, drug associations, and recurrence monitoring. We further highlight key challenges such as ontology standardization, cross-institutional interoperability, dynamic knowledge updating, and reliability of automated knowledge extraction. Future work should focus on establishing reusable, engineering-oriented pathways for the synergy of "KG + large language models (LLMs)/multimodal AI", the development of explainability evaluation metrics, privacy-compliant frameworks, and deployable solutions for primary care settings, in order to accelerate progress toward the global cervical cancer elimination goal.

title: Tackling the Growing Threat of Multidrug-Resistant <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i> in Sub-Saharan Africa: Challenges, Strategies, and the Way Forward.
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a dangerous pathogen that has shown multidrug resistance in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and has significantly impacted healthcare, where poor infection control and limited resources are common. This narrative review examines strategies in the SSA region to control this pathogen, reports its prevalence, highlights key challenges, and suggests future research. Studies published between 2010 and 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, focusing on AMR surveillance, prevalence, infection control, and treatment strategies for AMR P. aeruginosa in SSA, were reviewed. Data were qualitatively and quantitatively summarized and mapped as descriptive median resistance (%) across SSA countries in a geographic heatmap. The results, illustrated in the heatmap, reveal substantial median resistance to common first-line agents, whereas significant data gaps indicate a critical lack of standardized surveillance in the region. Nations such as South Africa and Kenya have progressed with surveillance and stewardship programs. However, challenges persist in other countries, especially in diagnostics, access to new antibiotics, and infection control. New emerging therapies, including phage therapy and new antibiotics, have shown promise but are limited by regulatory frameworks, costs, and availability. Infection prevention measures are equally weak, resulting in high infection rates due to overcrowding and inadequate hygiene facilities. A more integrated approach that strengthens surveillance, improves infection control, and increases access to novel treatments is needed to combat MDR P. aeruginosa in SSA. Future research must prioritize affordable diagnostics and bridge the "data silence" identified in the regional resistance mapping to address the region's unique challenges.

title: Development of a master of science in digital health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Tanzania: a mixed-methods curriculum development study.
abstract: Background The rapid expansion of digital technologies is transforming health systems and creating increasing demand for a workforce with competencies in health informatics, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, digital health governance, and implementation. However, digital health training remains fragmented in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Tanzania.
